name: Moses, and the Egyptian in the sand
charge: Slaying an Egyptian and hiding him in the sand
summary: Moses went out to his brethren, saw an Egyptian smiting a Hebrew, looked this way and that, and slew him. He supposed his brethren would have understood that God by his hand would deliver them; they understood not, and the man who did the wrong threw the killing in his face. Forty years in Midian were the sentence.
offense: He knew whose son he was before he struck anyone. Raised in Pharaoh's house and called the son of Pharaoh's daughter, he went out unto his brethren and looked on their burdens, and the account calls the man he defended one of his brethren (Exodus 2:11), so the lineage was never in doubt to him. Acts gives what he was thinking: he supposed his brethren would have understood how that God by his hand would deliver them, but they understood not (Acts 7:25). The deliverance was the right end and the means and the timing were his own. The record's own witness that he knew it was unlawful is in the two details it bothers to keep: he looked this way and that way, and when he saw that there was no man, he slew the Egyptian, and hid him in the sand (Exodus 2:12). A man who is executing judgment does not check whether he is being watched, and does not bury the body.
judgment: The next day two Hebrews strove, and he that did the wrong said, Who made thee a prince and a judge over us? intendest thou to kill me, as thou killedst the Egyptian? And Moses feared, and said, Surely this thing is known. Pharaoh heard the thing and sought to slay Moses, and Moses fled from the face of Pharaoh and dwelt in the land of Midian, a stranger, where he begat two sons. He came back at eighty to the work he had tried to begin at forty.

entries.commentary: A man of the house of Levi took to wife a daughter of Levi. These are Amram and Jochebed, the father and mother of Moses, Aaron, and Miriam.

The woman conceived and bare a son, and when she saw him that he was a goodly child, she hid him three months. Goodly means the child was exceeding fair; there was something special about this child from his birth.

When she could no longer hide him, she took for him an ark of bulrushes, daubed it with slime and with pitch, and laid it in the flags by the river's brink. Bulrushes are the river reeds known as cattails. His sister Miriam stood afar off, to wit what would be done to him. The movie tellings of this account do not give the full details; to get a full understanding of what happened in the days of Moses you have to read the scriptures.

The daughter of Pharaoh sent her maid to fetch the ark, and when she had opened it she saw the child, and the babe wept. She had compassion on him and said, This is one of the Hebrews' children. She knew the child was a Hebrew and no Egyptian because the Most High put a difference between the Egyptians and Israel; though both peoples were dark of skin, this was a child of the chosen nation.

Miriam was crafty. She offered to call a nurse of the Hebrew women, and Pharaoh's daughter sent the maid, who called the child's own mother, and wages were paid her to nurse him. So Moses was raised in his first years by his actual mother; the Most High allowed it, all praises to Him.

The child grew, and he became the son of Pharaoh's daughter. She called his name Moses, which means drawn out, because she drew him out of the water. So Moses grew up as an Egyptian, although he was a Hebrew.

When Moses was grown he went out unto his brethren the Israelites and looked on their burdens, and he spied an Egyptian smiting an Hebrew, one of his brethren. Moses knew the Israelites were his brothers; he knew he was not of the Egyptian lineage and that there was something different about him. He looked this way and that way, and when he saw that there was no man, he slew the Egyptian and hid him in the sand. He did not just marvel at the oppression; he used his position for his people, unlike many who hold a position of power today and will not risk it for their people. Moses is the ultimate revolutionary, as Christ is.

The second day two men of the Hebrews strove together, and he that did the wrong answered, Who made thee a prince and a judge over us? intendest thou to kill me, as thou killedst the Egyptian? When a people is oppressed they take the oppression out on one another, and brothers become their own enemies; the same spirit answers correction among Israel today, pointing the finger at the one who corrects. Moses feared, and said, Surely this thing is known.

When Pharaoh heard this thing, he sought to slay Moses; but Moses fled from the face of Pharaoh and dwelt in the land of Midian. Moses gave up his whole upbringing and position. By faith he refused to be called the son of Pharaoh's daughter, choosing rather to suffer affliction with the people of God than to enjoy the pleasures of sin for a season. In Egypt his head was shaved, his beard cut, his dress and customs Egyptian; he laid all of it down to be what he was called to be, an Israelite. The same claim stands now: the remnant does not want the names of the captivity but the natural heritage of Israel, esteeming the reproach of Christ greater riches than the treasures of this land.

The priest of Midian had seven daughters, and the shepherds drove them from the troughs; but Moses stood up and helped them, and watered their flock. Moses was a man of war, not a weak man. The daughters told their father, An Egyptian delivered us out of the hand of the shepherds. They took Moses for an Egyptian by his dress, by how he carried himself, and by his skin: Moses was a very dark-skinned man, the same color as the Egyptians. Israel was always being mistaken for Egyptians. Reuel the priest of Midian is the same man called Jethro, the father in law of Moses.

Moses was content to dwell with the man, and he gave Moses Zipporah his daughter. She bare him a son, and he called his name Gershom: for he said, I have been a stranger in a strange land; Gershom means stranger. Zipporah and her family were Midianites, not Israelites; Moses married a woman of the land where he dwelt those forty years.

In process of time the king of Egypt died, and the children of Israel sighed by reason of the bondage, and they cried, and their cry came up unto God, as Israel cries in this captivity today. God heard their groaning, and God remembered his covenant with Abraham, with Isaac, and with Jacob. The bondage itself was prophesied to Abraham: his seed would be a stranger in a land not theirs and be afflicted four hundred years, and afterward come out with great substance. That prophecy is about Egypt, not a date of release in this present day. God had respect unto them. The Most High has respect unto one nation, Israel: He is in the midst of Israel, and His people shall never be ashamed. Respect unto His chosen is not respect of persons. Within Israel there is no respect of persons: the Most High renders to every man according to his deeds, tribulation and anguish upon every soul that doeth evil, of the Jew first and also of the Gentile, the southern kingdom and the northern kingdom that was Hellenized; but glory, honour, and peace to every man that worketh good. The nation is chosen above the nations, and all Israel shall be saved through the Deliverer out of Sion.

This is Stephen at the council, addressing the audience just before he is put to death. He answers the high priest by going all the way back to the beginning: the God of glory appeared unto our father Abraham when he was in Mesopotamia, before he dwelt in Charran. Abraham came out of the land of the Chaldeans, dwelt in Charran, and after his father died the Most High removed him into this land wherein they now dwell, and gave him no inheritance in it, not so much as to set his foot on, yet promised to give it to him and his seed after him when as yet he had no child. Notice how Stephen recites this history off the top of his head. Our forefathers read more than their four chapters a day. When you read, you put these things to memory, so you can recite it. A lot of us cannot recite our own history, but we can recite LeBron James and the NBA stats, football stats. These men were studious; they constantly gave attendance to studying. They called Paul mad for reading so many letters. Our forefathers were addicted to this gospel.

The Most High spoke that Abraham's seed should sojourn in a strange land and be brought into bondage and treated evil four hundred years, and the nation to whom they were in bondage he would judge, and after that they would come forth and serve him in this place. Then he gave Abraham the covenant of circumcision, and so Abraham begat Isaac and circumcised him the eighth day, and Isaac begat Jacob, and Jacob begat the twelve patriarchs.

The patriarchs, moved with envy, sold Joseph into Egypt, but the Most High was with him and delivered him out of all his afflictions and gave him favor and wisdom in the sight of Pharaoh, who made him governor over Egypt and all his house. When the famine came over Egypt and Canaan, Jacob heard there was corn in Egypt and sent out our fathers first; the second time Joseph was made known to his brethren, and Joseph's kindred was made known to Pharaoh. Jacob went down into Egypt with threescore and fifteen souls, and he and our fathers died and were carried over into Sychem and laid in the sepulchre Abraham bought for a sum of money.

As the time of the promise drew near which the Most High had sworn to Abraham, the people grew and multiplied in Egypt, until another king arose who knew not Joseph. The same dealt subtly with our kindred and evil-treated our fathers, so that they cast out their young children to the end they might not live.

In that time Moses was born, exceeding fair, nourished up in his father's house three months, and when he was cast out, Pharaoh's daughter took him up and nourished him for her own son. Moses was learned in all the wisdom of the Egyptians and was mighty in words and in deeds. That corrects the doctrine that certain Christian pastors preach, that Moses stuttered and could not speak. You cannot be a stupid man and be a prince over Egypt. He was raised under Pharaoh, so he had to learn everything of Egypt, their gods, their laws, the language. He was not a stupid man, and he did not stutter.

When Moses was full forty years old, it came into his heart to visit his brethren the children of Israel. Contrary to the movie The Ten Commandments, Moses always knew who he was; his own mother raised and nursed him, so he knew his brothers, he was only raised under the household of the Egyptians. Seeing one of them suffer wrong, he defended him and smote the Egyptian, supposing his brethren would understand that the Most High by his hand would deliver them, but they understood not. The next day, striving to make peace, he was thrust away with, Who made thee a ruler and a judge over us? Only the Most High could set a man to judge. This is the crabs in a barrel spirit: even after you help somebody, they say, Who are you to be over us? Everybody wants to be the head, the chief, a leader, but nobody wants to be a follower, and nobody wants to give credit when credit is due. The Most High was using the status Moses had in Egypt to help his brother, and they used it against him: Wilt thou kill me as thou didst the Egyptian yesterday? Certain of us will be put in different positions in this society, in politics, in education, and the Most High will use those accolades to your advantage, the same way he used Moses to go to Pharaoh and not be put to death right off the bat. Then Moses fled and was a stranger in the land of Midian, understanding that if he stayed among his own people they would get him killed, and there he begat two sons. People use the excuse that Moses married an Ethiopian to justify interracial marriage, saying maybe the Lord would forgive them the same way. But the Most High says, I will have mercy on whom I will have mercy. You are not Moses. Ask Aaron and Miriam, whom the Most High plagued in the skin and put out of the camp seven days for speaking against a matter that did not concern them. Do not point fingers and compare yourself to the person next to you, wondering why one brother is judged for a matter and another is treated differently. Different judgments belong to the Most High. You are not David; do not weigh Saul's sins against David's and assume you know how the Most High will judge, the way men questioned why Uzza was struck for touching the ark. Work out your own soul salvation with fear and trembling, study to be quiet, and mind your own business.

Forty years later, Moses now eighty years old, an angel of the Lord appeared to him in a flame of fire in a bush at Mount Sinai. Brothers and sisters say they are too old to repent; you are never too old. The Most High used Moses at eighty to deliver the whole nation, and retained his strength. The voice of the Lord said, I am the God of thy fathers, the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. Moses trembled and durst not behold. He was told to put off his shoes, for the place was holy ground, and the Most High said, I have seen the affliction of my people in Egypt, I have heard their groaning, and I am come down to deliver them; now come, I will send thee into Egypt.

This Moses, whom they refused saying, Who made thee a ruler and a judge, the same did the Most High send to be a ruler and a deliverer by the hand of the angel that appeared in the bush. Be careful with one another; the same person you reject is the same person the Most High raises up over you. This is the spirit of preeminence, not wanting another brother to rule over you because you believe you should be in that position. The Most High sees the heart and knows the spirits he is setting up. Moses was the meekest, most humble man. For a prince to go down to people counted as slaves and servants, defend them, and risk himself for a stiffnecked and rebellious people, shows he loved his people even in his position of authority. This is that Moses who said, A prophet shall the Lord your God raise up unto you of your brethren like unto me; him shall ye hear. Stephen rehearsed all the history to bring them up to Christ, because the whole ministry throughout Acts is Christ's name preached in the place of animal sacrifice. Even as Pharisees, they knew this prophecy, so he made it plain: the prophet Moses spoke about is that Christ.

This is he that was in the church in the wilderness with the angel that spoke to him in Mount Sinai, and with our fathers, who received the lively oracles to give unto us. The one in the church in the wilderness is that Christ, the prophet of verse 37. Our fathers would not obey him but thrust him from them, and in their hearts turned back to Egypt, telling Aaron, Make us gods to go before us, for as for this Moses we know not what is become of him. They did not obey Christ in the wilderness, just as they did not obey Christ in his day. They made a calf, offered sacrifice to the idol, and rejoiced in the works of their own hands, so the Most High gave them up to worship the host of heaven; they took up the tabernacle of Moloch and the star of the god Remphan, figures they made to worship, and he carried them away beyond Babylon.

Our fathers had the tabernacle of witness in the wilderness, made according to the fashion Moses had seen, which our fathers brought in with Jesus into the possession of the Gentiles, whom the Most High drove out before their face. That Jesus is Joshua, and the Most High drove out the nations before the fathers. This continued unto the days of David, who found favor before the Most High and desired to find a tabernacle for the God of Jacob, but Solomon built him a house. Howbeit the Most High dwelleth not in temples made with hands: Heaven is my throne, and earth is my footstool; what house will ye build me, saith the Lord, or what is the place of my rest? Hath not my hand made all these things?

Stephen turns it on them: Ye stiffnecked and uncircumcised in heart and ears, ye do always resist the Holy Ghost; as your fathers did, so do ye. The Holy Ghost the fathers resisted in the wilderness is the same Holy Ghost resisted in Christ's day, and that Holy Ghost is first and foremost the laws. There are three forms of the Holy Ghost taught in this series: first the laws, when you keep the laws of the Most High; then wisdom and understanding, which comes after you keep the laws; and then power, as the apostles received power to speak in tongues and perform miracles. Which of the prophets did their fathers not persecute? They slew them that showed before of the coming of the Just One, of whom they had now been the betrayers and murderers, who received the law by the disposition of angels and kept it not.

When they heard these things they were cut to the heart and gnashed on him with their teeth. But Stephen, being full of the Holy Ghost, looked up steadfastly into heaven and saw the glory of the Most High and Jesus standing on the right hand of God, and said, Behold, I see the heavens opened and the Son of man standing on the right hand of God. They cried out with a loud voice, stopped their ears, ran upon him with one accord, cast him out of the city, and stoned him; the witnesses laid down their clothes at the feet of a young man named Saul. Stephen, calling on the Most High, said, Lord Jesus, receive my spirit, and kneeling down he cried, Lord, lay not this sin to their charge, and fell asleep. This is the same spirit Christ had when he said, Father, forgive them, for they know not what they do.

An image in itself is not the sin, except for that white image of the beast; making images to bow down to them and serve them is the transgression, for the Lord thy God is a jealous God. Visiting the iniquity of the fathers upon the children unto the third and fourth generation: Israel is yet this day in captivity, scattered for a reproach and a curse, according to all the iniquities of the fathers which departed from the Lord. Right now Israel is paying for the sins of the fathers; that is why the people are scattered to the four corners of the earth.

And shewing mercy unto thousands of them that love me, and keep my commandments. Judith recounted how the Most High tried the fathers for the examination of their hearts: he tried Abraham and Isaac, and Jacob in Mesopotamia of Syria keeping the sheep of Laban, serving twenty years with his wages changed and given Leah when he looked for Rachel. In Judith's day there was no tribe, family, people, nor city that worshipped gods made with hands, as had been aforetime; for that cause she trusted the Lord would not despise the nation. Mercy rests on them that know none other God, not Allah, not Buddha, not a white Jesus.

Remember the Sabbath day, to keep it holy. The word says remember because Israel would forget it: in this captivity the people were forced to serve other gods and their religions, and the Sabbath was lost through forced conversion. Look up the blue laws, also known as Sunday laws; they help give understanding of why the Bible says remember the Sabbath day.

An altar of stone was not to be built of hewn stone, for lifting up a tool upon it pollutes it; neither go up by steps unto the altar, that thy nakedness be not discovered thereon. This scripture helps explain pants, precept upon precept. The priests were given linen breeches to cover their nakedness from the loins even unto the thighs when they came near the altar, and Israel was called in this same reading to be a kingdom of priests, so do not be simple and say that law was only for Aaron and his sons. Those breeches were made for men and not for women, as the law of the garments also shows.

Moses commands the tribes to separate cities out of their own inheritance for the Levites to dwell in, with suburbs round about them. The Levites needed cities inside every tribe's territory because the Most High took them from among the children of Israel as a gift, to do the service of the tabernacle of the congregation. Every tribe needed that service done among them, so the Levites had to be spread out through all the children of Israel. The commandment was fulfilled when Israel came into the land: the heads of the fathers of the Levites came to Eleazar the priest and Joshua at Shiloh and claimed the cities the Lord commanded by the hand of Moses.

The cities were for the Levites to dwell in, and the suburbs were for their cattle, their goods, and all their beasts. The suburbs were measured out: a thousand cubits from the wall of the city round about, and two thousand cubits on the east, south, west, and north sides, with the city in the midst.

Among the Levite cities six were set apart for refuge, appointed for the manslayer to flee there, with forty and two more added: forty and eight cities in all, given from every tribe according to its inheritance, many from them that had many and few from them that had few. Why would the Lord permit a manslayer refuge? The Most High gave Moses the understanding of how to discern manslaughter from murder. For murder there was no refuge, but for manslaughter cities of refuge were given. The law itself was already instituted in [Exodus 21](/bible/exodus/21); [Numbers 35](/bible/numbers/35) answers where the manslayer goes: the Most High appointed him a place to flee.

Killeth any person unawares means he did not mean to do it; it was an accident that resulted in a death. Accidental deaths are of the Lord, beyond our control. Refuge means a condition of being safe or sheltered from pursuit, danger, or trouble. The cities of refuge exist because the manslayer is being pursued: someone has the right to avenge the death of the one who was killed. The city of refuge keeps the manslayer alive until he stands before the congregation in judgment, so the trial can discern between murder and manslaughter before the avenger reaches him.

Six cities of refuge stood, three on this side Jordan and three in the land of Canaan, and they served the children of Israel, the stranger, and the sojourner among them alike. The chapter lays out three categories when someone dies by the hand of another: he meant to hurt him but not kill him, yet he died, and that is murder; he hated him and killed him with premeditation, and that is murder; or he had no quarrel and never meant it, and that is manslaughter, not worthy of death.

Smite him with an instrument of iron, with a stone, or with a hand weapon of wood so that he die, and he is a murderer: even if the intent was only to hurt him and not to kill him, if he dies, the judgment is death. This is a precept for the street: the music culture glorifies slinging an iron, but the word says if you sling that iron and the brother dies, you are a murderer and your judgment is to die.

The revenger of blood himself slays the murderer when he meets him; there was no refuge and no mercy for murder. This is the law given to Israel at that time, an understanding of those judgments; it is not license for anyone to go about killing today.

Laying of wait means he was lurking and stalking, waiting to catch him slipping because of hatred between them; that is premeditated murder. Even without a weapon, smiting him in enmity with the hand so that he dies is murder; he that smote him shall surely be put to death.

The law repeats its key words on purpose, the way legal statutes do, because the details decide the case: suddenly, without enmity, without laying of wait, and seeing him not. Seeing him not matters because it is nearly impossible to kill a man by accident while looking straight at him; the victim was out of sight when the thing flew and struck him. He was not his enemy and sought not his harm: there could be no documented past hatred, and he could not even have been seeking to harm him, since seeking only to harm still makes the death murder. Then the congregation judges between the slayer and the revenger of blood according to these judgments.

Once the congregation clears him of murder, it delivers the slayer out of the hand of the revenger and restores him to his city of refuge; he still must abide there. He stays within the city until the death of the high priest which was anointed with the holy oil, whoever held that office when the incident happened.

If the slayer steps outside the borders of his city of refuge before that high priest dies and the revenger of blood finds him there and kills him, the revenger is not guilty of blood, because the slayer was instructed to remain within the borders. After the death of the high priest the slayer returns to the land of his possession, and the avenger can no longer touch him.

The murderer is put to death by the mouth of witnesses, plural: multiple people must testify, and their stories must match in the details for the murder to be established. One witness alone cannot cause a man to die, because a single witness could lie in the interest of the avenger and put an innocent man to death. The rule stood first for sins worthy of death and then had to become the principle for every matter: two or three witnesses establish any accusation of iniquity or sin.

The judges could take no satisfaction for the life of a murderer guilty of death, and no satisfaction for the manslayer to come home before the death of the high priest; a guilty man cannot buy himself off. No matter who stands before the judge or what money is offered, if they are guilty of death they are guilty of death; a gift blinds the eyes of the wise and perverts the words of the righteous. Israel's judges later fell into exactly this: they became covetous and took bribes to clear the guilty and turn aside the poor in the gate.

Blood defileth the land, and the land cannot be cleansed of the blood shed in it but by the blood of him that shed it; the murderer who escapes his judgment leaves the land polluted. That judgment was instituted back in the days of Noah, and Moses carried it forward in the statutes given to Israel, for the Lord himself dwells among the children of Israel.

name: Moses and the uncircumcised son
charge: Neglecting the sign of the covenant in his own house
summary: Sent back to Egypt with the rod of God in his hand, Moses took his wife and his sons and went. He had just been given the message for Pharaoh: Israel is my son, even my firstborn; let my son go, and if thou refuse, I will slay thy son, even thy firstborn. By the way in the inn the Lord met him and sought to kill him, because his own son was uncircumcised. Zipporah took a sharp stone and circumcised the child and cast the foreskin at his feet, and said, Surely a bloody husband art thou to me. So he let him go.
offense: Circumcision was not a Sinai ordinance. It was given to Abraham centuries earlier as the token of the covenant, every man child among you shall be circumcised, and he that is eight days old shall be circumcised among you, every man child in your generations (Genesis 17:10-12), with the penalty written into it: the uncircumcised man child whose flesh of his foreskin is not circumcised, that soul shall be cut off from his people, he hath broken my covenant (Genesis 17:14). That is why the deliverer of Israel was worthy of death on the road, and it is why the case belongs in this volume as evidence that the law was in force long before it was written in stone. Two things sharpen it. Egypt did not practise it, and Israel was afterwards told plainly, after the doings of the land of Egypt, wherein ye dwelt, shall ye not do (Leviticus 18:3), so a man raised in Pharaoh's house had taken up the omission of the country he was raised in. And the errand he was carrying makes it intolerable: he had just been given the words, Israel is my son, even my firstborn; let  my son go, and if thou refuse, I will slay thy son, even thy firstborn (Exodus 4:22-23). He was going to demand another man's firstborn on pain of death while his own son bore no token of the covenant he was invoking.
judgment: The Lord met him and sought to kill him (Exodus 4:24), which is the sentence of Genesis 17:14 falling on the head of the house rather than on the child. The remedy was immediate and it was performed by his wife: then Zipporah took a sharp stone, and cut off the foreskin of her son, and cast it at his feet, and said, Surely a bloody husband art thou to me (Exodus 4:25). So he let him go; then she said, A bloody husband thou art, because of the circumcision (Exodus 4:26), and the record explains her own words so that they are not mistaken for a complaint about anything else. The record gives no further comment, and the placing is the comment: the thing had to be set right in his own house before he could carry a word from God into Pharaoh's. The same neglect cost the next generation as well, for all the people born in the wilderness had not been circumcised, and Joshua had to make sharp knives and circumcise them again the second time before they took the land (Joshua 5:2-5). The token was never withdrawn: Abraham was ninety years old and nine when he was circumcised  (Genesis 17:24), and Paul took and circumcised Timothy because of the Jews which were in those quarters (Acts 16:3). Circumcision verily profiteth, if thou keep the law (Romans 2:25), and the circumcision of the heart is commanded alongside it and not instead of it, circumcise yourselves to the Lord, and take away the foreskins of your heart (Jeremiah 4:4).

verses.text: 22And thou shalt say unto Pharaoh, Thus saith the Lord, Israel is my son, even my firstborn: 23And I say unto thee, Let my son go, that he may serve me: and if thou refuse to let him go, behold, I will slay thy son, even thy firstborn.

entries.commentary: Moses answered, But, behold, they will not believe me, nor hearken unto my voice. Moses knew the spirit of his people: Israel is impudent, hardhearted, and stiffnecked, a rebellious house that does not like to listen even when shown precept upon precept. The word to Ezekiel is the same commission: Israel is not a people of a strange speech and hard language; had the prophet been sent to such, they would have hearkened; but the house of Israel will not hearken. Go, get thee to them of the captivity, and speak unto them, whether they will hear or whether they will forbear. That stubbornness is itself a mark of who the Israelites are among the nations today.

The first sign: the rod cast on the ground became a serpent, and Moses fled from before it; he caught it by the tail and it became a rod in his hand. The sign was given that they may believe that the LORD God of their fathers, the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob, hath appeared unto thee. Israel would not believe on a man's word alone; it took a miracle, because we were a people of little faith.

The second sign: Moses put his hand into his bosom, and when he took it out, his hand was leprous as snow; he put it in again, and it was turned again as his other flesh. This was a miracle precisely because Moses was a very dark-skinned man; the daughters of the priest of Midian had taken him for an Egyptian. The hand came out white as snow and went back to his natural dark skin; had he been white already there would have been no sign in it. If they will not believe the first sign, they will believe the voice of the latter sign; the magicians of Egypt could imitate serpents, but not this.
The third sign: if they will not believe the first two, take of the water of the river and pour it upon the dry land, and the water shall become blood upon the dry land.

Moses said, O my Lord, I am not eloquent, but I am slow of speech, and of a slow tongue. Moses did not stutter, as is commonly taught; he was not fluent in the Hebrew tongue. He was learned in all the wisdom of the Egyptians and mighty in words and in deeds, but he grew up in Pharaoh's house speaking the Egyptian language and then spent forty years in Midian, and a language moves on in forty years. The LORD answered, Who hath made man's mouth? Now therefore go, and I will be with thy mouth, and teach thee what thou shalt say.

Moses pressed, Send, I pray thee, by the hand of him whom thou wilt send; and the anger of the LORD was kindled against Moses. Is not Aaron the Levite thy brother? I know that he can speak well; he spoke the Hebrew of the people fluently. Aaron shall be thy spokesman unto the people: he shall be to thee instead of a mouth, and thou shalt be to him instead of God. Moses stood as God in this instance, speaking through Aaron his prophet, who interpreted to the people. And thou shalt take this rod in thine hand, wherewith thou shalt do signs.

Moses returned to Jethro his father in law and asked leave, and Jethro said, Go in peace. The LORD said, Go, return into Egypt: for all the men are dead which sought thy life; the Pharaoh of chapter 2 had died. Moses took his wife and his sons and returned to the land of Egypt, and Moses took the rod of God in his hand. The LORD told him, Do all those wonders before Pharaoh which I have put in thine hand: but I will harden his heart, that he shall not let the people go. Thou shalt say unto Pharaoh, Thus saith the LORD, Israel is my son, even my firstborn. Israel was not the first nation created; it was among the last. But Israel is the first nation the Most High chose, the apple of His eye from Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob down. If thou refuse to let him go, behold, I will slay thy son, even thy firstborn.

By the way in the inn, the LORD met him, and sought to kill him, because Moses had not circumcised his son. Zipporah took a sharp stone, cut off the foreskin of her son, and said, Surely a bloody husband art thou to me: bloody because of the circumcision she had to perform herself. This shows the laws did not begin at Sinai. Circumcision was the covenant given to Abraham for every man child in his generations, on the eighth day, and the uncircumcised man child whose flesh is not circumcised, that soul shall be cut off from his people: he hath broken my covenant. That is why Moses was worthy of death.

The LORD sent Aaron into the wilderness to meet Moses, and he met him in the mount of God and kissed him; Aaron believed right away. Moses told Aaron all the words of the LORD and all the signs. Aaron spake all the words which the LORD had spoken unto Moses and did the signs in the sight of the people, and the people believed: and when they heard that the LORD had visited the children of Israel, and that he had looked upon their affliction, they bowed their heads and worshipped. After a long time in which the Lord had not been dealing with them, He finally heard their prayers.

At ninety and nine years old Abram was commanded to walk before the Most High and be perfect. There is no age excuse; Christ said nothing new in [Matthew 5:48](/bible/matthew/5#v48), for the command to be perfect was given thousands of years before. Perfect according to the scriptures means to walk in His statutes and keep His commandments; that is how Israel perfects itself.

When the Most High began dealing with Abram on a covenant level, his name was changed: Abram became Abraham, a father of many nations, and kings would come out of him. Father of many nations does not mean everybody is spiritually a child of Abraham. The same promise was passed down the seed line: Jacob's name was changed to Israel and told a nation and a company of nations and kings would come out of his loins. The blessing of all men and the covenant were made to rest upon the head of Jacob and divided among the twelve tribes. Kings come out of that seed, including Christ, the King of kings.
The covenant is with Abraham's seed after him, and seed is literal offspring, not a spiritual metaphor. The Most High promised to be a God to Abraham and to his seed after him.

Circumcision is the token of the covenant: every man child circumcised at eight days, and the uncircumcised soul cut off from his people. Abraham received circumcision as a seal of the righteousness of the faith he had yet being uncircumcised. He believed and obeyed first, and circumcision sealed it; likewise a brother can come into the truth, get built up in the faith, and then go through with the process. It still has to be done. A covenant is a contract with terms; the covenant was confirmed to Jacob for a law, and circumcision is one of the laws within the covenant.

Sarai's name was changed to Sarah, and she shall be a mother of nations; those are the same nations of the covenant, and she and Abraham had one child together, Isaac. Abraham fell on his face and laughed in his heart: shall a child be born to a hundred year old man, and Sarah bear at ninety? The Most High read his thought and named the child from it: Isaac means he will laugh.

Ishmael received a blessing: fruitful, multiplied exceedingly, twelve princes, a great nation. But the word to Abraham was kings shall come out of thee, and the covenant passes to Isaac: my covenant will I establish with Isaac. Not all who are of Abraham's seed are the children; in Isaac shall thy seed be called. Ishmael was born of the flesh, of Sarai's plan, with no word from God ordaining it; the children of the promise are counted for the seed.

The selfsame day Abraham circumcised every male of his house, himself at ninety and nine and Ishmael at thirteen. That is the righteous example: he received the commandment and performed it the same day.

The kings of the Amorites and the Canaanites heard that the Lord had dried up the waters of Jordan from before the children of Israel, and their heart melted: they were paralyzed with fear. They had heard how the Most High split the Red sea in Exodus, and now he had done it again at Jordan, so neither was there spirit in them any more because of the children of Israel.

Circumcise again the children of Israel the second time: the children of Israel had not been keeping the commandments, being stiffnecked and hardheaded, and the Lord told Joshua to fix them. Circumcision is the covenant the Most High instituted with our forefather Abraham: every man child circumcised at eight days old, and the servant born in the house or bought with money circumcised likewise and keeping the laws as well. When Abraham received the commandment he performed it, circumcising every male of his house the selfsame day; he showed the Lord by his actions that he believed. So the men in Joshua who had not been circumcised showed a form of repentance by applying the law of circumcision.

This is the cause of the circumcision: all the men of war that came out of Egypt died in the wilderness because they obeyed not the voice of the Lord, and the generation born by the way had not been circumcised. That they had not circumcised themselves means they did not obey the voice of the Lord: they should have been circumcised physically and also mentally and spiritually. The land that floweth with milk and honey is understood by the Bible's own dictionary, precept upon precept: the rebels in Numbers called Egypt the land flowing with milk and honey, and Israel was brought out of the land of Egypt, so the phrase describes a land abundant in food. The milk goes into your cattle and your meats, and the honey goes into your vegetation. The mixed multitude and the children of Israel wept for the fish, cucumbers, melons, leeks, onions, and garlic they ate in Egypt: they were comfortable in their oppression and did not understand they were not free, the same mindset among our people in captivity today who say they are free and living their best life. The honey teaching carries a dietary lesson: hast thou found honey, eat so much as is sufficient for thee. Do not overeat; balance your salts, sugars, meats, and dainties moderately.

Their children raised up in their stead Joshua circumcised, for they had not circumcised them by the way. A father can have his son circumcised in the flesh yet never circumcise him from the heart: if he never teaches him the laws and to obey the voice of the Lord, the physical circumcision alone profits him nothing. It is symbolic of obeying the voice of the Lord.
They abode in their places in the camp till they were whole: these were grown men, not eight day old babies, so they had to remain in the camp until they healed from the circumcision.

This day have I rolled away the reproach of Egypt from off you: they finally believed and obeyed, circumcising themselves and obeying the voice of the Lord, so they were no longer a reproach, an embarrassment, or a disgrace. The children of Israel finally sanctified themselves, and the name of the place is called Gilgal unto this day.

The children of Israel encamped in Gilgal and kept the passover on the fourteenth day of the month at even in the plains of Jericho; the passover was instituted by the Most High, and you can read about it in [Exodus 12](/bible/exodus/12). They did eat of the old corn of the land on the morrow after the passover, and the manna ceased; the children of Israel had manna no more, but ate of the fruit of the land of Canaan that year.

Joshua lifted up his eyes by Jericho and saw a man standing over against him with his sword drawn, a warrior. Joshua did not run; he went straight to him and asked, Art thou for us, or for our adversaries? There was no fear in the heart of Joshua. The man answered, Nay; but as captain of the host of the Lord am I now come. Host means army: he is the captain, the leader, of the army of the Lord. When Joshua realized who stood before him, the fear came: he fell on his face to the earth and did worship, and the leader of Israel's army called himself a servant, saying, What saith my lord unto his servant? Joshua had cleaved to Moses and understood who the captain of the host is. The captain of the host of the Lord is Christ, the captain of our salvation. This is why Joshua was afraid: the return of Christ is not the soft picture Christianity paints, for he is not coming back made like unto his brethren as at the first, but with the power of the living God, to take vengeance and destroy. No missiles or fighter jets will do anything against him.
The captain of the Lord's host said, Loose thy shoe from off thy foot; for the place whereon thou standest is holy. And Joshua did so.

name: The magicians of Egypt
charge: Withstanding Moses with their enchantments, and hardening Pharaoh in his refusal
summary: Pharaoh called the wise men and the sorcerers, and they matched the rod and the blood and the frogs with their enchantments. At the lice they could not, and said, This is the finger of God. At the boils they could not so much as stand before Moses, because the boil was upon them.
offense: Pharaoh called the wise men and the sorcerers, and the magicians of Egypt did in like manner with their enchantments (Exodus 7:11), and what they did was witchcraft, which the law puts under death and names among the abominations for which the nations were cast out (Deuteronomy 18:10-12; Exodus 22:18). But mark the limit of the craft: they could copy a plague and they could not lift one. They turned water into blood and could not turn it back clear, and the fish still died and the river still stank; they brought up frogs and could not remove a frog. Every imitation therefore added to the affliction of their own country while giving the king a reason to refuse, and the record gives that reason each time: and Pharaoh's heart was hardened, neither did he hearken unto them, as the Lord had said (Exodus 7:22). The use of the craft was to hold a king in his sin, and it was practised on a people who were suffering for it.
judgment: Aaron's rod swallowed up their rods before the contest had properly begun (Exodus 7:12). At the third plague the craft ran out: the magicians did so with their enchantments to bring forth lice, but they could not, and they said unto Pharaoh, This is the finger of God (Exodus 8:18-19), and even that confession did not move the king. At the sixth they could not so much as stand in the room, for the boil was upon the magicians, and upon all the Egyptians (Exodus 9:11). The whole contest was a judgment on what they served, for the Lord had said, against all the gods of Egypt I will execute judgment: I am the Lord (Exodus 12:12), and Numbers records that it was done, upon their gods also the Lord executed judgments (Numbers 33:4). Paul names the two and gives the standing sentence on every imitator after them: as Jannes and Jambres withstood Moses, so do these also resist the truth, but they shall proceed no further, for their folly shall be manifest unto all men (2 Timothy 3:8-9).

verses.text: 10And Moses and Aaron went in unto Pharaoh, and they did so as the Lord had commanded: and Aaron cast down his rod before Pharaoh, and before his servants, and it became a serpent. 11Then Pharaoh also called the wise men and the sorcerers: now the magicians of Egypt, they also did in like manner with their enchantments. 12For they cast down every man his rod, and they became serpents: but Aaron’s rod swallowed up their rods. 13And he hardened Pharaoh’s heart, that he hearkened not unto them; as the Lord had said.

16And the Lord said unto Moses, Say unto Aaron, Stretch out thy rod, and smite the dust of the land, that it may become lice throughout all the land of Egypt. 17And they did so; for Aaron stretched out his hand with his rod, and smote the dust of the earth, and it became lice in man, and in beast; all the dust of the land became lice throughout all the land of Egypt. 18And the magicians did so with their enchantments to bring forth lice, but they could not: so there were lice upon man, and upon beast. 19Then the magicians said unto Pharaoh, This is the finger of God: and Pharaoh’s heart was hardened, and he hearkened not unto them; as the Lord had said.

entries.commentary: The Lord made Moses a god to Pharaoh, and Aaron his brother was his prophet. Moses was as God and Aaron was the mouthpiece, because Moses kept saying he was of uncircumcised lips. This is why you do not move in a spirit of speaking against your leadership. Airing your complaints in front of everybody instead of bringing them in order only shows what type of spirit you are moving in; it is completely out of order.

It was Aaron who cast down the rod before Pharaoh, and it became a serpent. A lot of people to this day say it was Moses with the rod, because they do not read the Bible; Moses was telling Aaron what to do, and it was Aaron's rod that turned into the serpent. The magicians of Egypt did in like manner with their enchantments, and their rods became serpents; but Aaron's rod swallowed up their rods.

All the waters of Egypt were turned to blood, in the streams, the rivers, the ponds, the pools, and in vessels of wood and vessels of stone; the fish died and the river stank. With this first plague the Most High was mocking Sobek, the Egyptian idol god of the rivers, showing that he could not defend his own waters. The magicians did so with their enchantments, but they could only copy the plague; they could not turn the water back clear. Seven days were fulfilled after the Lord had smitten the river. Many Egyptologists claim this never happened, because to admit it happened is to admit that the idols they claim to be gods and goddesses were powerless before our God, and that those idols do not exist at all.

Aaron stretched out his hand over the waters, and the frogs came up and covered the land of Egypt. With this second plague the Most High was mocking Heqet, the Egyptian idol god of the frogs. The magicians did so with their enchantments and brought up frogs, but just as with the water they could only add to the plague; they could not take the frogs away. So Pharaoh called for Moses and Aaron and said, Entreat the Lord that he may take away the frogs. Why did Pharaoh not call on Heqet, the god of frogs? He had to go to the Lord.

All the dust of the land became lice in man and in beast throughout all the land of Egypt. Imagine that: the dust of the whole land of Egypt turned to lice. The magicians did so with their enchantments to bring forth lice, but this time they could not; and the magicians said unto Pharaoh, This is the finger of God. Yet Pharaoh's heart was hardened. With the third and fourth plagues, the lice and the swarms of flies, the Most High was mocking Beelzebub, the idol lord of flies and uncleanness.

These were no ordinary flies. They were biting and killing men and animals; the scripture records that the bitings of flies killed and no remedy was found. The Lord severed the land of Goshen, where His people dwelt, so that no swarms of flies were there, and put a division between His people and Pharaoh's people, to the end Pharaoh may know that the Lord is in the midst of the earth. Goshen was Israel's own quarter in Egypt, where we had our own houses and our own cattle; it was given to us in the days of Joseph, as we read in the book of Genesis.

Pharaoh said, Go sacrifice to your God in the land; but Moses answered, It is not meet, for we should sacrifice the abomination of the Egyptians before their eyes, and will they not stone us? Israel's sacrifices were the very animals Egypt held sacred, so Israel must go three days' journey into the wilderness. Moses warned Pharaoh, Let not Pharaoh deal deceitfully any more. The Lord removed the swarms so that there remained not one; and Pharaoh hardened his heart at this time also, and would not let the people go.

A grievous murrain fell upon the cattle of Egypt, upon the horses, asses, camels, oxen, and sheep; and with this fifth plague the Most High was mocking Hathor, the Egyptian idol goddess of cattle. The Lord severed between the cattle of Israel and the cattle of Egypt: all the cattle of Egypt died, but of the cattle of the children of Israel died not one. Pharaoh sent, and behold, there was not one of the cattle of the Israelites dead; and his heart was hardened. Picture what was taking place in the land: flies all over Egypt, but where Israel dwelt there were no flies; the water was blood, but where Israel dwelt the water was good; the cattle of Egypt died, but Israel's cattle lived. The plagues touched Pharaoh, his servants, and the Egyptians only; they did not touch the Israelites at all, because this was the Lord redeeming the Israelites. The Egyptians could not pray to their idols to help them, because the Lord was mocking them, showing them that Hathor does not exist, Sobek does not exist, Heqet does not exist, and Beelzebub does not exist.

Moses sprinkled ashes of the furnace toward heaven, and it became a boil breaking forth with blains upon man and upon beast throughout all the land of Egypt. The magicians could not stand before Moses because of the boils, for the boils were upon the magicians themselves and upon all the Egyptians. With this sixth plague the Most High was mocking Sekhmet, the Egyptian idol goddess of health and beauty.

Some mock and ask, What type of God says let my people go and then keeps hardening Pharaoh's heart so he will not let them go? That is exactly the God we serve, and the Lord tells you Himself why He did it: for this cause have I raised thee up, for to shew in thee my power, and that my name may be declared throughout all the earth. The same thing is happening now, right here in this captivity. The powers of Babylon know what is being taught, yet the Lord hardens their hearts so that they keep passing laws and pressing against His people, so that the Most High can show His power again, just as He did in Egypt.

Before the hail the Lord gave warning: gather thy cattle and all that thou hast in the field, for upon every man and beast found in the field the hail shall come down, and they shall die. He that feared the word of the Lord among the servants of Pharaoh made his servants and his cattle flee into the houses; they began to recognize the God of heaven and earth, the God of the Israelites. He that regarded not the word of the Lord left his servants and his cattle in the field. Many in Egypt held certain idols in more favor than others, and these trusted that Nut, the idol goddess of the sky, would keep them safe.

This was no regular hail. There was hail, and fire mingled with the hail, very grievous, such as there was none like it in all the land of Egypt since it became a nation; the fire ran along upon the ground. With this seventh plague the Most High was mocking Nut and Geb, the Egyptian idol gods of the sky and the earth, striking from the sky and burning along the ground they were supposed to rule. Only in the land of Goshen, where the children of Israel were, was there no hail. The Lord does not play; our God is a terrible God.

Pharaoh said, I have sinned this time: the Lord is righteous, and I and my people are wicked. This time? So all the other times, none of that was sin? Only now, under the thunder and hail, does he see it. Moses answered that the thunder and hail would cease, that thou mayest know how that the earth is the Lord's; but as for thee and thy servants, I know that ye will not yet fear the Lord God.
The flax and the barley were smitten, for the barley was in the ear and the flax was bolled; but the wheat and the rie were not smitten, for they were not grown up.

When Pharaoh saw that the rain and the hail and the thunders were ceased, he sinned yet more and hardened his heart, he and his servants. He still had the wheat and the rie in the ground, because they were not grown up yet, and that is part of why he went right back to hardening himself. --- Topics: [Idolatry](/encyclopedia/idolatry) · [Sacrifice and Atonement](/encyclopedia/sacrifice-and-atonement) · [The Covenant](/encyclopedia/the-covenant) · [The Feasts of the Most High](/encyclopedia/the-feasts-of-the-most-high) · [The Priesthood](/encyclopedia/the-priesthood)

The priests the Levites, and all the tribe of Levi, shall have no part nor inheritance with Israel; they shall eat the offerings of the Lord made by fire, and his inheritance. Therefore shall they have no inheritance among their brethren: the Lord is their inheritance, as he hath said unto them.

This shall be the priest's due from the people, from them that offer a sacrifice, whether ox or sheep: they shall give unto the priest the shoulder, and the two cheeks, and the maw. The firstfruit also of thy corn, of thy wine, and of thine oil, and the first of the fleece of thy sheep, shalt thou give him. For the Most High hath chosen him out of all thy tribes to stand to minister in the name of the Lord, him and his sons for ever.

If a Levite come from any of thy gates out of all Israel, and come with all the desire of his mind unto the place which the Lord shall choose, then he shall minister in the name of the Lord his God, as all his brethren the Levites do which stand there before the Lord. They shall have like portions to eat, beside that which cometh of the sale of his patrimony.

When thou art come into the land, thou shalt not learn to do after the abominations of those nations: there shall not be found among you any one that maketh his son or his daughter to pass through the fire, or that useth divination, or an observer of times, or an enchanter, or a witch, or a charmer, or a consulter with familiar spirits, or a wizard, or a necromancer. These things actually existed and they are all real: wizards, necromancers, divination, observers of times, people that consult with familiar spirits. If they were not real, they would not be in the Bible with the Most High telling us not to do them. All that do these things are an abomination unto the Lord, and because of these abominations the Most High driveth those nations out from before thee. Thou shalt be perfect with the Lord thy God, meaning upright; the nations hearken unto observers of times and unto diviners, but as for thee, the Most High hath not suffered thee so to do.

The Lord thy God will raise up unto thee a Prophet from the midst of thee, of thy brethren, like unto me; unto him ye shall hearken. This is talking about Christ, Yeshua. This answers what Israel desired of the Most High in Horeb in the day of the assembly, saying, Let me not hear again the voice of the Lord my God, neither let me see this great fire any more, that I die not; and the Lord said, They have well spoken that which they have spoken. I will put my words in his mouth, and he shall speak unto them all that I shall command him; and whosoever will not hearken unto my words which he shall speak in my name, I will require it of him. If we do not follow Christ and do what Christ says, that judgment falls on us.

The prophet which shall presume to speak a word in the name of the Most High which he hath not commanded him to speak, or that shall speak in the name of other gods, even that prophet shall die. By this law a lot of these pastors stand condemned: they say things and claim Christ said them, when the Most High never commanded Christ to say it and Christ is not telling them to say it. How shall we know the word which the Lord hath not spoken? When a prophet speaketh in the name of the Lord, if the thing follow not, nor come to pass, that is the thing which the Lord hath not spoken; the prophet hath spoken it presumptuously, and thou shalt not be afraid of him. --- Topics: [Clean and Unclean Meats](/encyclopedia/clean-and-unclean-meats) · [Esau and Edom](/encyclopedia/esau-and-edom) · [Idolatry](/encyclopedia/idolatry) · [Sacrifice and Atonement](/encyclopedia/sacrifice-and-atonement) · [The Covenant](/encyclopedia/the-covenant) · [The Feasts of the Most High](/encyclopedia/the-feasts-of-the-most-high) · [The Priesthood](/encyclopedia/the-priesthood) · [The Sabbath](/encyclopedia/the-sabbath)

If a man steal an ox or a sheep and kill it or sell it, he restores five oxen for an ox and four sheep for a sheep. We are in a different situation where we do not keep oxen and sheep, but the principle of restitution still applies among brothers and sisters in the body: if something is stolen, the law written here governs the payback. Do not be stealing.

If a thief be found breaking up means breaking in. He entered your home and you defended yourself and he died: that is what is called self-defense today, and no blood is shed for him, meaning there is no judgment. The judgment was already passed in the breaking in. If the sun be risen upon him, the thief got away, and there shall be blood shed for him means there shall be a judgment; then the verse gives the judgment. He makes full restitution, and if he have nothing he is sold for his theft: not sold into slavery, but into work servitude until he pays off the debt of what he stole. If the theft be found in his hand alive, he restores double. Verse three covers the thief who already got rid of what he stole; verse four covers the one still holding it.

These are self-explanatory: if a man lets his beast feed in another man's field or vineyard, he makes restitution of the best of his own field and vineyard; and he that kindles a fire that consumes another man's corn surely makes restitution.

If a man deliver money or stuff to his neighbor to keep and it be stolen, the thief found pays double. If the thief be not found, the master of the house is brought unto the judges, to see whether he put his hand unto his neighbor's goods, whether he was part of a scheme to deceive the owner out of his goods. For all manner of trespass, whether for ox, ass, sheep, raiment, or any lost thing, both parties come before the judges, and whom the judges condemn pays double unto his neighbor.

If a beast delivered to a neighbor to keep die or be hurt or driven away, no man seeing it, an oath of the Lord is between them both. In layman's terms he swears: I did not take the stuff, I did not set you up, I do not know where it is. The owner accepts the oath and the matter ends there; it is not to be spoken of again. Paul uses this civil law to show how the Most High is unchangeable. An oath for confirmation is the end of all strife; God confirmed his counsel by an oath, and by two immutable things, that it is impossible for God to lie and that he will not take back what went out of his mouth, we have strong consolation. The same way, once the oath of this law is applied, the matter is over.

If the thing kept be stolen from him, he makes restitution; if it be torn in pieces, he brings it for witness and does not make it good. If a man borrow ought of his neighbor, ought meaning anything, and it be hurt or die with the owner not present, he surely makes it good. You borrowed it, it got messed up, you owe the man. But if the owner be with it, or if it be an hired thing, it came for its hire. If you came to plow a man's field for ten shekels with your own donkey and your donkey breaks his leg, you cannot expect the owner to pay for your own faulty equipment; the same as a business loan today, the property owner is not liable when your own equipment breaks down.

If a man entice a maid that is not betrothed and lie with her, he shall surely endow her to be his wife; he has to sign the papers. He is at fault for not going through the proper channels of marriage, and she is at fault for being enticed and laying down. The proper channel was that the father married off the daughter. To marry thy daughter is to perform a weighty matter, for the father gives her over to that man for the rest of her life and is out of all watching over her; so she is to be given to a man of understanding, one keeping the commandments as a wise man. In our own land the daughter went from her father's house to a husband's house with the blessing of the father.

Thou shalt not suffer a witch to live: witchcraft goes into horoscopes, palm readings, and all things of that nature. Whosoever lieth with a beast, bestiality, shall surely be put to death. He that sacrificeth unto any god save unto the Lord only shall be utterly destroyed.

This is twofold, and first and foremost the stranger is your brother from a different area, our own people. [Leviticus 25](/bible/leviticus/25) shows it: if thy brother be waxen poor, though he be a stranger or a sojourner, sojourn meaning travel, thou shalt relieve him that he may live with thee. A brother of another tribe who falls on hard times and travels down to live with you is that stranger; neither vex him nor oppress him, for ye were strangers in the land of Egypt.

Ye shall not afflict any widow or fatherless child. A wife without a husband already has a hard life, and a son or daughter without a father the same; do not make their life harder than it already is. If thou afflict them in any wise and they cry unto the Most High, he will surely hear their cry, and his wrath shall wax hot: he will kill you with the sword, and your own wives shall be widows and your children fatherless. That is the Lord's plain warning against mistreating those less fortunate.

Usury means interest. You cannot charge your brother or sister interest: if you lend twenty dollars, you get twenty dollars back, nothing more, nothing less; no little bit more off the top. This is the same law read in [Leviticus 25:36-37](/bible/leviticus/25#v36).

If thou take thy neighbor's raiment to pledge, deliver it unto him by that the sun goeth down, for that is his covering only; wherein shall he sleep? The tunics and overcoats worn then were also sleeping garments to keep a man warm at night, especially the poor. A well-off man does not have to work for you; this speaks of the less fortunate who extend their services for money and give what is most valuable to them, their raiment, as the pledge. If he cries unto the Most High, he will hear, for he is gracious.

Thou shalt not revile the gods means do not hate or speak evil of your leaders. The word gods here is the leaders over you: the Most High says in the psalm, I have said, Ye are gods, and all of you are children of the Most High, speaking of us. [Acts 23](/bible/acts/23) is the example: when Paul spoke against the high priest, they that stood by said, Revilest thou God's high priest? And Paul answered, I wist not, brethren, that he was the high priest: for it is written, Thou shalt not speak evil of the ruler of thy people, quoting this very verse.

Thou shalt not delay to offer the first of thy ripe fruits and of thy liquors, and the firstborn of thy sons shalt thou give unto me. The firstborn sons that opened the matrix were consecrated unto the Lord, and the father redeemed them back from the priest with shekels. Likewise with the oxen and the sheep: seven days the firstling stayed with his dam, his mother, and on the eighth day it was given. The Lord did not want it too young, taken as soon as it popped out; it had to be its appointed time with the mother, then brought to the priest.

Ye shall be holy men unto me: neither shall ye eat any flesh that is torn of beasts in the field; ye shall cast it to the dogs. This is twofold, and the dogs are the strangers of other nations, the aliens and foreigners. Always get the context of the law, because sometimes the stranger is your brother and sometimes it is literally the other nations. [Deuteronomy 14:21](/bible/deuteronomy/14#v21) doubles this law: that which dieth of itself thou shalt give unto the stranger that is in thy gates, or sell it unto an alien, for thou art an holy people unto the Lord thy God. Cast the torn flesh to the other nations; ye shall not eat it, because ye are holy people.
