name: Bezaleel and Aholiab
charge: Making all that the Lord commanded, and no more; and teaching others to do it
summary: Two men were called by name and filled with the spirit of God in wisdom, understanding, knowledge and all manner of workmanship, to devise the work of the tabernacle in gold, silver, brass, stone and timber. They made every piece to the pattern shewed in the mount, and Moses looked upon all the work and blessed them. God also put in their hearts that they might teach.
offense: The obedience is exactness in craft, which the record treats as seriously as any other obedience in the volume. They worked to a pattern given on the mount and are commended for adding nothing to it: according to all that the Lord commanded Moses, so the children of Israel made all the work (Exodus 39:42). Bezaleel was of Judah and Aholiab of Dan, one of the least of the tribes, which the account sets side by side without comment (Exodus 31:2,6). The same chapter that lists their filling with the spirit lists it as being for cutting stones and carving timber (Exodus 31:5), so the first men in scripture said to be filled with the spirit of God were filled for manual work (Exodus 31:3).
judgment: Moses did look upon all the work, and behold, they had done it as the Lord had commanded (Exodus 39:43), even so had they done it: and Moses blessed them. The glory of the Lord filled the tent they had made (Exodus 40:34). They were also given the capacity to teach, so the skill was not held privately, and the tabernacle they built stood for four centuries and every case in Leviticus and Numbers takes place inside or around it.

verses.text: 1And the Lord spake unto Moses, saying, 2See, I have called by name Bezaleel the son of Uri, the son of Hur, of the tribe of Judah: 3And I have filled him with the spirit of God, in wisdom, and in understanding, and in knowledge, and in all manner of workmanship, 4To devise cunning works, to work in gold, and in silver, and in brass, 5And in cutting of stones, to set them, and in carving of timber, to work in all manner of workmanship. 6And I, behold, I have given with him Aholiab, the son of Ahisamach, of the tribe of Dan: and in the hearts of all that are wise hearted I have put wisdom, that they may make all that I have commanded thee;

30And Moses said unto the children of Israel, See, the Lord hath called by name Bezaleel the son of Uri, the son of Hur, of the tribe of Judah; 31And he hath filled him with the spirit of God, in wisdom, in understanding, and in knowledge, and in all manner of workmanship; 32And to devise curious works, to work in gold, and in silver, and in brass, 33And in the cutting of stones, to set them, and in carving of wood, to make any manner of cunning work. 34And he hath put in his heart that he may teach, both he, and Aholiab, the son of Ahisamach, of the tribe of Dan. 35Them hath he filled with wisdom of heart, to work all manner of work, of the engraver, and of the cunning workman, and of the embroiderer, in blue, and in purple, in scarlet, and in fine linen, and of the weaver, even of them that do any work, and of those that devise cunning work.

42According to all that the Lord commanded Moses, so the children of Israel made all the work. 43And Moses did look upon all the work, and, behold, they had done it as the Lord had commanded, even so had they done it: and Moses blessed them.

entries.commentary: The Lord called by name Bezaleel the son of Uri, the son of Hur, of the tribe of Judah, and filled him with the spirit of God, in wisdom, in understanding, in knowledge, and in all manner of workmanship, to devise cunning works, to work in gold, in silver, in brass, in cutting of stones, and in carving of timber. With him the Lord gave Aholiab the son of Ahisamach, of the tribe of Dan, and put wisdom in the hearts of all that were wise hearted, that they might make all that he had commanded. The Most High still works the same way. Brothers and sisters come into the congregation who are carpenters, plumbers, electricians, builders, painters, cooks, and tech savvy, and he sets every one in the body as it pleases him; no one appoints himself over the camp or the kitchen. All the diverse gifts together build the work today the way the tabernacle was built then.

The wise hearted made all that was commanded: the tabernacle of the congregation, the ark of the testimony, the mercy seat that is thereupon, all the furniture of the tabernacle, the table and his furniture, the pure candlestick with all his furniture, the altar of incense, the altar of burnt offering with all his furniture, and the laver and his foot. They made the cloths of service, the holy garments for Aaron the priest and the garments of his sons to minister in the priest's office, the anointing oil, and the sweet incense for the holy place, according to all that the Lord commanded. That spirit of workmanship on Israel is why the tabernacle, and later the house Solomon built for the Lord, outshined anything the world had seen; and though strangers shall build up our walls in the kingdom, it will be Israel directing how the Lord wants it done.

Verily my sabbaths ye shall keep, for it is a sign between me and you throughout your generations, that ye may know that I am the LORD that doth sanctify you. Keeping the weekly sabbath and the feast days shows that Israel are his children and he is their God; the nations do not have this sabbath, and adopted Sunday worship is not the true sabbath given to the children of Israel. Every one that defileth the sabbath shall surely be put to death. The stoning was done away in Christ, but the judgment for breaking the sabbath still stands, and people still die on the sabbath day, Friday sundown to Saturday sundown; the Most High is justified, because it is his sign between him and his people. Six days may work be done, but in the seventh is the sabbath of rest, holy to the LORD. It is more than a day of rest and congregating; it is the sign of who Israel's God is, which is why saying the sabbath is done away takes away the very sign between Israel and God.

The children of Israel shall keep the sabbath, to observe the sabbath throughout their generations, for a perpetual covenant; it is a sign between the Most High and the children of Israel for ever, for in six days the LORD made heaven and earth, and on the seventh day he rested, and was refreshed. Christians use [Mark 2:27](/bible/mark/2#v27) to say the sabbath is done away, but that is not what Christ said. The sabbath was made for man, the children of Israel; man was not put on the earth for the sabbath, the sabbath was put on the earth for man, and the Son of man is Lord of the sabbath because Christ instituted it. He rested for our sakes, that we should rest after the same similitude.

When he had made an end of communing with Moses upon mount Sinai, he gave him two tables of testimony, tables of stone, written with the finger of God. God literally wrote the testimony with his finger, and we know that was Christ.

Moses gathered all the congregation of the children of Israel: six days shall work be done, but on the seventh day there shall be to you an holy day, a sabbath of rest to the Lord; whosoever doeth work therein shall be put to death. Ye shall kindle no fire throughout your habitations upon the sabbath day: kindling fire goes to cooking. Bake that which ye will bake today, and seethe that ye will seethe, and lay up what remains to be kept unto the morning; you could not cook on the sabbath, so the day before is the prep day, and what you prepare that day is what you eat.

Whosoever is of a willing heart, let him bring the Lord's offering: gold, silver, and brass; blue, purple, scarlet, fine linen, and goats' hair; rams' skins dyed red and badgers' skins; shittim wood; oil for the light and spices for the anointing oil and the sweet incense; and onyx stones and stones to be set for the ephod and the breastplate. These are the offerings the people would bring unto the Lord.

Every wise hearted among you shall come and make all that the Lord hath commanded: those who had skill, the crafty ones. The list runs through the whole work: the tabernacle, his tent, his covering, his taches, boards, bars, pillars, and sockets; the ark of the covenant with the staves and the mercy seat, and the vail of the covering; the table with his staves and vessels and the shewbread; the candlestick, which is the menorah, with his lamps and the oil for the light; the incense altar; the altar of burnt offering, where the burnt offering was burnt, with his brasen grate; the laver; the hangings of the court; and the cloths of service, the holy garments for Aaron the priest and the garments of his sons, to minister in the priest's office.

The congregation departed from the presence of Moses, and they came, every one whose heart stirred him up and every one whom his spirit made willing, and brought the Lord's offering for the work of the tabernacle; the people brought the gold and silver and all the things listed willingly. Both men and women, as many as were willing hearted, brought bracelets, and earrings, and rings, and tablets, all jewels of gold; and every man with whom was found blue, purple, scarlet, fine linen, goats' hair, red skins of rams, badgers' skins, silver, brass, or shittim wood brought it. All the women that were wise hearted did spin with their hands; the women knew how to sew, and brought that which they had spun of blue, purple, scarlet, and fine linen, and the women whose heart stirred them up in wisdom spun goats' hair. The rulers brought onyx stones, stones for the ephod and breastplate, spice, and oil.

The Lord called by name Bezaleel the son of Uri, the son of Hur, of the tribe of Judah, and filled him with the spirit of God, in wisdom, in understanding, and in knowledge, and in all manner of workmanship; the Most High put His spirit on him to be gifted in what he did, to devise curious works in gold, silver, and brass, in cutting of stones, and in carving of wood. He hath put in his heart that he may teach, both he and Aholiab the son of Ahisamach, of the tribe of Dan; the two brothers the Most High was dealing with in workmanship trained and taught their fellow brethren how to do it. It is the same today: the Most High puts His spirit on brothers and sisters with different talents, and they put their talents to use and teach others in the congregation; Israel was putting their talents together and building, showing each other how to do these works.

Chapter 39 is the application of the instructions of chapter 28: the holy garments for Aaron the priest, the clothes of service to do service in the holy place, made of the blue, purple, and scarlet as the Lord commanded Moses.

The breastplate carried four rows of stones, and the stones were according to the names of the children of Israel, twelve according to their names, like the engravings of a signet, every one with his name according to the twelve tribes; the shoulders of the ephod carried onyx stones graven the same way, stones for a memorial to the children of Israel. The Most High had us representing: when the priest stepped on the scene you already knew what nationality he was. Nationality is very important to the Lord, and he took it very seriously.

The pomegranates and the bells of gold went upon the hem of the robe round about; the word keeps saying round about, because the fringes go all throughout the garment, round about, not gathered only at four corners. Old depictions show Israelites with the fringes all the way around, and it would not hurt to put them all throughout, out of the fear of God.

They made the plate of the holy crown of pure gold, written like the engravings of a signet, HOLINESS TO THE LORD, fastened on high upon the mitre with a lace of blue. Black man, this is your heritage: our forefathers the priests wore crowns of real pure gold. It is a blessing to come back to this knowledge; they will not teach you this anywhere else.

Thus was all the work of the tabernacle finished, and the children of Israel did according to all that the Lord commanded Moses; they brought every piece to Moses, and he looked upon all the work, and behold, they had done it as the Lord had commanded, and Moses blessed them. It is like getting a building today and doing all the painting, sanding, nailing, and screwing, and then standing back and seeing the finished product: all praises to the Most High, we did it; then the people are blessed.

name: Aaron and Israel at the golden calf
charge: Idolatry within weeks of the covenant
summary: While Moses was on the mountain receiving the law that forbade it, the people made a golden calf and worshipped it. The covenant was broken almost before the ink was dry.
offense: Not forty days had passed since they heard the voice from the mount. When the people saw that Moses delayed to come down, they gathered themselves together unto Aaron and said, up, make us gods, which shall go before us; for as for this Moses, we wot not what is become of him (Exodus 32:1). Any time deliverance did not come when Israel wanted it, the nation turned, and it turned toward what it had carried out of Egypt: the spirit that was in Israel in Egypt was still in Israel when they left, and it corrupted them the moment the man was out of sight. Aaron's part is the heavier for who he was. He had seen every plague and stood before Pharaoh and been set apart to the priesthood, and he received the gold and fashioned it with a graving tool, after he had made it a molten calf, and they said, these be thy gods, O Israel, which brought thee up out of the land of Egypt (Exodus 32:4). Then he built an altar before it and proclaimed, to morrow is a feast to the Lord (Exodus 32:5), which is the offence named in the second commandment performed under the name of the first. They rose up early, offered burnt offerings and peace offerings, sat down to eat and to drink, and rose up to play (Exodus 32:6), and the Lord's own verdict was given before Moses had seen any of it: they have turned aside quickly out of the way which I commanded them (Exodus 32:8), and, I have seen this people, and, behold, it is a stiffnecked people (Exodus 32:9).
judgment: Moses ground the calf to powder and made them drink it. The Levites, called to the Lord's side, put about three thousand to the sword, and the Lord sent a plague on the people. Aaron was spared but not excused.

entries.commentary: When the people saw that Moses delayed to come down out of the mount, they gathered unto Aaron: Up, make us gods, which shall go before us; for as for this Moses, we wot not what is become of him. Any time deliverance did not come when Israel wanted it, the nation rebelled, and Moses and the leadership got the blame; the same spirit is against the leadership of Israel to this day. Aaron said break off the golden earrings which are in the ears of your wives, of your sons, and of your daughters. Men and women both wore earrings in the scriptures, and it is not sin. Aaron received the gold, fashioned it with a graving tool, and made a molten calf, and they said, These be thy gods, O Israel, which brought thee up out of the land of Egypt. Aaron saw the miracles in Egypt and was set up as high priest, yet he succumbed to the pressure of the people; that is why the Lord chose Moses specifically to lead, because Moses could not be moved by any means. Aaron built an altar before it and made proclamation, To morrow is a feast to the LORD; and the people rose up early, offered burnt offerings and peace offerings, sat down to eat and to drink, and rose up to play. Israel kept provoking God, and the Lord still brought the nation into the promised land as he promised Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.

The Lord told Moses, Go, get thee down; for thy people, which thou broughtest out of the land of Egypt, have corrupted themselves. They turned aside quickly out of the way, made a molten calf, worshipped it, and sacrificed thereunto. Not forty days gone, and they had already left his commandments. The spirit that was in Israel in Egypt was still in Israel when they left. It is the same coming into this truth: the evil carried in from the world will corrupt you and turn you from the Lord if it is not put off. I have seen this people, and, behold, it is a stiffnecked people. That has been Israel's reputation with the Father from the beginning; without the laws of God we are a carnal, rebellious people, which is why these last days call for humbleness and repentance, not bringing the world's rhetoric into the congregation. Now therefore let me alone, that my wrath may wax hot against them, and that I may consume them: and I will make of thee a great nation. Moses was of the tribe of Levi, of the seed of Jacob, so the Lord could have started over with him.

Moses besought the LORD his God: LORD, why doth thy wrath wax hot against thy people, which thou hast brought forth out of the land of Egypt with great power, and with a mighty hand? Moses had compassion and stood in the middle, interceding and mediating between the people and God. Wherefore should the Egyptians speak, and say, For mischief did he bring them out, to slay them in the mountains? And remember Abraham, Isaac, and Israel, to whom thou swarest by thine own self to multiply their seed as the stars of heaven, and to give the land to their seed for ever. And the LORD repented of the evil which he thought to do unto his people. The Most High does not repent as a man; he has no one to answer to, he simply turned from the anger of that moment. He was never going to break his covenant, for consuming the people would have destroyed all the seed of Jacob except Moses; Moses was there to remind him of his own word. From the questions: the Lord dealt with Moses on a level where Moses could speak to him so, but the outcome stood on what was declared from the beginning; had it been his pleasure to destroy, nothing Moses said could have stayed it.

Moses went down from the mount with the two tables of the testimony in his hand, written on both their sides; the tables were the work of God, and the writing was the writing of God, graven upon the tables. Joshua heard the noise of the people and said, There is a noise of war in the camp; Moses answered, It is not the voice of them that shout for mastery, neither the voice of them that cry for being overcome, but the noise of them that sing do I hear. They were feasting and dancing around the idol. Joshua's loyalty at the mount is one of the main reasons the Lord chose him to succeed Moses. As soon as he came nigh unto the camp and saw the calf and the dancing, Moses' anger waxed hot, and he cast the tables out of his hands and brake them beneath the mount. He took the calf which they had made, burnt it in the fire, ground it to powder, strawed it upon the water, and made the children of Israel drink of it. Our forefathers were no joke about the law; Nehemiah likewise put hands on those who profaned the sabbath in his day.

Moses said unto Aaron, What did this people unto thee, that thou hast brought so great a sin upon them? He had left Aaron in charge, and came back to a camp deep in wickedness. Aaron answered, Let not the anger of my lord wax hot: thou knowest the people, that they are set on mischief; they said make us gods, I cast the gold into the fire, and there came out this calf. A leader cannot blame the congregation, the same excuse Saul gave; the charge has to be carried. The psalm gives the depth of it: they soon forgat his works and waited not for his counsel, they made a calf in Horeb and changed their glory into the similitude of an ox that eateth grass, and they forgat God their saviour, which had done great things in Egypt, wondrous works in the land of Ham, and terrible things by the Red sea.

The people were naked, for Aaron had made them naked unto their shame among their enemies. That is the same nakedness of [Genesis 3](/bible/genesis/3), the shame of sin uncovered. Moses stood in the gate of the camp and said, Who is on the LORD's side? let him come unto me. And all the sons of Levi gathered themselves together unto him. Every man put his sword by his side and went in and out from gate to gate throughout the camp, and there fell of the people that day about three thousand men. The Lord chose those particular ones to die; that spirit would have wrecked the nation down the road, so he moved it out of the congregation. Do not be broken when someone leaves the truth; the Lord moves spiritually. Consecrate yourselves to day to the LORD, even every man upon his son, and upon his brother, that he may bestow upon you a blessing this day.

Moses said unto the people, Ye have sinned a great sin. They had broken the first two commandments just given at Sinai: no other gods before him, and no graven image to bow down to and serve. Moses returned unto the LORD to mediate: yet now, if thou wilt forgive their sin; and if not, blot me, I pray thee, out of thy book which thou hast written. That is a real leader, putting himself in the way of harm for his people. The Lord answered, Whosoever hath sinned against me, him will I blot out of my book; therefore now go, lead the people, and mine Angel shall go before thee; nevertheless in the day when I visit I will visit their sin upon them. And the LORD plagued the people, because they made the calf, which Aaron made.

Hear, O Israel: thou art to pass over Jordan this day, to possess nations greater and mightier than thyself, a people great and tall, the children of the Anakims, of whom it was said, who can stand before the children of Anak. The Anakims are Hamites, scattered now in the land of Ham; do not ask which nation they are today, for the Most High has not told us. The Lord thy God goeth over before thee as a consuming fire; he shall destroy them and bring them down before thy face, so shalt thou drive them out and destroy them quickly.

Speak not thou in thine heart, saying, for my righteousness the Lord hath brought me in to possess this land: here is more of the Christianity spirit corrected. Israel entered for the wickedness of those nations and to perform the word sworn unto Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, not for their own uprightness. Understand that the only reason any of us have a roof over our head and food in our stomach right now is the mercy and righteousness of the Most High, for thou art a stiffnecked people; it is because of him that we survive every single day.

Remember, and forget not, how thou provokedst the Lord thy God to wrath in the wilderness: from the day of leaving Egypt unto this place, ye have been rebellious against the Lord. Moses abode in the mount forty days and forty nights, neither eating bread nor drinking water, when he went up to receive the tables of the covenant. What was he doing those forty days? He was receiving the understanding of the beginning of times, the midst of times, and the end of times; that is why some things Moses wrote, like [Genesis 49](/bible/genesis/49) and [Deuteronomy 32](/bible/deuteronomy/32) and 33, are hard to understand, hidden in plain view, while keep the commandments is written easy.

The Lord delivered unto me two tables of stone written with the finger of God: God took his time and wrote the ten commandments down himself, according to all the words which the Lord spake with you in the mount out of the midst of the fire.

Arise, get thee down quickly; thy people have corrupted themselves and made them a molten image. That molten image was the calf, the Egyptian goddess Hathor; you can look that up yourself. Let me alone, that I may destroy them, and blot out their name from under heaven, and I will make of thee a nation mightier and greater than they. The Most High was ready to go back to the days of the flood and start over with one man; time means nothing to the Ancient of days. Religion has tried to remove the fierceness, the wrath, and the severity of the Most High and push an effeminate white Jesus in front of us that loves everybody, forgives everything at the last breath with no commandments kept, and can do no wrong. We are suffering in all our cities, in Africa, in Europe, and in the Caribbean from that lack of fear of God before our eyes.

Moses came down from the mount, the mount burning with fire, the two tables of the covenant in his two hands, and behold, ye had sinned against the Lord your God and made you a molten calf. Ye had turned aside quickly out of the way which the Lord had commanded you: the Most High had been proving them through hard times, and they quickly turned back, just as many today go right back to their old ways the moment they are left alone. Brothers and sisters, check yourselves; we must endure to the end and rehearse the righteous acts now. Moses took the two tables, cast them out of his two hands, and brake them before your eyes.

Moses fell down before the Lord, as at the first, forty days and forty nights, neither eating bread nor drinking water, because of all your sins; that is two forty-day fasts, for he was afraid of the anger and hot displeasure wherewith the Lord was wroth against the people. The Lord was very angry with Aaron to have destroyed him, and Moses prayed for Aaron also at the same time. Moses prayed, and the Lord hearkened unto him; there arose no prophet like Moses, a mighty great man in the scriptures. He took your sin, the calf which ye had made, burnt it with fire, stamped it, ground it very small until it was as small as dust, and cast the dust into the brook that descended out of the mount.

At Taberah, at Massah, and at Kibrothhattaavah ye provoked the Lord to wrath, and at Kadeshbarnea ye rebelled against the commandment of the Lord and believed him not. Ye have been rebellious against the Lord from the day that I knew you: Moses called Israel out plainly, and it is real talk still.

Moses fell down before the Lord forty days and forty nights because the Lord had said he would destroy the people, and prayed: O Lord God, destroy not thy people and thine inheritance, which thou hast redeemed through thy greatness. Remember thy servants, Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob; look not unto the stubbornness of this people, nor to their wickedness, lest the land whence thou broughtest us out say the Lord was not able to bring them in, and because he hated them he brought them out to slay them. Esdras prayed the same prayer as Moses for the children of Israel, so precept these two prayers together: pay no attention to the fakers, for they remove themselves, but be merciful to us who have no works of righteousness, for by that mercy thou shalt be called merciful. When we are in the midst of sin we live worse than beasts, for a beast runs on instinct, but we consciously choose to go against the laws of the Most High.

Give thanks unto the Most High, for He is good and His mercy endures forever; who can show forth all His praise. Blessed are they that keep judgment and do righteousness at all times. At all times, not only when convenient. David asks to be remembered with the favor toward His people, to see the good of His chosen and rejoice in the gladness of His nation.

We have sinned with our fathers and done wickedly; our fathers understood not His wonders in Egypt and provoked Him at the Red Sea. Nevertheless He saved them for His name's sake, rebuked the Red Sea so it dried up, and led them through the depths as through the wilderness. Esau's science says a wind blew it into a tsunami, but the Most High said He rebuked it. The waters covered their enemies, and then they believed His words and sang His praise.

They soon forgot His works and waited not for His counsel, but lusted exceedingly in the wilderness and tempted God, so He sent leanness into their soul. They envied Moses and Aaron the saint of the Lord; the earth swallowed Dathan and the company of Abiram for their insurrection. They made a calf and worshipped the molten image, changing their glory into the likeness of an ox that eats grass, forgetting God their savior. He would have destroyed them had not Moses stood in the breach. -

They despised the pleasant land and believed not His word but brought up a false report and murmured in their tents; therefore He lifted His hand to overthrow them and scatter their seed among the nations. They joined themselves to Baal-peor and ate the sacrifices of the dead, provoking Him to anger, and the plague broke in upon them. Then Phinehas stood up and executed judgment, and the plague was stayed; it was counted to him for righteousness unto all generations, for he had zeal in the fear of the Most High. -

They angered Him at the waters of strife, so it went ill with Moses, who spoke unadvisedly with his lips. Moses lost the promised land because he smote the rock and called the people rebels instead of speaking to it and sanctifying the Most High. They did not destroy the nations as commanded but were mingled among the heathen and learned their works. They served idols, sacrificed their sons and daughters to devils, and shed innocent blood, polluting the land and going a-whoring with their own inventions. -

The wrath of the Most High was kindled against His people so that He abhorred His own inheritance and gave them into the hand of the heathen, who ruled over them. The heathen ruling in our communities today, the legal system and the government, is the law and the prophets agreeing; He delivered them many times, but they provoked Him and were brought low for their iniquity. Nevertheless He regarded their affliction, remembered His covenant, and repented according to His mercies; David prays: save us and gather us from among the heathen. Blessed be the Lord God of Israel from everlasting to everlasting. -

This is Stephen at the council, addressing the audience just before he is put to death. He answers the high priest by going all the way back to the beginning: the God of glory appeared unto our father Abraham when he was in Mesopotamia, before he dwelt in Charran. Abraham came out of the land of the Chaldeans, dwelt in Charran, and after his father died the Most High removed him into this land wherein they now dwell, and gave him no inheritance in it, not so much as to set his foot on, yet promised to give it to him and his seed after him when as yet he had no child. Notice how Stephen recites this history off the top of his head. Our forefathers read more than their four chapters a day. When you read, you put these things to memory, so you can recite it. A lot of us cannot recite our own history, but we can recite LeBron James and the NBA stats, football stats. These men were studious; they constantly gave attendance to studying. They called Paul mad for reading so many letters. Our forefathers were addicted to this gospel.

The Most High spoke that Abraham's seed should sojourn in a strange land and be brought into bondage and treated evil four hundred years, and the nation to whom they were in bondage he would judge, and after that they would come forth and serve him in this place. Then he gave Abraham the covenant of circumcision, and so Abraham begat Isaac and circumcised him the eighth day, and Isaac begat Jacob, and Jacob begat the twelve patriarchs.

The patriarchs, moved with envy, sold Joseph into Egypt, but the Most High was with him and delivered him out of all his afflictions and gave him favor and wisdom in the sight of Pharaoh, who made him governor over Egypt and all his house. When the famine came over Egypt and Canaan, Jacob heard there was corn in Egypt and sent out our fathers first; the second time Joseph was made known to his brethren, and Joseph's kindred was made known to Pharaoh. Jacob went down into Egypt with threescore and fifteen souls, and he and our fathers died and were carried over into Sychem and laid in the sepulchre Abraham bought for a sum of money.

As the time of the promise drew near which the Most High had sworn to Abraham, the people grew and multiplied in Egypt, until another king arose who knew not Joseph. The same dealt subtly with our kindred and evil-treated our fathers, so that they cast out their young children to the end they might not live.

In that time Moses was born, exceeding fair, nourished up in his father's house three months, and when he was cast out, Pharaoh's daughter took him up and nourished him for her own son. Moses was learned in all the wisdom of the Egyptians and was mighty in words and in deeds. That corrects the doctrine that certain Christian pastors preach, that Moses stuttered and could not speak. You cannot be a stupid man and be a prince over Egypt. He was raised under Pharaoh, so he had to learn everything of Egypt, their gods, their laws, the language. He was not a stupid man, and he did not stutter.

When Moses was full forty years old, it came into his heart to visit his brethren the children of Israel. Contrary to the movie The Ten Commandments, Moses always knew who he was; his own mother raised and nursed him, so he knew his brothers, he was only raised under the household of the Egyptians. Seeing one of them suffer wrong, he defended him and smote the Egyptian, supposing his brethren would understand that the Most High by his hand would deliver them, but they understood not. The next day, striving to make peace, he was thrust away with, Who made thee a ruler and a judge over us? Only the Most High could set a man to judge. This is the crabs in a barrel spirit: even after you help somebody, they say, Who are you to be over us? Everybody wants to be the head, the chief, a leader, but nobody wants to be a follower, and nobody wants to give credit when credit is due. The Most High was using the status Moses had in Egypt to help his brother, and they used it against him: Wilt thou kill me as thou didst the Egyptian yesterday? Certain of us will be put in different positions in this society, in politics, in education, and the Most High will use those accolades to your advantage, the same way he used Moses to go to Pharaoh and not be put to death right off the bat. Then Moses fled and was a stranger in the land of Midian, understanding that if he stayed among his own people they would get him killed, and there he begat two sons. People use the excuse that Moses married an Ethiopian to justify interracial marriage, saying maybe the Lord would forgive them the same way. But the Most High says, I will have mercy on whom I will have mercy. You are not Moses. Ask Aaron and Miriam, whom the Most High plagued in the skin and put out of the camp seven days for speaking against a matter that did not concern them. Do not point fingers and compare yourself to the person next to you, wondering why one brother is judged for a matter and another is treated differently. Different judgments belong to the Most High. You are not David; do not weigh Saul's sins against David's and assume you know how the Most High will judge, the way men questioned why Uzza was struck for touching the ark. Work out your own soul salvation with fear and trembling, study to be quiet, and mind your own business.

Forty years later, Moses now eighty years old, an angel of the Lord appeared to him in a flame of fire in a bush at Mount Sinai. Brothers and sisters say they are too old to repent; you are never too old. The Most High used Moses at eighty to deliver the whole nation, and retained his strength. The voice of the Lord said, I am the God of thy fathers, the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. Moses trembled and durst not behold. He was told to put off his shoes, for the place was holy ground, and the Most High said, I have seen the affliction of my people in Egypt, I have heard their groaning, and I am come down to deliver them; now come, I will send thee into Egypt.

This Moses, whom they refused saying, Who made thee a ruler and a judge, the same did the Most High send to be a ruler and a deliverer by the hand of the angel that appeared in the bush. Be careful with one another; the same person you reject is the same person the Most High raises up over you. This is the spirit of preeminence, not wanting another brother to rule over you because you believe you should be in that position. The Most High sees the heart and knows the spirits he is setting up. Moses was the meekest, most humble man. For a prince to go down to people counted as slaves and servants, defend them, and risk himself for a stiffnecked and rebellious people, shows he loved his people even in his position of authority. This is that Moses who said, A prophet shall the Lord your God raise up unto you of your brethren like unto me; him shall ye hear. Stephen rehearsed all the history to bring them up to Christ, because the whole ministry throughout Acts is Christ's name preached in the place of animal sacrifice. Even as Pharisees, they knew this prophecy, so he made it plain: the prophet Moses spoke about is that Christ.

This is he that was in the church in the wilderness with the angel that spoke to him in Mount Sinai, and with our fathers, who received the lively oracles to give unto us. The one in the church in the wilderness is that Christ, the prophet of verse 37. Our fathers would not obey him but thrust him from them, and in their hearts turned back to Egypt, telling Aaron, Make us gods to go before us, for as for this Moses we know not what is become of him. They did not obey Christ in the wilderness, just as they did not obey Christ in his day. They made a calf, offered sacrifice to the idol, and rejoiced in the works of their own hands, so the Most High gave them up to worship the host of heaven; they took up the tabernacle of Moloch and the star of the god Remphan, figures they made to worship, and he carried them away beyond Babylon.

Our fathers had the tabernacle of witness in the wilderness, made according to the fashion Moses had seen, which our fathers brought in with Jesus into the possession of the Gentiles, whom the Most High drove out before their face. That Jesus is Joshua, and the Most High drove out the nations before the fathers. This continued unto the days of David, who found favor before the Most High and desired to find a tabernacle for the God of Jacob, but Solomon built him a house. Howbeit the Most High dwelleth not in temples made with hands: Heaven is my throne, and earth is my footstool; what house will ye build me, saith the Lord, or what is the place of my rest? Hath not my hand made all these things?

Stephen turns it on them: Ye stiffnecked and uncircumcised in heart and ears, ye do always resist the Holy Ghost; as your fathers did, so do ye. The Holy Ghost the fathers resisted in the wilderness is the same Holy Ghost resisted in Christ's day, and that Holy Ghost is first and foremost the laws. There are three forms of the Holy Ghost taught in this series: first the laws, when you keep the laws of the Most High; then wisdom and understanding, which comes after you keep the laws; and then power, as the apostles received power to speak in tongues and perform miracles. Which of the prophets did their fathers not persecute? They slew them that showed before of the coming of the Just One, of whom they had now been the betrayers and murderers, who received the law by the disposition of angels and kept it not.

When they heard these things they were cut to the heart and gnashed on him with their teeth. But Stephen, being full of the Holy Ghost, looked up steadfastly into heaven and saw the glory of the Most High and Jesus standing on the right hand of God, and said, Behold, I see the heavens opened and the Son of man standing on the right hand of God. They cried out with a loud voice, stopped their ears, ran upon him with one accord, cast him out of the city, and stoned him; the witnesses laid down their clothes at the feet of a young man named Saul. Stephen, calling on the Most High, said, Lord Jesus, receive my spirit, and kneeling down he cried, Lord, lay not this sin to their charge, and fell asleep. This is the same spirit Christ had when he said, Father, forgive them, for they know not what they do.

name: The sons of Levi at the golden calf
charge: Answering, Who is on the Lord's side? and executing the sentence on their own brethren
summary: When Moses stood in the gate of the camp and asked who was on the Lord's side, all the sons of Levi gathered to him, took their swords, and went through the camp. Three thousand fell. For that day the priesthood and the service of the sanctuary were given to the tribe, and Moses' last blessing names it.
offense: Moses stood in the gate of the camp with the calf ground to powder (Exodus 32:20) and put a question rather than an order: who is on the Lord's side? The whole tribe came to him (Exodus 32:26). What they were then commanded was the hardest thing in the law, to execute the sentence on apostates without regard to kinship, slay every man his brother, and every man his companion, and every man his neighbour (Exodus 32:27). Deuteronomy 13 states the statute they were applying, that a brother or a son or the wife of thy bosom who entices to other gods is not to be spared or concealed (Deuteronomy 33:8-11). Three thousand fell, and the account is careful that the sword did not fall on strangers.
judgment: Moses read the day as a consecration: consecrate yourselves today to the Lord, even every man upon his son and upon his brother (Exodus 32:29), that he may bestow upon you a blessing this day. The priesthood and the whole service of the sanctuary were given to the tribe (Numbers 3:31), and the Levites were taken instead of the firstborn of Israel (Numbers 3:12). Moses' final blessing on Levi names the cause exactly (Numbers 3:17), that they observed God's word and kept his covenant (Deuteronomy 33:9), and did not acknowledge their own brethren nor know their own children. Malachi holds the covenant with Levi up centuries later as what a priesthood is supposed to be (Malachi 2:4-7).

entries.commentary: When the people saw that Moses delayed to come down out of the mount, they gathered unto Aaron: Up, make us gods, which shall go before us; for as for this Moses, we wot not what is become of him. Any time deliverance did not come when Israel wanted it, the nation rebelled, and Moses and the leadership got the blame; the same spirit is against the leadership of Israel to this day. Aaron said break off the golden earrings which are in the ears of your wives, of your sons, and of your daughters. Men and women both wore earrings in the scriptures, and it is not sin. Aaron received the gold, fashioned it with a graving tool, and made a molten calf, and they said, These be thy gods, O Israel, which brought thee up out of the land of Egypt. Aaron saw the miracles in Egypt and was set up as high priest, yet he succumbed to the pressure of the people; that is why the Lord chose Moses specifically to lead, because Moses could not be moved by any means. Aaron built an altar before it and made proclamation, To morrow is a feast to the LORD; and the people rose up early, offered burnt offerings and peace offerings, sat down to eat and to drink, and rose up to play. Israel kept provoking God, and the Lord still brought the nation into the promised land as he promised Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.

The Lord told Moses, Go, get thee down; for thy people, which thou broughtest out of the land of Egypt, have corrupted themselves. They turned aside quickly out of the way, made a molten calf, worshipped it, and sacrificed thereunto. Not forty days gone, and they had already left his commandments. The spirit that was in Israel in Egypt was still in Israel when they left. It is the same coming into this truth: the evil carried in from the world will corrupt you and turn you from the Lord if it is not put off. I have seen this people, and, behold, it is a stiffnecked people. That has been Israel's reputation with the Father from the beginning; without the laws of God we are a carnal, rebellious people, which is why these last days call for humbleness and repentance, not bringing the world's rhetoric into the congregation. Now therefore let me alone, that my wrath may wax hot against them, and that I may consume them: and I will make of thee a great nation. Moses was of the tribe of Levi, of the seed of Jacob, so the Lord could have started over with him.

Moses besought the LORD his God: LORD, why doth thy wrath wax hot against thy people, which thou hast brought forth out of the land of Egypt with great power, and with a mighty hand? Moses had compassion and stood in the middle, interceding and mediating between the people and God. Wherefore should the Egyptians speak, and say, For mischief did he bring them out, to slay them in the mountains? And remember Abraham, Isaac, and Israel, to whom thou swarest by thine own self to multiply their seed as the stars of heaven, and to give the land to their seed for ever. And the LORD repented of the evil which he thought to do unto his people. The Most High does not repent as a man; he has no one to answer to, he simply turned from the anger of that moment. He was never going to break his covenant, for consuming the people would have destroyed all the seed of Jacob except Moses; Moses was there to remind him of his own word. From the questions: the Lord dealt with Moses on a level where Moses could speak to him so, but the outcome stood on what was declared from the beginning; had it been his pleasure to destroy, nothing Moses said could have stayed it.

Moses went down from the mount with the two tables of the testimony in his hand, written on both their sides; the tables were the work of God, and the writing was the writing of God, graven upon the tables. Joshua heard the noise of the people and said, There is a noise of war in the camp; Moses answered, It is not the voice of them that shout for mastery, neither the voice of them that cry for being overcome, but the noise of them that sing do I hear. They were feasting and dancing around the idol. Joshua's loyalty at the mount is one of the main reasons the Lord chose him to succeed Moses. As soon as he came nigh unto the camp and saw the calf and the dancing, Moses' anger waxed hot, and he cast the tables out of his hands and brake them beneath the mount. He took the calf which they had made, burnt it in the fire, ground it to powder, strawed it upon the water, and made the children of Israel drink of it. Our forefathers were no joke about the law; Nehemiah likewise put hands on those who profaned the sabbath in his day.

Moses said unto Aaron, What did this people unto thee, that thou hast brought so great a sin upon them? He had left Aaron in charge, and came back to a camp deep in wickedness. Aaron answered, Let not the anger of my lord wax hot: thou knowest the people, that they are set on mischief; they said make us gods, I cast the gold into the fire, and there came out this calf. A leader cannot blame the congregation, the same excuse Saul gave; the charge has to be carried. The psalm gives the depth of it: they soon forgat his works and waited not for his counsel, they made a calf in Horeb and changed their glory into the similitude of an ox that eateth grass, and they forgat God their saviour, which had done great things in Egypt, wondrous works in the land of Ham, and terrible things by the Red sea.

The people were naked, for Aaron had made them naked unto their shame among their enemies. That is the same nakedness of [Genesis 3](/bible/genesis/3), the shame of sin uncovered. Moses stood in the gate of the camp and said, Who is on the LORD's side? let him come unto me. And all the sons of Levi gathered themselves together unto him. Every man put his sword by his side and went in and out from gate to gate throughout the camp, and there fell of the people that day about three thousand men. The Lord chose those particular ones to die; that spirit would have wrecked the nation down the road, so he moved it out of the congregation. Do not be broken when someone leaves the truth; the Lord moves spiritually. Consecrate yourselves to day to the LORD, even every man upon his son, and upon his brother, that he may bestow upon you a blessing this day.

Moses said unto the people, Ye have sinned a great sin. They had broken the first two commandments just given at Sinai: no other gods before him, and no graven image to bow down to and serve. Moses returned unto the LORD to mediate: yet now, if thou wilt forgive their sin; and if not, blot me, I pray thee, out of thy book which thou hast written. That is a real leader, putting himself in the way of harm for his people. The Lord answered, Whosoever hath sinned against me, him will I blot out of my book; therefore now go, lead the people, and mine Angel shall go before thee; nevertheless in the day when I visit I will visit their sin upon them. And the LORD plagued the people, because they made the calf, which Aaron made.

This is the blessing wherewith Moses the man of God blessed the children of Israel before his death. This chapter is prophetic concerning who the tribes would be in the last days: the blessings point to where you can examine history and identify each tribe. The Lord came from Sinai and shined forth from mount Paran, and came with ten thousands of saints; from his right hand went a fiery law for them. Moses commanded us a law, even the inheritance of the congregation of Jacob: the laws of the Most High are our inheritance. And he was king in Jeshurun, when the heads of the people and the tribes of Israel were gathered together.

Let Reuben live, and not die; and let not his men be few. Reuben is the Seminole Indians: under Andrew Jackson the Indian removal campaign set out to exterminate them, and many were slaughtered, but they were not able to kill them all. They tried it, but they were not fully successful; that is why the blessing says let Reuben live, and not die.

Hear, Lord, the voice of Judah, and bring him unto his people: let his hands be sufficient for him; and be thou an help to him from his enemies. The Most High said we would be scattered into the four corners and the nations would conspire that we not remember who we are; but he wakes Judah first. Judah, the so-called blacks in America, are the first to remember that they are the Israelites, and once Judah learns who they are, they go and teach the other tribes scattered throughout the four corners; that is bring him unto his people. That is why Judah is at the forefront of this work. The gates of hell will try to prevail against the quest to wake up the twelve tribes, but the Most High is a help to Judah from his enemies to fulfill that mission.

And of Levi he said, Let thy Thummim and thy Urim be with thy holy one. The Urim and the Thummim were worn in the garment of the high priest, as [Exodus 28](/bible/exodus/28) lays out; that pertains to the Levites, the lineage of Aaron, whom thou didst prove at Massah, and with whom thou didst strive at the waters of Meribah, in [Exodus 17](/bible/exodus/17). Who said unto his father and to his mother, I have not seen him; neither did he acknowledge his brethren, nor knew his own children: for they have observed thy word, and kept thy covenant. This is the zeal Levi had for the Most High. At the golden calf, when Moses stood in the gate of the camp and said, Who is on the Lord's side? let him come unto me, only the sons of Levi gathered themselves unto him. They took every man his sword and did according to the word of Moses without hesitating, and there fell of the people that day about three thousand men. That is why the blessing says they saw not father or mother nor acknowledged their brethren: that is the devotion they had for the covenant.

They shall teach Jacob thy judgments, and Israel thy law: they shall put incense before thee, and whole burnt sacrifice upon thine altar. This is the office the Most High gave Levi, and in particular the high priest. Aaron was chosen out of all men living to offer sacrifices, incense, and a sweet savour, to make reconciliation for the people, and that office pertained to his lineage: to teach Jacob the testimonies and inform Israel in his laws. That is why Levi had no land of their own but dwelt among all the tribes of Israel: they were responsible for making the sacrifices and teaching the laws to the people.

Bless, Lord, his substance, and accept the work of his hands. His substance goes into the tithes that Levi would receive, and the work of his hands goes into the freewill offerings brought forth to the Lord. Smite through the loins of them that rise against him, and of them that hate him, that they rise not again. In history you see it in the Haitian revolution under Toussaint Louverture: they smote through the loins of them that hated them. Levi was about that action to a magnitude the other tribes never matched. That they rise not again is ultimately fulfilled when Christ returns.

And of Benjamin he said, The beloved of the Lord shall dwell in safety by him. Dwelling in safety means Benjamin would not be killed off in slavery. The Lord shall cover him all the day long, and he shall dwell between his shoulders: between the shoulders of the Lord represents the skies and the earth, going into the good climate and the good land they would have.

And of Joseph he said, Blessed of the Lord be his land. Joseph is Ephraim and Manasseh: Joseph was one of the twelve sons of Jacob, but Jacob put his name on Joseph's two sons, so his grandsons make up two tribes of Israel; when we read of Joseph we are reading of Ephraim and Manasseh. The precious things of heaven refer to the good weather on their land, and the dew and the deep that coucheth beneath go into the seas whose benefits they reap. The precious fruits brought forth by the sun are the crops their land grows: mango, papaya, avocado, pineapple, coconut, banana, sugar cane, fruits you cannot grow in north Florida. The precious things put forth by the moon go into the coqui, a frog species that exists only in Puerto Rico and comes out at night with its distinct call. The chief things of the ancient mountains are the diamonds, gold, and silver in their land, and the precious things of the lasting hills include the coffee beans that come out of their hills. Let the blessing come upon the head of Joseph, him that was separated from his brethren. Ephraim said, Yet I am become rich: hence the very name Puerto Rico, the port of riches. But like we read earlier, they waxed fat and became prideful as well.

His glory is like the firstling of his bullock: as in the law that sanctified the firstborn unto the Most High, that is the glory of the birthright given to Joseph. His horns are like the horns of unicorns: two horns, Ephraim and Manasseh. With them he shall push the people together to the ends of the earth: the Most High used Ephraim and Manasseh as the heads to push the ten tribes over to this side of the world, as the account of the tribes taking counsel to go forth into a further country shows. And they are the ten thousands of Ephraim, and they are the thousands of Manasseh: the blessing on Jacob's grandsons was to grow into a multitude in the midst of the earth. The Most High gets geographic with it: they went from the east to the west and multiplied in the midst of the hemisphere, in Central America.

And of Zebulun he said, Rejoice, Zebulun, in thy going out; and, Issachar, in thy tents. Notice the grouping: Zebulun and Issachar are blessed together because they would dwell very close, with linked cities at their borders. They shall call the people unto the mountain; there they shall offer sacrifices of righteousness. In the promised land they linked up to make sacrifices of righteousness; but when they linked up on this side of the world as the Aztecs and the Mayans, they erected pyramids and eventually went off and sacrificed to other gods, even human sacrifice, as Hosea testifies of their sacrificing. For they shall suck of the abundance of the seas, and of treasures hid in the sand: the gold and silver discovered in their land, which is why the conquistadors were so glad to stumble upon it.

And of Gad he said, Blessed be he that enlargeth Gad. Gad alone holds over three hundred Indian tribes within itself; it is a very large tribe. He dwelleth as a lion, and teareth the arm with the crown of the head: Gad was a warlike, predator people, and the tearing of the arm goes into the blood brother pact they were known for making, the chief with the crown of feathers having a man tear his arm to be accepted into the tribe. And he provided the first part for himself: that is North America, the mainland, the largest and best portion. Because there, in a portion of the lawgiver, was he seated: the tribe of Gad served as the lawgivers for the northern kingdom. And he came with the heads of the people: the travel to this side of the earth was made with Ephraim and Manasseh, the horns, at the head, dealing with the so-called Hispanics and Indians together. He executed the justice of the Lord, and his judgments with Israel, before they went off.

And of Dan he said, Dan is a lion's whelp: he shall leap from Bashan. Dan is a warlike people; the Carib Indians did not play. He shall leap from Bashan says a lot in a short verse: Bashan was in the most northern part of Israel, so leaping from Bashan lands Dan in the middle of all Israel. That is why Dan today is not their own tribe but is absorbed into all the other tribes, primarily Benjamin, dwelling in the Caribbean. Amos says they shall fall, and never rise up again: Dan fell and never rose again as a tribe, which is why Dan is not mentioned among the tribes of the 144,000 in [Revelation 7](/bible/revelation/7). And as [Genesis 49](/bible/genesis/49) says, Dan is an adder in the path: look how the islands are shaped geographically, like a serpent.

And of Naphtali he said, O Naphtali, satisfied with favour: Naphtali is Argentina and Chile today. Satisfied with favour goes into the grapes they are able to produce in their land for wine, and coffee as well. And full with the blessing of the Lord: to this day their land is rich with agriculture and cattle. Possess thou the west and the south: the Most High gets geographic again. Look at a map of the world: what land sits in the southwestern region of the earth? Argentina and Chile. Stop playing with the prophets; we know who we are.

And of Asher he said, Let Asher be blessed with children. Asher is also a large tribe: the countries that make up Asher today include Brazil, Peru, Colombia, and Uruguay, and Brazil has the largest population of children in the world. Let him be acceptable to his brethren: for a period of time they became so wild in their ways that they were not acceptable in the sight of their brethren. And let him dip his foot in oil: one of the largest outputs of crude oil resources is Colombia. Thy shoes shall be iron and brass: the Hebrew word for iron is barzel; say it fast and you hear Brazil. It goes into the mineral resources in that land, iron, copper, zinc. And as thy days, so shall thy strength be.

There is none like unto the God of Jeshurun, who rideth upon the heaven in thy help. The eternal God is thy refuge, and underneath are the everlasting arms: he shall thrust out the enemy from before thee. Notice how the song and blessing have evolved: from Israel provoking the Most High and being punished, the teeth of beasts sent upon us, now it goes into our salvation, how the Most High will be our refuge. Israel then shall dwell in safety alone. Happy art thou, O Israel: who is like unto thee, O people saved by the Lord! And thine enemies shall be found liars unto thee: after all these years of the crafty counsel, being told you are anything but Israel and that everybody else holds your heritage, the Most High said your enemies shall be found liars, and thou shalt tread upon their high places. Never trust your enemy: your enemy will do everything in his power to keep you oppressed and subject to him, including lying to you about your history. As in the days of the Maccabees, the leaders show the people the falsehood of the heathen and the breach of their oaths, the covenants and treaties they broke with our people; after so long you learn that your enemies have been liars this whole time.

Aaron and his sons were appointed to wait on the priest's office, and the stranger that cometh nigh shall be put to death. Anybody outside the tribe of Levi, when it came to doing the service of the Lord, was considered a stranger.

The Most High took the Levites from among the children of Israel instead of all the firstborn that openeth the matrix. The matrix is the womb; that is what the Lord calls it. All the firstborn are his from the day he smote all the firstborn in the land of Egypt. Verse 13 proves the Most High does not love everybody; he killed all the firstborn of Egypt.

The children of Levi were numbered after the houses of their fathers, by their families. Your lineage is determined by your father, not your mother. The claim that identity passes through the mother is nowhere in the Bible; number the children of Levi after the house of their fathers is the standard of scripture.

Of Gershon were the families of the Libnites and the Shimites, numbered 7,500 males from a month old and upward, and they pitched behind the tabernacle westward. Depending on your family lineage you had a specific side of the tabernacle that you and all your descendants had to be on. The charge of the sons of Gershon was the tabernacle and the tent, the covering thereof, the hanging for the door, the hangings of the court, and the cords of it; that was their responsibility.

The ending "ites" denotes the people of; the Kohathites are the people of Kohath. They numbered 8,600 and pitched on the side of the tabernacle southward. Their charge was the ark, the table, the candlestick, the altars, and the vessels of the sanctuary. Only they were responsible for the ark; anybody outside of that suffered the judgment of the Most High, as Uzzah did generations later when he put forth his hand to the ark and God smote him on the spot.
Eleazar the son of Aaron was chief over the chief of the Levites, with the oversight of them that keep the charge of the sanctuary. He was the manager of the tabernacle.

Of Merari were the families of the Mahlites and the Mushites, numbered 6,200, and they pitched on the side of the tabernacle northward. Their custody and charge was the boards of the tabernacle, the bars, the pillars, the sockets, the vessels, and the pillars of the court round about with their sockets, pins, and cords.

Moses and Aaron and his sons encamped before the tabernacle toward the east, keeping the charge of the sanctuary; and the stranger that cometh nigh shall be put to death. Anybody outside the tribe of Levi that approached unto the tabernacle was considered a stranger.

All the Levites numbered from a month old and upward were 22,000; the Most High was separating the tribe of Levi unto himself instead of all the firstborn among the children of Israel. The firstborn males of the children of Israel were twenty and two thousand two hundred and threescore and thirteen. A score is twenty, so threescore and thirteen is 73; the count is 22,273.

The firstborn of Israel outnumbered the Levites by 273, and those odd ones were redeemed at five shekels apiece by the poll, after the shekel of the sanctuary, which is twenty gerahs. Moses took the redemption money, 1,365 shekels, and gave it unto Aaron and to his sons. The money went to Aaron and the priests because they had to take care of the widows, the fatherless, and the strangers; the strangers are our people that come from different parts of the land down to Jerusalem needing help. That is how the Most High put money into the sanctuary to take care of those that could not take care of themselves.

The prophet or dreamer of dreams who speaks to turn you away from the Lord your God was put to death under the kingdom. Today Israel is in the land of its oppressors and cannot exact that judgment, and no kind of violence is advocated; the deceived and the deceiver are his, and the judgment belongs to the Most High. What is done today: mark them which cause divisions and offences contrary to the doctrine which ye have learned, and avoid them. The doctrine learned is the law, for I give you good doctrine, forsake ye not my law. Going contrary to the laws of marriage, of the sabbath, of raising children righteously, or of going to thy brother alone when there is an ought between you, and secretly enticing others to follow, is how one turns people away from the Lord; those men and those women have to be put out from among the body.

If thy brother, thy son, thy daughter, the wife of thy bosom, or thy friend which is as thine own soul entice thee secretly to serve other gods: these are the people closest to you, the ones that can have influence on you. Thou shalt not consent, nor hearken, nor pity, nor spare, neither shalt thou conceal him, meaning hide him; when wickedness is concealed, the whole nation is put in jeopardy. Trust in a person is no cover for your soul: when someone you love and trust has the devil on them, they will lead you astray. Nobody can make you do anything, but they can influence you; do not give anyone that credit and let them cause you to lose your crown. This is why [Leviticus 5:1](/bible/leviticus/5#v1) is opened at the start of class: if you know of anything, you are supposed to utter it. Many grew up on snitches get stitches, but in repentance we have to understand that concealing sin is part of why Israel is in the condition it is in, and we have to teach righteousness. It is that simple.

If certain men, the children of Belial, withdraw the inhabitants of a city, saying, let us go and serve other gods: inquire, make search, and ask diligently, and if it be truth and the thing certain, that city was smitten with the edge of the sword, gathered into the midst of the street, and burnt with fire, an heap for ever, not to be built again. Achan is the example of this kind of judgment: Israel committed a trespass in the accursed thing, and one man's folly kindled the anger of the Lord against all Israel. Wars Israel had been winning without losing a man began to be lost, and Joshua had to search and seek out who had committed the crime in Israel. All Israel stoned Achan with stones and burned him with fire in the valley of Achor, and the Lord turned from the fierceness of his anger; righteous judgment lifted the wrath and the people were able to move forward.
