name: Nadab and Abihu
charge: Offering strange fire not commanded
summary: Two priests, sons of Aaron, offered fire before the Lord that he had not commanded. Fire came out from the Lord and consumed them on the spot.
offense: The instructions for the incense had already been given, and given to their own father: Aaron was to burn sweet incense every morning and at even, a perpetual incense before the Lord throughout the generations, and ye shall offer no strange incense thereon (Exodus 30:7-9). So the fault is not an error of enthusiasm but the offering of a thing expressly excluded. They took either of them his censer, and put fire therein, and put incense thereon, and offered strange fire before the Lord, which he commanded them not (Leviticus 10:1). The office itself was guarded to this degree: Aaron and his sons were appointed to wait on the priest's office, and the stranger that cometh nigh shall be put to death (Numbers 3:10), so nearness to the altar was the most closely regulated standing in Israel and these two held it.
judgment: There went out fire from the Lord and devoured them, and they died before the Lord (Leviticus 10:2). The record notes what fire it was: the same that had come out from before the Lord and consumed the burnt offering upon the altar in the chapter before, while the people shouted and fell on their faces (Leviticus 9:24). The fire that had accepted the lawful offering consumed the unlawful one. Aaron, Eleazar and Ithamar were then forbidden to uncover their heads or rend their clothes lest they die and wrath come upon all the people, and the mourning was given to the whole house of Israel instead (Leviticus 10:6). The father was not permitted to mourn his own sons, because they died in the midst of the sin, and the sentence pronounced over it is the standing rule of the sanctuary: I will be sanctified in them that come nigh me, and before all the people I will be glorified (Leviticus 10:3).

verses.text: 1And Nadab and Abihu, the sons of Aaron, took either of them his censer, and put fire therein, and put incense thereon, and offered strange fire before the Lord, which he commanded them not. 2And there went out fire from the Lord, and devoured them, and they died before the Lord. 3Then Moses said unto Aaron, This is it that the Lord spake, saying, I will be sanctified in them that come nigh me, and before all the people I will be glorified. And Aaron held his peace.
1And the Lord spake unto Moses after the death of the two sons of Aaron, when they offered before the Lord, and died;

4And Nadab and Abihu died before the Lord, when they offered strange fire before the Lord, in the wilderness of Sinai, and they had no children: and Eleazar and Ithamar ministered in the priest’s office in the sight of Aaron their father.

entries.commentary: Nadab and Abihu, the sons of Aaron, took either of them his censer, put fire therein and incense thereon, and offered strange fire before the Lord, which he commanded them not; and fire went out from the Lord and devoured them. The instructions for the incense were already given: Aaron shall burn sweet incense every morning and at even, a perpetual incense before the Lord throughout your generations, and ye shall offer no strange incense thereon. There were instructions on what could be burned and what could not; the strange fire is that Nadab and Abihu put strange incense before the Lord. When the Most High gave instructions through Moses on what to sacrifice and how, it was with specificity; you were to do it exactly the way he told you. They were also not the ones authorized to burn the incense; in the tabernacle service you had to be appointed to certain services and could not take a service upon yourself. Zacharias shows the pattern throughout the generations: he executed the priest's office in the order of his course, and his lot, his appointed job, was to burn incense when he went into the temple of the Lord. The fire that went out from the Lord was the same fire that came out from before the Lord in [Leviticus 9](/bible/leviticus/9) and consumed the burnt offering upon the altar.
Then Moses said unto Aaron, this is what the Lord spake: I will be sanctified in them that come nigh me, and before all the people I will be glorified. And Aaron held his peace.
Moses called Mishael and Elzaphan, the sons of Uzziel the uncle of Aaron, and they came near and carried them in their coats out of the camp, as Moses had said.

Aaron, Eleazar, and Ithamar were told, uncover not your heads, neither rend your clothes, lest ye die and wrath come upon all the people; basically they were told not to mourn for them, because Nadab and Abihu died in the midst of sin and what they did was abominable to the Most High. The whole house of Israel would bewail the burning which the Lord kindled. Ezekiel is the example of that word: the Most High took away the desire of his eyes, his wife, with a stroke, and told him make no mourning for the dead, neither weep, and Ezekiel went and taught the people that morning, and at even his wife died. The same standard fell on Jehoiakim the son of Josiah: they shall not lament for him, saying, Ah my brother, or, Ah lord.
They were not to go out from the door of the tabernacle, for the anointing oil of the Lord was upon them. The anointing oil had already been put on them, so they could not leave the sanctuary.

Some read this and think Aaron and his sons could never drink, but going precept upon precept, this speaks of when they went into the tabernacle of the congregation: they were at work doing the Lord's work, and there was no drinking on the job. Ezekiel lays out the priests' work rules. The priests the Levites, the sons of Zadok, kept the charge of the sanctuary; when they entered the gates of the inner court they were clocking in, clothed in linen garments and linen bonnets, girded with nothing that causeth sweat; and going out to the people in the utter court they put off the garments wherein they ministered and put on other garments, like taking off a work uniform. Neither shall any priest drink wine when they enter into the inner court; that is exactly what verse 9 speaks of. They had to be sober minded because they taught the people the difference between the holy and profane and caused them to discern between the unclean and the clean, and in controversy they stood in judgment, judging according to the judgments of the Most High. On the priests' hair: they were not to shave their heads nor suffer their locks to grow long, but only poll their heads. Polling the head means keeping the hair trimmed and maintained; you can grow it, but keep it up.

Moses told Aaron, Eleazar, and Ithamar to take the meat offering that remained of the offerings made by fire and eat it without leaven beside the altar, in the holy place, for it was their due; and the wave breast and heave shoulder were eaten in a clean place, the due of Aaron and his sons and his daughters by a statute for ever. The wave offering is explained in chapter 7: his own hands shall bring the offerings of the Lord made by fire, the fat with the breast, that the breast may be waved for a wave offering before the Lord.

Moses diligently sought the goat of the sin offering, and behold, it was burnt; and he was angry with Eleazar and Ithamar, because the Most High had given it to them to bear the iniquity of the congregation, and seeing the blood of it was not brought in within the holy place, they should indeed have eaten it in the holy place, as he commanded. Those were the instructions of the law of the sin offering: the priest that offereth it for sin shall eat it in the holy place, and all the males among the priests shall eat thereof; but no sin offering whereof any of the blood is brought into the tabernacle to reconcile withal shall be eaten, it shall be burnt in the fire.

Aaron answered Moses: this day have they offered their sin offering and their burnt offering, and such things have befallen me; and if I had eaten the sin offering today, should it have been accepted in the sight of the Lord? And when Moses heard that, he was content.

*1 And the LORD spake unto Moses after the death of the two sons of Aaron, when they offered before the LORD, and died; 2 And the LORD said unto Moses, Speak unto Aaron thy brother, that he come not at all times into the holy place within the vail before the mercy seat, which is upon the ark; that he die not: for I will appear in the cloud upon the mercy seat. 3 Thus shall Aaron come into the holy place: with a young bullock for a sin offering, and a ram for a burnt offering. 4 He shall put on the holy linen coat, and he shall have the linen breeches upon his flesh, and shall be girded with a linen girdle, and with the linen mitre shall he be attired: these are holy garments; therefore shall he wash his flesh in water, and so put them on. 5 And he shall take of the congregation of the children of Israel two kids of the goats for a sin offering, and one ram for a burnt offering. 6 And Aaron shall offer his bullock of the sin offering, which is for himself, and make an atonement for himself, and for his house. 7 And he shall take the two goats, and present them before the LORD at the door of the tabernacle of the congregation. 8 And Aaron shall cast lots upon the two goats; one lot for the LORD, and the other lot for the scapegoat. 9 And Aaron shall bring the goat upon which the LORD’s lot fell, and offer him for a sin offering. 10 But the goat, on which the lot fell to be the scapegoat, shall be presented alive before the LORD, to make an atonement with him, and to let him go for a scapegoat into the wilderness. 11 And Aaron shall bring the bullock of the sin offering, which is for himself, and shall make an atonement for himself, and for his house, and shall kill the bullock of the sin offering which is for himself: 12 And he shall take a censer full of burning coals of fire from off the altar before the LORD, and his hands full of sweet incense beaten small, and bring it within the vail: 13 And he shall put the incense upon the fire before the LORD, that the cloud of the incense may cover the mercy seat that is upon the testimony, that he die not: 14 And he shall take of the blood of the bullock, and sprinkle it with his finger upon the mercy seat eastward; and before the mercy seat shall he sprinkle of the blood with his finger seven times. 15 Then shall he kill the goat of the sin offering, that is for the people, and bring his blood within the vail, and do with that blood as he did with the blood of the bullock, and sprinkle it upon the mercy seat, and before the mercy seat: 16 And he shall make an atonement for the holy place, because of the uncleanness of the children of Israel, and because of their transgressions in all their sins: and so shall he do for the tabernacle of the congregation, that remaineth among them in the midst of their uncleanness. 17 And there shall be no man in the tabernacle of the congregation when he goeth in to make an atonement in the holy place, until he come out, and have made an atonement for himself, and for his household, and for all the congregation of Israel. 18 And he shall go out unto the altar that is before the LORD, and make an atonement for it; and shall take of the blood of the bullock, and of the blood of the goat, and put it upon the horns of the altar round about. 19 And he shall sprinkle of the blood upon it with his finger seven times, and cleanse it, and hallow it from the uncleanness of the children of Israel. 20 And when he hath made an end of reconciling the holy place, and the tabernacle of the congregation, and the altar, he shall bring the live goat: 21 And Aaron shall lay both his hands upon the head of the live goat, and confess over him all the iniquities of the children of Israel, and all their transgressions in all their sins, putting them upon the head of the goat, and shall send him away by the hand of a fit man into the wilderness: 22 And the goat shall bear upon him all their iniquities unto a land not inhabited: and he shall let go the goat in the wilderness. 23 And Aaron shall come into the tabernacle of the congregation, and shall put off the linen garments, which he put on when he went into the holy place, and shall leave them there: 24 And he shall wash his flesh with water in the holy place, and put on his garments, and come forth, and offer his burnt offering, and the burnt offering of the people, and make an atonement for himself, and for the people. 25 And the fat of the sin offering shall he burn upon the altar. 26 And he that let go the goat for the scapegoat shall wash his clothes, and bathe his flesh in water, and afterward come into the camp. 27 And the bullock for the sin offering, and the goat for the sin offering, whose blood was brought in to make atonement in the holy place, shall one carry forth without the camp; and they shall burn in the fire their skins, and their flesh, and their dung. 28 And he that burneth them shall wash his clothes, and bathe his flesh in water, and afterward he shall come into the camp. 29 And this shall be a statute for ever unto you: that in the seventh month, on the tenth day of the month, ye shall afflict your souls, and do no work at all, whether it be one of your own country, or a stranger that sojourneth among you: 30 For on that day shall the priest make an atonement for you, to cleanse you, that ye may be clean from all your sins before the LORD. 31 It shall be a sabbath of rest unto you, and ye shall afflict your souls, by a statute for ever. 32 And the priest, whom he shall anoint, and whom he shall consecrate to minister in the priest’s office in his father’s stead, shall make the atonement, and shall put on the linen clothes, even the holy garments: 33 And he shall make an atonement for the holy sanctuary, and he shall make an atonement for the tabernacle of the congregation, and for the altar, and he shall make an atonement for the priests, and for all the people of the congregation. 34 And this shall be an everlasting statute unto you, to make an atonement for the children of Israel for all their sins once a year. And he did as the LORD commanded Moses.*

That is how the Most High put money into the sanctuary to take care of those that could not take care of themselves.

After the plague the Lord commanded a new numbering of the congregation, from twenty years old and upward, all that are able to go to war in Israel. Twenty is the biblical age of a man: Israel sent men to war, not children, so the numbering of them able for war fixes the age of manhood at twenty years old.

Of Hanoch, the family of the Hanochites; of Pallu, the family of the Palluites. The ending ites means the descendants of, the people you belong to: Israelites are the descendants of Israel, Edomites the descendants of Edom, and so it goes all down the line through the scriptures. Reading these family names aloud loosens the tongue to say the names of the scriptures fluently and without hesitation. [1 Chronicles 1](/bible/1-chronicles/1) serves the same practice, and it carries the names of Israel's families together with Edom and Ishmael, the nations that come out of Abraham's line.

Dathan and Abiram were famous in the congregation, who strove against Moses and against Aaron in the company of Korah, when they strove against the Lord; the account is back in [Numbers 16](/bible/numbers/16). The earth opened her mouth and swallowed them up together with Korah, the fire devoured two hundred and fifty men, and they became a sign. Notwithstanding, the children of Korah died not.

Er and Onan died in the land of Canaan, and the families of Judah continued through Shelah, Pharez, and Zerah, threescore and sixteen thousand and five hundred numbered. Do not hear Pharez and think the Pharisees came from the Pharzites; the Pharisees did not come out of that family. The rise of those sects is read of in the books of the Maccabees.

The numbered of the children of Israel were six hundred thousand and a thousand seven hundred and thirty. Unto these the land shall be divided for an inheritance according to the number of names: to many the more inheritance, to few the less, and the land divided by lot according to the tribes of their fathers. Land is how wealth is built, and Esau knows how important land is; that is why the land is kept in his generations and why Gad, the Native Indian, was never given one square inch of his land back, only the casinos and the little plots called reservations. Israel is getting the most fertile land back; as for this land here, let it burn.

Jochebed the daughter of Levi bare unto Amram Aaron and Moses and Miriam their sister; and unto Aaron were born Nadab and Abihu, Eleazar and Ithamar. Nadab and Abihu died when they offered strange fire before the Lord; go back and read that account.

Among these numbered by Moses and Eleazar in the plains of Moab there was not a man of them that was numbered in the wilderness of Sinai, for the Lord had said of them, they shall surely die in the wilderness; and there was not left a man of them, save Caleb the son of Jephunneh and Joshua the son of Nun. Why Caleb and Joshua? They had another spirit on them and did not doubt when the Lord sent them to spy out the land. My servant Caleb, because he had another spirit with him and hath followed me fully, him will I bring into the land; he let nobody keep him from serving the Most High. Christ said the same thing: he that loveth father or mother more than me is not worthy of me. If the Lord finds you lukewarm, choosing your kids, your parents, or your spouse over following God and Christ and keeping the commandments wholly, you will not enter into the land; you must follow fully like Caleb and zealously like Phinehas. Let that be a lesson learned, for whatsoever things were written aforetime were written for our learning, that we through patience and comfort of the scriptures might have hope.

name: The blasphemer in the camp
charge: Blaspheming the Name in a quarrel
summary: In a fight within the camp, a man blasphemed the Name and cursed. He was held until the Lord's mind was made known, and his case set the statute for all Israel.
offense: He is identified by his lineage before his act, and the lineage is the first thing the case teaches. The son of an Israelitish woman, whose father was an Egyptian, went out among the children of Israel, and this son of the Israelitish woman and a man of Israel strove together in the camp (Leviticus 24:10). His mother was Shelomith, the daughter of Dibri, of the tribe of Dan (Leviticus 24:11), so the mother was named and the tribe was named, and he was conceived in Egypt while Israel dwelt among the Egyptians; there is no half Israel, and he was counted with his mother's people. In the strife the Israelitish woman's son blasphemed the name of the Lord, and cursed (Leviticus 24:11). The offence was against God directly, in the camp, spoken aloud and heard.
judgment: The Lord commanded that the whole congregation stone him outside the camp, the witnesses laying their hands on his head. From his case came the law: whoever blasphemes the Name shall be put to death.

entries.commentary: The children of Israel were commanded to bring pure oil olive beaten for the light, to cause the lamps to burn continually. Aaron ordered it from the evening unto the morning before the Lord continually, upon the pure candlestick, a statute for ever in your generations.

Twelve cakes of fine flour were set in two rows, six on a row, upon the pure table before the Lord, with pure frankincense upon each row, every sabbath, taken from the children of Israel by an everlasting covenant. It shall be Aaron's and his sons', and they shall eat it in the holy place, for it is most holy unto him of the offerings of the Lord made by fire.

The son of an Israelitish woman, whose father was an Egyptian, went out among the children of Israel, and strove in the camp with a man of Israel, and blasphemed the name of the Lord, and cursed. His mother was Shelomith, the daughter of Dibri, of the tribe of Dan. They put him in ward, that the mind of the Lord might be shewed them; and the Lord commanded that he that had cursed be brought forth without the camp, that all that heard him lay their hands upon his head, and that all the congregation stone him. The strife in the camp likely arose from a man of Israel correcting him concerning the law. His father being an Egyptian shows he was conceived while Israel was in captivity in the land of Egypt, dwelling among the Egyptians; in the same way Moses, outside of Egypt with Jethro the priest of Midian, took a wife there. And there is no such thing as being half Israelite or a fourth Israelite: if your parent is Israel, you are Israel. Whosoever curseth his God shall bear his sin, and he that blasphemeth the name of the Lord, he shall surely be put to death, as well the stranger as he that is born in the land.

He that killeth any man shall surely be put to death, and he that killeth a beast shall make it good, beast for beast. If a man cause a blemish in his neighbour, as he hath done, so shall it be done to him: breach for breach, eye for eye, tooth for tooth. One manner of law stood for the stranger as for one of your own country. When Christ came he taught the proper understanding of eye for eye for dealing inside the nation: ye have heard that it hath been said, an eye for an eye, and a tooth for a tooth, but I say unto you that ye resist not evil. As the Son of God he had authority to magnify the law: whosoever smites thee on thy right cheek, turn to him the other also; if any man sue thee and take away thy coat, let him have thy cloak also; whosoever compels thee to go a mile, go with him twain. Inside our nation we must practice forgiveness, patience, and long-suffering; we are dealing with our own people, brothers with a conscience. We are the most forgiving people on the planet; the only time we do not know how to forgive is when it comes to each other, and Christ dealt with that.

An image in itself is not the sin, except for that white image of the beast; making images to bow down to them and serve them is the transgression, for the Lord thy God is a jealous God. Visiting the iniquity of the fathers upon the children unto the third and fourth generation: Israel is yet this day in captivity, scattered for a reproach and a curse, according to all the iniquities of the fathers which departed from the Lord. Right now Israel is paying for the sins of the fathers; that is why the people are scattered to the four corners of the earth.

And shewing mercy unto thousands of them that love me, and keep my commandments. Judith recounted how the Most High tried the fathers for the examination of their hearts: he tried Abraham and Isaac, and Jacob in Mesopotamia of Syria keeping the sheep of Laban, serving twenty years with his wages changed and given Leah when he looked for Rachel. In Judith's day there was no tribe, family, people, nor city that worshipped gods made with hands, as had been aforetime; for that cause she trusted the Lord would not despise the nation. Mercy rests on them that know none other God, not Allah, not Buddha, not a white Jesus.

Remember the Sabbath day, to keep it holy. The word says remember because Israel would forget it: in this captivity the people were forced to serve other gods and their religions, and the Sabbath was lost through forced conversion. Look up the blue laws, also known as Sunday laws; they help give understanding of why the Bible says remember the Sabbath day.

An altar of stone was not to be built of hewn stone, for lifting up a tool upon it pollutes it; neither go up by steps unto the altar, that thy nakedness be not discovered thereon. This scripture helps explain pants, precept upon precept. The priests were given linen breeches to cover their nakedness from the loins even unto the thighs when they came near the altar, and Israel was called in this same reading to be a kingdom of priests, so do not be simple and say that law was only for Aaron and his sons. Those breeches were made for men and not for women, as the law of the garments also shows.

name: The complainers at Taberah and the lusters at Kibroth-hattaavah
charge: Murmuring against the Lord; lusting after flesh and despising the manna
summary: The people complained and the fire of the Lord burned in the outskirts of the camp. Days later the mixed multitude fell to lusting and Israel wept for the meat of Egypt. Quail came, and with the quail a plague.
offense: The first sentence names the whole offence: when the people complained, it displeased the Lord, and the Lord heard it, and his anger was kindled (Numbers 11:1). Egypt had been destroyed for them, its firstborn, its army, its land, and at the first trial on the far side of the sea they murmured. Nothing spoken is hidden, and the wise man's warning is the  precept the case sits on: beware of murmuring, which is unprofitable, and refrain your tongue from backbiting, for there is no word so secret that shall go for nought, and the mouth that belieth slayeth the soul (Wisdom of Solomon 1:11). The second stage came from outside the nation before it came from inside it: the mixt multitude that was among them fell a lusting, and the children of Israel also wept again (Numbers 11:4). The nations sprinkled in among Israel lusted first, and Israel followed them, as it always has, and wept for the fish they did eat in Egypt freely, the cucumbers, the melons, the leeks, the onions, and the garlick (Numbers 11:5), the diet of the house of bondage, weeks after the bondage ended. They had just watched the Lord consume the complainers in the uttermost parts of the camp and went back and did the same thing, and the psalm names it: they tempted God in their heart by asking meat for their lust, and they spake against God (Psalms 78:18-19).
judgment: Fire consumed the complainers at Taberah until Moses prayed. At Kibroth-hattaavah, while the flesh was yet between their teeth, the Lord smote the people with a very great plague; the place is named for the graves of the lusters. Paul: these things were our examples.

entries.commentary: The Most High hates it when His people complain. He had just destroyed Egypt for Israel, its land, its infrastructure, its firstborn, and drowned its army in the sea, all to save the people out; then on the other side of the wilderness, at the first trial or tribulation, the people jumped off His bandwagon, and the same is still being done to this day. The Lord heard the complaining, and His anger was kindled, and the fire of the Lord burnt among them. Vengeance, when it punisheth, does not pass by him that speaketh unrighteous things; the murmurer receives the vengeance of the Lord. Nothing spoken behind closed doors is hidden. Inquisition is made into the counsels of the ungodly, by the Lord and His angels, the same council seen when the Lord asked who shall persuade Ahab that he may fall at Ramothgilead; the sound of a man's words comes unto the Lord, for the ear of jealousy heareth all things. Beware of murmuring and refrain the tongue from backbiting, for there is no word so secret that shall go for nought, and the mouth that belieth, that slandereth a brother, a sister, the leadership, or the Lord, slayeth the soul. Many speak evil against leadership because they do not like when judgment comes out; a problem with the leadership the Most High set up is a problem with the Most High Himself.

The people cried unto Moses, and when Moses prayed unto the Lord, the fire was quenched; the Most High quenched the fire because Moses prayed on behalf of the children of Israel. The place was called Taberah, because the fire of the Lord burnt among them.

The mixed multitude that fell a lusting were the other nations sprinkled in among Israel, the mixed multitude that went up with the people out of Egypt; the law in Leviticus tells what they were for, to be the bondmen and bondmaids of Israel. It was not Israel complaining at first; it was the nations lusting after the food of Egypt, and the children of Israel, gullible and assimilated as always, followed right after them and murmured against their God. The same spirit is on the people now: whatever the other nations want to do, our people want to be part of it. They wept for the fish they ate freely in Egypt, the cucumbers, the melons, the leeks, the onions, and the garlic, right after the Lord destroyed the Egyptians to bring them out of bondage. It is the same today with the entertainments and comforts of this captivity, and some will do the same thing again in the wilderness when the Most High brings the people back out. They had just seen the Lord consume the complainers in the uttermost parts of the camp, and they went back and did the same thing. We are the same people today; there is nothing new under the sun, and these things were written aforetime for our learning, so we can read them and refuse to do as they did.

The manna was as coriander seed, the colour of bdellium; the people gathered it, ground it, baked it in pans, and the taste of it was as the taste of fresh oil. Read precept upon precept to understand what they despised: manna is angels' food, the food the Lord feeds the angels, sent from heaven prepared without their labour; they only had to pick it up. The manna was able to content every man's delight and agreed to every taste, tempering itself to every man's liking; whatever the tongue craved that day, the manna tasted like it. To complain about that provision, including the very garlic and onions and melons they wept for, was pure rebellion against the Lord God of heaven and earth.
Moses heard the people weep throughout their families, every man in the door of his tent; the anger of the Lord was kindled greatly, and Moses also was displeased.

Moses asked the Most High why He had afflicted His servant and laid the burden of all this people on him: have I conceived all this people, that thou shouldest say, Carry them in thy bosom as a nursing father? He was carrying grown people who acted like children. The people Moses bore are the same people today; this teaching identifies the children of Israel with the so-called Blacks, Hispanics, and Native American Indians, and the sheer rebellion and complaining in these chapters is one of the marks of the people. Moses said, If thou deal thus with me, kill me, I pray thee, out of hand; he would rather die than bear so rebellious a people alone and look upon his own wretchedness.

The Lord told Moses to gather seventy men of the elders of Israel to the tabernacle, and He would take of the spirit upon Moses and put it upon them, that they bear the burden of the people with him. Leadership works the same way today. The spirit on the head, the willingness to put in work, the humility, the patience, is meant to trickle down to the men below him, and the spirit the lead sisters roll in sets the spirit of the sisters in the congregation. That is why the leaders must be right according to the scriptures, because the Most High takes their spirit and lets it come upon the others.

The Lord said, Sanctify yourselves against to morrow, and ye shall eat flesh; ye have wept in the ears of the Lord, saying, It was well with us in Egypt, therefore the Lord will give you flesh. Not one day, nor two, nor five, nor ten, nor twenty days, but a whole month, until it come out at your nostrils and it be loathsome unto you. He fed them so much of the flesh they begged for that they would grow sick of it and hate it. The reason for the judgment is stated plainly: because ye have despised the Lord which is among you. They spoke evil of His manna and wept to go back among the oppressors He had just destroyed.

Moses inquired how it could be done: the people are six hundred thousand footmen, and that count is not including women and children; there were millions in the wilderness. Shall the flocks and the herds be slain for them, or all the fish of the sea gathered together for them, to suffice them? The Lord answered, Is the LORD'S hand waxed short? The One who destroyed Egypt asks whether His hand is short; thou shalt see now whether my word shall come to pass unto thee or not. Be patient and watch the word come to pass.

Moses gathered the seventy elders round about the tabernacle, and the Lord came down in a cloud and took of the spirit that was upon Moses and gave it unto the seventy elders; and when the spirit rested upon them, they prophesied, and did not cease. The same thing happened with Elijah and Elisha. Elisha, Elijah's right hand and disciple, asked for a double portion of his master's spirit before Elijah was taken up, and when the sons of the prophets saw Elisha smite Jordan with the mantle, they said, The spirit of Elijah doth rest on Elisha. It was the same in the time of Christ: the apostles taught like Christ, and men could tell that spirit was on them, just as the elders carried the spirit of Moses.

Two of the men, Eldad and Medad, remained in the camp, and the spirit rested upon them, and they prophesied in the camp. A young man ran and told Moses, and Joshua the son of Nun said, My lord Moses, forbid them. Moses answered, Enviest thou for my sake? would God that all the LORD'S people were prophets. Joshua was carrying a spirit of envy, and Moses corrected it; the Most High wants all His people to be prophets. The same is a lesson today: do not envy the gift on another brother or sister, but glean from it. A brother may be a better teacher, a sister a better labourer; go and learn from them rather than rolling in envy, for the Lord would put His spirit upon them all.

A wind from the Lord brought quails from the sea and let them fall by the camp, a day's journey on this side and on the other, two cubits high upon the face of the earth, and the people gathered them. While the flesh was yet between their teeth, ere it was chewed, the wrath of the Lord was kindled and He smote the people with a very great plague, exactly as He had warned. The place was called Kibrothhattaavah, the graves of lust, because there they buried the people that lusted. The Most High had overfed them because they murmured, but the lesson also stands in nature: excess of meat brings sickness. Animal protein is good for the body, but it is a matter of moderation, not overindulgence.

Give thanks unto the Most High, for He is good and His mercy endures forever; who can show forth all His praise. Blessed are they that keep judgment and do righteousness at all times. At all times, not only when convenient. David asks to be remembered with the favor toward His people, to see the good of His chosen and rejoice in the gladness of His nation.

We have sinned with our fathers and done wickedly; our fathers understood not His wonders in Egypt and provoked Him at the Red Sea. Nevertheless He saved them for His name's sake, rebuked the Red Sea so it dried up, and led them through the depths as through the wilderness. Esau's science says a wind blew it into a tsunami, but the Most High said He rebuked it. The waters covered their enemies, and then they believed His words and sang His praise.

They soon forgot His works and waited not for His counsel, but lusted exceedingly in the wilderness and tempted God, so He sent leanness into their soul. They envied Moses and Aaron the saint of the Lord; the earth swallowed Dathan and the company of Abiram for their insurrection. They made a calf and worshipped the molten image, changing their glory into the likeness of an ox that eats grass, forgetting God their savior. He would have destroyed them had not Moses stood in the breach. -

They despised the pleasant land and believed not His word but brought up a false report and murmured in their tents; therefore He lifted His hand to overthrow them and scatter their seed among the nations. They joined themselves to Baal-peor and ate the sacrifices of the dead, provoking Him to anger, and the plague broke in upon them. Then Phinehas stood up and executed judgment, and the plague was stayed; it was counted to him for righteousness unto all generations, for he had zeal in the fear of the Most High. -

They angered Him at the waters of strife, so it went ill with Moses, who spoke unadvisedly with his lips. Moses lost the promised land because he smote the rock and called the people rebels instead of speaking to it and sanctifying the Most High. They did not destroy the nations as commanded but were mingled among the heathen and learned their works. They served idols, sacrificed their sons and daughters to devils, and shed innocent blood, polluting the land and going a-whoring with their own inventions. -

The wrath of the Most High was kindled against His people so that He abhorred His own inheritance and gave them into the hand of the heathen, who ruled over them. The heathen ruling in our communities today, the legal system and the government, is the law and the prophets agreeing; He delivered them many times, but they provoked Him and were brought low for their iniquity. Nevertheless He regarded their affliction, remembered His covenant, and repented according to His mercies; David prays: save us and gather us from among the heathen. Blessed be the Lord God of Israel from everlasting to everlasting. -

name: Eldad and Medad
charge: Prophesying in the camp when the spirit rested on them, and being defended by Moses
summary: Seventy elders were gathered to the tabernacle to be given of the spirit that was on Moses. Two of the written men stayed in the camp, and the spirit rested on them there, and they prophesied. A young man ran and told Moses, and Joshua said, My lord Moses, forbid them. Moses answered, Enviest thou for my sake? would God that all the Lord's people were prophets.
offense: They were of the written number but they were not at the tent. Nothing in the account says they refused to go, and the record does not accuse them; what it records is that the spirit rested on them where they were (Numbers 11:25), and that they did not conceal it or wait for permission before speaking. The complaint against them came from the camp and from Moses' own servant (Numbers 11:27), and the two men are not shown answering it.
judgment: Moses refused to silence them and turned the rebuke on the man who wanted it done: enviest thou for my sake? would God that all the Lord's people were prophets (Numbers 11:29), and that the Lord would put his spirit upon them. The case is entered because the blessing was defended by the one person whose standing it might have threatened, and because the wish Moses expressed is the thing Joel later prophesies and Peter cites at Pentecost as fulfilled. Two men who were not in the room are the volume's earliest evidence that the gift is not confined to the appointed place.

verses.text: 16And the Lord said unto Moses, Gather unto me seventy men of the elders of Israel, whom thou knowest to be the elders of the people, and officers over them; and bring them unto the tabernacle of the congregation, that they may stand there with thee. 17And I will come down and talk with thee there: and I will take of the spirit which is upon thee, and will put it upon them; and they shall bear the burden of the people with thee, that thou bear it not thyself alone.

24And Moses went out, and told the people the words of the Lord, and gathered the seventy men of the elders of the people, and set them round about the tabernacle. 25And the Lord came down in a cloud, and spake unto him, and took of the spirit that was upon him, and gave it unto the seventy elders: and it came to pass, that, when the spirit rested upon them, they prophesied, and did not cease. 26But there remained two of the men in the camp, the name of the one was Eldad, and the name of the other Medad: and the spirit rested upon them; and they were of them that were written, but went not out unto the tabernacle: and they prophesied in the camp. 27And there ran a young man, and told Moses, and said, Eldad and Medad do prophesy in the camp.

28And Joshua the son of Nun, the servant of Moses, one of his young men, answered and said, My lord Moses, forbid them. 29And Moses said unto him, Enviest thou for my sake? would God that all the Lord’s people were prophets, and that the Lord would put his spirit upon them!

The same spirit is on the people now: whatever the other nations want to do, our people want to be part of it. They wept for the fish they ate freely in Egypt, the cucumbers, the melons, the leeks, the onions, and the garlic, right after the Lord destroyed the Egyptians to bring them out of bondage. It is the same today with the entertainments and comforts of this captivity, and some will do the same thing again in the wilderness when the Most High brings the people back out. They had just seen the Lord consume the complainers in the uttermost parts of the camp, and they went back and did the same thing. We are the same people today; there is nothing new under the sun, and these things were written aforetime for our learning, so we can read them and refuse to do as they did.

The manna was as coriander seed, the colour of bdellium; the people gathered it, ground it, baked it in pans, and the taste of it was as the taste of fresh oil. Read precept upon precept to understand what they despised: manna is angels' food, the food the Lord feeds the angels, sent from heaven prepared without their labour; they only had to pick it up. The manna was able to content every man's delight and agreed to every taste, tempering itself to every man's liking; whatever the tongue craved that day, the manna tasted like it. To complain about that provision, including the very garlic and onions and melons they wept for, was pure rebellion against the Lord God of heaven and earth.
Moses heard the people weep throughout their families, every man in the door of his tent; the anger of the Lord was kindled greatly, and Moses also was displeased.

Moses asked the Most High why He had afflicted His servant and laid the burden of all this people on him: have I conceived all this people, that thou shouldest say, Carry them in thy bosom as a nursing father? He was carrying grown people who acted like children. The people Moses bore are the same people today; this teaching identifies the children of Israel with the so-called Blacks, Hispanics, and Native American Indians, and the sheer rebellion and complaining in these chapters is one of the marks of the people. Moses said, If thou deal thus with me, kill me, I pray thee, out of hand; he would rather die than bear so rebellious a people alone and look upon his own wretchedness.

The Lord told Moses to gather seventy men of the elders of Israel to the tabernacle, and He would take of the spirit upon Moses and put it upon them, that they bear the burden of the people with him. Leadership works the same way today. The spirit on the head, the willingness to put in work, the humility, the patience, is meant to trickle down to the men below him, and the spirit the lead sisters roll in sets the spirit of the sisters in the congregation. That is why the leaders must be right according to the scriptures, because the Most High takes their spirit and lets it come upon the others.

The Lord said, Sanctify yourselves against to morrow, and ye shall eat flesh; ye have wept in the ears of the Lord, saying, It was well with us in Egypt, therefore the Lord will give you flesh. Not one day, nor two, nor five, nor ten, nor twenty days, but a whole month, until it come out at your nostrils and it be loathsome unto you. He fed them so much of the flesh they begged for that they would grow sick of it and hate it. The reason for the judgment is stated plainly: because ye have despised the Lord which is among you. They spoke evil of His manna and wept to go back among the oppressors He had just destroyed.

Moses inquired how it could be done: the people are six hundred thousand footmen, and that count is not including women and children; there were millions in the wilderness. Shall the flocks and the herds be slain for them, or all the fish of the sea gathered together for them, to suffice them? The Lord answered, Is the LORD'S hand waxed short? The One who destroyed Egypt asks whether His hand is short; thou shalt see now whether my word shall come to pass unto thee or not. Be patient and watch the word come to pass.

Moses gathered the seventy elders round about the tabernacle, and the Lord came down in a cloud and took of the spirit that was upon Moses and gave it unto the seventy elders; and when the spirit rested upon them, they prophesied, and did not cease. The same thing happened with Elijah and Elisha. Elisha, Elijah's right hand and disciple, asked for a double portion of his master's spirit before Elijah was taken up, and when the sons of the prophets saw Elisha smite Jordan with the mantle, they said, The spirit of Elijah doth rest on Elisha. It was the same in the time of Christ: the apostles taught like Christ, and men could tell that spirit was on them, just as the elders carried the spirit of Moses.

Two of the men, Eldad and Medad, remained in the camp, and the spirit rested upon them, and they prophesied in the camp. A young man ran and told Moses, and Joshua the son of Nun said, My lord Moses, forbid them. Moses answered, Enviest thou for my sake? would God that all the LORD'S people were prophets. Joshua was carrying a spirit of envy, and Moses corrected it; the Most High wants all His people to be prophets. The same is a lesson today: do not envy the gift on another brother or sister, but glean from it. A brother may be a better teacher, a sister a better labourer; go and learn from them rather than rolling in envy, for the Lord would put His spirit upon them all.

A wind from the Lord brought quails from the sea and let them fall by the camp, a day's journey on this side and on the other, two cubits high upon the face of the earth, and the people gathered them. While the flesh was yet between their teeth, ere it was chewed, the wrath of the Lord was kindled and He smote the people with a very great plague, exactly as He had warned. The place was called Kibrothhattaavah, the graves of lust, because there they buried the people that lusted. The Most High had overfed them because they murmured, but the lesson also stands in nature: excess of meat brings sickness. Animal protein is good for the body, but it is a matter of moderation, not overindulgence.

name: Aaron and Miriam
charge: Speaking against Moses; challenging his authority
summary: Miriam and Aaron spoke against Moses, using his marriage as a pretext to ask whether the Lord had not also spoken through them. God summoned all three and answered plainly.
offense: The occasion is named and it was a pretext: Miriam and Aaron spake against Moses because of the Ethiopian woman whom he had married (Numbers 12:1). That is Zipporah, the daughter of the priest of Midian, whom he had married in the forty years outside Egypt and whom the Lord had allowed him; they had said nothing about her when he was bringing them out of Egypt, nor when he set Aaron over the men and Miriam over the women. What they actually said is the charge: hath the Lord indeed spoken only by Moses? hath he not spoken also by us? And the Lord heard it (Numbers 12:2). It was a claim of equality with the man God had set over them, and Miriam is named first because she led it. The record answers it before the Lord does, with the one line Moses did not write about himself: now the man Moses was very meek, above all the men which were upon the face of the earth (Numbers 12:3).
judgment: The Lord called all three to the tabernacle and came down in the pillar of the cloud, and declared the difference to their faces: to a prophet I make myself known in a vision, and speak in a dream; my servant Moses is not so, who is faithful in all mine house, with him will I speak mouth to mouth, even apparently, and not in dark speeches; wherefore then were ye not afraid to speak against my servant Moses (Numbers 12:6-8). The anger of the Lord was

entries.commentary: Miriam and Aaron spake against Moses because of the Ethiopian woman whom he had married. This is still Zipporah, the daughter of the priest of Midian, whom Moses married in the forty years he dwelt outside Egypt, and whom the Lord allowed him to marry; a place being called Midian and the woman called an Ethiopian is no contradiction. They did not speak against Moses when he was saving them out of Egypt, nor when he set Aaron over the men and Miriam over the women; the murmuring came from somewhere else and they took hold of it. They said, Hath the LORD indeed spoken only by Moses? hath he not spoken also by us? And the LORD heard it.

The man Moses was very meek, above all the men which were upon the face of the earth. The Lord suddenly called Moses, Aaron, and Miriam to the tabernacle, came down in the pillar of the cloud, and called Aaron and Miriam forth. He declared the difference: to a prophet He makes Himself known in a vision and speaks in a dream, but with His servant Moses, faithful in all His house, He speaks mouth to mouth, even apparently, and not in dark speeches. Wherefore then were ye not afraid to speak against my servant Moses?

The anger of the Lord was kindled, and the cloud departed from off the tabernacle, and Miriam became leprous, white as snow. Aaron pleaded, Lay not the sin upon us; and Moses cried unto the Lord, Heal her now, O God, I beseech thee. The Lord answered that if her father had but spit in her face, she should be ashamed seven days; so she was shut out from the camp seven days, and the people journeyed not till Miriam was brought in again. The spit is correction, a father putting his child in her place; had she been raised to respect the men of the Lord, this would not have befallen her. This is a charge to raise children in the fear of the Lord and to teach them to respect the elders and the men of the Lord. Parents who let their children speak evil to the men of the Lord provoke them to wrath and bring judgment on the household.

When a man hath taken a wife and she find no favour in his eyes because he hath found some uncleanness in her, then let him write her a bill of divorcement, give it in her hand, and send her out of his house. Christ magnified this law: when the Pharisees asked why Moses then commanded to give a writing of divorcement, he said, Moses because of the hardness of your hearts suffered you to put away your wives, but from the beginning it was not so. Whosoever shall put away his wife, except it be for fornication, and shall marry another, committeth adultery; and whoso marrieth her which is put away doth commit adultery.

If the latter husband hate her and write her a bill of divorcement, or if the latter husband die, her former husband which sent her away may not take her again to be his wife after that she is defiled, for that is abomination before the Lord. The question is whether a woman who leaves her husband and becomes another man's wife can be joined to the first again; the prophet asks the same thing: shall he return unto her again? shall not that land be greatly polluted?

When a man hath taken a new wife, he shall not go out to war, neither shall he be charged with any business; he shall be free at home one year and shall cheer up his wife which he hath taken. Make it plain: the first year, stay at home and make a baby. Husband and wife render due benevolence to one another; benevolence means good, it is a good thing. The war laws give the same understanding: the man that had betrothed a wife and not taken her was sent back to his house, lest he die in the battle and another man take her, for the Lord is the one that goeth with the host to fight against the enemies.

No man shall take the nether or the upper millstone to pledge, for he taketh a man's life to pledge. The millstone is a tool for grinding meal: the manna was gathered and ground in mills or beaten in a mortar and baked into cakes. Taking a man's tool takes away his living, like somebody stealing your tools so you cannot make a living. It is better that they steal your money, because with your tools you can go back and make more money.

Remember what the Lord thy God did unto Miriam by the way, after that ye were come forth out of Egypt: Miriam and Aaron spake against Moses because of the Ethiopian woman whom he had married, and Miriam was not supposed to be speaking against Moses. The anger of the Lord was kindled against them, the cloud departed from off the tabernacle, and behold, Miriam became leprous, white as snow. The Lord said, if her father had but spit in her face, should she not be ashamed seven days? Had her father chastised her and rebuked her sharply, she would not have had that tongue. That is for a lot of our sisters today who do not have that understanding.

When thou dost lend thy brother any thing, thou shalt not go into his house to fetch his pledge; stand abroad, and let the man bring the pledge out unto thee. If the man be poor, thou shalt not sleep with his pledge; deliver him the pledge again when the sun goeth down, that he may sleep in his own raiment and bless thee, and it shall be righteousness unto thee before the Lord thy God. The law was already given: if thou at all take thy neighbour's raiment to pledge, deliver it by that the sun goeth down, for that is his covering only, and when he crieth unto the Most High, he will hear, for he is gracious. The history shows how wicked we were to each other: Israel laid themselves down upon clothes laid to pledge by every altar, stacking up people's raiment like pallets and drinking the wine of the condemned in the house of their god, instead of returning the pledge before the sun went down as righteousness. That is why the Lord was judging us.

The fathers shall not be put to death for the children, neither shall the children be put to death for the fathers: every man shall be put to death for his own sin. The example: as soon as the kingdom was confirmed in Amaziah's hand, he slew his servants which had slain the king his father, but the children of the murderers he slew not, according unto that which is written in the book of the law of Moses. The soul that sinneth, it shall die: the son shall not bear the iniquity of the father, neither shall the father bear the iniquity of the son.

name: The ten spies
charge: Bringing an evil report; making the congregation to murmur
summary: Twelve men searched Canaan forty days. Ten came back and told the people the land eats its inhabitants and the giants made them as grasshoppers. Caleb and Joshua said the Lord would bring them in. The people believed the ten.
offense: They were sent as rulers of their tribes, and they searched the land forty days (Numbers 13:2, 25), and their report did not deny the land was good, for they carried back one cluster of grapes borne between two upon a staff and said, surely it floweth with milk and honey (Numbers 13:23, 27). What they denied was that God could give it, and they said it in the presence of the whole congregation: we be not able to go up against the people, for they are stronger than we (Numbers 13:31). Then they brought up an evil report of the land, calling it a land that eateth up the inhabitants thereof, and there we saw the giants, the sons of Anak, and we were in our own sight as grasshoppers, and so we were in their sight (Numbers 13:32-33). Ten rulers who had watched Egypt destroyed and the sea part measured themselves against men, and the evil report spread its spirit through the whole camp in a night. Caleb had already answered them in front of the people: let us go up at once, and possess it; for we are well able to overcome it (Numbers 13:30).
judgment: Because of the report the whole congregation wept that night, said one to another, let us make a captain, and let us return into Egypt (Numbers 14:4), and bade stone Caleb and Joshua with stones, and the glory of the Lord appeared in the tabernacle before all the children of Israel (Numbers 14:10). The men that brought up the evil report died by the plague before the Lord (Numbers 14:37), the ten of them, while Joshua and Caleb, of the men that went to search the land, lived still (Numbers 14:38). The nation's sentence is entered separately, but it is measured from this act: after the number of the days in which ye searched the land, even forty days, each day for a year, shall ye bear your iniquities (Numbers 14:34). Forty-five years later Caleb, at eighty-five, asked for the mountain the ten had feared and took it (Joshua 14:10-12), and Mattathias on his deathbed put the two together as the pattern for his sons: Caleb for bearing witness before the congregation received the heritage of the land, and Joshua for fulfilling the word was made a judge in Israel (1 Maccabees 2:55-56).

entries.commentary: The Lord told Moses to send men to search the land of Canaan, one ruler of every tribe of their fathers. Among them were Caleb the son of Jephunneh of the tribe of Judah, and Oshea the son of Nun, whom Moses called Jehoshua, that is Joshua. Sending out spies to learn the landscape, the people, and their strength is the wisdom of war; Moses had learned such things as a leader in Egypt.

Moses sent them up to see the land, whether the people were strong or weak, few or many, the cities open or walled, the land fat or lean; and they searched it forty days. They came to the brook of Eshcol and cut down a branch with one cluster of grapes, and bare it between two upon a staff. The cluster was so great it took two men to carry it, for the earth was younger then and brought forth greater stature in its fruit and its men.

They returned and reported the land floweth with milk and honey, and showed the fruit; nevertheless the people be strong, the cities walled and very great, and the children of Anak were there. Caleb stilled the people and said, Let us go up at once, and possess it; for we are well able to overcome it. But the men that went up with him said, We be not able to go up against the people; for they are stronger than we; and they brought up an evil report, calling it a land that eateth up the inhabitants, where they saw the giants, the sons of Anak, and were in their own sight as grasshoppers. The Lord had willed them to go up, but these men were so out of the spirit that they forgot He had already destroyed mightier nations before them. An evil report spreads a spirit of fear, but the Most High has not given His people the spirit of fear.

All the congregation lifted up their voice and cried, and the people wept that night, and murmured against Moses and Aaron, saying, Would God that we had died in the land of Egypt, or in this wilderness. Because of the evil report, they said, Wherefore hath the LORD brought us unto this land, to fall by the sword? and they said one to another, Let us make a captain, and let us return into Egypt, forgetting there was nothing to return to, for Pharaoh and his army were destroyed and Egypt laid waste.

Moses and Aaron fell on their faces before all the assembly, and Joshua and Caleb rent their clothes and exhorted the people: the land is an exceeding good land; if the Lord delight in us, He will bring us into it; only rebel not against the Lord, neither fear the people of the land, for they are bread for us, and the Lord is with us. But all the congregation bade stone them with stones, and the glory of the Lord appeared in the tabernacle. It is the same today: when the truth is brought that the Most High loves the people and has something great for them if they repent, they do not believe it and are ready to kill the messenger, hating him that rebuketh in the gate.

The Lord said, How long will this people provoke me? and how long will it be ere they believe me, for all the signs which I have shewed among them? He would smite them with pestilence, disinherit them, and make of Moses a greater nation. Moses interceded: the Egyptians and the nations would hear that the Lord was not able to bring the people into the land and slew them in the wilderness. He pleaded, Let the power of my Lord be great, the Lord is longsuffering and of great mercy, forgiving iniquity; pardon this people according to the greatness of thy mercy, as thou hast forgiven them from Egypt until now. This is a true leader interceding for the people rather than seeing them destroyed.

The Lord said, I have pardoned according to thy word; but as truly as I live, all the earth shall be filled with the glory of the Lord. The men who had seen His glory and His miracles in Egypt and in the wilderness, and had tempted Him now these ten times, would not see the land which He sware unto their fathers. But His servant Caleb, because he had another spirit with him and followed the Lord fully, would be brought into the land, and his seed should possess it.

The Lord asked how long He should bear with this evil congregation which murmured against Him, and declared, As ye have spoken in mine ears, so will I do to you: your carcasses shall fall in this wilderness, all that were numbered from twenty years old and upward that murmured against Him, save Caleb and Joshua. The little ones they said would be a prey, those He would bring into the land; but the children would wander in the wilderness forty years, a year for each of the forty days the land was searched, and bear the whoredoms of their fathers until their carcasses were wasted. The very men that brought up the evil report died by the plague before the Lord, but Joshua and Caleb lived still.

When Moses told the people these sayings, they mourned greatly, then rose up early and presumed to go up to the top of the mountain, saying, We have sinned; we will go up unto the place which the Lord hath promised. Moses said, Wherefore now do ye transgress the commandment of the LORD? it shall not prosper; go not up, for the LORD is not among you, that ye be not smitten before your enemies. But they presumed to go up, though the ark of the covenant and Moses departed not out of the camp, and the Amalekites and the Canaanites came down and smote them and discomfited them, even unto Hormah. All they had to do was follow counsel. Their refusal was written for us, that we would learn to follow the counsel of the men the Most High sets up rather than lean on our own presumption. --- Topics: [The Covenant](/encyclopedia/the-covenant) · [The Priesthood](/encyclopedia/the-priesthood)

These be the words which Moses spake unto all Israel on this side Jordan in the wilderness: the audience of the entire book of Deuteronomy is the Israelites. Moses spake in the fortieth year, in the eleventh month, on the first day of the month, according unto all that the Lord had given him in commandment unto them.

Moses declares this law after he had slain Sihon the king of the Amorites. When the Lord told Abraham his seed would serve four hundred years, he set the time of the return by the Amorites: the iniquity of the Amorites is not yet full. By this point their iniquity was fulfilled, like Babylon whose sins reached unto heaven, so the Lord loosed Israel to come through the land of the Amorites and slay Sihon their king.

Ye have dwelt long enough in this mount: the Lord set the land before them, from the mount of the Amorites to Lebanon and the great river Euphrates, to go in and possess it. The land was sworn unto Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob and to their seed after them; the Most High reiterated that covenant to the fathers over and over through Genesis, reassuring them that their seed would possess the land of Canaan. Israel entered not for their own righteousness but for the sake of the promise made to the fathers; the rebellious generation was cut off, yet their children were still brought in because the Most High sware it.

I am not able to bear you myself alone: the people were multiplied as the stars of heaven, and every one of them came with cumbrance, burden, and strife. Moses refers back to what his father in law saw in Exodus 18: Moses sat judging the people alone from morning until evening, the people waiting all day in line, because they came to him to inquire of God and be shown the statutes and laws. His father in law told him the thing was not good: judging alone would wear away both Moses and the people. The counsel was to provide able men that fear God and set them in ranks over thousands, hundreds, fifties, and tens.

The people answered that the thing was good to do, and Moses took the chief of the tribes, wise men and known, and made them captains over thousands, hundreds, fifties, and tens, and officers among the tribes. Rank in a congregation is biblical. With schools worldwide, every issue cannot come to one man; soldiers, officers, captains, deacons, and bishop follow the same order the fathers ordained here, and the terminology of this verse is the terminology used in the body today.

The charge to the judges: hear the causes between brethren and judge righteously between every man and his brother and the stranger with him, and hear the small as well as the great. Ye shall not respect persons in judgment: a poor man gets no pass for being poor, and a mighty man with money and possessions is not above the laws of the Most High; no one can buy himself out of judgment. Ye shall not be afraid of the face of man, for the judgment is God's: no tough face may intimidate or sway a verdict, because it is the Most High passing the judgment through the judge. The cause too hard goes up the chain to Moses, and that chain itself was instituted here.

Israel came through that great and terrible wilderness to Kadesh-barnea, to the mountain of the Amorites, and the commandment was plain: the Lord hath set the land before thee; go up and possess it; fear not, neither be discouraged. The people asked to send men first to search out the land and bring word of the way and the cities, and the saying pleased Moses; twelve men, one of a tribe, went up to the valley of Eshcol. The spies brought of the fruit of the land in their hands and brought word again: it is a good land which the Lord our God doth give us.

Notwithstanding ye would not go up, but rebelled against the commandment of the Lord: they acknowledged the land was good, yet all refused except Caleb and Joshua, who had faith to go take it. They murmured in their tents that the Lord hated them and brought them out of Egypt to deliver them into the hand of the Amorites to destroy them. The spies had discouraged their hearts with the report: the people greater and taller than we, cities great and walled up to heaven, and the sons of the Anakims, the giants, in the land.

Dread not, neither be afraid of them: the Lord your God which goeth before you, he shall fight for you, according to all that he did in Egypt before your eyes. The Amorites were no mightier than Egypt, and these same Israelites witnessed how the Lord broke Egypt to bring them out; where was their faith? The principle still applies: the body still has adversaries that rise against it, and the command remains to be in nothing terrified by them. Fear of the adversary is a spirit the Most High never gave his people; whoever is terrified of the enemy is out of the Spirit.

The Lord bare Israel in the wilderness as a man doth bear his son, went before them in fire by night and in a cloud by day to search out a place to pitch their tents; yet in this thing ye did not believe the Lord your God. That is the amazing part of this history: they saw all the miracles and were carried like a son, and still believed the Lord was setting them up to be killed by giants, when a giant has nothing on the Most High. The fathers in the wilderness had the gospel preached to them as we have: deliverance from captivity into the promised kingdom. But the word did not profit them, not being mixed with faith; they had the laws without the faith, and it is impossible to have one without the other.

The Lord heard their words and was wroth and sware: not one of the men of that evil generation would see the good land, save Caleb the son of Jephunneh, because he wholly followed the Lord, and Joshua the son of Nun, who would cause Israel to inherit it. Also the Lord was angry with me for your sakes: at the waters the people fell into the same disbelief they had shown over and over, and Moses in his anger called them rebels and smote the rock twice when the Lord had said to speak to the rock. Anger lets the commandments slip: be angry and sin not, but when anger takes hold, a man fails to apply what he knows, and Moses failed to sanctify the Most High in the eyes of the children of Israel. His judgment was to be kept out of the land. Moses is still good; he stood with Elias before Christ on the mount. He missed the promised land at that time, not the kingdom. But leadership carries the greater condemnation: the more given unto you, the more stripes when you fail.

The little ones, the children which in that day had no knowledge between good and evil, would go in and possess the land the Most High sware to the fathers. As for that generation, the command was to turn and take their journey into the wilderness by the way of the Red sea.

Then ye answered, We have sinned: only after the judgment fell did they want to repent, girding on weapons of war and declaring themselves ready to go up. The Lord had given chance after chance to obey and not fear, and every time the same trial brought the same unbelief; do nothing without advice, and when thou hast once done, repent not. The Lord said go not up, neither fight, for I am not among you, lest ye be smitten before your enemies; and they went up presumptuously anyway, boldly doing what they were told not to do, as recorded in [Numbers 14](/bible/numbers/14). The Amorites came out against them and chased them as bees do, and destroyed them in Seir unto Hormah. They returned and wept before the Lord, but the Lord would not hearken to their voice nor give ear. When counsel is set at nought until the judgment lands, the weeping comes too late; they that hated knowledge and did not choose the fear of the Lord seek him early and do not find him. So they abode in Kadesh many days.

The countries in the land of Canaan were distributed by Eleazar the priest, Joshua the son of Nun, and the heads of the fathers of the tribes, by lot, as the Most High commanded by the hand of Moses, for the nine tribes and the half tribe; Moses had already given the two tribes and a half their inheritance on the other side Jordan. The children of Joseph were two tribes, Manasseh and Ephraim, therefore no part was given unto the Levites in the land, save cities to dwell in with their suburbs for their cattle and for their substance. The Levites were living in the suburbs, which is the towns, right among the people. They did not have a land designated to themselves; they were spread throughout all the many tribes.

Caleb the son of Jephunneh the Kenezite comes to Joshua in Gilgal and reminds him of the thing the Most High said unto Moses concerning them both in Kadeshbarnea: Caleb was forty years old when Moses sent him from Kadeshbarnea to spy out the land, and he brought word again as it was in his heart. His brethren that went up with him made the heart of the people melt, but he wholly followed the Lord his God. The men that went with him brought up an evil report, made the people afraid, and made them doubt. Caleb was not playing any games; he was about that business, ready to go and take the land, because he understood the Most High had already promised us the land, so he had no fear. That is the spirit that says, let us go up at once and possess it. So Moses sware on that day that the land whereon Caleb's feet had trodden would be his inheritance and his children's for ever, because he wholly followed the Lord.

The Most High has kept Caleb alive these forty and five years, and now at fourscore and five years old he is as strong this day as he was in the day Moses sent him; as his strength was then, even so is his strength now, for war, both to go out and to come in. This man is eighty-five years old and in perfect health. Moses was the same way: a hundred and twenty years old with the strength and the vision of a young man. A lot of us are not living to a hundred and twenty, but at the same time we are making it to sixty and seventy, and at fifty we are hooked up on machines. We are all going to die at some point, but that does not mean you have to be miserable, sitting there hooked up to all kind of machines while you are here. name: Caleb and Joshua
charge: Wholly following the Lord when ten spies and the whole congregation would not
summary: Twelve men saw the same land, the same cities and the same giants. Ten said, We be not able. Two said, The Lord is with us: fear them not. The ten died of the plague; the whole generation died in the wilderness; and Caleb and Joshua were the only two of six hundred thousand who walked into the land.
offense: Twelve men walked the same ground, saw the same walled cities and the same giants (Numbers 13:28), and came back with the same facts (Numbers 13:26). The difference was not information. Ten reported that the people were stronger (Numbers 13:31); two reported that the Lord was with them, and their fear is departed from them (Numbers 14:9). Caleb and Joshua rent their clothes (Numbers 14:6) and stood before a congregation that was reaching for stones (Joshua 14:6-14). The formula the Lord uses of Caleb is the exact standard of the case: he hath followed me fully, and again, he wholly followed the Lord God of Israel (Joshua 14:14). The obedience was not silence under pressure but public contradiction of a settled majority.
judgment: Of six hundred thousand men numbered from twenty years old and upward (Numbers 14:29), these two entered the land. Every other man of that generation died in the wilderness (Numbers 14:2), and the sentence was measured to the offense at a year for a day. Caleb at eighty-five asked for the mountain with the giants on it rather than an easier portion, and got it, and Hebron became his inheritance because he wholly followed the Lord (Joshua 14:14). Joshua succeeded Moses and divided the land he had been the first to say could be taken (Joshua 14:6-14).

6And Joshua the son of Nun, and Caleb the son of Jephunneh, which were of them that searched the land, rent their clothes: 7And they spake unto all the company of the children of Israel, saying, The land, which we passed through to search it, is an exceeding good land. 8If the Lord delight in us, then he will bring us into this land, and give it us; a land which floweth with milk and honey. 9Only rebel not ye against the Lord, neither fear ye the people of the land; for they are bread for us: their defence is departed from them, and the Lord is with us: fear them not. 10But all the congregation bade stone them with stones.
