name: Israel at Baal-peor
charge: Fornication with the daughters of Moab; sacrificing to their gods
summary: In Shittim the people began to commit whoredom with the daughters of Moab, who called them to the sacrifices of their gods. Israel ate, bowed down, and joined himself unto Baal-peor. The plague took twenty-four thousand.
offense: It was Balaam's counsel executed. He could not curse a people God had blessed, so he taught Balak the one thing that works: put another god in front of Israel and send the women to bring them to it (Numbers 31:16; Revelation 2:14). Israel abode in Shittim, and the people began to commit whoredom with the daughters of Moab (Numbers 25:1), and they called the people unto the sacrifices of their gods, and the people did eat, and bowed down to their gods (Numbers 25:2). The whoredom and the worship were not two sins but one; the rite of Baal-peor was whoredom, and Israel joined himself unto Baal-peor (Numbers 25:3), joined as a man is joined to a wife. Hosea gives the verdict on the whole affair: they went to Baal-peor, and separated themselves unto that shame, and their abominations were according as they loved (Hosea 9:10), and the psalm adds what they ate: they joined themselves also unto Baal-peor, and ate the sacrifices of the dead (Psalms 106:28). It was the golden calf again, for the people sat down to eat and drink, and rose up to play, and that play was the same play (1 Corinthians 10:7-8).
judgment: The Lord's sentence began with the leadership: take all the heads of the people, and hang them up before the Lord against the sun, that the fierce anger of the Lord may be turned away from Israel (Numbers 25:4), and Moses said unto the judges of Israel, slay ye every one his men that were joined unto Baal-peor (Numbers 25:5), every judge by his rank  taking the men under him. A plague ran through the camp while the sentence was being carried out, and it was stayed by the javelin of Phinehas, which is entered separately as a blessing, and those that died in the plague were twenty and four thousand (Numbers 25:9). Paul, counting the day itself, says three and twenty thousand fell in one day (1 Corinthians 10:8). Moses set the outcome before the next generation as a thing their own eyes had seen: all the men that followed Baal-peor, the Lord thy God hath destroyed them from among you, but ye that did cleave unto the Lord your God are alive every one of you this day (Deuteronomy 4:3-4). Then the judgment turned outward against the nation that had supplied the women, which is entered under the Midianites.

verses.text: 1And Israel abode in Shittim, and the people began to commit whoredom with the daughters of Moab. 2And they called the people unto the sacrifices of their gods: and the people did eat, and bowed down to their gods. 3And Israel joined himself unto Baal–peor: and the anger of the Lord was kindled against Israel. 4And the Lord said unto Moses, Take all the heads of the people, and hang them up before the Lord against the sun, that the fierce anger of the Lord may be turned away from Israel. 5And Moses said unto the judges of Israel, Slay ye every one his men that were joined unto Baal–peor.
9And those that died in the plague were twenty and four thousand.
16Behold, these caused the children of Israel, through the counsel of Balaam, to commit trespass against the Lord in the matter of Peor, and there was a plague among the congregation of the Lord.

lawDetails.text: Anyone that has served or worshipped false or pagan gods shall be put to death.

entries.commentary: Israel abode in Shittim, and the people began to commit whoredom with the daughters of Moab. Why? Balaam could not curse us, because God said you cannot curse what is blessed; so his counsel was the best the enemy can ever do: throw another god in front of Israel and send the women, and let Israel bring the trespass on himself. That counsel is why the Lord put Balaam to death. They called the people unto the sacrifices of their gods, and the people did eat and bowed down; Israel joined himself unto Baal-peor, and the anger of the Lord was kindled. The worship of Baal-peor went into whoredom, that orgy worship: we started worshipping another god and messing with the women together.

The Lord said, take all the heads of the people and hang them up before the Lord against the sun, that His fierce anger be turned away; and Moses said unto the judges, slay ye every one his man that were joined unto Baal-peor. Every one his man means every judge by his rank: the officer over ten took ten, the officer over fifty took fifty, and so on. With the Most High it is two options only, life and death. Under the old covenant there was no winking at ignorance; judgment was instant. The only reason we are not judged that way now for the gods we served is the grace and mercy given through Christ: the times of this ignorance God winked at, the Christianity with the white Jesus, the Islam, the Buddhism, the Hinduism, the Egyptology, the atheism; but now He commandeth all men every where to repent, because He hath appointed a day in which He will judge the world in righteousness by that man whom He hath ordained, Jesus the Christ. Do not take that mercy lightly, and do not frustrate the grace of God until He is finished with you. He can cut a man's days down whenever He wants; do not press Him to it.

While the whole congregation wept before the door of the tabernacle, one of the children of Israel brought a Midianitish woman unto his brethren in the sight of Moses and all the congregation: a man that did not care about his people while everyone around him mourned. When Phinehas the son of Eleazar, the son of Aaron the priest, saw it, he rose up from among the congregation, took a javelin in his hand, went after the man of Israel into the tent, and thrust both of them through; so the plague was stayed from the children of Israel, and those that died in the plague were twenty and four thousand. Let us now praise famous men: Phinehas stands third in glory, because he had zeal in the fear of the Lord and stood up with good courage of heart when the people were turned back, and made reconciliation for Israel; therefore a covenant of peace was made with him, that he and his posterity should have the dignity of the priesthood for ever. These things were our examples, that we should not lust after evil things as they lusted. The people sat down to eat and drink and rose up to play, and that play means sex; that was the golden calf. Neither commit fornication as they did, when three and twenty thousand fell in one day; neither tempt Christ, for it was Christ with us in the wilderness. These things are written for our admonition, that we be warned: idolatry leads to whoredom, spiritual whoredom against the Most High and physical whoredom with it.

Phinehas turned the wrath of the Most High away from the children of Israel, because he was zealous for his God's sake among them; wherefore the Lord gave him His covenant of peace, and to his seed after him the covenant of an everlasting priesthood, because he made an atonement for the children of Israel. That covenant of peace is what all of us are striving for, rest from this servitude of bondage; but the wisdom in reading the acts of Phinehas is that you must be zealous for the law of the Most High to obtain it. Be ye zealous for the law, and give your lives for the covenant of your fathers; Phinehas our father, in being zealous and fervent, obtained the covenant of an everlasting priesthood. Being zealous today is confessing Christ before men, and you confess him mainly through your actions. Christ suffered for us, leaving us an example that we should follow his steps, and his steps were keeping the commandments of God; the first way you deny Christ is by rejecting the commandments. Christ came not to send peace on earth but a sword, setting a man at variance against his own household; he that loveth father or mother more than him is not worthy of him. We stay zealous by letting nothing separate us from following Christ in his steps: keeping the laws of God, teaching the gospel, and spreading the word with wisdom.

The man of Israel that was slain was Zimri the son of Salu, a prince of a chief house among the Simeonites; the woman was Cozbi the daughter of Zur, head over a people of a chief house in Midian. The charge stands to Simeon to get it together; Simeon is coming back with the rest of the tribes. The Lord said unto Moses, vex the Midianites and smite them, for they vex you with their wiles, wherewith they have beguiled you in the matter of Peor and in the matter of Cozbi.

The Most High told Israel to avenge the children of Israel of the Midianites. The reason for this vengeance is the history of [Numbers 25](/bible/numbers/25); go back and read that chapter to see what Midian did.

A thousand of every tribe, twelve thousand armed for war, were sent with Phinehas the son of Eleazar the priest, with the holy instruments and the trumpets to blow. Phinehas is the one who killed the man of Israel that was fornicating with the woman of the other nation, in the history of [Numbers 25](/bible/numbers/25).

They warred against the Midianites as the Lord commanded Moses, slew all the males, and slew the five kings of Midian: Evi, Rekem, Zur, Hur, and Reba. Balaam also the son of Beor they slew with the sword. Balaam was a soothsayer, a diviner; he was a witch, so to speak.

Israel took the women of Midian captives with their little ones, took the spoil of all their cattle, flocks, and goods, and burnt all their cities and all their goodly castles with fire. Midian comes from the lineage of Ishmael, the people known today as the Arab man. This shows Esau was not the one who first came up with castles; the castles seen in the movies were conquered from other nations. They took all the spoil and all the prey, both of men and of beasts: the Midianites had captives of their own, and Israel took over both the men and the beasts when they overcame them.

Moses was wroth with the officers of the host, the leaders of the army of Israel, because they saved all the women alive. These women caused the children of Israel, through the counsel of Balaam, to commit trespass against the Lord in the matter of Peor. Balaam took it upon himself to send the women of the other nations to Israel, and it caused the people to go into fornication, and the Lord began putting them to death, over twenty and four thousand, in the history of [Numbers 25](/bible/numbers/25). Therefore every male among the little ones was to be killed, and every woman that had known man by lying with him; but the women children that had not known a man they kept alive for themselves. Moses allowed the men to keep those women so they would not commit sin and go raping the women, being out at war. That does not mean it is done today; it was a time that the Most High allowed it so the men would not be in the midst of sin.

Whoever killed any person or touched any slain had to abide without the camp seven days and purify himself and his captives on the third day and on the seventh day. That is the law going back to [Numbers 5:2](/bible/numbers/5#v2), putting the defiled outside the camp. Purifying the raiment, all that is made of skins, all work of goats' hair, and all things made of wood goes back to the law of purification in [Numbers 19](/bible/numbers/19). Eleazar the priest gave the ordinance: gold, silver, brass, iron, tin, and lead, everything that may abide the fire, goes through the fire and is purified with the water of separation; whatever abides not the fire goes through the water; and on the seventh day they wash their clothes, are clean, and come into the camp.

Moses, Eleazar the priest, and the chief fathers of the congregation took the sum of the prey, both of man and of beast, adding up all that was taken from the Midianites. The prey was divided into two parts: between the army who went out to battle and took the prey, and all the congregation that did not go to war. The nation looked out for each other. A tribute was levied unto the Lord: of the men of war, one soul of five hundred, of persons, beeves, asses, and sheep, given to Eleazar the priest for a heave offering, because he was the priest; and of the children of Israel's half, one portion of fifty, given to the Levites which kept the charge of the tabernacle.

Moses gave the tribute, the Lord's heave offering, unto Eleazar the priest, as the Lord commanded Moses. The heave offerings belong to the priesthood by statute forever, a covenant of salt, because Aaron and Levi have no inheritance in the land; the Most High is their part and their inheritance.

Hearken, O Israel: hearken means listen, pay attention, and there is a difference between hearing and listening. The statutes and judgments are taught for to do them; knowing you are an Israelite is only half the battle. The main thing is applying the scriptures, doing what the Most High is telling you to do, that ye may live. The promise is to go in and possess the land, and possessing land is true wealth: your milk and honey, your cattle, your agriculture, where you cultivate and take care of your family. It is not the diamonds, the cars, the sneakers, or the newest phone; a big house with no land is not wealth, and that is why the heathen boxes our people into apartments.

Ye shall not add unto the word, neither diminish ought from it. This was spoken around 1500 BC, and on the last page of the Bible the same charge closes the book: the prophets across millenniums and captivities all speak the same thing, Moses, Isaiah, Jeremiah, Christ, and John, and that consistency proves the Bible is a true book, because twenty people cannot keep one story straight for five minutes. The watered down versions such as the NIV and ESV show what taking away looks like: many of them remove [Matthew 18:11](/bible/matthew/18#v11) and other scriptures, and they have taken out the Apocrypha.

Your eyes have seen what the Lord did because of Baal-peor: all the men that followed Baal-peor were destroyed from among the people, and this recalls the history of Balaam. Balaam was a Midianite, an Ishmaelite. But ye that did cleave unto the Lord your God are alive every one of you this day: those who said they would not go after that foolishness were saved alive. The Bible is that simple, and it destroys the confusion of the world's religions: keep the commandments and live, or break them and die. Follow after the ways of the nations and be put to death; keep the laws, statutes, and commandments and have life.

Keep therefore and do them, for this is your wisdom and your understanding in the sight of the nations. Israel deals with the Almighty; having the omnipotent God on your side is the wisdom the nations do not have, and it is what they are mad at. When Israel keeps the laws it makes them a peculiar nation: peculiar by definition means characteristic of only one person, group, or thing, and different from the usual or normal. The Most High made this people different and set them above the other nations. Royal means of a kingly ancestry, and the King of kings is Christ; but rulership belongs to the lineage only when the laws are kept. When Israel is fallen into sin, the people look worse than the nations instead of wise and understanding. Which shall hear all these statutes and say, surely this great nation is a wise and understanding people: they may not say it out loud today, but when they see Israel united in Christ and in order, that is what rises in their minds.

What nation is there so great, who hath God so nigh unto them? The Most High is near unto Israel in all things they call upon him for, and no nation has statutes and judgments so righteous as this law. When Israel keeps the laws, statutes, and commandments, they are the light of the world; in the days when the brothers and sisters were in order, the nations looked on and marveled at what nation this was, so great and so beautiful.

Take heed to thyself and keep thy soul diligently, lest thou forget the things thine eyes have seen; and teach them thy sons, and thy sons' sons. These are generational commandments: children's children, cousins' cousins, so that no generation misses a beat. Gather me the people together, and I will make them hear my words, that they may learn to fear me all the days that they shall live upon the earth, and that they may teach their children. Why learn to fear the Most High? Verses 3 and 4 of this same chapter answer it: those that followed the idols were destroyed, and those that cleaved to him are alive. Follow after idols, after the nations and their religions, and he will destroy you. Fear is the first spirit required, before love, before confession: fear and respect go hand in hand, and if you fear him you will do what he says, and do it with joyfulness and gladness for the reward no nation can touch.

The mountain burned with fire unto the midst of heaven, and the Most High spake out of the midst of the fire; ye heard the voice of the words, but saw no similitude. He declared his covenant, even ten commandments: the ten are the umbrella over all the other commandments, the sub-laws and sub-statutes beneath them. And he wrote them upon two tables of stone. The laws men call the mosaic laws did not belong to Moses; they were written with the finger of God and given to Israel by Christ, and they endure for ever.

The Most High commanded Moses at that time to teach the statutes and judgments, and Israel is charged to take good heed, for ye saw no manner of similitude on the day the Lord spake in Horeb. No similitude means he spoke plainly and clearly, not in dark speeches: when the commandments were given there was no arguing over what they meant. Fringes on the borders of the garments, no swine, thou shalt not kill; it was simple and easy to understand. Lest ye corrupt yourselves and make a graven image, the similitude of any figure, the likeness of male or female: Israel had come out of Egypt, where graven images filled the land and where the likeness of the female was worshipped. Egypt is where feminism was already incorporated: Hathor the cattle goddess and Qetesh the goddess of beauty were among the idols learned there, so the Most High had to say plainly, no deity male or female. There is no goddess in the scriptures.

The likeness of any beast on the earth goes back to idols like Heqet the frog god and Sobek the god of the river; the likeness of any winged fowl to Horus the falcon; anything that creepeth on the ground to the beetles, flies, and locusts they deified; any fish in the waters to Sobek and to Dagon the fish god of the Babylonians, whose symbolism carries into pagan imagery to this day. The eagle and the falcon symbols of the powers of this world trace back to the gods and goddesses of Egypt, because this present power is spiritual Egypt and takes after her. Lest thou lift up thine eyes unto heaven and be driven to worship the sun, the moon, and the stars: that is Ra the sun god and Nut the sky goddess, and it is also astrology, the zodiac, and witchcraft today. Calling yourself a Gemini or a Taurus is the same star worship; none of it is the way to the kingdom, and it was filth learned in Egypt. Why worship what the Most High created to serve you? The sun, moon, and stars are ordinances that keep their order and do their job, which is why the new moon can be kept; Israel is the one out of order when the commandments are not kept.

The Lord hath taken you and brought you forth out of the iron furnace, even out of Egypt, to be unto him a people of inheritance. Furthermore the Lord was angry with me for your sakes: again Moses lays his barred crossing on the people. It is how the workers feel when they go out to preach truth and catch anger for it; you are not arguing with the messenger, you are mad at the Bible, so speak the oracles and neither add nor diminish to please anybody. Moses must die in this land and not go over Jordan, but ye shall go over and possess that good land; he kept repeating it, longing for what he would not see.

Take heed unto yourselves, lest ye forget the covenant and make a graven image, for the Lord thy God is a consuming fire, even a jealous God. When children's children are begotten and the stay in the land grows long, corruption creeps in; make the graven image and do evil to provoke him, and ye shall soon utterly perish from off the land. Heaven and earth are called to witness against Israel this day; the warning was on record before it ever came to pass.

And the Lord shall scatter you among the nations, and ye shall be left few in number among the heathen: this is future prophecy of the scattering to the four corners of the earth. And there ye shall serve gods, the work of men's hands, wood and stone: the wood is the cross of christianity and the stone is the kaaba stone at Mecca. Israel would fall into the heathen religions, christianity and islam, in the lands of the scattering.

But if from thence thou shalt seek the Lord thy God, thou shalt find him, if thou seek him with all thy heart and with all thy soul; the seeking begins with the spirit of fear, to get right with the Most High. When thou art in tribulation, and all these things are come upon thee, even in the latter days: the latter days began when Christ came, for God who spake in time past by the prophets hath in these last days spoken by his Son. And shalt be obedient unto his voice: the voice of the Most High tells you to keep his commandments. If someone claims God spoke to him in a dream and told him everything but obedience, that is not the voice of the Most High. For the Lord thy God is a merciful God; he will not forsake thee, nor destroy thee, nor forget the covenant of thy fathers.

Ask now of the days that are past, since the day that God created man upon the earth: you are supposed to search out your forefathers and look up your history, and not slavery only, but the reign under David and Solomon and the empires where Israel ruled, and slavery too, because failing to keep the laws is why the people went into it. Did ever people hear the voice of God speaking out of the midst of the fire and live? Hath God assayed to take him a nation from the midst of another nation, by temptations, by signs, and by wonders, and by war, and by a mighty hand? There is no such history anywhere else; the Most High did this for Israel alone. Unto thee it was shewed, that thou mightest know that the Lord he is God; there is none else beside him.

Out of heaven he made thee to hear his voice, that he might instruct thee; and because he loved thy fathers, therefore he chose their seed after them, and brought thee out of Egypt in his sight with his mighty power. To drive out nations from before thee greater and mightier than thou art: they had more economic might and more military power, but the Most High delivered Israel out of their hands, and to this day the twelve tribes are still here. Know therefore this day, and consider it in thine heart, that the Lord he is God in heaven above and upon the earth beneath; there is none else. Consider is the key word: really appreciate all of it, for Israel could have been born of any nation, but the Most High ordained this people, and the way to cash in is simply keeping the commandments.

Thou shalt keep therefore his statutes and his commandments, that it may go well with thee and with thy children after thee, and that thou mayest prolong thy days upon the earth. This is the solution. The voting, protesting, and marching have never worked and never will; trust in the Most High and keep his laws, and he will take care of his people with long days, families, and the land.

Then Moses severed three cities on this side Jordan toward the sunrising, that the slayer which killed his neighbour unawares, and hated him not in times past, might flee thither and live: Bezer in the wilderness for the Reubenites, Ramoth in Gilead for the Gadites, and Golan in Bashan for the Manassites. The chapter closes with the summary: this is the law, the testimonies, the statutes, and the judgments which Moses spake unto the children of Israel after they came forth out of Egypt, in the land of Sihon and of Og, the two kings of the Amorites.

Give thanks unto the Most High, for He is good and His mercy endures forever; who can show forth all His praise. Blessed are they that keep judgment and do righteousness at all times. At all times, not only when convenient. David asks to be remembered with the favor toward His people, to see the good of His chosen and rejoice in the gladness of His nation.

We have sinned with our fathers and done wickedly; our fathers understood not His wonders in Egypt and provoked Him at the Red Sea. Nevertheless He saved them for His name's sake, rebuked the Red Sea so it dried up, and led them through the depths as through the wilderness. Esau's science says a wind blew it into a tsunami, but the Most High said He rebuked it. The waters covered their enemies, and then they believed His words and sang His praise.

They soon forgot His works and waited not for His counsel, but lusted exceedingly in the wilderness and tempted God, so He sent leanness into their soul. They envied Moses and Aaron the saint of the Lord; the earth swallowed Dathan and the company of Abiram for their insurrection. They made a calf and worshipped the molten image, changing their glory into the likeness of an ox that eats grass, forgetting God their savior. He would have destroyed them had not Moses stood in the breach. -

They despised the pleasant land and believed not His word but brought up a false report and murmured in their tents; therefore He lifted His hand to overthrow them and scatter their seed among the nations. They joined themselves to Baal-peor and ate the sacrifices of the dead, provoking Him to anger, and the plague broke in upon them. Then Phinehas stood up and executed judgment, and the plague was stayed; it was counted to him for righteousness unto all generations, for he had zeal in the fear of the Most High. -

name: The Midianites, in the matter of Peor
charge: Beguiling Israel with their wiles into fornication and the worship of Baal-peor
summary: Balaam could not curse Israel, so he taught Balak how to make Israel curse itself. The daughters of Midian and Moab drew the people to Peor, and twenty-four thousand died in the plague. The Lord then told Moses to avenge Israel of the Midianites before he was gathered to his people.
offense: On Balaam's counsel the women of Midian invited the people to the sacrifices of their gods (Numbers 25:2); the people ate, and bowed down, and joined themselves to Baal-peor (Numbers 25:3). Cozbi, the daughter of a prince of Midian, was brought into the camp itself (Numbers 31:12). They vexed Israel with their wiles, wherewith they beguiled you in the matter of Peor (Numbers 25:18).
judgment: Vex the Midianites, and smite them. Israel warred against Midian as the Lord commanded Moses and slew all the males (Numbers 31:7), the five kings of Midian, and Balaam the son of Beor with the sword (Numbers 31:8). Moses was angry that the women who had caused the trespass were kept alive (Numbers 31:15), and the sentence was carried through on them also.

entries.commentary: Israel abode in Shittim, and the people began to commit whoredom with the daughters of Moab. Why? Balaam could not curse us, because God said you cannot curse what is blessed; so his counsel was the best the enemy can ever do: throw another god in front of Israel and send the women, and let Israel bring the trespass on himself. That counsel is why the Lord put Balaam to death. They called the people unto the sacrifices of their gods, and the people did eat and bowed down; Israel joined himself unto Baal-peor, and the anger of the Lord was kindled. The worship of Baal-peor went into whoredom, that orgy worship: we started worshipping another god and messing with the women together.

The Lord said, take all the heads of the people and hang them up before the Lord against the sun, that His fierce anger be turned away; and Moses said unto the judges, slay ye every one his man that were joined unto Baal-peor. Every one his man means every judge by his rank: the officer over ten took ten, the officer over fifty took fifty, and so on. With the Most High it is two options only, life and death. Under the old covenant there was no winking at ignorance; judgment was instant. The only reason we are not judged that way now for the gods we served is the grace and mercy given through Christ: the times of this ignorance God winked at, the Christianity with the white Jesus, the Islam, the Buddhism, the Hinduism, the Egyptology, the atheism; but now He commandeth all men every where to repent, because He hath appointed a day in which He will judge the world in righteousness by that man whom He hath ordained, Jesus the Christ. Do not take that mercy lightly, and do not frustrate the grace of God until He is finished with you. He can cut a man's days down whenever He wants; do not press Him to it.

While the whole congregation wept before the door of the tabernacle, one of the children of Israel brought a Midianitish woman unto his brethren in the sight of Moses and all the congregation: a man that did not care about his people while everyone around him mourned. When Phinehas the son of Eleazar, the son of Aaron the priest, saw it, he rose up from among the congregation, took a javelin in his hand, went after the man of Israel into the tent, and thrust both of them through; so the plague was stayed from the children of Israel, and those that died in the plague were twenty and four thousand. Let us now praise famous men: Phinehas stands third in glory, because he had zeal in the fear of the Lord and stood up with good courage of heart when the people were turned back, and made reconciliation for Israel; therefore a covenant of peace was made with him, that he and his posterity should have the dignity of the priesthood for ever. These things were our examples, that we should not lust after evil things as they lusted. The people sat down to eat and drink and rose up to play, and that play means sex; that was the golden calf. Neither commit fornication as they did, when three and twenty thousand fell in one day; neither tempt Christ, for it was Christ with us in the wilderness. These things are written for our admonition, that we be warned: idolatry leads to whoredom, spiritual whoredom against the Most High and physical whoredom with it.

Phinehas turned the wrath of the Most High away from the children of Israel, because he was zealous for his God's sake among them; wherefore the Lord gave him His covenant of peace, and to his seed after him the covenant of an everlasting priesthood, because he made an atonement for the children of Israel. That covenant of peace is what all of us are striving for, rest from this servitude of bondage; but the wisdom in reading the acts of Phinehas is that you must be zealous for the law of the Most High to obtain it. Be ye zealous for the law, and give your lives for the covenant of your fathers; Phinehas our father, in being zealous and fervent, obtained the covenant of an everlasting priesthood. Being zealous today is confessing Christ before men, and you confess him mainly through your actions. Christ suffered for us, leaving us an example that we should follow his steps, and his steps were keeping the commandments of God; the first way you deny Christ is by rejecting the commandments. Christ came not to send peace on earth but a sword, setting a man at variance against his own household; he that loveth father or mother more than him is not worthy of him. We stay zealous by letting nothing separate us from following Christ in his steps: keeping the laws of God, teaching the gospel, and spreading the word with wisdom.

The man of Israel that was slain was Zimri the son of Salu, a prince of a chief house among the Simeonites; the woman was Cozbi the daughter of Zur, head over a people of a chief house in Midian. The charge stands to Simeon to get it together; Simeon is coming back with the rest of the tribes. The Lord said unto Moses, vex the Midianites and smite them, for they vex you with their wiles, wherewith they have beguiled you in the matter of Peor and in the matter of Cozbi.

The Most High told Israel to avenge the children of Israel of the Midianites. The reason for this vengeance is the history of [Numbers 25](/bible/numbers/25); go back and read that chapter to see what Midian did.

A thousand of every tribe, twelve thousand armed for war, were sent with Phinehas the son of Eleazar the priest, with the holy instruments and the trumpets to blow. Phinehas is the one who killed the man of Israel that was fornicating with the woman of the other nation, in the history of [Numbers 25](/bible/numbers/25).

They warred against the Midianites as the Lord commanded Moses, slew all the males, and slew the five kings of Midian: Evi, Rekem, Zur, Hur, and Reba. Balaam also the son of Beor they slew with the sword. Balaam was a soothsayer, a diviner; he was a witch, so to speak.

Israel took the women of Midian captives with their little ones, took the spoil of all their cattle, flocks, and goods, and burnt all their cities and all their goodly castles with fire. Midian comes from the lineage of Ishmael, the people known today as the Arab man. This shows Esau was not the one who first came up with castles; the castles seen in the movies were conquered from other nations. They took all the spoil and all the prey, both of men and of beasts: the Midianites had captives of their own, and Israel took over both the men and the beasts when they overcame them.

Moses was wroth with the officers of the host, the leaders of the army of Israel, because they saved all the women alive. These women caused the children of Israel, through the counsel of Balaam, to commit trespass against the Lord in the matter of Peor. Balaam took it upon himself to send the women of the other nations to Israel, and it caused the people to go into fornication, and the Lord began putting them to death, over twenty and four thousand, in the history of [Numbers 25](/bible/numbers/25). Therefore every male among the little ones was to be killed, and every woman that had known man by lying with him; but the women children that had not known a man they kept alive for themselves. Moses allowed the men to keep those women so they would not commit sin and go raping the women, being out at war. That does not mean it is done today; it was a time that the Most High allowed it so the men would not be in the midst of sin.

Whoever killed any person or touched any slain had to abide without the camp seven days and purify himself and his captives on the third day and on the seventh day. That is the law going back to [Numbers 5:2](/bible/numbers/5#v2), putting the defiled outside the camp. Purifying the raiment, all that is made of skins, all work of goats' hair, and all things made of wood goes back to the law of purification in [Numbers 19](/bible/numbers/19). Eleazar the priest gave the ordinance: gold, silver, brass, iron, tin, and lead, everything that may abide the fire, goes through the fire and is purified with the water of separation; whatever abides not the fire goes through the water; and on the seventh day they wash their clothes, are clean, and come into the camp.

Moses, Eleazar the priest, and the chief fathers of the congregation took the sum of the prey, both of man and of beast, adding up all that was taken from the Midianites. The prey was divided into two parts: between the army who went out to battle and took the prey, and all the congregation that did not go to war. The nation looked out for each other. A tribute was levied unto the Lord: of the men of war, one soul of five hundred, of persons, beeves, asses, and sheep, given to Eleazar the priest for a heave offering, because he was the priest; and of the children of Israel's half, one portion of fifty, given to the Levites which kept the charge of the tabernacle.

Moses gave the tribute, the Lord's heave offering, unto Eleazar the priest, as the Lord commanded Moses. The heave offerings belong to the priesthood by statute forever, a covenant of salt, because Aaron and Levi have no inheritance in the land; the Most High is their part and their inheritance.

The seven nations cast out before Israel, the Hittites, Girgashites, Amorites, Canaanites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites, greater and mightier than Israel, are Hamitic nations. Thou shalt smite them and utterly destroy them; thou shalt make no covenant with them, nor shew mercy unto them. Since the days of old the Most High has never been about the love-of-the-world gospel; throw that doctrine in the trash. This is why they do not want you reading the old covenant: verses like this correct the miseducation received through Christianity, and the mind begins to correct itself as you read.

Neither shalt thou make marriages with them: the Most High forbids marrying outside the nation. The seed of the fathers today is found among the so-called blacks, Hispanics, and Native Indians, who make up the twelve tribes of Israel; a spouse may come from any of the twelve tribes, but from within the tribes only. Going outside your nation for a husband or wife is despising your brethren in your heart. Whom you marry is the greatest commitment you make in this life; if you truly loved your people, you would choose one of your own people to become aged together with. They will turn away thy son from following me: the nations are strangers to the Most High and cannot come into this covenant, so they draw the Israelite spouse off to religions that accept everything. Christianity accepts that union, and that is how they turn you away from your God.
Thus shall ye deal with them: destroy their altars, break down their images, cut down their groves, and burn their graven images with fire. Nothing of their worship was to be spared or adopted.

For thou art an holy people unto the Lord thy God: this is one of the most uplifting scriptures in the book, and it should be etched into your children's minds from the moment they begin to read, until it is implanted into their spirit. The mind controls the body: what goes into the mind comes out through the body, so a people that knows it is holy and special above all people walks and carries itself differently. Being chosen above all people keeps you out of the affairs of this world, their fashions, their hairstyles, their trends and challenges, and keeping up with the Joneses; you cannot flip-flop with every new wave and still carry the speciality the Most High put on you.

The Lord did not choose Israel for their number, for ye were the fewest of all people: only threescore and ten souls came out of the loins of Jacob when Israel first went down, as Genesis records, some places reading seventy and some counting seventy-five. But because the Lord loved you: the Most High needs no other reason, he simply loved us, and we should never apologize for that. He kept the oath sworn unto the fathers and redeemed Israel out of the house of bondmen, from the hand of Pharaoh king of Egypt; Israel came out from under Rameses.

Know therefore that the Lord thy God, he is God, the faithful God, which keepeth covenant and mercy with them that love him and keep his commandments to a thousand generations, and repayeth them that hate him to their face. This is the same teaching as the new testament: loving the Most High is keeping his commandments, and refusing his commandments shows him with your actions that you hate him, and then judgment comes. From the jump it has always been the same: love God, keep the commandments; nothing changed between the covenants.

If ye hearken to these judgments and keep and do them, the Lord keeps the covenant and the mercy: he will love thee, bless thee, and multiply thee, blessing the fruit of thy womb, thy land, thy corn, wine, oil, kine, and sheep, blessed above all people, which goes right back to verse 6. The Lord will take away from thee all sickness and put none of the evil diseases of Egypt upon thee, but will lay them upon all them that hate thee. That still reigns true today: keep the commandments and the Most High will keep you from the diseases of modern-day Egypt, and if you do catch something, he will revive you and bring you back to your health.

Thou shalt consume all the people which the Lord thy God shall deliver thee; thine eye shall have no pity upon them, neither shalt thou serve their gods, for that will be a snare unto thee. Those days are coming back when Christ returns.

If thou shalt say in thine heart, these nations are more than I: fear them not, but remember what the Lord did unto Pharaoh and unto all Egypt, the signs, the wonders, the mighty hand and the stretched out arm; so shall he do unto all the people of whom thou art afraid. The Lord will send the hornet among them until even those that hide themselves are destroyed, and he will put out those nations before thee by little and little, lest the beasts of the field increase upon thee. He shall deliver their kings into thine hand, and thou shalt destroy their name from under heaven. There is no way to read [Deuteronomy 7](/bible/deuteronomy/7) and still say God loves everybody; that idea is being drunk on Christianity, not reading the book.

The graven images of their gods shall ye burn with fire: desire not the silver or gold that is on them, lest thou be snared therein, for it is an abomination to the Lord thy God. Neither shalt thou bring an abomination into thine house, lest thou be a cursed thing like it. Bring it up to today: the Jesus pieces, the crosses, the ankhs, and the rosary beads wrapped around the neck and rubbed in prayer make the wearer an abomination and a cursed thing just like the idol. The main abomination we bring into our house is the Christmas tree of Jeremiah 10: the tree cut down, fastened with nails and hammers, and decked with silver and with gold, whether cut from the forest or bought as a fake tree from the store.

name: Phinehas
charge: Zealous for his God at Peor; making an atonement for the children of Israel
summary: While the congregation wept at the door of the tabernacle and the plague was running, a prince of Simeon walked a Midianite woman into the camp in front of them. Phinehas took a javelin and went in after them, and the plague was stayed at twenty-four thousand. The Lord gave him the covenant of an everlasting priesthood.
offense: The plague was already running and the congregation was weeping at the door of the tabernacle when a prince of Simeon brought a Midianite woman past them all into the camp (Numbers 25:6). It was done in the sight of Moses and the whole assembly, which makes it a public defiance rather than a private sin, and no one moved. Phinehas rose from among the congregation (Numbers 25:7), took a javelin, and followed them in. The act was summary and without trial, and the record neither disguises that nor apologises for it. What the text emphasises is the standing of the man and the state of the camp: a priest, in a time of open apostasy, executing a sentence the law already prescribed on parties taken in the act.
judgment: The plague was stayed at twenty-four thousand (Numbers 25:9), and the account attributes the stopping to the act. God's own reading of the motive is given: he was zealous for my sake among them, so that I consumed not the children of Israel in my jealousy (Numbers 25:11). He received a covenant of peace and of an everlasting priesthood for himself and his seed (Numbers 25:13), and the high priesthood ran in his line down to the captivity. The psalm files it under the language of the law court, that it was counted unto him for righteousness unto all generations (Psalms 106:31), which is a phrase used elsewhere only of Abraham's faith (Psalms 106:28-31).

So the plague was stayed from the children of Israel. 9And those that died in the plague were twenty and four thousand.

10And the Lord spake unto Moses, saying, 11Phinehas, the son of Eleazar, the son of Aaron the priest, hath turned my wrath away from the children of Israel, while he was zealous for my sake among them, that I consumed not the children of Israel in my jealousy. 12Wherefore say, Behold, I give unto him my covenant of peace: 13And he shall have it, and his seed after him, even the covenant of an everlasting priesthood; because he was zealous for his God, and made an atonement for the children of Israel.

They angered Him at the waters of strife, so it went ill with Moses, who spoke unadvisedly with his lips. Moses lost the promised land because he smote the rock and called the people rebels instead of speaking to it and sanctifying the Most High. They did not destroy the nations as commanded but were mingled among the heathen and learned their works. They served idols, sacrificed their sons and daughters to devils, and shed innocent blood, polluting the land and going a-whoring with their own inventions. -

The wrath of the Most High was kindled against His people so that He abhorred His own inheritance and gave them into the hand of the heathen, who ruled over them. The heathen ruling in our communities today, the legal system and the government, is the law and the prophets agreeing; He delivered them many times, but they provoked Him and were brought low for their iniquity. Nevertheless He regarded their affliction, remembered His covenant, and repented according to His mercies; David prays: save us and gather us from among the heathen. Blessed be the Lord God of Israel from everlasting to everlasting. -

Joshua called the Reubenites, the Gadites, and the half tribe of Manasseh and told them they had kept all that Moses commanded them and obeyed his voice; they had not left their brethren these many days, but kept the charge of the commandment of the Most High. The charge was the condition Moses set when these two and a half tribes asked to stay on the other side Jordan: whenever it was time to go to war they had to show up and fight with their brethren, not sit over there while Israel took the land.

Now that the Most High had given rest to their brethren as he promised, there was no war going on, so Joshua sent them home: return ye unto your tents and unto the land of your possession which Moses gave you on the other side Jordan. The release came with a charge: take diligent heed to do the commandment and the law, to love the Lord your God, to walk in all his ways, to keep his commandments, to cleave unto him, and to serve him with all your heart and all your soul. Rest did not end the duty; if their brethren ever needed them again they had to show up, as all the tribes did show up later in this same chapter.

Joshua blessed them and sent them away rich: return with much riches unto your tents, with very much cattle, with silver, gold, brass, iron, and very much raiment, and divide the spoil of your enemies with your brethren. The children of Reuben, the children of Gad, and the half tribe of Manasseh departed from Shiloh in the land of Canaan to go into the country of Gilead, the land of their possession according to the word of the Lord by the hand of Moses.

When the two and a half tribes came to the borders of Jordan they built a great altar by Jordan, an altar great to see to. They hid nothing; they built it on purpose so that it could be seen. When the children of Israel heard of it, the whole congregation gathered themselves together at Shiloh to go up to war against them. They thought the two and a half tribes had built the altar to worship idols and do their own thing, and they were ready to cleanse it before judgment fell on the whole nation like it had before.

Israel sent Phinehas the son of Eleazar the priest with ten princes, one head of a chief house from every tribe. When you send Phinehas it is a problem, because of the kind of man Phinehas was: where he showed up, the zeal of the Most High showed up with him. At Baalpeor the men of Israel began to commit whoredom with the daughters of Moab, bowed down to their gods, and joined themselves unto Baalpeor, and the anger of the Most High was kindled against Israel. One man of Israel was so bold he brought a Midianitish woman to his brethren in the sight of Moses and all the congregation while they wept before the door of the tabernacle. It was once a shameful thing for our men to be seen like that; today men and women of Israel walk boldly and proudly with the nations, that same spirit. Phinehas saw it, rose up from among the congregation, took a javelin, went after the man of Israel into the tent, and thrust both of them through, and the plague was stayed from the children of Israel; those that died in the plague were twenty and four thousand. So when Phinehas showed up at Gilead, everybody knew it was about to go down.

The delegation asked what trespass is this that ye have committed against the God of Israel, to build you an altar that ye might rebel this day against the Lord. They saw the altar and immediately thought the two and a half tribes were going into idolatry. Is the iniquity of Peor too little for us? All those thousands died in that plague, and Israel had just gotten into the land and gotten peace; why would anyone bring that thing back on the nation again? Their reasoning was national: if ye rebel today against the Lord, tomorrow he will be wroth with the whole congregation of Israel. Judgment does not fall on pieces of the nation; [Deuteronomy 28](/bible/deuteronomy/28) happened to all of us, and they understood that, so they showed up quick, fast, and in a hurry rather than sit around and let it happen.

They even offered their own land: if the land of your possession be unclean, pass ye over unto the land of the possession of the Lord and take possession among us, close by where we can keep an eye on you; only rebel not against the Lord, nor build you an altar beside the altar of the Lord our God. They cited the proof from their own history: did not Achan the son of Zerah commit a trespass in the accursed thing, and wrath fell on all the congregation of Israel, and that man perished not alone in his iniquity. One man trespassed and the whole nation felt it.

The two and a half tribes answered: the LORD God of gods, the LORD God of gods, he knoweth, and Israel he shall know; if it be in rebellion or in transgression against the Lord, save us not this day. They put their own lives on the line: if we built this thing in rebellion, put us to death today. If we built an altar to turn from following the Lord, or to offer burnt offerings, meat offerings, or peace offerings on it, let the Lord himself require it.

This is why they built it: for fear of this thing, that in time to come your children might speak unto our children, saying, What have ye to do with the LORD God of Israel? The Lord hath made Jordan a border between us and you; ye have no part in the LORD. They feared that generations later the children on one side of Jordan would tell the children on the other side that they were not the children of Israel, shutting them out from fearing the Lord, from the temple, the feast days, and the sacrifices.

The altar was not for burnt offering nor for sacrifice; it was a witness between us and you and our generations after us, a memorial, so the two and a half tribes could do the service of the Lord before him in the place he chose, along with the rest of the tribes, and nobody could stop them. If anyone ever said to their generations, Ye have no part in the Lord, the answer would stand built in stone: behold the pattern of the altar of the LORD, which our fathers made, not for burnt offerings nor for sacrifices, but it is a witness between us and you. The same thing is happening today with the northern kingdom. Our people left their own witnesses over here: the writings on the Los Lunas stone identify with the northern kingdom, and the traditions, artifacts, practices, laws, and books that are being brought out in the classes all prove our people were here long ago and that they are the children of Israel. Yet with all that proof out there, people still deny it, the very thing the two and a half tribes feared. Nobody else could have built that altar to the pattern of the altar of the Lord, because no other nation was keeping the laws; only Israel keeps the precepts, not the heathen. That is why the memorial could stand as identification.

When Phinehas and the princes heard the words of the children of Reuben, Gad, and Manasseh, it pleased them. Phinehas said, This day we perceive that the LORD is among us, because ye have not committed this trespass against the Lord. Now ye have delivered the children of Israel out of the hand of the LORD: because they were not going off, nobody had to die that day, and coming from Phinehas that meant everything, because if it had been rebellion he would have been the one to start it.

Phinehas and the princes returned from Gilead to the land of Canaan and brought the children of Israel word again: all is good, the altar is a memorial so the generations after do not forget that our people are on that side Jordan too, and they can come in and keep the feasts and do their sacrifices with us. The thing pleased the children of Israel; they blessed God, dismantled from war, and did not go up to destroy the land where the children of Reuben and Gad dwelt. The children of Reuben and Gad called the altar Ed: for it shall be a witness between us that the LORD is God.

name: Zimri and Cozbi
charge: Bringing a Midianite woman into the camp in the sight of the congregation
summary: While the congregation wept at the tabernacle door over the plague, Zimri, a prince of Simeon, walked a Midianite princess past them into his tent. Phinehas followed with a javelin and thrust them both through.
offense: The act was public and it was done in the middle of a national mourning. The people had already joined themselves unto Baal-peor, called to the sacrifices of their gods and eating and bowing down, and the anger of the Lord was kindled (Numbers 25:2-3), so the worship and the whoredom were one thing and not two. Then, while the whole congregation was weeping before the door of the tabernacle of the congregation, one of the children of Israel brought a Midianitish woman unto his brethren in the sight of Moses and in the sight of all the congregation (Numbers 25:6). It was a man who did not care about his own people while everyone around him mourned. Both are named afterwards, which the record does deliberately: Zimri the son of Salu, a prince of a chief house among the Simeonites, and Cozbi the daughter of Zur, head over a people of a chief house in Midian (Numbers 25:14-15).
judgment: Both died on the javelin, and the plague was stayed. God gave Phinehas a covenant of everlasting priesthood because he was zealous for his God and made an atonement. Sirach ranks him third in glory; the Maccabees claim him as father.

entries.commentary: Israel abode in Shittim, and the people began to commit whoredom with the daughters of Moab. Why? Balaam could not curse us, because God said you cannot curse what is blessed; so his counsel was the best the enemy can ever do: throw another god in front of Israel and send the women, and let Israel bring the trespass on himself. That counsel is why the Lord put Balaam to death. They called the people unto the sacrifices of their gods, and the people did eat and bowed down; Israel joined himself unto Baal-peor, and the anger of the Lord was kindled. The worship of Baal-peor went into whoredom, that orgy worship: we started worshipping another god and messing with the women together.

The Lord said, take all the heads of the people and hang them up before the Lord against the sun, that His fierce anger be turned away; and Moses said unto the judges, slay ye every one his man that were joined unto Baal-peor. Every one his man means every judge by his rank: the officer over ten took ten, the officer over fifty took fifty, and so on. With the Most High it is two options only, life and death. Under the old covenant there was no winking at ignorance; judgment was instant. The only reason we are not judged that way now for the gods we served is the grace and mercy given through Christ: the times of this ignorance God winked at, the Christianity with the white Jesus, the Islam, the Buddhism, the Hinduism, the Egyptology, the atheism; but now He commandeth all men every where to repent, because He hath appointed a day in which He will judge the world in righteousness by that man whom He hath ordained, Jesus the Christ. Do not take that mercy lightly, and do not frustrate the grace of God until He is finished with you. He can cut a man's days down whenever He wants; do not press Him to it.

While the whole congregation wept before the door of the tabernacle, one of the children of Israel brought a Midianitish woman unto his brethren in the sight of Moses and all the congregation: a man that did not care about his people while everyone around him mourned. When Phinehas the son of Eleazar, the son of Aaron the priest, saw it, he rose up from among the congregation, took a javelin in his hand, went after the man of Israel into the tent, and thrust both of them through; so the plague was stayed from the children of Israel, and those that died in the plague were twenty and four thousand. Let us now praise famous men: Phinehas stands third in glory, because he had zeal in the fear of the Lord and stood up with good courage of heart when the people were turned back, and made reconciliation for Israel; therefore a covenant of peace was made with him, that he and his posterity should have the dignity of the priesthood for ever. These things were our examples, that we should not lust after evil things as they lusted. The people sat down to eat and drink and rose up to play, and that play means sex; that was the golden calf. Neither commit fornication as they did, when three and twenty thousand fell in one day; neither tempt Christ, for it was Christ with us in the wilderness. These things are written for our admonition, that we be warned: idolatry leads to whoredom, spiritual whoredom against the Most High and physical whoredom with it.

Phinehas turned the wrath of the Most High away from the children of Israel, because he was zealous for his God's sake among them; wherefore the Lord gave him His covenant of peace, and to his seed after him the covenant of an everlasting priesthood, because he made an atonement for the children of Israel. That covenant of peace is what all of us are striving for, rest from this servitude of bondage; but the wisdom in reading the acts of Phinehas is that you must be zealous for the law of the Most High to obtain it. Be ye zealous for the law, and give your lives for the covenant of your fathers; Phinehas our father, in being zealous and fervent, obtained the covenant of an everlasting priesthood. Being zealous today is confessing Christ before men, and you confess him mainly through your actions. Christ suffered for us, leaving us an example that we should follow his steps, and his steps were keeping the commandments of God; the first way you deny Christ is by rejecting the commandments. Christ came not to send peace on earth but a sword, setting a man at variance against his own household; he that loveth father or mother more than him is not worthy of him. We stay zealous by letting nothing separate us from following Christ in his steps: keeping the laws of God, teaching the gospel, and spreading the word with wisdom.

The man of Israel that was slain was Zimri the son of Salu, a prince of a chief house among the Simeonites; the woman was Cozbi the daughter of Zur, head over a people of a chief house in Midian. The charge stands to Simeon to get it together; Simeon is coming back with the rest of the tribes. The Lord said unto Moses, vex the Midianites and smite them, for they vex you with their wiles, wherewith they have beguiled you in the matter of Peor and in the matter of Cozbi.

At all times, not only when convenient. David asks to be remembered with the favor toward His people, to see the good of His chosen and rejoice in the gladness of His nation.

We have sinned with our fathers and done wickedly; our fathers understood not His wonders in Egypt and provoked Him at the Red Sea. Esau's science says a wind blew it into a tsunami, but the Most High said He rebuked it. The waters covered their enemies, and then they believed His words and sang His praise.

name: The daughters of Zelophehad
charge: Asking rightly for their father's inheritance, and marrying within their tribe as commanded
summary: Five sisters with no brother came to the door of the tabernacle and asked why their father's name should be done away from among his family because he had no son. The Lord said, The daughters of Zelophehad speak right, and made a statute of judgment for all Israel. They then married as they were told, and kept the inheritance in Manasseh.
offense: Five women with no brother came to the door of the tabernacle and made a legal argument, and the record names them, Mahlah, Noah, Hoglah, Milcah and Tirzah, and names their tribe, Manasseh (Numbers 27:1). They did not ask for pity and they did not accuse anyone. They set out the facts: our father died in the wilderness, and he was not in the company of them that gathered themselves together against the Lord in the company of Korah, but died in his own sin, and had no sons (Numbers 27:3). Then the question, and it was the question of the lineage: why should the name of our father be done away from among his family, because he hath no son? give unto us therefore a possession among the brethren of our father (Numbers 27:4). They brought a gap in the law to the only authority who could fill it, in the proper form and at the proper place, and Moses did not answer out of his own judgment: Moses brought their cause before the Lord (Numbers 27:5). When the answer created a second question, that an inheritance might pass out of the tribe by marriage, the chief fathers of Gilead brought that too (Numbers 36:1-4), and the daughters accepted the further ruling and married within their father's tribe as commanded (Numbers 36:10-12).
judgment: The Lord did not merely grant the request; he endorsed the reasoning: the daughters of Zelophehad speak right, thou shalt surely give them a possession of an inheritance among their father's brethren (Numbers 27:7). Their case became the order of inheritance for the whole nation: if a man die, and have no son, then ye shall cause his inheritance to pass unto his daughter, and if he have no daughter, to his brethren, and if no brethren, to his father's brethren, and if his father have no brethren, to his kinsman that is next to him of his family, and it shall be unto the children of Israel a statute of judgment (Numbers 27:8-11). The second ruling set the rule on marriage where an

entries.commentary: The daughters of Zelophehad, of the tribe of Manasseh, stood before Moses, Eleazar the priest, the princes, and all the congregation at the door of the tabernacle. Their father died in the wilderness in his own sin; he was not in the company of Korah that gathered together against the Lord. He had no sons, only these five daughters. Their question was the question of the lineage: since the man puts the seed in the woman, if a man had only daughters, why should his name be done away from among his family? So they asked for a possession among the brethren of their father.

Moses brought their cause before the Lord. He did not do his own thing; he sought counsel and asked the Most High what to do in this instance. The Lord said the daughters of Zelophehad speak right: give them a possession of an inheritance among their father's brethren, and cause the inheritance of their father to pass unto them.

Here the Lord set the order of inheritance for all Israel: if a man die and have no son, it passes to his daughter; if no daughter, to his brethren; if no brethren, to his father's brethren; and if his father had no brethren, to the kinsman that is next to him of his family. Every angle was covered so the inheritance stayed within the tribe. Israel always had questions, just as we do when we read, and the Lord put these statutes in place to answer them before they were asked. But what if a daughter who received the inheritance married into another tribe? You have to go precept upon precept: [Numbers 36](/bible/numbers/36) takes up that very case with these same daughters. The chief fathers of Gilead brought it to Moses, and the word came back that the daughters of Zelophehad may marry to whom they think best, only to the family of the tribe of their father shall they marry.

The Lord told Moses to get up into mount Abarim and see the land given to the children of Israel; he would see it but not enter it, and then be gathered unto his people as Aaron his brother was gathered. The reason is written: Moses rebelled against the commandment of the Most High in the desert of Zin at the water of Meribah. The Lord gave a specific commandment to speak unto the rock before their eyes, and Moses instead smote the rock twice; the water still came out abundantly, but Moses and Aaron did not sanctify the Lord in the eyes of the children of Israel, and for that neither of them brought the congregation into the land.

Before his death Moses asked the Lord to set a man over the congregation, to go out before them and come in before them, to lead them out and bring them in, that the congregation of the Lord be not as sheep which have no shepherd. Moses asked for a man because the leadership of the nation belongs to men. The woman was made to be an help meet unto the man, not to rule over him; she is the weaker vessel, and the congregation is not set up for her to lead it. A sister helping to build up other sisters new in the congregation is right, and the sisters bless the nation with real talents, raising the children in the commandments, and the aged women teaching the young women. But teaching and leading the nation is not the place the Most High set for her.

The Lord answered: take thee Joshua the son of Nun, a man in whom is the spirit, and lay thine hand upon him. Joshua was set before Eleazar the priest and before all the congregation and given his charge in their sight, and some of Moses' honour was put upon him, so all Israel could see with their own eyes the man the Most High ordained to lead the nation after the death of Moses. Joshua was to stand before Eleazar the priest, who would ask counsel for him after the judgment of Urim before the Lord; at his word they would go out and come in, he and all the children of Israel with him.

Moses did as the Lord commanded him: he took Joshua, set him before Eleazar the priest and all the congregation, laid his hands upon him, and gave him a charge, as the Lord commanded by the hand of Moses.

The chief fathers of the families of Gilead of the tribe of Manasseh bring an issue rising out of what was already ruled in Numbers 27: when Zelophehad died in the wilderness with no sons, the Lord ruled that his inheritance pass to his daughters. Their concern is real: if the daughters marry men of another tribe, their father's inheritance passes with them to the husband's tribe, and at the jubilee it is fixed to that tribe, so the tribe of Manasseh loses that land forever.

The Most High affirms the tribe of the sons of Joseph: they have said well. The solution: the daughters of Zelophehad may marry whom they think best, only within the family of the tribe of their father. The purpose is stated plainly: so shall not the inheritance of the children of Israel remove from tribe to tribe; the marriage boundary here was instituted because of land inheritance.

Every daughter that possessed an inheritance had to marry within her father's tribe, so every man of Israel would enjoy the inheritance of his fathers and no inheritance would remove from one tribe to another. The tribal restriction belonged to the time when Israel dwelt in the land; it existed because of inheritance. Today Israel has no inheritance in the lands of captivity, so the rule that still applies is marrying within the nation of Israel, not tribe-only marriage. No one today knows his exact tribe with certainty; a Judahite could have been dropped off anywhere in the captivity. Without the history of [Numbers 36](/bible/numbers/36), [Tobit 4:12](/bible/tobit/4#v12) gets twisted into a doctrine that a man may only marry his own tribe, and that is a heresy born of not knowing why the law was given.

The daughters of Zelophehad did as the Lord commanded Moses: Mahlah, Tirzah, Hoglah, Milcah, and Noah married their father's brothers' sons, within the families of Manasseh, and their inheritance remained in the tribe of the family of their father. These are the commandments and the judgments which the Lord commanded by the hand of Moses in the plains of Moab by Jordan near Jericho; with this verse the book of Numbers is completed. --- Topics: [The Feasts of the Most High](/encyclopedia/the-feasts-of-the-most-high) · [The Priesthood](/encyclopedia/the-priesthood)

A lot goes into an allotment, a portion; there was a portion for the tribe of Manasseh, for he was the firstborn of Joseph. Machir, the firstborn of Manasseh and the father of Gilead, was a man of war, therefore he had Gilead and Bashan. Bashan was the kingdom of Og, one of the giants that Israel conquered under Joshua. Before the conquest all this territory was called the land of Canaan, with the Canaanites, the Perizzites, and the Jebusites and their families dwelling in it. Prior to this chapter Judah received his inheritance in chapter 15 and the inheritance of Joseph, Ephraim, came in chapter 16; after the victories the Most High gave through Christ, the land was divided by lot so that every tribe had its portion. The Bible maps that even the enemies of Israel put together according to the scriptures show this history: Manasseh held Bashan and a portion by Gilead on the other side of Jordan. The so-called Cubans come from this tribe; this is their history that their enemies do not want them to know.

There was also a lot for the rest of the children of Manasseh by their families, Abiezer, Helek, Asriel, Shechem, Hepher, and Shemida: these were the male children of Manasseh the son of Joseph. Remember that Manasseh was the son of Joseph; Joseph had two sons, Ephraim and Manasseh.

Zelophehad the son of Hepher had no sons, but daughters: Mahlah, Noah, Hoglah, Milcah, and Tirzah. They came near before Eleazar the priest, before Joshua the son of Nun, and before the princes, saying the Lord commanded Moses to give them an inheritance among their brethren; and according to the commandment of the Lord he gave them an inheritance among the brethren of their father.

Ten portions fell to Manasseh, beside the land of Gilead and Bashan which were on the other side of Jordan. On the map the Jordan river flows down through the land, and across the river sat Gilead and Bashan, the lands Manasseh already held. Down south the Jordan empties into the Dead Sea, and Sodom and Gomorrah sat south of the Dead Sea, by where Edom was residing; the maps give a good feel for what the Bible is talking about. The daughters of Manasseh had an inheritance among his sons, just as the Lord commanded for the daughters of Zelophehad, and the rest of Manasseh's sons had the land of Gilead.

The coast of Manasseh ran from Asher to Michmethah; Manasseh had the land of Tappuah, but Tappuah itself on the border of Manasseh belonged to the children of Ephraim. We have to know where our forefathers came from and what the Bible is speaking about; that is why we search out these borders on the maps, where Tappuah sat on the southern border by Shechem.

The coast descended to the river Kanah: southward of the river the cities were Ephraim's, and northward it was Manasseh's, the sea was his border, and they met together in Asher on the north and in Issachar on the east. This land of Canaan is also known as Israel, and this is where our foremothers and forefathers lived: the so-called Mexicans, Guatemalans, and Hondurans lived here, and the so-called Brazilians, Colombians, and Venezuelans up in these coasts. A lot of times we read that Asher lived here and forget it is talking about us; our people need the visual. Manasseh also had within Issachar and Asher the cities of Beth-shean, Ibleam, Dor, En-dor, Taanach, and Megiddo with their towns, even three countries.

Even though Israel conquered the majority of the land of Canaan, there were still areas the Canaanites kept possession of; the children of Manasseh could not drive out the inhabitants of those cities, but the Canaanites would dwell in that land. When the children of Israel were waxen strong, they put the Canaanites to tribute, but did not utterly drive them out; they kept them as servants and handmaids.

The children of Joseph, led by Ephraim, asked Joshua why he gave them but one lot to inherit, seeing they are a great people; great here means numerous. Ephraim and Manasseh were among the most populated tribes, and Ephraim's own portion had already been given back in chapter 16. Their fruitfulness was prophesied when Israel blessed Joseph; the very name Ephraim goes into being fruitful.

The children of Joseph answered that the hill is not enough for them, and the Canaanites that dwell in the land of the valley have chariots of iron; those nations had military power too. On the map those Canaanites sat right north of Manasseh, in Beth-shean and her towns and in the valley of Jezreel, dwelling in the midst of our brothers with an army; they were a problem, and Manasseh was already having a hard time with them.

Joshua told the house of Joseph, thou art a great people and hast great power; the mountain shall be thine, and thou shalt drive out the Canaanites, though they have iron chariots and though they be strong. Going through the wood means going through the dense forest; it would be a struggle, but at the end of the day they would overcome. Manasseh had issues driving the Canaanites out, but Ephraim did it. The difference between the two brothers goes back to [Genesis 48](/bible/genesis/48), where Israel blessed Joseph's sons and crossed his hands, guiding them wittingly, meaning he knew exactly what he was doing.

The sons of Issachar are named, and the heads of their fathers' houses are counted as valiant men of might in their generations. In the days of David their number was two and twenty thousand and six hundred, and reckoned by all their genealogies they were fourscore and seven thousand mighty men.

The sons of Benjamin are set down, Bela, Becher, and Jediael, with the heads of their houses reckoned as mighty men of valor. Issachar and Benjamin were warriors, not a joke. Our brethren have always been warriors who only lost their spirit in these last days.
The sons of Naphtali are named, and the sons of Manasseh through his concubine, down to the line of Gilead. The daughters of Zelophehad are noted, and the sons of Gilead are set in order.

The sons of Ephraim are traced, and Ezer and Elead are named, whom the men of Gath slew when they came down to take their cattle. Ephraim their father mourned many days, and his brethren came to comfort him, and afterward Beriah was born and the line continued to Joshua, with their possessions and habitations named.

The sons of Asher are named, and their line is traced through the heads of their fathers' houses. Asher were warriors too, choice and mighty men of valor, chief of the princes, numbered twenty and six thousand men fit for the battle.
