name: Rahab
charge: Receiving the spies with peace, and believing that the Lord had given Israel the land
summary: A harlot of Jericho hid two Israelite spies under the flax on her roof, confessed that the Lord their God is God in heaven above and in earth beneath, and asked for her father's house. She bound the scarlet line in the window. When the wall fell, hers was the one house left, and she is in the line of Christ.
offense: She was a Canaanite, a harlot, and a resident of a city under the ban, and her faith came by report before it came by sight: we have heard how the Lord dried up the water of the Red sea for you, and what ye did unto the two kings of the Amorites, Sihon and Og (Joshua 2:10). She said what the report had done to the city, and to her: as soon as we had heard these things, our hearts did melt, neither did there remain any more courage in any man (Joshua 2:11). Faith and fear went together in her. What she feared was not the king of Jericho, who could have had her killed for hiding the men, but the judgment of the God she had heard of, and that fear is what gave her the faith to put her life on the line. Her confession is complete and it is in her own mouth: the Lord your God, he is God in heaven above, and in earth beneath (Joshua 2:11). She hid the men on the roof under the flax, answered the king's men with truth in part and misdirection in the rest, and sent the pursuers toward Jordan after men who had gone nowhere (Joshua 2:4-7). Then she bargained, as one who had something to sell: swear unto me by the Lord, since I have shewed you kindness, that ye will also shew kindness unto my father's house (Joshua 2:12-13). James selects her as the standing example that faith which does not act is dead, and pairs her with Abraham (James 2:25).
judgment: The spies answered, our life for yours, if ye utter not this our business (Joshua 2:14), so the covenant was conditional: if she uttered it, they would be quit of the oath (Joshua 2:20). The token was the line of scarlet thread bound in the window she had let them down by, and the terms were that everyone in the house behind it would live and anyone who went out of the doors into the street would answer for himself (Joshua 2:18-19). She said, according unto your words, so be it, and bound the scarlet line in the window (Joshua 2:21). When the wall fell down flat, her house stood, and Joshua sent the two spies to bring her out with her father, her mother, her brethren, and all that she had (Joshua 6:22-23). Everything else in the city was devoted. Joshua saved Rahab the harlot alive, and her father's household, and she dwelleth in Israel even unto this day, because she hid the messengers (Joshua 6:25). Hebrews lists her among those who perished not with them that believed not, when she had received the spies with peace (Hebrews 11:31), and Matthew places her in the direct line of David and of Christ, Salmon begat Booz of Rachab (Matthew 1:5), so that the woman spared from the ban became an ancestor of the one who ends it.

verses.text: 1And Joshua the son of Nun sent out of Shittim two men to spy secretly, saying, Go view the land, even Jericho. And they went, and came into an harlot’s house, named Rahab, and lodged there. 2And it was told the king of Jericho, saying, Behold, there came men in hither to night of the children of Israel to search out the country. 3And the king of Jericho sent unto Rahab, saying, Bring forth the men that are come to thee, which are entered into thine house: for they be come to search out all the country. 4And the woman took the two men, and hid them, and said thus, There came men unto me, but I wist not whence they were: 5And it came to pass about the time of shutting of the gate, when it was dark, that the men went out: whither the men went I wot not: pursue after them quickly; for ye shall overtake them. 6But she had brought them up to the roof of the house, and hid them with the stalks of flax,

entries.commentary: Joshua sent two men out of Shittim to spy secretly and view the land, even Jericho, and they came into the house of a harlot named Rahab and lodged there. Word made its way to the king of Jericho that men of the children of Israel had come to search out the country, and he sent unto Rahab to bring them forth. She had taken the two men and hid them on the roof under the stalks of flax she had laid in order there. She told the king's men the truth in part and misdirection in the rest: men came unto me, but I wist not whence they were, and they went out about the time of the shutting of the gate; pursue after them quickly. The pursuers chased toward Jordan after men who had gone nowhere, the gate was shut behind them, and the spies had clearance to escape. A heathen woman looked out for Israel, and she did it out of the fear of the Lord, as her own words show.

Before the spies lay down, Rahab came up to the roof and confessed: I know that the Lord hath given you the land, and that your terror is fallen upon us, and that all the inhabitants of the land faint because of you. That is faith and belief; a heathen acknowledged that the God of Israel had ordained them to conquer her land.

Rahab asked the spies to swear unto her by the Lord, since she had shewed them kindness, that they would shew kindness unto her father's house and give her a true token, saving her father, mother, brethren, and sisters alive. The men answered, our life for yours, if ye utter not this our business: since she looked out for Israel, Israel would look out for her, on condition the plan stayed secret. If she uttered the business, the oath was null and void. The token was the line of scarlet thread bound in the window by which she let them down, for her house was upon the town wall. That scarlet line marked her house so no one in it would be slain when Israel came into the land; the terms were that whosoever went out of the doors into the street, his blood would be on his own head, and whosoever stayed within, his blood on Israel's head if any hand touched him. She sent them to the mountain to hide three days until the pursuers returned, said according unto your words, so be it, and bound the scarlet line in the window.

The spies abode in the mountain three days until the pursuers returned, having sought them throughout all the way and found them not. They came again to Joshua and reported: truly the Lord hath delivered into our hands all the land, for even all the inhabitants of the country do faint because of us. The land was theirs for the taking, exactly as the Lord had promised.

Jericho was straitly shut up because of the children of Israel: none went out and none came in. Jericho had a military, and a garrison, a military base, was built there, with the walls shut so nobody could enter or leave. The Lord said unto Joshua, See, I have given into thine hand Jericho, and the king thereof, and the mighty men of valour: the battle was already decided.

The battle plan came from the Lord: compass the city with all the men of war once a day for six days, seven priests bearing seven trumpets of rams' horns before the ark; on the seventh day compass the city seven times, and at the long blast all the people shout with a great shout, and the wall shall fall down flat. The blowing of the trumpets activates the armies of the Lord, the angels, to help in battle. Remember Elisha's servant: when his eyes were opened he saw the host of angels that were there warring and protecting Israel. This is the spirit behind the men of Israel rehearsing the righteous acts with trumpets and shofars today, at the camps and at the new moons; it is spiritual and an act of faith.

Joshua called the priests and gave the order: seven priests bear seven trumpets before the ark, the armed men pass on before the ark, and the rereward, the guards in the rear, came after the ark. Joshua commanded the people, Ye shall not shout, nor make any noise with your voice, neither shall any word proceed out of your mouth, until the day I bid you shout; then shall ye shout. The ark of the Lord compassed the city once, and they came into the camp and lodged there.

They repeated the act six days back to back, rising early, the priests bearing the ark and blowing the trumpets, the armed men before and the rereward after, one compass of the city each day. Every army in the world stole this from the Israelites: the pass and review of the militaries, with their battalions and units, their guidons with the eagle on the tip of the spear, marching round the field sounding off with cadences and trumpets, is patterned after what Israel did here.

On the seventh day they rose about the dawning of the day and compassed the city seven times. There is something about the number seven that the Lord loves; you read about it in Revelation. At the seventh time, when the priests blew with the trumpets, Joshua said unto the people, Shout; for the Lord hath given you the city. The men apply [Joshua 6](/bible/joshua/6) to this day: when a scoffer will not hear the word and thinks to outcry the truth, the brothers say the scripture together with one mind, one body, one spirit. That unity is spiritual, a rehearsal of the righteous acts. Unity and order are what the enemies fear: not gangs and drug dealing, but the so-called Black man, Hispanic man, and Native American man unified in the order of a military, with structure and organization. That is what puts fear in the nations.

The city shall be accursed, even it and all that are therein, to the Lord: only Rahab the harlot shall live, she and all that are with her in the house, because she hid the messengers. She made a covenant with the spies: she would conceal them and assist Israel, knowing the Lord was with Israel, as long as her family was saved when the city fell. Rahab was a Canaanite, a heathen, yet the heathen can be blessed when they do it to benefit Israel; blessed is he that blesseth thee. Rahab is the scripture's own example that a man is justified by works and not by faith only: faith and works go hand in hand, for your actions prove whether you believe. Was not Rahab the harlot justified by works, when she had received the messengers and sent them out another way? As the body without the spirit is dead, so faith without works is dead also. Works by the Bible's own dictionary is keeping his commandments: set your hope in God, forget not his works, but keep his commandments. Words say a lot, but actions always speak louder, and by him actions are weighed. Keep yourselves from the accursed thing, lest ye make yourselves accursed and make the camp of Israel a curse, and trouble it: your individual sins affect the whole nation of Israel, your brothers, your sisters, and the children. That is why we must examine ourselves whether we be in the faith. All the silver and gold and vessels of brass and iron were consecrated unto the Lord, separated and sanctified for his treasury alone: nobody was to gain personally from this war.

The people shouted when the priests blew with the trumpets, and the wall fell down flat. That shout is [Isaiah 58:1](/bible/isaiah/58#v1) in action, cry aloud and spare not: the sound coming out of their mouths with the trumpets broke everything down, like thousands of lions roaring at once. The people went up into the city, every man straight before him, and they took the city and utterly destroyed all that was in it, both man and woman, young and old, ox, sheep, and ass, with the edge of the sword.

Joshua sent the two spies into the harlot's house to bring out Rahab and all that she had, as they sware unto her; they brought out her father, mother, brethren, and all her kindred, and left them without the camp of Israel. They burnt the city with fire and all that was therein; only the silver, gold, and vessels of brass and iron went into the treasury of the house of the Lord. Joshua saved Rahab the harlot alive and her father's household, and she dwelleth in Israel even unto this day, because she hid the messengers. She helped the nation of Israel toward rulership, and that is the only help Israel wants from the other nations: not food stamps, welfare, or reparations, but tell our people who they are, the Israelites the Bible speaks of, the so-called Blacks, Hispanics, and Native Americans, and that we must keep the commandments of the Most High. Whoever does that will receive mercy just as Rahab did.

Joshua adjured them at that time: cursed be the man before the Lord that riseth up and buildeth this city Jericho; he shall lay the foundation thereof in his firstborn, and in his youngest son shall he set up the gates of it. The city was not to be rebuilt. So the Lord was with Joshua, and his fame was noised throughout all the country.

name: Achan
charge: Taking devoted spoil from Jericho
summary: Jericho's spoil was placed under the ban, devoted wholly to God. Achan took a garment, silver, and a wedge of gold and hid them in his tent. Israel's next battle failed because of it.
offense: The first sentence of the chapter names the party, and it is not one man: the children of Israel committed a trespass in the accursed thing, for Achan the son of Carmi took of the accursed thing, and the anger of the Lord was kindled against the children of Israel (Joshua 7:1). The record charges the nation for what one man did in secret in his own tent, which is the point of the case and the reason it is entered under Israel as well as under Achan. His own confession gives the sequence: I saw, I coveted, I took, and hid them in the earth in the midst of my tent (Joshua 7:21). Every step of it was private, and the sin the nation carried was a sin nobody in the nation knew about.
judgment: Three thousand men went up against Ai and fled, and the men of Ai smote about thirty and six of them and chased them from before the gate, and the hearts of the people melted and became as water (Joshua 7:4-5). That melting is itself the sentence written in the law for disobedience, that the Lord shall send faintness into their hearts, and the sound of a shaken leaf shall chase them, and they shall flee as fleeing from a sword when none pursueth (Leviticus 26:36). Israel could not stand before its enemies until the accursed thing was destroyed from among them, and Joshua was told the nation could not be with him until then (Joshua 7:12-13). The man was taken by lot, tribe by family by household, and he and all that he had were brought up to the valley of Achor and stoned and burned (Joshua 7:24-25). The Lord turned from the fierceness of his anger only after that, and the place keeps the name to this day.

verses.text: 1But the children of Israel committed a trespass in the accursed thing: for Achan, the son of Carmi, the son of Zabdi, the son of Zerah, of the tribe of Judah, took of the accursed thing: and the anger of the Lord was kindled against the children of Israel.

11Israel hath sinned, and they have also transgressed my covenant which I commanded them: for they have even taken of the accursed thing, and have also stolen, and dissembled also, and they have put it even among their own stuff.

20And Achan answered Joshua, and said, Indeed I have sinned against the Lord God of Israel, and thus and thus have I done: 21When I saw among the spoils a goodly Babylonish garment, and two hundred shekels of silver, and a wedge of gold of fifty shekels weight, then I coveted them, and took them; and, behold, they are hid in the earth in the midst of my tent, and the silver under it.

lawDetails.text: You shall not covet anything that is your neighbor's.
You shall not take as a spoil those things accursed of God (pagan artifacts, idols, etc.).

entries.commentary: Who committed the trespass? Many will answer Achan, but read the first sentence: the children of Israel committed a trespass in the accursed thing. Achan the son of Carmi, the son of Zabdi, the son of Zerah, of the tribe of Judah, took of the accursed thing, and the anger of the Lord was kindled against all the children of Israel. Your individual sins can hurt the rest of the nation. You can be the hindrance to why your camp is not growing, why your family, your marriage, or your children have issues, when you have a spirit on you that you know about and keep secret, not praying, not fasting, not seeking counsel. That is the spirit of Achan, and the children of Israel pay for it; we are supposed to be one mind, one body, one spirit.

The men who viewed Ai came back confident: let not all the people go up, but about two or three thousand men, for they are but few. The way Israel had been winning, they thought they could not lose; but what happened in verse 1 was about to play its part. About three thousand went up, and they fled before the men of Ai, who smote about thirty and six men and chased them from before the gate; the hearts of the people melted and became as water. The Lord is the one who wins the battles and gets the victory, not us. Pick out the weakest nation on earth: no matter how strong Israel is physically, if we are not spiritually right with the Lord, he will make us lose, for this fight is not carnal. Hearts melting as water is the curse for disobedience: the Most High sends a faintness into the heart, so that the mighty flee as fleeing from a sword and fall when none pursueth, like the athlete in the scary movie suddenly stumbling from sheer fear.

Joshua rent his clothes and fell to the earth upon his face before the ark until the eventide, he and the elders of Israel, and put dust upon their heads, grieving over the war just lost and the men that died. Israel turning their backs means they were fleeing, retreating, defeated. Joshua understood what the nations do when they see Israel take a loss: the Canaanites would hear of it, environ us round, surround us, capitalize while we are down, and cut off our name from the earth. And what wilt thou do unto thy great name? If Israel is cut off, who will be there to praise the Most High?

The Lord said, Get thee up; wherefore liest thou upon thy face? Israel hath sinned. It does not say Achan sinned; it says Israel. This walk is not selfish or individual: when you are in sin you hurt your wife, your husband, your children, the congregation, and the leadership, for we are all our brother's keeper and responsible for one another. They have taken of the accursed thing, and stolen, and dissembled, and put it among their own stuff: the Lord says they. As a father who finds mischief chastens all his children together when none confesses, so the Most High deals with his children as one house; we pay for one another's sins. Therefore the children of Israel could not stand before their enemies: the Lord was not going to let them win, and he put a mightier warring spirit on the men of Ai. However well you train with your sword and shield, the Most High controls the outcome. His power cannot be comprehended: great things doeth he, which we cannot comprehend; touching the Almighty, we cannot find him out. Stop trying to figure the Creator out and questioning why he created what he created; you are the creation, so keep the commandments and play your role. Neither will I be with you any more, except ye destroy the accursed from among you: what is accursed must be destroyed; that is the only way to remove it.

Up, sanctify the people against tomorrow: there is an accursed thing in the midst of thee, O Israel; thou canst not stand before thine enemies until ye take away the accursed thing from among you. The search would narrow by the Lord's own taking: tribe, then family, then household, then man by man; and he that is taken with the accursed thing shall be burnt with fire, he and all that he hath. The folly was wrought against a plain commandment: Joshua had already charged them in [Joshua 6:18-19](/bible/joshua/6#v18) to keep from the accursed thing lest they trouble the camp, and adjured them in [Joshua 6:26](/bible/joshua/6#v26); the transgressor troubled the camp, the army and congregation of Israel.

Joshua rose up early and brought Israel by their tribes, and the tribe of Judah was taken; then the family of the Zarhites, then the household of Zabdi man by man, and Achan the son of Carmi, the son of Zabdi, the son of Zerah, of the tribe of Judah, was taken.

My son, give, I pray thee, glory to the Lord God of Israel, and make confession unto him; and tell me now what thou hast done; hide it not from me. Joshua said hide it not from me because it was already not hidden from One mightier than he: we cannot hide what we do from the Lord. The eyes of the Lord are in every place, beholding the evil and the good; he sees everything we do. If you are in this walk as a manpleaser, the Lord sees what you do away from the brotherhood and the sisterhood. The Lord gives a dispensation of time and grace to get the mind right, to repent, pray, and fast over what we struggle with; the just man falleth seven times and riseth up again. When leadership corrects you, do not think evil of them: the Lord did not have to send leadership, he could have sent evil your way instead; correction is the warning and the mercy.

Achan confessed: indeed I have sinned against the Lord God of Israel. He saw among the spoils a goodly Babylonish garment, two hundred shekels of silver, and a wedge of gold of fifty shekels weight; he coveted them, took them, and hid them in the earth in the midst of his tent. Joshua had said all the silver and gold and vessels were consecrated unto the Lord for his treasury, so Achan was not stealing from men; he was literally stealing from the Most High. I coveted them: covetousness is the last of the ten commandments, and as a father saves the weightiest warning for last but not least, the Lord ends the ten with thou shalt not covet. To covet is to carry the spirit of jealousy and envy, and there is not a more wicked thing than a covetous man: he sets his own soul to sale, selling out his dignity and self-respect to fulfil his desires no matter what it takes.

Joshua sent messengers, and they ran unto the tent, and behold, it was hid in his tent, and the silver under it; they laid it all out before the Lord with the whole congregation present. The Lord revealed it, and the scripture cannot be broken: as Jericho was made a curse, so the one who took of it. Joshua and all Israel took Achan, the silver, the garment, the wedge of gold, and his sons, and his daughters, and his oxen, asses, sheep, tent, and all that he had, unto the valley of Achor. His sons and daughters did not steal it, yet because he lacked knowledge and understanding they paid for the covetous spirit he carried. Why hast thou troubled us? the Lord shall trouble thee this day. Achan was the reason men died in that battle and the nation was nearly overtaken; his selfish, individual spirit never weighed what his family would pay. All Israel stoned him with stones, and burned them with fire, after they had stoned them with stones: them, because his household went with him. My people are destroyed for lack of knowledge: reject knowledge and the Lord will reject thee, and the end of [Hosea 4:6](/bible/hosea/4#v6) that we seldom quote says, I will also forget thy children. The Lord hits where it hurts, and your sin reaches your children, your wife, your husband, your brothers and sisters. It is a fearful thing to fall into the hands of the living God, and that is where Achan fell, and unfortunately his sons and daughters and all he had with him. Some of our people in the islands and elsewhere still ignorantly carry out such public executions to this day; we do not condone it, for we are not under the law of sacrifice now but under grace, and the judgment is of the Lord. Consider the contrast that closes these chapters: Achan, an Israelite of Judah, lacked faith and was put to death, while Rahab the Canaanite harlot was saved alive for her faith. When Israel will not obey his voice, the Lord likens the house of Judah unto all the heathen; so we must have the fear of the Lord in our hearts. They raised over him a great heap of stones unto this day, and the Lord turned from the fierceness of his anger; wherefore the name of that place was called the valley of Achor unto this day.

Joshua called the Reubenites, the Gadites, and the half tribe of Manasseh and told them they had kept all that Moses commanded them and obeyed his voice; they had not left their brethren these many days, but kept the charge of the commandment of the Most High. The charge was the condition Moses set when these two and a half tribes asked to stay on the other side Jordan: whenever it was time to go to war they had to show up and fight with their brethren, not sit over there while Israel took the land.

Now that the Most High had given rest to their brethren as he promised, there was no war going on, so Joshua sent them home: return ye unto your tents and unto the land of your possession which Moses gave you on the other side Jordan. The release came with a charge: take diligent heed to do the commandment and the law, to love the Lord your God, to walk in all his ways, to keep his commandments, to cleave unto him, and to serve him with all your heart and all your soul. Rest did not end the duty; if their brethren ever needed them again they had to show up, as all the tribes did show up later in this same chapter.

Joshua blessed them and sent them away rich: return with much riches unto your tents, with very much cattle, with silver, gold, brass, iron, and very much raiment, and divide the spoil of your enemies with your brethren. The children of Reuben, the children of Gad, and the half tribe of Manasseh departed from Shiloh in the land of Canaan to go into the country of Gilead, the land of their possession according to the word of the Lord by the hand of Moses.

When the two and a half tribes came to the borders of Jordan they built a great altar by Jordan, an altar great to see to. They hid nothing; they built it on purpose so that it could be seen. When the children of Israel heard of it, the whole congregation gathered themselves together at Shiloh to go up to war against them. They thought the two and a half tribes had built the altar to worship idols and do their own thing, and they were ready to cleanse it before judgment fell on the whole nation like it had before.

Israel sent Phinehas the son of Eleazar the priest with ten princes, one head of a chief house from every tribe. When you send Phinehas it is a problem, because of the kind of man Phinehas was: where he showed up, the zeal of the Most High showed up with him. At Baalpeor the men of Israel began to commit whoredom with the daughters of Moab, bowed down to their gods, and joined themselves unto Baalpeor, and the anger of the Most High was kindled against Israel. One man of Israel was so bold he brought a Midianitish woman to his brethren in the sight of Moses and all the congregation while they wept before the door of the tabernacle. It was once a shameful thing for our men to be seen like that; today men and women of Israel walk boldly and proudly with the nations, that same spirit. Phinehas saw it, rose up from among the congregation, took a javelin, went after the man of Israel into the tent, and thrust both of them through, and the plague was stayed from the children of Israel; those that died in the plague were twenty and four thousand. So when Phinehas showed up at Gilead, everybody knew it was about to go down.

The delegation asked what trespass is this that ye have committed against the God of Israel, to build you an altar that ye might rebel this day against the Lord. They saw the altar and immediately thought the two and a half tribes were going into idolatry. Is the iniquity of Peor too little for us? All those thousands died in that plague, and Israel had just gotten into the land and gotten peace; why would anyone bring that thing back on the nation again? Their reasoning was national: if ye rebel today against the Lord, tomorrow he will be wroth with the whole congregation of Israel. Judgment does not fall on pieces of the nation; [Deuteronomy 28](/bible/deuteronomy/28) happened to all of us, and they understood that, so they showed up quick, fast, and in a hurry rather than sit around and let it happen.

They even offered their own land: if the land of your possession be unclean, pass ye over unto the land of the possession of the Lord and take possession among us, close by where we can keep an eye on you; only rebel not against the Lord, nor build you an altar beside the altar of the Lord our God. They cited the proof from their own history: did not Achan the son of Zerah commit a trespass in the accursed thing, and wrath fell on all the congregation of Israel, and that man perished not alone in his iniquity. One man trespassed and the whole nation felt it.

The two and a half tribes answered: the LORD God of gods, the LORD God of gods, he knoweth, and Israel he shall know; if it be in rebellion or in transgression against the Lord, save us not this day. They put their own lives on the line: if we built this thing in rebellion, put us to death today. If we built an altar to turn from following the Lord, or to offer burnt offerings, meat offerings, or peace offerings on it, let the Lord himself require it.

This is why they built it: for fear of this thing, that in time to come your children might speak unto our children, saying, What have ye to do with the LORD God of Israel? The Lord hath made Jordan a border between us and you; ye have no part in the LORD. They feared that generations later the children on one side of Jordan would tell the children on the other side that they were not the children of Israel, shutting them out from fearing the Lord, from the temple, the feast days, and the sacrifices.

The altar was not for burnt offering nor for sacrifice; it was a witness between us and you and our generations after us, a memorial, so the two and a half tribes could do the service of the Lord before him in the place he chose, along with the rest of the tribes, and nobody could stop them. If anyone ever said to their generations, Ye have no part in the Lord, the answer would stand built in stone: behold the pattern of the altar of the LORD, which our fathers made, not for burnt offerings nor for sacrifices, but it is a witness between us and you. The same thing is happening today with the northern kingdom. Our people left their own witnesses over here: the writings on the Los Lunas stone identify with the northern kingdom, and the traditions, artifacts, practices, laws, and books that are being brought out in the classes all prove our people were here long ago and that they are the children of Israel. Yet with all that proof out there, people still deny it, the very thing the two and a half tribes feared. Nobody else could have built that altar to the pattern of the altar of the Lord, because no other nation was keeping the laws; only Israel keeps the precepts, not the heathen. That is why the memorial could stand as identification.

When Phinehas and the princes heard the words of the children of Reuben, Gad, and Manasseh, it pleased them. Phinehas said, This day we perceive that the LORD is among us, because ye have not committed this trespass against the Lord. Now ye have delivered the children of Israel out of the hand of the LORD: because they were not going off, nobody had to die that day, and coming from Phinehas that meant everything, because if it had been rebellion he would have been the one to start it.

Phinehas and the princes returned from Gilead to the land of Canaan and brought the children of Israel word again: all is good, the altar is a memorial so the generations after do not forget that our people are on that side Jordan too, and they can come in and keep the feasts and do their sacrifices with us. The thing pleased the children of Israel; they blessed God, dismantled from war, and did not go up to destroy the land where the children of Reuben and Gad dwelt. The children of Reuben and Gad called the altar Ed: for it shall be a witness between us that the LORD is God.

name: The Gibeonites, and Israel's oath
charge: Obtaining a covenant by fraud; Israel making it without asking counsel of the Lord
summary: The Gibeonites came to Joshua in old clothes with moldy bread claiming to be from a far country, and Israel made peace with them. Three days later the fraud was found out. The oath stood anyway.
offense: Two offenses, and the record weighs Israel's as the heavier. The Gibeonites were Hivites, one of the nations named for destruction in the same chapter (Joshua 9:1, 7), and their only hope was to pretend they were not, so they did work wilily, with old sacks upon their asses, wine bottles old and rent, old shoes and old garments, and bread dry and mouldy (Joshua 9:4-5), and said, we be come from a far country, now therefore make ye a league with us (Joshua 9:6). They leaned on the fame of the Most High to sell it: from a very far country thy servants are come because of the name of the Lord thy God, for we have heard the fame of him, and all that he did in Egypt (Joshua 9:9). The props sold the story. Israel's fault is set down in one clause and it is the whole of it: and the men took of their victuals, and asked not counsel at the mouth of the Lord (Joshua 9:14). They were suspicious, they asked the right questions, and then they reasoned it out among themselves instead of inquiring, which is exactly what the proverb forbids: trust in the Lord with all thine heart, and lean not unto thine own understanding, in all thy ways acknowledge him (Proverbs 3:5-6). The league the law forbade with the inhabitants of the land (Exodus 23:32; Deuteronomy 20:16-17) was made through not asking, and it became a snare and a trap to the nation for centuries after.
judgment: Because the princes had sworn by the Lord, the Gibeonites could not be killed, but were made hewers of wood and drawers of water for the congregation and the altar. Centuries later, when Saul broke that oath, God sent famine on Israel for it.

entries.commentary: The kings on this side Jordan, in the hills, in the valleys, and in all the coasts of the great sea over against Lebanon: the Hittite, the Amorite, the Canaanite, the Perizzite, the Hivite, and the Jebusite. These are Hamites, better known as Nilotic Africans. When they heard what had been done, they gathered themselves together to fight with Joshua and with Israel with one accord.

The inhabitants of Gibeon heard what Joshua had done to Jericho and to Ai, and they did work wilily: they made as if they had been ambassadors, with old sacks upon their asses, wine bottles old and rent and bound up, old shoes and old garments, and bread dry and mouldy. They came to Joshua at the camp at Gilgal saying, We be come from a far country: now therefore make ye a league with us. Israel was commanded to destroy all the inhabitants of the land, the very nations listed in verse 1, so the Gibeonites' only hope was to pretend they were not of the land.

The men of Israel were suspicious at first: peradventure ye dwell among us, and how shall we make a league with you? Joshua pressed them, Who are ye, and from whence come ye? The Gibeonites leaned on the fame of the Most High: we have heard all that he did in Egypt, and to Sihon king of Heshbon and Og king of Bashan, the two kings of the Amorites beyond Jordan. Their props sold the story. In ancient times wine did not come in bottles like ours; wine came in bags, sometimes made of leather, and they would rend through wear and tear over time.

The men took of their victuals, and asked not counsel at the mouth of the LORD. That is the first mistake, and not asking counsel of the Most High at this moment ended up being a snare and a trap to us as a people, as the rest of the scriptures show. Let reason think on whether it is the right move, and even before you reason within yourself, the Most High says counsel, counsel, counsel before every action. This type of ordeal will play out again in the times when Christ returns: the sons of strangers shall come to build up Israel's walls, their kings shall minister unto Israel, and the nation and kingdom that will not serve thee shall perish. There is nothing new under the sun.

At the end of three days Israel heard that they were their neighbours, dwelling among them. The children of Israel smote them not, because the princes of the congregation had sworn unto them by the LORD God of Israel. All the congregation murmured against the princes, but the princes held the line: we have sworn unto them by the LORD God of Israel, now therefore we may not touch them. Our forefathers were wrong in one situation, but they were upright men in holding up to their word.

We will even let them live, lest wrath be upon us, because of the oath which we sware unto them. A vow made before the Most High stands, even one gotten by guile. Let them be hewers of wood and drawers of water unto all the congregation. Hewers of wood and drawers of water means slaves. This is according to the law of the Most High pertaining to other nations. If you just read the Old Testament, there was no equality among the nations, and there is still no equality among nations: they were made for a certain purpose. The reason they are not in that purpose now is because we have sinned and failed, and one day Israel will rise again to put them back in their rightful places.

Joshua called for them: wherefore have ye beguiled us, saying, We are very far from you, when ye dwell among us? Now therefore ye are cursed, and there shall none of you be freed from being bondmen, and hewers of wood and drawers of water for the house of my God. They were servants all the way up and through.

The Gibeonites answered honestly: it was certainly told thy servants how the LORD thy God commanded his servant Moses to give you all the land and to destroy all the inhabitants, therefore we were sore afraid of our lives because of you. Behold, we are in thine hand. So did he unto them, and delivered them out of the hand of the children of Israel, that they slew them not; and Joshua made them that day hewers of wood and drawers of water for the congregation and for the altar of the LORD, even unto this day.

When thou goest out to battle and seest horses and chariots and a people more than thou, be not afraid, for the Lord thy God is with thee, which brought thee up out of the land of Egypt. That goes for us now, because we are still in a battle. We are not physically out battling the nations as our forefathers were when they took the land; we are in a spiritual battle, for the nations are confederate against Israel being a nation any more and against our remembrance of Israel and our laws. This whole world is set up for our people to go into sin and iniquity. Fear makes people trim their ways: afraid of family at the pagan holiday table, tucking their fringes in certain places, scared to be seen in the truth. Stand boldly; the Lord has not given us the spirit of fear, for that spirit came from Satan himself.

When Israel came nigh unto the battle, the priest approached and spoke: let not your hearts faint, fear not, do not tremble, neither be ye terrified, for the Lord your God is he that goeth with you to fight for you against your enemies to save you. A lot of times you do not see that the Lord is fighting for you in the spirit; that is where faith comes in, for the Bible is a faith-based book. You have to have faith that the Most High is fighting for you, with angels encamped round about the righteous, as David told us.

The officers sent home the man that had built a new house and not dedicated it, the man that had planted a vineyard and not eaten of it, and the man that had betrothed a wife and not taken her, lest he die in the battle and another man take his portion. You could very well die fighting for your people, so go enjoy these things first: dedicate your new house unto the Lord, eat the fruits of your labour from your vineyard, take your wife, then come to war for your people.

The fearful and fainthearted man was also sent home, lest his brethren's heart faint as well as his heart. The spirit of fear spreads: one man's fear makes the next man wonder what he knows, and soon the whole company questions the battle.

When the officers finished speaking, they made captains of the armies to lead the people, because you cannot have order without a ranking structure. Everybody cannot be calling the shots; there is one shot caller and the people follow, and that same order set in Moses' time is why a body under rank is proficient in everything it does.

When thou comest nigh unto a city to fight against it, first proclaim peace unto it. If it answered peace and opened, all the people found in it became tributaries unto Israel and served them. In this time Israel had the power to make nations tributaries. Right now we are not even a nation, just a people with Bibles and nothing established; but wait until Christ comes, for Israel will be established as a nation again and rule the earth, and the nations will be tributaries.

Israel came to a land with terms: agree, pay the tribute, and there is peace. If the city would make no peace but made war, Israel besieged it, and when the Lord delivered it into their hands, every male was smitten with the edge of the sword. The women, the little ones, the cattle, and all the spoil of the city Israel took unto themselves and ate the spoil of their enemies which the Lord their God had given them.

That was the rule for the cities very far off. But of the cities of the nations given Israel for an inheritance, thou shalt save alive nothing that breatheth; everything had to die, from humans to animals. The Hittites, the Amorites, the Canaanites, the Perizzites, the Hivites, and the Jebusites were to be utterly destroyed for a stated purpose: that they teach you not to do after all their abominations which they have done unto their gods, their whoredoms, their idolatry, and their wicked ways of living, so that Israel sin not against the Lord.

In a long siege the trees for meat were not to be destroyed by forcing an axe against them, for thou mayest eat of them; the tree of the field is man's life. Only the trees known not to be trees for meat could be cut down to build bulwarks against the city that maketh war with thee, until it be subdued.

Thou shalt not raise a false report, nor put thine hand with the wicked to be an unrighteous witness: basically, thou shalt not lie. If you did not see it, do not make up a story like you were there; keep your mouth shut. Thou shalt not follow a multitude to do evil. Enter not into the path of the wicked; sinners entice, saying come with us, cast in thy lot among us, but walk not thou in the way with them, for their feet run to evil and make haste to shed blood. Many of our young men's lives end short because they follow a multitude to do evil. To be in the midst of the singing, like the whole school hollering fight, fight, fight, is to be in the multitude the Most High warns of; a soul without knowledge of the laws of God hastes with his feet and sins.

Neither shalt thou countenance a poor man in his cause. This deals with judgment: do not be a respecter of persons because a man is poor, as if he is automatically wrong when he brings a matter against a rich man. The judges were charged to hear the small as well as the great. In this corrupt system in Babylon, how innocent or guilty you come out depends on how much lawyer you can afford. Our law was holy and righteous because none of that made a difference: either you were right or you were wrong, whether poor or rich. The Pharisees learned the ways of the heathen and began respecting persons, which the book of James speaks against.

If thou meet thine enemy's ox or his ass going astray, thou shalt surely bring it back to him again; if thou see the ass of him that hateth thee lying under his burden, thou shalt surely help with him. This enemy that hates you is your brother, your own nation, not the other nations as [Matthew 5:44](/bible/matthew/5#v44) is misconstrued to mean. [Deuteronomy 22:1-4](/bible/deuteronomy/22#v1) proves it, saying the same law with thy brother in the place of thine enemy: thou shalt not see thy brother's ox or sheep go astray; in any case, no matter how you feel, bring them again unto thy brother. And if thou know him not, keep it in thine own house until thy brother seek after it. He is still your brother even if you never grew up with him; that is real love for your own people. Deuteronomy means the second law; it speaks the law plain in case you did not understand it here. Keep [Deuteronomy 22:1-4](/bible/deuteronomy/22#v1) and [Leviticus 19:17-18](/bible/leviticus/19#v17) in your hip pocket with this verse.

Thou shalt not wrest the judgment of thy poor in his cause: verse six explains verse three again in case you did not catch it, do not be partial in judgment. Keep thee far from a false matter; the innocent and righteous slay thou not, for the Most High will not justify the wicked. Thou shalt take no gift, for the gift blindeth the wise and perverteth the words of the righteous: do not take a bribe when it comes to judgment; be upright and honest.

Also thou shalt not oppress a stranger, for ye know the heart of a stranger, seeing ye were strangers in the land of Egypt. This is speaking about us, as [Exodus 22:21](/bible/exodus/22#v21) already laid out with [Leviticus 25:35](/bible/leviticus/25#v35).

Six years thou shalt sow thy land, but the seventh year thou shalt let it rest and lie still, that the poor of thy people may eat, and the beasts of the field after them; likewise the vineyard and the oliveyard. That is mercy from the Lord: in the seventh year the land itself fed the poor. The seventh year ties into the count of the jubilee: seven sabbaths of years to the forty-ninth year, and in the fiftieth year no plowing of the land, which the law takes up later.

Six days do thy work, and on the seventh day rest, that thine ox and thine ass may rest, and the son of thy handmaid and the stranger may be refreshed. The stranger here can be another nation working for you: they too get their due rest on the sabbath. When the Lord sets Israel back up to rule, the nations will kick and scream at first, but once these laws are applied there will be righteousness reigning over the earth like they have never seen, and all will be refreshed on the sabbath, spiritually and physically.

Make no mention of the name of other gods is not saying you cannot pronounce the names Buddha, Allah, Krishna, Ra. Christ himself named Beelzebub, the chief of the devils, a name derived from the Philistine god of Ekron, and Christ did no sin; so the verse cannot mean the bare saying of a name. The Lord says this same thing three ways in this one chapter, and the other two places show the meaning: verse 24, thou shalt not bow down to their gods nor serve them nor do after their works; and verses 32 and 33, thou shalt make no covenant with them nor with their gods, for if thou serve their gods it will surely be a snare unto thee. Make no mention means do not learn how to serve and worship them. Joshua and Deuteronomy double it: neither make mention of the name of their gods, nor cause to swear by them, neither serve them, nor bow yourselves unto them; and if thy brother or son or wife entice thee secretly, saying, Let us go and serve other gods, thou shalt not consent. Wherever you are, do not go trying to find out how the nations worship their gods.

Three times thou shalt keep a feast unto me in the year: all the males appeared before the Lord God three times in the year. The feast of unleavened bread is the Passover, kept in the time appointed of the month Abib, the first month of the year, as it is written, the feast of unleavened bread drew nigh, which is called the Passover. None shall appear before me empty: you could not come empty-handed. You brought the tenth of your oil, your wine, whatever was required, for the priests to replenish the storehouses. The feast of harvest, the firstfruits of thy labours, is also known as Pentecost and the feast of weeks; and the feast of ingathering, in the end of the year, is also known as the feast of tabernacles and the feast of booths.

Thou shalt not offer the blood of my sacrifice with leavened bread, neither shall the fat of my sacrifice remain until the morning. The first of the firstfruits of thy land thou shalt bring into the house of the Lord thy God. Thou shalt not seethe a kid in his mother's milk: the Lord repeats what was read at [Exodus 22:30](/bible/exodus/22#v30), that the young one was not to be taken too young and too soon; it stayed its seven days with his dam before it was given.

Behold, I send an Angel before thee, to keep thee in the way and to bring thee into the place which I have prepared. Beware of him, obey his voice, provoke him not, for he will not pardon your transgressions: for my name is in him. That Angel is speaking of Christ. If thou indeed obey his voice, I will be an enemy unto thine enemies and an adversary unto thine adversaries. These enemies are not the same enemy of verse four: the enemy of verse four is your brother whom you must help and shew mercy; these enemies in verse 22 the Lord himself deals with and destroys for you.

The Angel goes before Israel unto the Amorites, Hittites, Perizzites, Canaanites, Hivites, and Jebusites, to cut them off. Thou shalt not bow down to their gods nor serve them nor do after their works, but utterly overthrow them and quite break down their images. Serve the Lord your God, and he shall bless thy bread and thy water, take sickness away from the midst of thee, none casting their young nor barren in the land, and the number of thy days he will fulfil. He drives the nations out by little and little, lest the land become desolate and the beasts multiply, until Israel be increased and inherit the land. The bounds are set from the Red Sea even unto the sea of the Philistines, and from the desert unto the river, the river Euphrates. That little sliver on the map today is not how big Israel is supposed to be: the land was to encompass all the way out to the Euphrates by Babylon, taking in parts of what is Iraq and Iran, and it will be filled one day.

Thou shalt make no covenant with them, nor with their gods. They shall not dwell in thy land, lest they make thee sin against me: for if thou serve their gods, it will surely be a snare unto thee. This is the third way the Lord states the command of verse 13 in this chapter: no learning their worship, no serving, no covenant.

There was a famine in the days of David, three years, year after year, and David inquired of the Lord. The Lord answered that it was for Saul and for his bloody house, because he slew the Gibeonites. Saul broke his word. The Gibeonites were not of the children of Israel but of the remnant of the Amorites, and Israel had sworn unto them, yet Saul sought to slay them in his zeal. David asked the Gibeonites what he should do and wherewith he should make the atonement. The blessing was not truly coming from the Gibeonites who are of Ammon; it was coming from the Most High, who was teaching Israel a lesson through this famine. The Gibeonites would take no silver nor gold of Saul nor of his house, but asked for seven of Saul's sons to be hanged unto the Lord in Gibeah of Saul. The lesson the Most High is teaching Israel here is to pay what you vow. Let your yea be yea and your nay be nay; Saul went back on his word after he had given his yea to the Amorites, and the whole house paid for it.

The king spared Mephibosheth, the son of Jonathan, the son of Saul, because of the Lord's oath that was between David and Jonathan. David did not go back on his oath; earlier he had promised Jonathan that his seed would always eat at David's table as long as there was family of the lineage of Jonathan. But the king took the two sons of Rizpah and the five sons of Michal and delivered them into the hands of the Gibeonites, and they hanged them in the hill before the Lord. They fell all seven together and were put to death in the days of harvest, in the first days, in the beginning of barley harvest.

Rizpah, the daughter of Aiah, took sackcloth and spread it upon the rock from the beginning of harvest until water dropped upon them out of heaven, and she suffered neither the birds of the air by day nor the beasts of the field by night to touch them. When David was told, he went and took the bones of Saul and Jonathan from the men of Jabesh-gilead, which had stolen them from the street of Beth-shan where the Philistines had hanged them when Saul was slain in Gilboa. Jonathan's body had been hanged in the temple of Dagon, the fish god of the Hamites. David buried the bones of Saul and Jonathan in the country of Benjamin in Zelah, in the sepulchre of Kish his father, and performed all that the king commanded. After that the Most High was entreated for the land.

The Philistines had war again with Israel, and David went down and waxed faint. Ishbi-benob, of the sons of the giant, thought to slay him, but Abishai the son of Zeruiah succoured him and killed the Philistine. Then the men of David swore that he should go no more out with them to battle, that he quench not the light of Israel; he was getting up in age and it was time to sit on the throne. There were further battles at Gob and at Gath. Sibbechai slew Sippai, Elhanan slew the brother of Goliath the Gittite whose spear staff was like a weaver's beam, and Jonathan the son of Shimeah, David's brother, slew a man of great stature with six fingers on every hand and six toes on every foot. These four were born to the giant in Gath and fell by the hand of David and his servants. These giants were tall men, one about eight or nine feet, not the twenty foot giants of fairy tales. Goliath had kin, and eventually they were all served by David and his servants.

name: The five kings at Makkedah
charge: Confederating against Gibeon for making peace with Israel
summary: Five Amorite kings joined to punish Gibeon for coming to terms with Joshua. Israel came up all night from Gilgal, the Lord cast great stones from heaven on them, and the sun stood still. The five fled into a cave at Makkedah. Joshua had great stones rolled on the mouth of it and posted men, finished the battle, and then brought them out, had the captains put their feet on their necks, and hanged them on five trees until evening.
offense: The attack was on Gibeon rather than on Israel (Joshua 10:1), and Gibeon's only offense was making peace. The record gives their motive as fear, because Gibeon was a great city and the men of it mighty (Joshua 10:2), and states the aggression plainly: they came up and encamped against Gibeon, and made war against it. Israel was bound by an oath to defend the city, an oath obtained by deceit and entered separately in this volume, so the campaign is Israel keeping a covenant it had been tricked into.
judgment: The Lord discomfited them, and more died from the hailstones than Israel killed with the sword (Joshua 10:11). They were taken alive from the cave, and the treading on their necks was done in front of the army with the words spoken over it, fear not, nor be dismayed, be strong and of good courage, for thus shall the Lord do to all your enemies (Joshua 10:25). They were hanged on five trees and taken down at sundown (Joshua 10:26), which is Deuteronomy 21 kept exactly in the middle of a war, and the stones that had shut them in the cave were rolled back over their bodies (Deuteronomy 21:22-23).

name: Othniel and Achsah
charge: Taking Kirjath-sepher at Caleb's word; and asking for the springs as well as the land
summary: Caleb offered his daughter to whoever would smite Kirjath-sepher and take it. His younger brother's son Othniel took it and was given her. As she came to him she moved him to ask her father for a field, and lighted off her ass, and Caleb said, What wouldest thou? She asked for a blessing: thou hast given me a south land, give me also springs of water. He gave her the upper springs and the nether springs. Othniel became the first judge of Israel.
offense: Two obediences, one of arms and one of speech. Othniel took a fortified city on the strength of a word rather than a strategy (Joshua 15:17). Achsah's is the more instructive: she had been given a portion in the dry south (Joshua 15:19), which was a lawful gift and an insufficient one, and rather than resent it she got down off the ass and asked, framing the request as a blessing rather than a complaint, thou hast given me a south land, give me also springs of water. She asked the right person, at the right moment, for the thing the land actually needed.
judgment: He gave her the upper springs and the nether springs (Joshua 15:19), which is more than she asked for, and the detail is repeated in Joshua and in Judges so that the record carries it twice (Joshua 15:16-19). Othniel afterwards had the Spirit of the Lord come upon him (Judges 3:9), judged Israel, went out to war, and the land had rest forty years (Judges 3:11). The first deliverer in the book of Judges came out of a household in (Judges 1:1) which a daughter asked well and a father gave more than was requested (Joshua 15:13).

verses.text: 16And Caleb said, He that smiteth Kirjath–sepher, and taketh it, to him will I give Achsah my daughter to wife. 17And Othniel the son of Kenaz, the brother of Caleb, took it: and he gave him Achsah his daughter to wife. 18And it came to pass, as she came unto him, that she moved him to ask of her father a field: and she lighted off her ass; and Caleb said unto her, What wouldest thou? 19Who answered, Give me a blessing; for thou hast given me a south land; give me also springs of water. And he gave her the upper springs, and the nether springs.

12And Caleb said, He that smiteth Kirjath–sepher, and taketh it, to him will I give Achsah my daughter to wife. 13And Othniel the son of Kenaz, Caleb’s younger brother, took it: and he gave him Achsah his daughter to wife. 14And it came to pass, when she came to him, that she moved him to ask of her father a field: and she lighted from off her ass; and Caleb said unto her, What wilt thou? 15And she said unto him, Give me a blessing: for thou hast given me a south land; give me also springs of water. And Caleb gave her the upper springs and the nether springs.

entries.commentary: This is the lot of the tribe of the children of Judah by their families, even to the border of Edom: the south border ran from the shore of the salt sea, up the south side of Kadeshbarnea, and out unto the river of Egypt, with the goings out of that coast at the sea. We are not locating every one of these places as we read, but as you go back and listen, look these places up in your Bible atlas so you can see the actual areas being read about in the region.

The east border was the salt sea unto the end of Jordan; the north border went up from the bay of the sea, by Bethhogla and the stone of Bohan the son of Reuben, and up by the valley of the son of Hinnom unto the south side of the Jebusite: the same is Jerusalem. The border went to the top of the mountain before the valley of Hinnom westward, at the end of the valley of the giants northward, then out by Kirjathjearim, Bethshemesh, and Ekron, and the west border was to the great sea. This is the coast of the children of Judah round about according to their families.

Unto Caleb the son of Jephunneh was given a part among the children of Judah according to the commandment of the Lord to Joshua: the city of Arba the father of Anak, which city is Hebron. And Caleb drove thence the three sons of Anak: Sheshai, and Ahiman, and Talmai, the children of Anak. He went up thence to the inhabitants of Debir, whose name before was Kirjathsepher, and said, he that smiteth Kirjathsepher and taketh it, to him will I give Achsah my daughter to wife. Othniel the son of Kenaz, the brother of Caleb, took it, and got Achsah to wife. Achsah moved him to ask of her father a field, and said, give me a blessing, for thou hast given me a south land; give me also springs of water. And Caleb gave her the upper springs and the nether springs.

This is the inheritance of the tribe of the children of Judah according to their families, and the chapter counts out their cities district by district through verse 62: the uttermost cities toward the coast of Edom southward, twenty and nine cities with their villages; the cities in the valley in their groups of fourteen, sixteen, and nine; Ekron, Ashdod, and Gaza with their towns and villages unto the river of Egypt and the great sea; the cities in the mountains in their groups of eleven, nine, ten, six, and two; and six cities in the wilderness, all with their villages.

As for the Jebusites, the inhabitants of Jerusalem, the children of Judah could not drive them out, but the Jebusites dwell with the children of Judah at Jerusalem unto this day. Later on David conquered this place. The Jebusites thought David could not come in, that he was not getting past those walls, saying except thou take away the blind and the lame thou shalt not come in hither; nevertheless David took the stronghold of Zion, the same is the city of David, and dwelt in the fort and built round about. The people that were left of the Amorites, Hittites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites, whom Israel was not able utterly to destroy, upon those did Solomon levy a tribute of bondservice unto this day. They were forced to become our bondservants.

After the death of Joshua the children of Israel ask the Most High who shall go up first against the Canaanites, and the answer is Judah: behold, I have delivered the land into his hand. Judah asks Simeon his brother to come up with him into his lot, and promises to go likewise with Simeon into his lot, so Simeon went with him.

The Most High delivers the Canaanites and the Perizzites into Judah's hand, and they slay ten thousand men in Bezek. Adonibezek flees and is caught, and his thumbs and great toes are cut off. He confesses it himself: threescore and ten kings with their thumbs and great toes cut off gathered their meat under his table, and as he had done, so God requited him.

The children of Judah fought against Jerusalem, took it, smote it with the edge of the sword, and set the city on fire. This verse ties back into the history we just finished reading in Joshua. Judah was supposed to drive the Jebusites, the inhabitants of Jerusalem, out of the land, but could not, and the Jebusites dwelt with the children of Judah at Jerusalem. Jerusalem sat right on Judah's border by the valley of the son of Hinnom. The king of Jerusalem was already among the kings of the land which the children of Israel smote and whose land they possessed, so this fight in Judges is Judah taking the city itself.

Judah goes down against the Canaanites in the mountain, the south, and the valley, and against Hebron, which before was called Kirjath-arba, slaying Sheshai, Ahiman, and Talmai. Caleb offers Achsah his daughter to wife to whoever smites Kirjath-sepher, and Othniel the son of Kenaz, Caleb's younger brother, takes it. Achsah asks her father for a blessing, springs of water with the south land, and Caleb gives her the upper springs and the nether springs. This is a review of the history we just read in Joshua; it was not that many days ago in the reading that we covered this, and it repeats again here at the opening of Judges.

The children of the Kenite, Moses' father in law, go up out of the city of palm trees with the children of Judah and dwell among the people in the wilderness of Judah. Judah goes with Simeon his brother, slays the Canaanites in Zephath and utterly destroys it, calling the city Hormah, and takes Gaza, Askelon, and Ekron with their coasts. The Most High was with Judah, and he drave out the inhabitants of the mountain, but could not drive out the inhabitants of the valley, because they had chariots of iron.

Hebron is given unto Caleb, as Moses said, and he expels thence the three sons of Anak. The children of Benjamin did not drive out the Jebusites that inhabited Jerusalem, but the Jebusites dwell with the children of Benjamin in Jerusalem unto this day.

The house of Joseph goes up against Bethel, which before was called Luz, and the Most High was with them. The spies see a man come out of the city and promise him mercy for showing the entrance. They smite the city with the edge of the sword, but let the man and all his family go, and he goes into the land of the Hittites and builds a city and calls it Luz.

Tribe after tribe repeats the same failure: neither did Manasseh, nor Ephraim, nor Zebulun, nor Asher, nor Naphtali drive out the inhabitants of their cities, and the Amorites forced the children of Dan into the mountain. What we are reading is how we did not drive out all the inhabitants of the land, which the Most High had commanded us. Each tribe did not drive them out, and what did we do? We dwelt among them. When Israel was strong, we put the Canaanites to tribute, but we still did not utterly drive them out; we still dwelt among them. Chapter 2 gets into what that dwelling among the inhabitants of the land brought upon us.

name: Adoni-bezek
charge: Mutilating seventy kings
summary: Judah defeated the Canaanite king Adoni-bezek and cut off his thumbs and great toes. He said it himself: seventy kings with thumbs and toes cut off had gathered their meat under my table; as I have done, so God hath requited me.
offense: Judah went up first at the Lord's word, with Simeon his brother, and the Lord delivered the Canaanites and the Perizzites into their hand, and they slew ten thousand men in Bezek (Judges 1:1-4). The king who fled from that field had made a practice of mutilation and counted it as his glory. He says the number himself: threescore and ten kings, having their thumbs and their great toes cut off, gathered their meat under my table (Judges 1:7). Seventy kings maimed so that they could neither hold a sword nor stand in a rank, kept alive to eat scraps as a display of his power. The law of Israel limits punishment to measure, breach for breach, eye for eye, tooth for tooth, as he hath caused a blemish in a man, so shall it be done to him again (Leviticus 24:19-20); he had exceeded all measure seventy times.
judgment: They pursued after him, and caught him, and cut off his thumbs and his great toes (Judges 1:6): the same mutilation, once. The verdict is pronounced by the condemned man himself, and the record leaves it in his mouth: as I have done, so God hath requited me (Judges 1:7). A Canaanite king recognised the measure of the God of Israel from his own case and named it as justice. They brought him to Jerusalem, and there he died (Judges 1:7). Christ states the rule he fell under as a rule for everyone: with what measure ye mete, it shall be measured to you again (Matthew 7:2).

verses.text: 5And they found Adoni–bezek in Bezek: and they fought against him, and they slew the Canaanites and the Perizzites. 6But Adoni–bezek fled; and they pursued after him, and caught him, and cut off his thumbs and his great toes. 7And Adoni–bezek said, Threescore and ten kings, having their thumbs and their great toes cut off, gathered their meat under my table: as I have done, so God hath requited me. And they brought him to Jerusalem, and there he died.

19And if a man cause a blemish in his neighbour; as he hath done, so shall it be done to him; 20Breach for breach, eye for eye, tooth for tooth: as he hath caused a blemish in a man, so shall it be done to him again.
23And if any mischief follow, then thou shalt give life for life, 24Eye for eye, tooth for tooth, hand for hand, foot for foot, 25Burning for burning, wound for wound, stripe for stripe.

lawDetails.text: The restitution and punishment should be according to the crime--Life for life, eye for eye, tooth for tooth, wound for wound, stripe for stripe.
If a man causes injury or blemish to another, he shall have the same injury done to him.
Punishment is the fruit and reward for iniquity and wicked ways (you shall reap that which you sow).

The children of Israel were commanded to bring pure oil olive beaten for the light, to cause the lamps to burn continually. Aaron ordered it from the evening unto the morning before the Lord continually, upon the pure candlestick, a statute for ever in your generations.

Twelve cakes of fine flour were set in two rows, six on a row, upon the pure table before the Lord, with pure frankincense upon each row, every sabbath, taken from the children of Israel by an everlasting covenant. It shall be Aaron's and his sons', and they shall eat it in the holy place, for it is most holy unto him of the offerings of the Lord made by fire.

The son of an Israelitish woman, whose father was an Egyptian, went out among the children of Israel, and strove in the camp with a man of Israel, and blasphemed the name of the Lord, and cursed. His mother was Shelomith, the daughter of Dibri, of the tribe of Dan. They put him in ward, that the mind of the Lord might be shewed them; and the Lord commanded that he that had cursed be brought forth without the camp, that all that heard him lay their hands upon his head, and that all the congregation stone him. The strife in the camp likely arose from a man of Israel correcting him concerning the law. His father being an Egyptian shows he was conceived while Israel was in captivity in the land of Egypt, dwelling among the Egyptians; in the same way Moses, outside of Egypt with Jethro the priest of Midian, took a wife there. And there is no such thing as being half Israelite or a fourth Israelite: if your parent is Israel, you are Israel. Whosoever curseth his God shall bear his sin, and he that blasphemeth the name of the Lord, he shall surely be put to death, as well the stranger as he that is born in the land.

He that killeth any man shall surely be put to death, and he that killeth a beast shall make it good, beast for beast. If a man cause a blemish in his neighbour, as he hath done, so shall it be done to him: breach for breach, eye for eye, tooth for tooth. One manner of law stood for the stranger as for one of your own country. When Christ came he taught the proper understanding of eye for eye for dealing inside the nation: ye have heard that it hath been said, an eye for an eye, and a tooth for a tooth, but I say unto you that ye resist not evil. As the Son of God he had authority to magnify the law: whosoever smites thee on thy right cheek, turn to him the other also; if any man sue thee and take away thy coat, let him have thy cloak also; whosoever compels thee to go a mile, go with him twain. Inside our nation we must practice forgiveness, patience, and long-suffering; we are dealing with our own people, brothers with a conscience. We are the most forgiving people on the planet; the only time we do not know how to forgive is when it comes to each other, and Christ dealt with that.

If thou buy an Hebrew servant, six years he shall serve, and in the seventh he shall go out free for nothing. If he came in by himself he goes out by himself; if he were married when he came in, his wife goes out with him. Deuteronomy repeats the same judgment for a Hebrew man or a Hebrew woman sold unto thee. [Nehemiah 5](/bible/nehemiah/5) shows how brethren came into servitude: in the dearth some mortgaged lands, vineyards, and houses to buy corn, some borrowed money for the king's tribute, and some brought their sons and daughters into bondage. The brother that waxes poor is not to be compelled to serve as a bondservant, but as an hired servant, and not ruled over harshly. If the master gave him a wife and she bare him sons or daughters, the wife and her children are the master's, and he goes out by himself; he did not bring them in. His two choices are to go out alone, or to plainly say, I love my master, my wife, and my children, have his ear bored through with an aul at the door post, and serve his master for ever. Zedekiah's covenant in Jeremiah confirms the law in the prophets: every man was to let his Hebrew manservant and maidservant go free at the appointed release.

If a man sell his daughter to be a maidservant, she shall not go out as the menservants do. The reason is that her master betrothed her to himself, or unto his son; she is a wife, not a six-year servant, so the release of the menservants does not apply to her. If she please not her master who hath betrothed her to himself, he must let her be redeemed; he has no power to sell her unto a strange nation, seeing he hath dealt deceitfully with her. The deceit is that he betrothed her to himself and then would not deal with her, keeping her to himself when she could have been another man's wife. If he take him another wife, her food, her raiment, and her duty of marriage shall he not diminish; the duty of marriage is the marriage bed. If he lay with her, she belongs to him and he cannot send her away; and if he do not these three unto her, then shall she go out free without money. He must take care of her.

If a man lie not in wait, but God deliver him into his hand, a place was appointed whither he shall flee. That is the case of the slayer that kills his neighbour ignorantly, as when a man hews wood with his neighbour and the axe head slips from the helve and lights upon him that he die: he flees to the appointed city and lives, lest the avenger of blood overtake him while his heart is hot, for he was not worthy of death, having hated him not in time past. But if a man come presumptuously upon his neighbour to slay him with guile, thou shalt take him from mine altar, that he may die. Men would run and grab the horns of the altar, but wilful murder found no refuge there.

If men strive and one smite another so that he keep his bed, he that smote him shall pay for the loss of his time and shall cause him to be thoroughly healed. That is restitution: paying for the time the man was down and could not work and provide for his family. That is what the court system calls a civil suit today.

If a man smite his servant with a rod and he die under his hand, he shall surely be punished; but if he continue a day or two, he shall not be punished, for he is his money. The wisdom writings teach not to be ashamed of much correction of children, nor of making the side of an evil servant to bleed. An evil servant that will not get right could be corrected physically, so long as he was not killed.

If men strive and hurt a woman with child so that her fruit depart from her, this judgment covers the miscarriage: if no mischief follow, he is punished as the woman's husband lays upon him and the judges determine; and if any mischief follow, then life for life, eye for eye, tooth for tooth, wound for wound.

If an ox gore a man or a woman that they die, the ox is stoned and his flesh not eaten, and the owner is quit. But if the ox were wont to push with his horns in time past, and it hath been testified to his owner, and he hath not kept him in, and it kill a man or a woman, the ox is stoned and his owner also put to death. Most do not have oxen today, but the same judgment reaches the yard dogs, the pit bulls, German shepherds, and rottweilers. If the dog has bitten before and it was reported to you, and it gets out again through a snapped chain or a breach in the fence and mauls or kills somebody, the scripture holds the owner responsible unto death; that is why animal control writes the ticket and warns you to keep your dogs in. The law is slack right now, as Habakkuk says, so many punishments worthy of death in the scriptures, like rape or this judgment, come out today as a fine or a slap on the hand.
