entries.commentary: Hannah prayed, and said, My heart rejoiceth in the Lord, mine horn is exalted in the Lord: I rejoice in thy salvation. There is none holy as the Lord: for there is none beside thee: neither is there any rock like our God.

Talk no more so exceeding proudly; let not arrogancy come out of your mouth: for the Lord is a God of knowledge, and by him actions are weighed. What the Lord weighs is actions: if it came out of your mouth, are you going to do it? All of us in this walk, keeping the commandments and the faith in Christ, have taken covenant and proclaimed out of our mouths that we are going to endure to the end; we broke the bread and drank the wine and took the covenant with the Lord. Now the Lord is judging you by your actions: are you going to endure to the end, whether to Christ's return or until you leave this earth, if you truly love him?
The bows of the mighty men are broken, and they that stumbled are girded with strength. The Lord is prophesying through Hannah here.
The Lord killeth, and maketh alive: he bringeth down to the grave, and bringeth up. The Lord decides who wakes up and the Lord decides who passes; that is all of the Lord.
The Lord maketh poor, and maketh rich: he bringeth low, and lifteth up.

He raiseth up the poor out of the dust: out of the dust means out of confusion; he brings the poor out of confusion, and lifteth up the beggar from the dunghill, to set them among princes, and to make them inherit the throne of glory: for the pillars of the earth are the Lord's, and he hath set the world upon them.

He will keep the feet of his saints, and the wicked shall be silent in darkness; for by strength shall no man prevail. The adversaries of the Lord shall be broken to pieces; and he shall give strength unto his king, which is Christ, and exalt the horn of his anointed.

Elkanah went to Ramah to his house, and the child did minister unto the Lord before Eli the priest. Now the sons of Eli were sons of Belial; they knew not the Lord. They were the devil. They were Levites, priests in the house of the Lord doing the work of the Lord, and yet it says they knew not the Lord. Why? Because they did not keep the commandments true in their spirit; they kept it on the surface where you can see it. They looked the part: they had on the fringes, they had the beard, they showed up on the sabbath day; but their spirit was not right with the Lord, and they were really the sons of the devil. Do not let that be you, Israel.

The priests' custom with the people was that when any man offered sacrifice, the priest's servant came, while the flesh was in seething, with a fleshhook of three teeth in his hand, and struck it into the pan, or kettle, or caldron, or pot; all that the fleshhook brought up the priest took for himself. They would dip it in, and what came up was the priest's portion of meat for that day; all the Levites did that, based on the sacrifices Israel brought in. This is how the Lord took care of Levi. He told Levi in the law that Levi would have no inheritance of land among the tribes; the Lord provided for them through the sacrifices that Israel brought, so they had need of nothing.

Also, before they burnt the fat, the priest's servant came and said to the man that sacrificed, Give flesh to roast for the priest; for he will not have sodden flesh of thee, but raw: I will cook it up my own way, give it to me now, before it is done. And if any man said, Let them not fail to burn the fat presently, and then take as much as thy soul desireth, he would answer, Nay; but thou shalt give it me now: and if not, I will take it by force. These were devils serving in the house of the Lord, strong-arming the offerings. Wherefore the sin of the young men was very great before the Lord: for men abhorred the offering of the Lord. These priests were disrespecting the offering of the Lord.

But Samuel ministered before the Lord, being a child, girded with a linen ephod; moreover his mother made him a little coat, and brought it to him from year to year, when she came up with her husband to offer the yearly sacrifice. Eli blessed Elkanah and his wife, saying, The Lord give thee seed of this woman for the loan which is lent to the Lord. And the Lord visited Hannah, so that she conceived and bare three sons and two daughters; and the child Samuel grew before the Lord.

Eli was very old, and heard all that his sons did unto all Israel, and how they lay with the women that assembled at the door of the tabernacle of the congregation: the harlots hanging around the temple, and Eli's sons dealing with them. He said unto them, Why do ye such things? for I hear of your evil dealings by all this people; ye make the Lord's people to transgress. The Levites were the leaders, so the people followed their actions: what the priests did, the people did also. They saw the sons of Eli sleeping with the harlots and said, it must be all right, look what they have, look how they live in the temple; let us follow their lead. Notwithstanding they hearkened not unto the voice of their father, because the Lord would slay them. And the child Samuel grew on, and was in favour both with the Lord, and also with men. Eli might have said something to his children, but he did not remove them and put them out of the priesthood for their evil dealings; he said something, but he did not go further than words, he took no action with it. Watch what happened to his children.

There came a man of God unto Eli, saying, Thus saith the Lord, Did I plainly appear unto the house of thy father, when they were in Egypt in Pharaoh's house? That is talking about Levi, going into Moses. Did I choose him out of all the tribes of Israel to be my priest, to offer upon mine altar, to burn incense, to wear an ephod before me? and did I give unto the house of thy father all the offerings made by fire of the children of Israel? They had need of nothing; they were well taken care of. Wherefore kick ye at my sacrifice and at mine offering, which I have commanded in my habitation; and honourest thy sons above me? You are disrespecting me, is what he is saying: I am supposed to be honoured in everything before the children of Israel, and you let your sons disrespect my offerings. Take that into account: do you honour your children above what the Lord says to do? Can they do no wrong, even when they are doing real wrong against the Lord, keeping no commandments, never showing up on the sabbath day, and still living under your roof grown? If they are of age, they know right from wrong, and they are under your roof while you keep the commandments, then they had better be keeping the commandments: showing up to every feast day, the blowing of trumpets, the day of atonement, the passover, the same as you. When they are of age they can go their own way; but they should not be living under your roof and breaking the commandments of God. You honour your children above God when you allow that.

Wherefore the Lord God of Israel saith, I said indeed that thy house, and the house of thy father, should walk before me for ever: but now the Lord saith, Be it far from me; for them that honour me I will honour, and they that despise me shall be lightly esteemed. Lightly esteemed means the Lord is not really looking out for you: you are not thinking about me, so I am not thinking about you; go ahead and see how it works out for yourself. That is why the Lord dealt with Abraham the way he did: Abraham was not going to choose his kids above the Most High, and they were going to do all that he commanded.

Behold, the days come, that I will cut off thine arm, and the arm of thy father's house, that there shall not be an old man in thine house. Cutting off the arm means cutting off thy strength: it was talking about his children. He was going to kill Eli's descendants young, and all the increase of his house would die in the flower of their age, in the full strength and peak of their youth. Why would the Lord judge the children of future generations of Eli's house? The thought might be, he is killing them for the sins of their forefather; I thought the sons did not die for the fathers. [Ezekiel 18](/bible/ezekiel/18) shows what it is talking about: the judgment falls on the son that continues in the sins of his father.

And this shall be a sign unto thee, that shall come upon thy two sons, on Hophni and Phinehas: in one day they shall die both of them. And I will raise me up a faithful priest, that shall do according to that which is in mine heart and in my mind; and I will build him a sure house, and he shall walk before mine anointed for ever. That is the same man we have to be: faithful unto the Lord, doing all that is in his heart and in his mind, not in our own. We cannot lean upon our own understanding, and we cannot lean upon our own emotions and how we feel; in whatever situation, at any given moment, it is what did the Lord say. Do not let the old man guide you and lead you; it should be the spirit of Christ which is in you, the hidden man.

It shall come to pass, that every one that is left in thine house shall come and crouch to him for a piece of silver and a morsel of bread. The Lord was going to make it hard on the descendants of Eli: he removed them from the priesthood, and it was written down that the descendants of Eli were not to be allowed into the house of the Lord any more. Remember, Levi was given no inheritance of land; so how would they eat, how would they live, how would they survive? Receiving their inheritance and their goods was based on them doing what thus saith the Lord told them to do, teaching the laws. Cut off from the priesthood, Eli's house was left to beg.

The word of Samuel came to all Israel, and Israel went out against the Philistines to battle, pitching beside Ebenezer while the Philistines pitched in Aphek. The Philistines never wanted to leave Israel alone. When they joined battle, Israel was smitten before the Philistines, and about four thousand men of the army fell in the field. The Philistines came up against us and whooped us in this first battle.

The elders of Israel asked the right question, Wherefore hath the Lord smitten us to day before the Philistines? But instead of examining the nation, they had an idea: fetch the ark of the covenant out of Shiloh, and when it comes among us it will save us out of the hand of our enemies. The two sons of Eli, Hophni and Phinehas, came with the ark, and when it entered the camp all Israel shouted with a great shout so that the earth rang again. That is how excited and ecstatic Israel was to have the ark of the covenant among them; they felt their enemies could not destroy them now. So what is the ark of the covenant, and what does it contain? The Lord told Moses to hew two tables of stone like the first ones he broke, and the Lord rewrote the ten commandments on them with his own finger, and Moses put the tables in the ark. The ark of the covenant contained the commandments that God wrote.

When the Philistines heard the noise of the shout and understood that the ark of the Lord was come into the camp, they were afraid, saying, God is come into the camp; woe unto us, for there hath not been such a thing heretofore. They had never had to battle Israel with the ark of the covenant in the camp. Think on what they said: Who shall deliver us out of the hand of these mighty Gods? These are the Gods that smote the Egyptians with all the plagues. The nations knew what the Most High did to Egypt; it was known throughout the earth, and to this day real history about what the Hebrews and their God did to the Egyptians is still taught on the other side of the earth. With the ark of the commandments among us, the nations understood they were dealing with something above a regular people. Everything our people try to glory in about Kemet, the Lord smote down. The ten plagues humiliated ten plus different gods that the Egyptians served, all their power, all their magicians and wizards. Come out of that Kemet movement; the Lord destroyed it and said Egypt would not rise again as a power in the earth. Still the Philistines rallied: be strong, and quit yourselves like men, O ye Philistines, that ye be not servants unto the Hebrews, as they have been to you. They remembered serving Israel in the days of the Judges and refused to be slaves again, so they got ready to fight.

The Philistines fought, Israel was smitten again, and every man fled into his tent; there was a very great slaughter, and thirty thousand footmen of Israel fell. A second loss, far worse than the first, even with the ark in the camp. The ark of God was taken, and the two sons of Eli, Hophni and Phinehas, were slain. Those two were wicked as hell, sleeping with the women that assembled at the door of the congregation and finessing the people's offerings, so in this battle the Most High allowed their lives to be taken, exactly as had been prophesied against the house of Eli.

A man of Benjamin ran out of the army to Shiloh the same day with his clothes rent and earth upon his head, and found Eli sitting by the wayside watching, for his heart trembled for the ark of God. Eli was very protective of the ark; he did not want anything to happen to it. Eli was the high priest who groomed Samuel up, and he was righteous as far as himself, but his sons were devils, and he honoured his sons above the Most High by not rebuking them like a true leader should have. Eli was ninety and eight years old and his eyes were dim, and when the messenger told him Israel fled, the slaughter was great, thy two sons are dead, and the ark of God is taken, at the mention of the ark of God he fell from off the seat backward by the side of the gate, and his neck brake, and he died, for he was an old man, and heavy. The shock of the ark being taken is what took him off that seat. He had judged Israel forty years, and his death was ultimately part of the judgment for how he dealt with his sons, in that he did not correct them as he should have.

Phinehas' wife was with child, near to be delivered, and when she heard the tidings that the ark of God was taken and that her father in law and her husband were dead, she bowed herself and travailed, giving birth before her time under all that misfortune. Dying, she named the child Ichabod, saying, The glory is departed from Israel: for the ark of God is taken. Remember what the ark contained, the commandments; with the ark gone, she said the glory of Israel was gone. It was a very sad time for the nation of Israel: thirty thousand mighty men lost, Eli dead, and the ark in the hands of the Philistines.

The child Samuel ministered unto the Lord before Eli. And the word of the Lord was precious in those days; there was no open vision. Precious means the Lord was not dealing with everybody: he was not dealing with the priests, and there were no prophets around saying, thus saith the Lord. The word was about to go only to Samuel.

Eli was laid down in his place, his eyes beginning to wax dim, and ere the lamp of God went out in the temple of the Lord, where the ark of God was, Samuel was laid down to sleep. Ere means before: before the lamp of God went out. That light in the temple by the ark was never to go out, though at a point in time it did go out.

The Lord called Samuel, and he answered, Here am I, and ran unto Eli; and Eli said, I called not; lie down again. The Lord called yet again, and again Samuel went to Eli. Now Samuel did not yet know the Lord, neither was the word of the Lord yet revealed unto him. Look at that. Samuel had been in the house of the Lord since he was weaned, three or four years old, and he still did not know the Lord. This goes in on those playing church with their children: just because your children come and sit and listen to the teaching does not mean they know the Lord; they are there because you brought them there. They can hear all the words they want, but until the Lord reveals himself to them, they do not know him. What makes your kid so special, greater than Samuel? Do not have your children going into a covenant with Christ that he will judge them for if they break it; the scripture says, for this cause many are weak and sickly among you, and many sleep. You do not know if your kids are going to serve the Lord when they go out on their own, or what kind of lusts are in them that will draw them away into the world when they come of age. It is your job as a parent to train them up and pray they stay in it: kids learn by watching, so let them see you take that covenant over and over again until they are ready, and make them rehearse the righteous acts. When the child comes to the age of reasoning and knows the Lord for himself, and the Lord reveals himself to him, you will know it; do not rush it.

The Lord called Samuel again the third time, and Eli perceived that the Lord had called the child; therefore Eli said unto Samuel, Go, lie down: and it shall be, if he call thee, that thou shalt say, Speak, Lord; for thy servant heareth. The Lord is merciful with us even in these days, in this wickedness: he calls out to us numerous times until we wake up. We do not know who is chosen, so we never know when we are going to wake up; it might be the first time, the second time, or the third time you hear the voice of the Lord calling. Some heard the call the first time because the Most High ordained them to be built up as leaders, to get the spirits of the world off of them so they could be a righteous example and a fit guide for you; you came in at the third call, after they were prepared. Your job is not to try to supersede those that came in before you, but to follow them; God set it up that way for a reason.

And the Lord came and stood, and called as at other times, Samuel, Samuel. The Lord did not just call from the heavens: the Lord came down and stood by Samuel and called out to him. That is cold-blooded. Samuel could not see him, but he heard him; that is what happens in the spirit to all of us. Notice in the scriptures that the Most High calls the name two times: Moses, Moses; Samuel, Samuel. That may be a question to ask Christ, Lord's will, for him that endures to the end. What was happening spiritually when the Most High was revealing himself to Samuel and about to pour his word into him? The same thing that happens to all Israel: he stands at the door and knocks. That door is your spirit. The knocking is the Lord calling out through the videos, the flyers, the four chapters a day, the classes; that is the Lord standing and knocking at the spirit of all Israel before he cuts you off.

The Lord said to Samuel, Behold, I will do a thing in Israel, at which both the ears of every one that heareth it shall tingle. In that day I will perform against Eli all things which I have spoken concerning his house: when I begin, I will also make an end. For I have told him that I will judge his house for ever for the iniquity which he knoweth; because his sons made themselves vile, and he restrained them not. Eli let his children break the commandments of the Lord and lead the people astray, and he restrained them not. Therefore I have sworn unto the house of Eli, that the iniquity of Eli's house shall not be purged with sacrifice nor offering for ever. When the Lord is mad, the Lord is mad: thus we are in the lands of our captivity 400 years and counting, and you have heard the history of the Spanish Inquisition, how we were burned for keeping the commandments; his anger burns unto the lowest hell. Do not let that be you. Do not let the Lord pass a judgment on your house where Christ prays for you and the Most High says, No, I will bring a judgment on his house for ever. Do not sin a sin so great that it cannot be prayed for, so that nothing is left but the fiery day of judgment.

Samuel lay until the morning, and opened the doors of the house of the Lord; and Samuel feared to shew Eli the vision. But Eli called him and said, What is the thing that the Lord hath said unto thee? I pray thee hide it not from me: God do so to thee, and more also, if thou hide any thing from me of all the things that he said unto thee. Samuel was going to be a judge of Israel, and here is his first test as a judge: do not sugarcoat what the Lord has said, and do not trim your words to seek love. And Samuel told him every whit, and hid nothing from him. Eli said, It is the Lord: let him do what seemeth him good. Eli had no control of his kids, but he accepted the judgment of the Lord: thy will be done. Maybe the Lord had mercy on Eli; that is of the Lord, and we will not know.

Samuel grew, and the Lord was with him, and did let none of his words fall to the ground. What does that mean? What Samuel said, it came to pass. All Israel from Dan even to Beersheba knew that Samuel was established to be a prophet of the Lord. And the Lord appeared again in Shiloh: for the Lord revealed himself to Samuel in Shiloh by the word of the Lord. That is good history we read today about Samuel; take heed to what you have heard, and do not let it slip. Some of you may be in these same situations: putting other people before God, honouring your children above God and not restraining them, or hearing the Lord call once, twice, three times without answering the call. This history is here for us to learn from; use it, lest the judgments of God be passed upon us when he is angry, for whatever the Most High says, Christ follows, because that is the order: God, Christ, man, woman, children.

name: The Philistines and the captured ark
charge: Setting the ark of God in the house of Dagon, and keeping it seven months
summary: The Philistines took the ark in battle and set it beside Dagon as a trophy. Dagon fell on his face before it twice, the second time without head or hands, and the men of Ashdod, Gath and Ekron were smitten with emerods until they sent it home on a new cart with golden offerings.
offense: After Israel's first defeat, the elders asked why the Lord had smitten them, but answered their trouble by fetching the ark. They expected it to save them, and the camp shouted when it arrived (1 Samuel 4:2-5). The ark contained the tables of the covenant (Deuteronomy 10:1-5). Bringing the commandments into camp was not the same as keeping them. Hophni and Phinehas came with it while the judgment upon their corruption still stood. The Philistines feared when they heard that the ark had come, remembering the plagues upon Egypt, but they fought and defeated Israel again. Thirty thousand footmen fell, the priests died, and the ark was taken (1 Samuel 4:6-11). Israel's confidence in possession had not replaced obedience. Samuel would later require the nation to put away its strange gods and serve the Lord only (1 Samuel 7:3-4). The victors made a corresponding error: they brought the ark into Dagon's house at Ashdod and set it beside their idol (1 Samuel 5:1-2). Capturing it did not make them masters of the God of Israel. The Lord had judged his people; he had not surrendered his power to the Philistines' god. Samson's last act had already brought destruction upon a gathering that glorified Dagon (Judges 16:23-30).
judgment: Dagon fell upon his face before the ark. They set him up again, but the following morning his head and the palms of his hands lay cut off upon the threshold (1 Samuel 5:3-4). The worshippers could restore the statue to its place but could not preserve its head or hands. The supposed victor had to be lifted by the very men who trusted it. The Lord's hand was heavy upon Ashdod with destruction and emerods. Moving the ark to Gath brought affliction there, and Ekron cried out when it was sent onward (1 Samuel 5:6-12). A change of city did not change whose hand was against them. Seven months later their priests counselled a trespass offering and warned them not to harden their hearts as Pharaoh had done (1 Samuel 6:1-6). The captured object was to be returned with an acknowledgment of offense. They placed it upon a new cart drawn by two cows that had never borne a yoke, shut up their calves at home, and watched whether they went toward Beth-shemesh. If they did, the Philistines would know that the Lord had sent the affliction. The cows took the straight way, lowing as they went, and did not turn aside (1 Samuel 6:7-12). Their own test answered the claim that the destruction had happened by chance.

entries.commentary: The Philistines took the ark of God from Ebenezer to Ashdod, and had the audacity to bring it into the house of Dagon and set it by Dagon, a fake god the Lord had already exposed. Now watch what the ark did to their idol. When they of Ashdod arose early on the morrow, Dagon was fallen upon his face to the earth before the ark of the Lord. This was no little souvenir you could knock over; it was a large statue, and nobody had been in there to touch it. They set him in his place again, as if maybe the wind blew a little harder, and the next morning Dagon was fallen on his face again before the ark, with the head of Dagon and both the palms of his hands cut off upon the threshold; only the stump of Dagon was left to him. No man did this: that is the power of the ark of God. Therefore the priests of Dagon tread not on the threshold of Dagon in Ashdod unto this day.

The hand of the Lord was heavy upon them of Ashdod, and he destroyed them, and smote them with emerods. Emerods are what we know today as hemorrhoids: swollen veins in the lower rectum that bleed and cause pain. The Most High was not playing games with the heathen; he literally afflicted them in their behinds for stealing the ark.

The men of Ashdod said, The ark of the God of Israel shall not abide with us: for his hand is sore upon us, and upon Dagon our god. So the lords of the Philistines gathered and decided to carry the ark about unto Gath, a different location in Philistia. The punishment followed the ark: the hand of the Lord was against Gath with a very great destruction, and he smote the men of the city, both small and great, and they had emerods in their secret parts. Moving it to another city changed nothing; the affliction went with it.

By the time they sent the ark to Ekron, the third location, the Ekronites had already heard what was happening and cried out, They have brought about the ark of the God of Israel to us, to slay us and our people. The lords of the Philistines were told, Send away the ark of the God of Israel, and let it go again to his own place; for there was a deadly destruction throughout all the city, and the hand of God was very heavy there. The men that died not were smitten with the emerods, and the cry of the city went up to heaven. That was the great suffering and affliction the Philistines earned for thinking they had done something by taking the ark.

The ark of the Lord was in the country of the Philistines seven months, and the Philistines called for the priests and the diviners, asking how to send it back to his place. Seven months of that plague and they had to get it out of the land. The priests answered, send it not empty, but in any wise return him a trespass offering; then ye shall be healed. A trespass offering acknowledges you did wrong. The offering was five golden emerods and five golden mice, according to the number of the lords of the Philistines, images of the very things that marred the land, and ye shall give glory unto the God of Israel; peradventure he will lighten his hand from off you, and from off your gods, and from off your land. Their own priests warned them from Israel's history: wherefore then do ye harden your hearts, as the Egyptians and Pharaoh hardened their hearts? They did not want to end up like Egypt, so they said, let us learn the lesson and get this ark back.

The test: make a new cart, take two milch kine on which there hath come no yoke, shut up their calves at home, lay the ark on the cart with the jewels of gold in a coffer, and send it away. If it goeth up by the way of his own coast to Beth-shemesh, then he hath done us this great evil: but if not, we shall know it was a chance that happened to us, maybe just a disease spreading through the nation. The kine took the straight way to the way of Beth-shemesh, lowing as they went, and turned not aside to the right hand or to the left, with the lords of the Philistines following to the border. Cows with no yoke, separated from their calves, walking a straight line home to Israel: that settled that it was the hand of the Lord.

They of Beth-shemesh were reaping their wheat harvest in the valley, and when they lifted up their eyes and saw the ark, they rejoiced to see it. As soon as the ark crossed that border coming home, it was rejoicing time in Israel. The cart came into the field of Joshua, a Beth-shemite, and stood by a great stone; they clave the wood of the cart and offered the kine a burnt offering unto the Lord, and the Levites took down the ark and the coffer with the jewels of gold. The golden emerods were one for each lord's city, Ashdod, Gaza, Askelon, Gath, and Ekron, and when the five lords of the Philistines had seen it, they returned to Ekron the same day. The Philistines understood it really was the Lord that had afflicted them.

He smote the men of Beth-shemesh, because they had looked into the ark of the Lord, even fifty thousand and threescore and ten men. It was not just the other nations that had to keep discretion with the ark of the covenant; it was forbidden to touch it or look into it unless the Lord gave you authority, no matter what tribe you were, even Levi. They got too excited and got nosy, taking a peek to see what the writing of God looked like, and the Lord smote fifty thousand and seventy of them just for peeking. That shows us we have to have a level of discipline over our eyes; with these devices today it is very easy to take a two second look at what you know you should not be looking at. Guard your eyes. The people lamented and said, Who is able to stand before this holy Lord God? So they sent messengers to Kirjath-jearim to come fetch the ark up. The Bible acknowledges the Most High God as the king of terrors: he was killing thousands at a time, and his judgments are terrifying.

name: The men of Beth-shemesh
charge: Looking into the ark of the Lord
summary: When the Philistines returned the ark on a cart, the men of Beth-shemesh rejoiced, offered the kine, and looked into the ark. The Lord smote them with a great slaughter, and they asked, who is able to stand before this holy Lord God?
offense: The people of Beth-shemesh were reaping wheat when they saw the returning ark and rejoiced. The cart came into the field of Joshua the Beth-shemite and stood by a great stone; the Levites took down the ark and the coffer, and offerings were made to the Lord (1 Samuel 6:13-15). The return was a cause for thanksgiving. The Philistines had not kept what they took, and the Lord had shown his hand in bringing it back. But the men looked into the ark, and the Lord smote them for that act (1 Samuel 6:19). Joy did not grant unrestricted access to holy things. The law had distinguished the service appointed to the Levites from what they were forbidden to touch or see. The boundary applied among Israel as surely as the Lord's power had applied among the Philistines. The people could not receive the ark with reverence and then treat its holiness as open to their curiosity. Obedience governs the eyes as well as the hands. What is near, available, or greatly desired to be seen is not therefore given to a man to examine.
judgment: The text gives the number as fifty thousand and threescore and ten men, a figure long debated; the sentence is not. They sent the ark on to Kirjath-jearim and it stayed there twenty years.

entries.commentary: The ark of the Lord was in the country of the Philistines seven months, and the Philistines called for the priests and the diviners, asking how to send it back to his place. Seven months of that plague and they had to get it out of the land. The priests answered, send it not empty, but in any wise return him a trespass offering; then ye shall be healed. A trespass offering acknowledges you did wrong. The offering was five golden emerods and five golden mice, according to the number of the lords of the Philistines, images of the very things that marred the land, and ye shall give glory unto the God of Israel; peradventure he will lighten his hand from off you, and from off your gods, and from off your land. Their own priests warned them from Israel's history: wherefore then do ye harden your hearts, as the Egyptians and Pharaoh hardened their hearts? They did not want to end up like Egypt, so they said, let us learn the lesson and get this ark back.

The test: make a new cart, take two milch kine on which there hath come no yoke, shut up their calves at home, lay the ark on the cart with the jewels of gold in a coffer, and send it away. If it goeth up by the way of his own coast to Beth-shemesh, then he hath done us this great evil: but if not, we shall know it was a chance that happened to us, maybe just a disease spreading through the nation. The kine took the straight way to the way of Beth-shemesh, lowing as they went, and turned not aside to the right hand or to the left, with the lords of the Philistines following to the border. Cows with no yoke, separated from their calves, walking a straight line home to Israel: that settled that it was the hand of the Lord.

They of Beth-shemesh were reaping their wheat harvest in the valley, and when they lifted up their eyes and saw the ark, they rejoiced to see it. As soon as the ark crossed that border coming home, it was rejoicing time in Israel. The cart came into the field of Joshua, a Beth-shemite, and stood by a great stone; they clave the wood of the cart and offered the kine a burnt offering unto the Lord, and the Levites took down the ark and the coffer with the jewels of gold. The golden emerods were one for each lord's city, Ashdod, Gaza, Askelon, Gath, and Ekron, and when the five lords of the Philistines had seen it, they returned to Ekron the same day. The Philistines understood it really was the Lord that had afflicted them.

He smote the men of Beth-shemesh, because they had looked into the ark of the Lord, even fifty thousand and threescore and ten men. It was not just the other nations that had to keep discretion with the ark of the covenant; it was forbidden to touch it or look into it unless the Lord gave you authority, no matter what tribe you were, even Levi. They got too excited and got nosy, taking a peek to see what the writing of God looked like, and the Lord smote fifty thousand and seventy of them just for peeking. That shows us we have to have a level of discipline over our eyes; with these devices today it is very easy to take a two second look at what you know you should not be looking at. Guard your eyes. The people lamented and said, Who is able to stand before this holy Lord God? So they sent messengers to Kirjath-jearim to come fetch the ark up. The Bible acknowledges the Most High God as the king of terrors: he was killing thousands at a time, and his judgments are terrifying.

The men of Kirjath-jearim fetched up the ark of the Lord into the house of Abinadab in the hill, and sanctified Eleazar his son to keep it. While the ark abode in Kirjath-jearim the time was long, twenty years, and all the house of Israel lamented after the Lord.

Samuel spake unto all the house of Israel: If ye do return unto the Lord with all your hearts, then put away the strange gods and Ashtaroth from among you, and prepare your hearts unto the Lord, and serve him only, and he will deliver you out of the hand of the Philistines. Go back to how we lost the battle even with the ark of God among us: we had strange gods among us. Deliverance is not just having the ark, it is applying the commandments that are in the ark, thou shalt have no other gods before me. Who is Ashtoreth? Astaroth in demonology is a chief figure of hell, named after the Near Eastern goddess Astarte, and Astarte is the Hellenized form of Ashtoreth, a form of Ishtar, the goddess called the queen of heaven, associated with love, beauty, sex, and war. Samuel was exhorting the people to depart from these fake gods and goddesses of the nations, and to this day there are Israelites that have not put away Ashtoreth from among them. Easter is at its roots the celebration of Ishtar, the goddess of fertility and sex. When Constantine set out to merge paganism with the faith of the apostles to bring everything under one empire, pagan rituals like Easter and Saturnalia were dressed up as honoring Christ, and that was the birth of Roman Catholicism. Nothing about it mathematically adds up to Christ rising, the apostles never celebrated it or taught it, and a bunny laying eggs has nothing to do with your Lord and Saviour; it is not of Christ. Then the children of Israel did put away Baalim and Ashtaroth, and served the Lord only. That is repentance.

Samuel said, Gather all Israel to Mizpeh, and I will pray for you unto the Lord. They gathered, drew water and poured it out before the Lord, fasted that day, and said, We have sinned against the Lord; and Samuel judged the children of Israel in Mizpeh. When the lords of the Philistines heard Israel was gathered at Mizpeh, they came up against Israel again, and Israel was afraid. But this time, instead of running for the ark, the children of Israel charged Samuel, Cease not to cry unto the Lord our God for us, that he will save us out of the hand of the Philistines. They knew the prayer of a righteous man reaches the ears of the Most High.

Samuel took a sucking lamb and offered it for a burnt offering wholly unto the Lord, and Samuel cried unto the Lord for Israel, and the Lord heard him. As Samuel was offering up the burnt offering, the Philistines drew near to battle, but the Lord thundered with a great thunder on that day upon the Philistines, and discomfited them, and they were smitten before Israel. That was no regular thunder; it was the Lord entering the battle himself. They had repented, put away the false gods, and the prayer of the righteous man reached his ears, so now the Philistines had to deal with the Most High. The Philistines were so terrified they put up no fight; the men of Israel went out of Mizpeh and pursued them, smiting them until they came under Beth-car. Then Samuel took a stone, set it between Mizpeh and Shen, and called the name of it Ebenezer, saying, Hitherto hath the Lord helped us. Samuel was one of the most respected prophets in the whole history of the prophets: he established the kingdom and anointed Saul, and by his faithfulness he was found a true prophet. Faithfulness translates loyalty. He came up under Eli, watched Eli's sons go wicked, Eli die, and the nation take losses, but Samuel stayed loyal to the Most High, just as Abraham's faith was tried again and again and he remained faithful.

So the Philistines were subdued, and they came no more into the coast of Israel: and the hand of the Lord was against the Philistines all the days of Samuel. As long as Samuel lived, the Lord kept them down. The cities the Philistines had taken from Israel were restored, from Ekron even unto Gath, and Israel delivered the coasts out of the hands of the Philistines; and there was peace between Israel and the Amorites.

Samuel judged Israel all the days of his life, and went from year to year in circuit to Bethel, and Gilgal, and Mizpeh, and judged Israel in all those places; and his return was to Ramah, for there was his house, and there he built an altar unto the Lord. Ramah was his headquarters. That yearly circuit is leadership making its rounds, establishing the people and coming back to check on them, the same example Paul followed with the churches. These chapters close with the ark lost and regained, and Samuel rising up for the nation: prayer is a superpower, and that is how our mighty forefathers rolled, from Moses to Samuel to Judas Maccabeus all the way to Christ. Keep the commandments and send up that prayer, and the Most High will come down in thunder against your enemies.

The sons of Kohath were numbered from thirty years old and upward even unto fifty years old, all that enter into the host to do the work in the tabernacle of the congregation. You took on that responsibility at thirty years old. Fifty was basically the age of retirement from the service; the law elsewhere shows the elder then sat down to be a judge amongst his brethren.

This is the service of the sons of Kohath about the most holy things. When the camp set forward, Aaron and his sons took down the covering vail and covered the ark of the testimony with it, with the covering of badgers' skins and a cloth wholly of blue. The design of the ark and the tabernacle, the pure gold dishes, spoons, and vessels, was laid out back in [Exodus 35](/bible/exodus/35) and 36; review it there.

The table of shewbread, the candlestick, the golden altar, and all the instruments of ministry were each wrapped in cloths of blue, scarlet, or purple and covered with badgers' skins before they were put on the staves and bars. Badger skin is something we would consider unclean today, yet the Lord had his holy things covered in it. Under the law of sacrifice, defilement came by touching unclean things to eat them; touching them to make something for the tabernacle still left you unclean until sundown, unable to sacrifice, but the skins themselves served the sanctuary.

After Aaron and his sons made an end of covering the sanctuary, the sons of Kohath came to bear it, but they shall not touch any holy thing, lest they die. The Most High is very particular about the most holy things. The Lord referred to all the tribes together as the camp. If you are not in a camp you are out of order; people avoid camps because a camp carries a certain level of order and subjection, and they want to do their own thing, which is to sit in the midst of sin. All twelve tribes are not gathered together right now, but we are still commanded to rehearse the righteous acts of the Lord, and that takes gathering; the body must move in one unison, in one direction, as a camp.

To the office of Eleazar pertained the oil for the light, the sweet incense, the daily meat offering, the anointing oil, and the oversight of all the tabernacle. The burning of the sweet incense stayed in that priestly line: Zacharias, of the course of Abia, descended from the line of the Kohathites, and his lot was to burn incense in the temple of the Lord. [Luke 1:6](/bible/luke/1#v6) is the New Testament precept for what it means to be righteous: walking in all the commandments and ordinances of the Lord blameless. Highlight that and commit it to memory. The son of Zacharias was John the Baptist, a Levite; and John the Baptist was Elijah back on the earth again, come to do what was prophesied of him. There is no reincarnation, coming back as a bird or such; there is regeneration, and we come back over and over again.

The Most High commanded that the families of the Kohathites not be cut off: Aaron and his sons appointed every one to his service and to his burden, but they shall not go in to see when the holy things are covered, lest they die. It was a heavy responsibility; your life was on the line and you could not be out of order. One slip, one curious peek at the shiny gold before it was covered, and God put you to death on the spot. You had to be serious about your job and follow all instructions. That is the God we are dealing with; that is why Christ came, to give us mercy and grace from that thing.

The sons of Gershon were numbered from thirty to fifty years old for their service: bearing the curtains of the tabernacle, the coverings of badgers' skins, the hangings of the court and the doors, the cords, and all the instruments of their service. Their charge was under the hand of Ithamar the son of Aaron the priest. Ithamar had to make sure the priests had covered all the most holy things before the Gershonites came in to bear them; he was responsible for the lives of all the Gershonites that served, and he had to be in order.

The sons of Merari were numbered from thirty to fifty years old, charged with the boards, bars, pillars, sockets, pins, and cords of the tabernacle and the court, reckoned by name, under the hand of Ithamar the son of Aaron. Only Eleazar and Ithamar were left to oversee, because Nadab and Abihu were killed by the Lord for offering strange fire; there were only two sons of Aaron remaining.

The numbered for service were 2,750 Kohathites, 2,630 Gershonites, and 3,200 Merarites; the total of those from thirty to fifty years old that entered the service of the tabernacle was 8,580, eight thousand and five hundred and fourscore. The Lord constantly repeats himself through these chapters to make sure you stay in order and do not go out of order, because going out of order cost your life. That is why you read the same thing in the Bible over and over again.

name: Samuel
charge: Speak, Lord, for thy servant heareth; and an accounting no man could contradict: whose ox have I taken?
summary: Dedicated to the Lord and brought to Shiloh as a child, Samuel received a word of judgment against Eli's house and delivered it without concealment. He judged Israel throughout his life, anointed Saul and David, and stood before the people to give an account of his conduct. They testified that he had neither oppressed them nor taken anything from them.
offense: Samuel's service began before he understood the voice that called him. He ministered before Eli, but the word of the Lord had not yet been revealed to him. When Eli perceived who was calling, he taught Samuel to answer as a servant ready to hear (1 Samuel 3:1-10). Growing up beside holy things was preparation for service; receiving the word required his own response. The first message placed him under a difficult obligation. The Lord pronounced judgment upon the house that had raised him because Eli knew his sons' iniquity and did not restrain them. Samuel feared to tell the vision, yet told Eli everything and hid nothing (1 Samuel 3:11-18). Affection for the hearer could not become permission to alter the judgment. Faithful teaching begins with being faithful to what was given to teach. When Israel demanded a king, Samuel submitted his own administration to examination. Before the Lord and the new king, he asked whose property he had taken, whom he had defrauded or oppressed, and whose bribe had blinded his eyes. The people testified that he had taken nothing (1 Samuel 12:1-5). Exodus 23:8 forbids the gift that blinds judgment. Samuel's authority was supported by an account the people themselves could verify. He then rebuked their demand without abandoning them. He rehearsed the Lord's deliverances, warned both people and king to obey, and declared that he would sin against the Lord if he ceased praying for them (1 Samuel 12:6-25). Correction and intercession belonged together. Their refusal of his counsel did not release him from teaching the good and right way.
judgment: The Lord was with Samuel and let none of his words fall to the ground. Israel from Dan to Beersheba knew him to be an established prophet (1 Samuel 3:19-21). His standing came through the fulfilment of the Lord's word, not through a title taken to himself. At Mizpeh the Lord heard his prayer and thundered against the Philistines; he continued his circuit of judgment through Bethel, Gilgal, Mizpeh, and Ramah (1 Samuel 7:9-17). He anointed Saul, mourned Saul's rejection, and obeyed the command to anoint David (1 Samuel 10:1; 15:35; 16:1-13). The work continued even when its history grieved him. All Israel lamented him at his death (1 Samuel 25:1). Ecclesiasticus (Sirach) 46:13-17 remembers his faithfulness in judging by the law and the prayer answered from heaven. His ministry joined an upright hand, an unaltered word, and continuing care for the nation.

verses.text: 8And the Lord called Samuel again the third time. And he arose and went to Eli, and said, Here am I; for thou didst call me. And Eli perceived that the Lord had called the child. 9Therefore Eli said unto Samuel, Go, lie down: and it shall be, if he call thee, that thou shalt say, Speak, Lord; for thy servant heareth. So Samuel went and lay down in his place. 10And the Lord came, and stood, and called as at other times, Samuel, Samuel. Then Samuel answered, Speak; for thy servant heareth. 11And the Lord said to Samuel, Behold, I will do a thing in Israel, at which both the ears of every one that heareth it shall tingle. 12In that day I will perform against Eli all things which I have spoken concerning his house: when I begin, I will also make an end. 13For I have told him that I will judge his house for ever for the iniquity which he knoweth; because his sons made themselves vile, and he restrained them not. 14And therefore I have sworn unto the house of Eli, that the iniquity of Eli’s house

entries.commentary: The child Samuel ministered unto the Lord before Eli. And the word of the Lord was precious in those days; there was no open vision. Precious means the Lord was not dealing with everybody: he was not dealing with the priests, and there were no prophets around saying, thus saith the Lord. The word was about to go only to Samuel.

Eli was laid down in his place, his eyes beginning to wax dim, and ere the lamp of God went out in the temple of the Lord, where the ark of God was, Samuel was laid down to sleep. Ere means before: before the lamp of God went out. That light in the temple by the ark was never to go out, though at a point in time it did go out.

The Lord called Samuel, and he answered, Here am I, and ran unto Eli; and Eli said, I called not; lie down again. The Lord called yet again, and again Samuel went to Eli. Now Samuel did not yet know the Lord, neither was the word of the Lord yet revealed unto him. Look at that. Samuel had been in the house of the Lord since he was weaned, three or four years old, and he still did not know the Lord. This goes in on those playing church with their children: just because your children come and sit and listen to the teaching does not mean they know the Lord; they are there because you brought them there. They can hear all the words they want, but until the Lord reveals himself to them, they do not know him. What makes your kid so special, greater than Samuel? Do not have your children going into a covenant with Christ that he will judge them for if they break it; the scripture says, for this cause many are weak and sickly among you, and many sleep. You do not know if your kids are going to serve the Lord when they go out on their own, or what kind of lusts are in them that will draw them away into the world when they come of age. It is your job as a parent to train them up and pray they stay in it: kids learn by watching, so let them see you take that covenant over and over again until they are ready, and make them rehearse the righteous acts. When the child comes to the age of reasoning and knows the Lord for himself, and the Lord reveals himself to him, you will know it; do not rush it.

The Lord called Samuel again the third time, and Eli perceived that the Lord had called the child; therefore Eli said unto Samuel, Go, lie down: and it shall be, if he call thee, that thou shalt say, Speak, Lord; for thy servant heareth. The Lord is merciful with us even in these days, in this wickedness: he calls out to us numerous times until we wake up. We do not know who is chosen, so we never know when we are going to wake up; it might be the first time, the second time, or the third time you hear the voice of the Lord calling. Some heard the call the first time because the Most High ordained them to be built up as leaders, to get the spirits of the world off of them so they could be a righteous example and a fit guide for you; you came in at the third call, after they were prepared. Your job is not to try to supersede those that came in before you, but to follow them; God set it up that way for a reason.

And the Lord came and stood, and called as at other times, Samuel, Samuel. The Lord did not just call from the heavens: the Lord came down and stood by Samuel and called out to him. That is cold-blooded. Samuel could not see him, but he heard him; that is what happens in the spirit to all of us. Notice in the scriptures that the Most High calls the name two times: Moses, Moses; Samuel, Samuel. That may be a question to ask Christ, Lord's will, for him that endures to the end. What was happening spiritually when the Most High was revealing himself to Samuel and about to pour his word into him? The same thing that happens to all Israel: he stands at the door and knocks. That door is your spirit. The knocking is the Lord calling out through the videos, the flyers, the four chapters a day, the classes; that is the Lord standing and knocking at the spirit of all Israel before he cuts you off.

The Lord said to Samuel, Behold, I will do a thing in Israel, at which both the ears of every one that heareth it shall tingle. In that day I will perform against Eli all things which I have spoken concerning his house: when I begin, I will also make an end. For I have told him that I will judge his house for ever for the iniquity which he knoweth; because his sons made themselves vile, and he restrained them not. Eli let his children break the commandments of the Lord and lead the people astray, and he restrained them not. Therefore I have sworn unto the house of Eli, that the iniquity of Eli's house shall not be purged with sacrifice nor offering for ever. When the Lord is mad, the Lord is mad: thus we are in the lands of our captivity 400 years and counting, and you have heard the history of the Spanish Inquisition, how we were burned for keeping the commandments; his anger burns unto the lowest hell. Do not let that be you. Do not let the Lord pass a judgment on your house where Christ prays for you and the Most High says, No, I will bring a judgment on his house for ever. Do not sin a sin so great that it cannot be prayed for, so that nothing is left but the fiery day of judgment.

Samuel lay until the morning, and opened the doors of the house of the Lord; and Samuel feared to shew Eli the vision. But Eli called him and said, What is the thing that the Lord hath said unto thee? I pray thee hide it not from me: God do so to thee, and more also, if thou hide any thing from me of all the things that he said unto thee. Samuel was going to be a judge of Israel, and here is his first test as a judge: do not sugarcoat what the Lord has said, and do not trim your words to seek love. And Samuel told him every whit, and hid nothing from him. Eli said, It is the Lord: let him do what seemeth him good. Eli had no control of his kids, but he accepted the judgment of the Lord: thy will be done. Maybe the Lord had mercy on Eli; that is of the Lord, and we will not know.

Samuel grew, and the Lord was with him, and did let none of his words fall to the ground. What does that mean? What Samuel said, it came to pass. All Israel from Dan even to Beersheba knew that Samuel was established to be a prophet of the Lord. And the Lord appeared again in Shiloh: for the Lord revealed himself to Samuel in Shiloh by the word of the Lord. That is good history we read today about Samuel; take heed to what you have heard, and do not let it slip. Some of you may be in these same situations: putting other people before God, honouring your children above God and not restraining them, or hearing the Lord call once, twice, three times without answering the call. This history is here for us to learn from; use it, lest the judgments of God be passed upon us when he is angry, for whatever the Most High says, Christ follows, because that is the order: God, Christ, man, woman, children.

name: Joel and Abiah, the sons of Samuel
charge: Turning aside after lucre, taking bribes, and perverting judgment in the seat of the judge
summary: Samuel made his sons judges over Israel, and they walked not in his ways. They took bribes and perverted judgment, and the elders of Israel used it as the reason to ask for a king. The sentence recorded falls on the nation that asked, not on the two men who gave them the excuse.
offense: Samuel appointed Joel and Abiah as judges in Beersheba, but they did not walk in his ways. They turned aside after gain, received bribes, and perverted judgment (1 Samuel 8:1-3). Their father's upright administration did not pass to them merely because his office did. The contrast was public: the people could testify that Samuel had taken nothing, while the sons made the seat of judgment serve their own increase (1 Samuel 12:3-5). The law names the corruption precisely. Judges were to judge with just judgment, without respecting persons or taking a gift that blinded the wise and perverted righteous words (Deuteronomy 16:18-20). Exodus 23:8 gives the same warning. A bribe does more than enrich an official. It bends what he is entrusted to see and say, placing those who seek justice at the mercy of those who can buy an answer. The elders brought the sons' conduct before Samuel when they asked for a king (1 Samuel 8:4-5). Corruption in an office that should protect the people gave force to their complaint. A father's reputation could not excuse his sons, and the people's knowledge of their wrongdoing could not be dismissed as a rejection of order. The judges themselves had violated the order established by the Lord.
judgment: The recorded consequence reaches the nation: the elders used the sons' departure as their reason to demand a king like the nations. The Lord identified that demand as a rejection of his reign and instructed Samuel to warn them what the king would take (1 Samuel 8:6-18). Their grievance against corrupt judges was real; the remedy they insisted upon brought obligations and burdens of its own. No personal penalty upon Joel or Abiah is recorded in this chapter. Their offense remains named without an account of their later punishment. Ecclesiastes 5:8 warns the observer of perverted judgment that one higher than the official regards the matter. Silence about the sons' end does not turn their bribery into righteousness. Their place in the history is the damage caused when inherited authority is exercised without the character required to govern.
