After many days the word of the Lord came to Elijah in the third year: Go show thyself unto Ahab, and I will send rain upon the earth. There was a sore famine in Samaria. Ahab called Obadiah, governor of his house, who feared the Lord greatly; when Jezebel cut off the prophets of the Lord, Obadiah took an hundred prophets and hid them by fifty in a cave and fed them with bread and water, putting his own life in danger to save them. The famine was so sore it was hitting the animals, so Ahab and Obadiah divided the land between them, each going his own way to seek fountains and brooks to find grass to save the horses and mules alive. This was the fruit of the drought Elijah had pronounced.

As Obadiah went his way, Elijah met him; Obadiah fell on his face and said, Art thou my lord Elijah? Elijah told him to go tell Ahab that Elijah is here. Obadiah was afraid, for Ahab had searched every nation and kingdom to find and slay Elijah; that is how badly Jezebel wanted him dead, so she got Ahab to do her bidding. This is why Elijah had been on the run, first by Jordan, then years with the widow. Obadiah feared that the spirit of the Lord would carry Elijah away and Ahab would slay him for a false report, so he pleaded his own record: he feared the Lord from his youth and had hidden a hundred of the Lord's prophets by fifty in a cave. Elijah swore by the Lord of hosts that he would surely show himself to Ahab that day, and so Obadiah went to Ahab, and Ahab came to meet Elijah.

When Ahab saw Elijah he said, Art thou he that troubleth Israel? That is the mind of a wicked person: he blamed the trouble on the ordained prophet of God rather than on his own wickedness. When the spirit is gone, wisdom cannot enter a malicious soul, so Ahab had thoughts without understanding. Elijah answered, I have not troubled Israel, but thou and thy father's house, in that ye have forsaken the commandments of the Lord and thou hast followed Baalim. It was Ahab following the sin of Jeroboam the son of Nebat, worshipping the golden calves, that brought the trouble. Elijah commanded that all Israel be gathered to Mount Carmel with the four hundred and fifty prophets of Baal and the four hundred prophets of the groves that eat at Jezebel's table. Jezebel was the one feeding these eight hundred and fifty false prophets and encouraging them, and Ahab never checked her.

Ahab gathered the prophets and all Israel to Mount Carmel, and Elijah said unto the people, How long halt ye between two opinions? If the Lord be God, follow him, but if Baal, then follow him. And the people answered him not a word. That is a call for all of us to examine ourselves: cast away every burden and sin and follow the Most High and his son fully, keeping the commandments, and do not keep one foot in and one foot out. Being lukewarm, playing the middle ground, ends with Christ spewing a man out of his mouth, and the next step after that is death. Elijah proposed the test: let each side dress a bullock, lay it on wood, and put no fire under, and the God that answereth by fire, let him be God. All the people said, It is well spoken.

The prophets of Baal dressed their bullock first and called on the name of Baal from morning until noon, saying, O Baal, hear us, but there was no voice nor any that answered, and they leaped upon the altar. Picture the scene: eight hundred and fifty men doing this, running wild, while Elijah sat back watching the madness. At noon Elijah mocked them, saying, Cry aloud, for he is a god; either he is talking, or pursuing, or on a journey, or peradventure he sleepeth and must be awaked. They cried aloud and cut themselves with knives and lancets till the blood gushed out, for cutting themselves was part of their false worship whenever they called on Baal. From midday past the time of the evening sacrifice there was neither voice nor any to answer nor any that regarded. No one answered because the Most High will not give his glory to another, and the gods of the nations are idols that are not real; they are made up by people who have no God, so when they call on them the idols cannot answer.

Elijah repaired the altar of the Lord with twelve stones according to the twelve tribes of the sons of Jacob, made a trench about it, laid the wood and the bullock in order, and had them drench the sacrifice with four barrels of water three times until the water filled the trench. At the time of the evening sacrifice Elijah prayed, Lord God of Abraham, Isaac, and of Israel, let it be known this day that thou art God in Israel and that I am thy servant. As the law appointed a sacrifice in the morning and in the evening, this was the evening sacrifice as the sun went down. Elijah prayed, Hear me, O Lord, that this people may know that thou art the Lord God and that thou hast turned their heart back again. Then the fire of the Lord fell and consumed the burnt sacrifice, the wood, the stones, and the dust, and licked up the water in the trench. When all the people saw it they fell on their faces and cried, The Lord, he is the God; the Lord, he is the God. Elijah commanded, Take the prophets of Baal, let not one of them escape, and they were brought down to the brook Kishon and slain there. In the last days it will be the same: when the Most High rains down fire again by the hands of Christ, no false prophet of Baal will escape, for they that feed the sheep of God lies will not be able to flee.

Elijah told Ahab to get up and eat and drink, for there was a sound of abundance of rain. Ahab went up to eat while Elijah went to the top of Carmel, cast himself down upon the earth, and put his face between his knees to pray. Elijah sent his servant seven times to look toward the sea; at the seventh time he reported a little cloud out of the sea like a man's hand. Elijah sent word to Ahab to prepare his chariot and get down before the rain stopped him, for the hand of the Lord was coming. The heaven grew black with clouds and wind and there was a great rain; Ahab rode to Jezreel, a city in the north in Samaria, and the hand of the Lord was on Elijah so that he girded up his loins and ran before Ahab to the entrance of Jezreel.

Ben-hadad the king of Syria gathered all his hosts, with thirty-two kings, horses, and chariots, and besieged Samaria. He sent to Ahab demanding his silver, gold, wives, and children, even the goodliest, and Ahab answered, My lord, O king, I am thine, and all that I have. Ben-hadad sent again, saying that his servants would come and search Ahab's house and take away whatsoever was pleasant in his eyes. This siege was Ahab's judgment from the Lord for trying to kill Elijah, for serving Baal, and for letting Jezebel run him and kill the prophets.

Ahab called the elders of the land, who told him not to hearken nor consent to Ben-hadad's demand, so Ahab sent word that he would grant the first demand but not the second. Ben-hadad swore by his gods to reduce Samaria to dust for handfuls among his people. Ahab answered, Let not him that girdeth on his harness boast himself as he that putteth it off. When Ben-hadad heard this while drinking with the kings in the pavilions, he commanded his servants to set themselves in array against the city; Ahab's boast had provoked him to prepare for battle.

A prophet came unto Ahab saying, Thus saith the Lord, Hast thou seen all this great multitude? I will deliver it into thine hand this day, and thou shalt know that I am the Lord. Asked by whom, the prophet answered, By the young men of the princes of the provinces, and that Ahab himself should order the battle. Two hundred and thirty-two young men of the princes of the provinces went out first, followed by the children of Israel, being seven thousand; they went out at noon while Ben-hadad was drinking himself drunk with the thirty-two kings, taking Israel lightly. The young men slew every one his man and the Syrians fled, and Israel pursued them; Ben-hadad escaped on a horse, and the king of Israel smote the horses and chariots and slew the Syrians with a great slaughter. The Most High gave the victory though Israel's numbers were small.

The prophet warned Ahab to strengthen himself and mark, for at the return of the year the king of Syria would come up against him again. The servants of Ben-hadad counseled that Israel's gods were gods of the hills, so they should fight in the plain, replace the kings with captains, and number a fresh army horse for horse and chariot for chariot; Ben-hadad hearkened and did so. At the return of the year Ben-hadad came up to fight, and the children of Israel pitched before them like two little flocks of kids while the Syrians filled the country; Israel's army was small compared to the great Syrian host. A man of God told Ahab, Because the Syrians have said the Lord is God of the hills but not of the valleys, I will deliver all this great multitude into thine hand, and ye shall know that I am the Lord. Here the Most High was giving Ahab a chance to repent, redeeming him by showing his power with fewer numbers; yet Ahab still did not repent, did not check Jezebel, and did not destroy the idols of Baal, for his sin had blinded him. Israel and Syria pitched one against the other seven days, and on the seventh day the battle was joined, and the children of Israel slew of the Syrians a hundred thousand footmen in one day. The rest fled to Aphek, where a wall fell upon twenty-seven thousand of the men left. Seven thousand against a hundred thousand, and the numbers did not matter because the Lord was with Israel; but Ahab still did not repent.

Ben-hadad fled into an inner chamber, and his servants, having heard that the kings of the house of Israel are merciful, put sackcloth on their loins and ropes on their heads and went to plead for his life. Ahab, hearing that Ben-hadad lived, called him his brother and had him brought up into his chariot. Look at Ahab's wickedness: this was a Syrian who was just trying to kill him last year, and he brought him up into the king's chariot. Ben-hadad offered to restore the cities his father had taken and give Ahab streets in Damascus, and Ahab said, I will send thee away with this covenant, and he made a covenant with the heathen and sent him away.

A son of the prophets told his neighbor to smite him in the word of the Lord; the man refused, and the prophet said a lion would slay him for not obeying the voice of the Lord, and a lion found him and slew him. Another man smote and wounded him, and the prophet disguised himself with ashes on his face and waited for the king, hiding the certain look that prophets carry, the same way we carry a certain look today. The prophet cried to the king a parable of a soldier charged to keep a prisoner on pain of his own life, who let the man escape; the king of Israel judged, So shall thy judgment be, thou thyself hast decided it. Then the prophet took the ashes away and Ahab discerned he was one of the prophets. The prophet declared, Thus saith the Lord, because thou hast let go a man whom I appointed to utter destruction, thy life shall go for his life and thy people for his people. Ben-hadad was supposed to die at war with Ahab, tied to the word that Hazael would move into the kingship of Syria, but Ahab made a covenant with him instead of killing him. The king of Israel went to his house heavy and displeased and came to Samaria, crying again over a just judgment because he would not obey the voice of the Lord. The lesson for us is the same: as it is written, so shall we do, that we may be justified and our life not be taken from us for rebellion against the Lord. --- Topics: [Idolatry](/encyclopedia/idolatry) · [Sacrifice and Atonement](/encyclopedia/sacrifice-and-atonement) · [The Covenant](/encyclopedia/the-covenant) · [The Feasts of the Most High](/encyclopedia/the-feasts-of-the-most-high) · [The Sabbath](/encyclopedia/the-sabbath)

Naboth had a vineyard next to Ahab's palace in Jezreel, and Ahab asked to trade or buy it, offering a better vineyard or its worth in money. Naboth refused because the land was the inheritance of his fathers. He could not simply hand off an inheritance that was given to him. -

Ahab went home heavy and displeased, laid down on his bed, turned away his face, and would eat no bread. He threw a fit and sulked because he could not get his way, angry that a subject would not surrender his inheritance.

Jezebel came to Ahab and asked why his spirit was so sad that he would not eat, and he told her Naboth's refusal. Jezebel mocked his weakness, telling him he was king and should let his heart be merry, and she promised to get the vineyard of Naboth for him.

Jezebel wrote letters in Ahab's name and sealed them with his seal, sending them to the elders and nobles of Naboth's city. The seal was a signet, an official mark of the king's authority, so the letters carried royal weight as if Ahab himself had written them. She commanded them to proclaim a fast, set Naboth on high, and set two sons of Belial before him to bear false witness that he blasphemed God and the king, then stone him. This was evil counsel and a murderous plot. -

The elders and nobles obeyed Jezebel's letters, proclaimed a fast, and set Naboth on high among the people. Two children of Belial, children of the devil, sat before Naboth and falsely witnessed that he had blasphemed God and the king. They carried Naboth out and stoned him to death, then sent word to Jezebel that he was dead.

When Jezebel heard Naboth was dead, she told Ahab to arise and take possession of the vineyard he had been refused. Ahab rose up and went down to take the vineyard. This is extortion, seizing what another has by violence and force. Ahab shares the guilt. He sat by and let Jezebel commit the crime because he coveted the field, then turned his face from the evil and went to claim the reward. -

The word of the Lord came to Elijah the Tishbite to go down and meet Ahab in the vineyard of Naboth. Elijah was to declare, Thus saith the Lord, hast thou killed and also taken possession, and in the place where dogs licked the blood of Naboth, dogs would lick Ahab's own blood.

Ahab called Elijah his enemy, and Elijah answered that he had found him because Ahab had sold himself to work evil in the sight of the Lord. The Most High would bring evil on Ahab, cut off every male of his house, and make his house like the house of Jeroboam and the house of Baasha because of the provocation by which he made Israel to sin. The phrase him that pisseth against the wall refers to the males, whom the Most High said he would cut off entirely. -

The Most High declared that the dogs would eat Jezebel by the wall of Jezreel. Any of Ahab's house dying in the city the dogs would eat, and any dying in the field the fowls of the air would eat, matching the curses spoken in the law. -

There was none like Ahab, who sold himself to work wickedness in the sight of the Lord, stirred up by Jezebel his wife. He did very abominably in following idols, as did the Amorites whom the Most High cast out before the children of Israel.

When Ahab heard these words he rent his clothes, put on sackcloth, fasted, and went softly, humbling himself before the Most High. Because Ahab humbled himself, the Most High told Elijah he would not bring the evil in Ahab's own days but would bring it upon his house in his son's days. The judgment was not cancelled but delayed and transferred to the next generation, showing that genuine humbling before the Most High moves his hand. --- Topics: [Idolatry](/encyclopedia/idolatry) · [Sacrifice and Atonement](/encyclopedia/sacrifice-and-atonement)

After three years without war between Syria and Israel, Jehoshaphat king of Judah comes down to the king of Israel. Ahab reminds his servants that Ramoth in Gilead belongs to Israel, yet they sit still and do not take it out of the hand of the king of Syria. Ahab asks Jehoshaphat to go with him to battle, and Jehoshaphat answers that he is as Ahab is, his people and horses as Ahab's, but first asks that they inquire at the word of the Lord. Ahab gathers about four hundred prophets, who all say with one mouth, go up, for the Lord shall deliver it into the hand of the king. This is the setting for a division that ran between the northern kingdom and the southern kingdom. After the split, the northern kingdom fell into idolatry and forsook the Levites, so a prophet of the Most High would want nothing to do with their manner of worship. -

Jehoshaphat is not moved by four hundred prophets speaking the same thing, and asks whether there is not yet a prophet of the Lord that they may inquire of him. He wants to hear from a true prophet of the Most High, not from prophets who serve the king. Ahab answers that there is one man, Micaiah the son of Imlah, but he hates him because Micaiah does not prophesy good concerning him, but evil. Jehoshaphat rebukes him, saying, let not the king say so.

The king of Israel calls an officer to hasten Micaiah, while Ahab and Jehoshaphat sit each on his throne in their robes at the entrance of the gate of Samaria, and all the prophets prophesy before them. Zedekiah the son of Chenaanah makes horns of iron and says, thus saith the Lord, with these shalt thou push the Syrians until thou have consumed them. Here again a man claims to speak for the Most High while the whole company presses Ahab to go up and prosper.

The messenger tells Micaiah that all the prophets declare good to the king with one mouth, and urges him to speak likewise. Micaiah answers that whatever the Lord saith unto him, that will he speak, and at first he echoes the others, prompting the king to adjure him to tell nothing but the truth. Micaiah then reveals what he saw, all Israel scattered on the hills as sheep having no shepherd, and the Lord saying these have no master. He saw the Lord on his throne with all the host of heaven, and a spirit that offered to be a lying spirit in the mouth of all Ahab's prophets to persuade him to fall at Ramoth-gilead. The Most High put a lying spirit in the mouth of these prophets and spoke evil concerning Ahab. The deceiver as well as the deceived are under the hand of the Most High, who uses the lie to bring the judgment he has already declared. -

Zedekiah the son of Chenaanah smites Micaiah on the cheek and asks which way the spirit of the Lord went from him to speak to Micaiah, defending his own false prophecy. The king of Israel orders Micaiah taken back and put in prison, fed with bread and water of affliction until Ahab returns in peace. Micaiah answers that if Ahab returns at all in peace, the Lord has not spoken by him, and calls all the people to hearken. His word stands as the test of who truly spoke for the Most High.

The king of Israel and Jehoshaphat go up to Ramoth-gilead. Ahab disguises himself and tells Jehoshaphat to wear his robes, hoping to escape the word spoken against him, while the king of Syria commands his captains to fight only against the king of Israel. The captains pursue Jehoshaphat until they perceive he is not the king of Israel and turn back. A certain man draws a bow at a venture and smites Ahab between the joints of the harness, and the king is held up in his chariot until he dies at even, the blood running into the chariot. When they wash the chariot in the pool of Samaria, the dogs lick up his blood according to the word of the Lord. The judgment pronounced earlier against Ahab and his house begins to be fulfilled exactly as spoken.

The rest of the acts of Ahab, the ivory house he made and the cities he built, are written in the book of the Chronicles of the kings of Israel. Ahab sleeps with his fathers, and Ahaziah his son reigns in his stead.

Jehoshaphat the son of Asa begins to reign over Judah in the fourth year of Ahab, at thirty-five years old, and reigns twenty-five years in Jerusalem. He walks in the ways of Asa his father, doing right in the eyes of the Lord, though the high places are not taken away and the people still burn incense there. Jehoshaphat makes peace with the king of Israel and puts the remnant of the sodomites out of the land. There is then no king in Edom but a deputy, because Edom had been subdued and had not yet revolted. -

Ahaziah the son of Ahab begins to reign over Israel in Samaria in the seventeenth year of Jehoshaphat and reigns two years. He does evil in the sight of the Lord and walks in the way of his father and his mother and in the way of Jeroboam the son of Nebat, who made Israel to sin. He serves Baal and worships him and provokes the Lord God of Israel to anger, according to all that his father had done. The sin of the house of Ahab continues into the next generation. --- Topics: [Esau and Edom](/encyclopedia/esau-and-edom) · [Idolatry](/encyclopedia/idolatry) · [The Priesthood](/encyclopedia/the-priesthood)

The seven nations cast out before Israel, the Hittites, Girgashites, Amorites, Canaanites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites, greater and mightier than Israel, are Hamitic nations. Thou shalt smite them and utterly destroy them; thou shalt make no covenant with them, nor shew mercy unto them. Since the days of old the Most High has never been about the love-of-the-world gospel; throw that doctrine in the trash. This is why they do not want you reading the old covenant: verses like this correct the miseducation received through Christianity, and the mind begins to correct itself as you read.

Neither shalt thou make marriages with them: the Most High forbids marrying outside the nation. The seed of the fathers today is found among the so-called blacks, Hispanics, and Native Indians, who make up the twelve tribes of Israel; a spouse may come from any of the twelve tribes, but from within the tribes only. Going outside your nation for a husband or wife is despising your brethren in your heart. Whom you marry is the greatest commitment you make in this life; if you truly loved your people, you would choose one of your own people to become aged together with. They will turn away thy son from following me: the nations are strangers to the Most High and cannot come into this covenant, so they draw the Israelite spouse off to religions that accept everything. Christianity accepts that union, and that is how they turn you away from your God.
Thus shall ye deal with them: destroy their altars, break down their images, cut down their groves, and burn their graven images with fire. Nothing of their worship was to be spared or adopted.

For thou art an holy people unto the Lord thy God: this is one of the most uplifting scriptures in the book, and it should be etched into your children's minds from the moment they begin to read, until it is implanted into their spirit. The mind controls the body: what goes into the mind comes out through the body, so a people that knows it is holy and special above all people walks and carries itself differently. Being chosen above all people keeps you out of the affairs of this world, their fashions, their hairstyles, their trends and challenges, and keeping up with the Joneses; you cannot flip-flop with every new wave and still carry the speciality the Most High put on you.

The Lord did not choose Israel for their number, for ye were the fewest of all people: only threescore and ten souls came out of the loins of Jacob when Israel first went down, as Genesis records, some places reading seventy and some counting seventy-five. But because the Lord loved you: the Most High needs no other reason, he simply loved us, and we should never apologize for that. He kept the oath sworn unto the fathers and redeemed Israel out of the house of bondmen, from the hand of Pharaoh king of Egypt; Israel came out from under Rameses.

Know therefore that the Lord thy God, he is God, the faithful God, which keepeth covenant and mercy with them that love him and keep his commandments to a thousand generations, and repayeth them that hate him to their face. This is the same teaching as the new testament: loving the Most High is keeping his commandments, and refusing his commandments shows him with your actions that you hate him, and then judgment comes. From the jump it has always been the same: love God, keep the commandments; nothing changed between the covenants.

If ye hearken to these judgments and keep and do them, the Lord keeps the covenant and the mercy: he will love thee, bless thee, and multiply thee, blessing the fruit of thy womb, thy land, thy corn, wine, oil, kine, and sheep, blessed above all people, which goes right back to verse 6. The Lord will take away from thee all sickness and put none of the evil diseases of Egypt upon thee, but will lay them upon all them that hate thee. That still reigns true today: keep the commandments and the Most High will keep you from the diseases of modern-day Egypt, and if you do catch something, he will revive you and bring you back to your health.

Thou shalt consume all the people which the Lord thy God shall deliver thee; thine eye shall have no pity upon them, neither shalt thou serve their gods, for that will be a snare unto thee. Those days are coming back when Christ returns.

If thou shalt say in thine heart, these nations are more than I: fear them not, but remember what the Lord did unto Pharaoh and unto all Egypt, the signs, the wonders, the mighty hand and the stretched out arm; so shall he do unto all the people of whom thou art afraid. The Lord will send the hornet among them until even those that hide themselves are destroyed, and he will put out those nations before thee by little and little, lest the beasts of the field increase upon thee. He shall deliver their kings into thine hand, and thou shalt destroy their name from under heaven. There is no way to read [Deuteronomy 7](/bible/deuteronomy/7) and still say God loves everybody; that idea is being drunk on Christianity, not reading the book.

The graven images of their gods shall ye burn with fire: desire not the silver or gold that is on them, lest thou be snared therein, for it is an abomination to the Lord thy God. Neither shalt thou bring an abomination into thine house, lest thou be a cursed thing like it. Bring it up to today: the Jesus pieces, the crosses, the ankhs, and the rosary beads wrapped around the neck and rubbed in prayer make the wearer an abomination and a cursed thing just like the idol. The main abomination we bring into our house is the Christmas tree of Jeremiah 10: the tree cut down, fastened with nails and hammers, and decked with silver and with gold, whether cut from the forest or bought as a fake tree from the store.

name: Jezebel
charge: Killing the prophets of the Lord; promoting Baal; witchcrafts
summary: Ahab's Zidonian queen cut off the prophets of the Lord, fed four hundred and fifty prophets of Baal at her table, swore to kill Elijah, and stirred up her husband to every evil. Jehu named her whoredoms and witchcrafts as the reason there could be no peace.
offense: Jezebel used the place she held beside Ahab to sustain false worship and attack the Lord's servants. While she cut off the prophets, Obadiah hid a hundred in caves and fed them with bread and water (1 Kings 18:4). Within the same royal household, one person's resources supported persecution while another's service preserved its intended victims. Elijah summoned the prophets of Baal and the prophets of the groves who ate at Jezebel's table (1 Kings 18:19). Royal provision helped maintain the worship that opposed the Lord. After Carmel, Jezebel answered the report of the prophets' deaths with an oath to kill Elijah (1 Kings 19:1-2). The public judgment did not bring her to submission; it brought a renewed threat against the man who had declared it. Her conduct toward Naboth showed the same use of authority. She wrote in Ahab's name, sealed the letters with his seal, and instructed the elders to proclaim a fast, install false witnesses, and stone an innocent man (1 Kings 21:8-14). Forms belonging to religion and judgment were used to obtain a coveted vineyard. A fast did not sanctify the lie, and the king's seal did not make murder lawful. Revelation 2:20 uses her name for a woman who claims prophetic standing while seducing the servants into fornication and idolatrous eating. The danger is not confined to an open enemy: corrupt teaching seeks a place within the company it turns aside.
judgment: Elijah declared that dogs would eat Jezebel by the wall of Jezreel (1 Kings 21:23). When Jehu was anointed, the charge against Ahab's house expressly included avenging the blood of the prophets and servants shed at her hand (2 Kings 9:7-10). The victims she had attempted to remove remained named before the Lord. As Jehu entered Jezreel, she looked from a window and challenged him with Zimri's fate. Jehu called for those on his side, and two or three eunuchs looked out. At his command they threw her down (2 Kings 9:30-33). The household from which she had exercised power no longer preserved her against the judgment. When men went to bury her, only the skull, feet, and palms of her hands remained. Jehu recalled Elijah's word concerning the dogs and the loss of an identifiable grave (2 Kings 9:34-37). Her rank as a king's daughter could not restore the body or overturn the sentence. The woman who had ordered others removed from the land could not secure her own remembrance within it.

entries.commentary: The word of the Most High comes to Jehu son of Hanani against Baasha, because though he was exalted out of the dust and made prince over Israel, he walked in the way of Jeroboam and made Israel sin. Therefore the Most High will make his house like the house of Jeroboam, and those who die in the city the dogs will eat and those in the field the fowls will eat. The same judgment falls because the same sin is repeated, just as descendants keep the pattern of their fathers though they saw the ruin it brought.

Elah son of Baasha reigns two years, and his servant Zimri, captain of half his chariots, conspires against him while he is drunk in a steward's house and kills him. Zimri, on taking the throne, slays all the house of Baasha, leaving not one male, according to the word spoken by Jehu against Baasha. All of it comes for the sins of Baasha and Elah, who provoked the Most High to anger with their vanities. -

Zimri reigns only seven days in Tirzah. When the people encamped against Gibbethon hear he has slain the king, they make Omri, captain of the host, king over Israel. Omri and Israel go up and besiege Tirzah, and when Zimri sees the city taken, he burns the king's house over himself and dies. His death comes for his sins in walking in the way of Jeroboam, and his treason is recorded, treason being punishable by death in that time.

Israel is divided: half follow Tibni son of Ginath and half follow Omri, but Omri's followers prevail, Tibni dies, and Omri reigns. Omri buys the hill Samaria from Shemer for two talents of silver, builds the city, and names it after Shemer. Omri does worse than all before him, walking in the way of Jeroboam, then sleeps with his fathers, and Ahab his son reigns in his place.

Ahab son of Omri reigns twenty-two years in Samaria and does evil above all that were before him. As if walking in Jeroboam's sins were a light thing, he takes Jezebel daughter of Ethbaal king of the Zidonians to wife and serves and worships Baal, rearing an altar and a grove, provoking the Most High more than all the kings before him. This mirrors Solomon, who followed Ashtoreth the goddess of the Zidonians, and the marrying outside the people that the law forbids because it turns the heart to other gods. In his days Hiel of Bethel rebuilds Jericho, laying its foundation in his firstborn Abiram and setting up its gates in his youngest Segub, according to the word spoken by Joshua. -

After many days the word of the Lord came to Elijah in the third year: Go show thyself unto Ahab, and I will send rain upon the earth. There was a sore famine in Samaria. Ahab called Obadiah, governor of his house, who feared the Lord greatly; when Jezebel cut off the prophets of the Lord, Obadiah took an hundred prophets and hid them by fifty in a cave and fed them with bread and water, putting his own life in danger to save them. The famine was so sore it was hitting the animals, so Ahab and Obadiah divided the land between them, each going his own way to seek fountains and brooks to find grass to save the horses and mules alive. This was the fruit of the drought Elijah had pronounced.

As Obadiah went his way, Elijah met him; Obadiah fell on his face and said, Art thou my lord Elijah? Elijah told him to go tell Ahab that Elijah is here. Obadiah was afraid, for Ahab had searched every nation and kingdom to find and slay Elijah; that is how badly Jezebel wanted him dead, so she got Ahab to do her bidding. This is why Elijah had been on the run, first by Jordan, then years with the widow. Obadiah feared that the spirit of the Lord would carry Elijah away and Ahab would slay him for a false report, so he pleaded his own record: he feared the Lord from his youth and had hidden a hundred of the Lord's prophets by fifty in a cave. Elijah swore by the Lord of hosts that he would surely show himself to Ahab that day, and so Obadiah went to Ahab, and Ahab came to meet Elijah.

When Ahab saw Elijah he said, Art thou he that troubleth Israel? That is the mind of a wicked person: he blamed the trouble on the ordained prophet of God rather than on his own wickedness. When the spirit is gone, wisdom cannot enter a malicious soul, so Ahab had thoughts without understanding. Elijah answered, I have not troubled Israel, but thou and thy father's house, in that ye have forsaken the commandments of the Lord and thou hast followed Baalim. It was Ahab following the sin of Jeroboam the son of Nebat, worshipping the golden calves, that brought the trouble. Elijah commanded that all Israel be gathered to Mount Carmel with the four hundred and fifty prophets of Baal and the four hundred prophets of the groves that eat at Jezebel's table. Jezebel was the one feeding these eight hundred and fifty false prophets and encouraging them, and Ahab never checked her.

Ahab gathered the prophets and all Israel to Mount Carmel, and Elijah said unto the people, How long halt ye between two opinions? If the Lord be God, follow him, but if Baal, then follow him. And the people answered him not a word. That is a call for all of us to examine ourselves: cast away every burden and sin and follow the Most High and his son fully, keeping the commandments, and do not keep one foot in and one foot out. Being lukewarm, playing the middle ground, ends with Christ spewing a man out of his mouth, and the next step after that is death. Elijah proposed the test: let each side dress a bullock, lay it on wood, and put no fire under, and the God that answereth by fire, let him be God. All the people said, It is well spoken.

The prophets of Baal dressed their bullock first and called on the name of Baal from morning until noon, saying, O Baal, hear us, but there was no voice nor any that answered, and they leaped upon the altar. Picture the scene: eight hundred and fifty men doing this, running wild, while Elijah sat back watching the madness. At noon Elijah mocked them, saying, Cry aloud, for he is a god; either he is talking, or pursuing, or on a journey, or peradventure he sleepeth and must be awaked. They cried aloud and cut themselves with knives and lancets till the blood gushed out, for cutting themselves was part of their false worship whenever they called on Baal. From midday past the time of the evening sacrifice there was neither voice nor any to answer nor any that regarded. No one answered because the Most High will not give his glory to another, and the gods of the nations are idols that are not real; they are made up by people who have no God, so when they call on them the idols cannot answer.

Elijah repaired the altar of the Lord with twelve stones according to the twelve tribes of the sons of Jacob, made a trench about it, laid the wood and the bullock in order, and had them drench the sacrifice with four barrels of water three times until the water filled the trench. At the time of the evening sacrifice Elijah prayed, Lord God of Abraham, Isaac, and of Israel, let it be known this day that thou art God in Israel and that I am thy servant. As the law appointed a sacrifice in the morning and in the evening, this was the evening sacrifice as the sun went down. Elijah prayed, Hear me, O Lord, that this people may know that thou art the Lord God and that thou hast turned their heart back again. Then the fire of the Lord fell and consumed the burnt sacrifice, the wood, the stones, and the dust, and licked up the water in the trench. When all the people saw it they fell on their faces and cried, The Lord, he is the God; the Lord, he is the God. Elijah commanded, Take the prophets of Baal, let not one of them escape, and they were brought down to the brook Kishon and slain there. In the last days it will be the same: when the Most High rains down fire again by the hands of Christ, no false prophet of Baal will escape, for they that feed the sheep of God lies will not be able to flee.

Elijah told Ahab to get up and eat and drink, for there was a sound of abundance of rain. Ahab went up to eat while Elijah went to the top of Carmel, cast himself down upon the earth, and put his face between his knees to pray. Elijah sent his servant seven times to look toward the sea; at the seventh time he reported a little cloud out of the sea like a man's hand. Elijah sent word to Ahab to prepare his chariot and get down before the rain stopped him, for the hand of the Lord was coming. The heaven grew black with clouds and wind and there was a great rain; Ahab rode to Jezreel, a city in the north in Samaria, and the hand of the Lord was on Elijah so that he girded up his loins and ran before Ahab to the entrance of Jezreel.

Ahab told Jezebel all that Elijah had done and how he had slain all the prophets with the sword. This shows the devil on Ahab: he ran back running his mouth about the slain false prophets and never once mentioned that Elijah had brought rain after a three-year drought. Jezebel sent a messenger swearing that she would make Elijah's life as the life of one of the slain prophets by the next day. She wanted him dead because he had taken away her power and the name she had gotten in Israel through her idolatry. This is the same wicked spirit named in Revelation, the top-notch wicked woman who feared no God at all. When Elijah saw it, he arose and went for his life and left his servant behind. He was an old man, not young like Elisha, and he knew Jezebel would truly try to kill him, so he fled.

Elijah went a day's journey into the wilderness, sat down under a juniper tree, and requested that he might die, saying, It is enough; now, O Lord, take away my life, for I am not better than my fathers. Our forefathers had ultimate faith and understood regeneration: they could ask the Most High to take their life and let them rest in the grave, trusting he would bring them back whenever he chose. They did not have the lust of the eyes and of this world as their main thought. Elijah counted himself no better than his fathers even though he was great; Christ later called John the Baptist, who came in the spirit of Elijah, the greatest of the prophets. As Elijah slept, an angel touched him and said, Arise and eat, and there was a cake baking on the coals and a cruise of water at his head. He ate and lay down again; a second time the angel touched him and said the journey was too great for him. He arose and ate, and went in the strength of that meat forty days and forty nights unto Horeb, the mount of God. The Most High made food through the angel that sustained Elijah for forty days; that was good spiritual food.

Elijah came to a cave in Horeb and lodged there, and the word of the Lord asked, What doest thou here, Elijah? He answered that he had been very zealous for the Lord God of hosts, for the children of Israel had forsaken the covenant, thrown down the altars, and slain the prophets, and he only was left and they sought his life. The Lord told him to stand upon the mount, and the Lord passed by: a great and strong wind rent the mountains, but the Lord was not in the wind; then an earthquake, but the Lord was not in the earthquake; then a fire, but the Lord was not in the fire; and after the fire a still small voice. That is the power of the Most High and of Christ: wind of extreme speed, an earthquake to catch up with it, then fire, and then he spoke in a still small voice. We do not know who we are dealing with; this is the same Most High who destroyed all but eight in the flood and rained fire on the cities of Sodom. Fear him who has the power to destroy the body. When Elijah heard it he wrapped his face in his mantle and stood in the cave entrance, and the voice asked again, What doest thou here, Elijah? He answered the same, that he was zealous for the Lord and that he alone was left and they sought his life.

The Lord sent Elijah back to the wilderness of Damascus to anoint Hazael to be king over Syria, Jehu the son of Nimshi to be king over Israel, and Elisha the son of Shaphat of Abel-meholah to be prophet in his room. Him that escaped the sword of Hazael would Jehu slay, and him that escaped Jehu would Elisha slay. The Most High was telling Elijah not to worry, for he had things set up: Syria would come against the northern kingdom, Jehu would rise up to slay Ahab and all his house, and Elisha would pick up where Elijah left off when it was his time to come home. The Lord said he had left himself seven thousand in Israel, all the knees which had not bowed unto Baal. Elijah was not by himself; the Lord had people reserved who had not yet awakened, ordained to come in at a certain time for a certain purpose. It is the same today: our job is to preach the word, for we never know what video or flyer will wake up the ones the Lord has reserved.

Elijah found Elisha plowing with twelve yoke of oxen and cast his mantle, like a cloak, upon him. Elisha left the oxen and ran after Elijah, asking to kiss his father and mother first, then he would follow. Elisha returned, took a yoke of oxen and slew them, boiled their flesh with the instruments of the oxen, and gave to the people, and they did eat; then he arose and followed Elijah and ministered unto him. He fed the people before he left and then he was gone on his mission, not turning back.

Naboth had a vineyard next to Ahab's palace in Jezreel, and Ahab asked to trade or buy it, offering a better vineyard or its worth in money. Naboth refused because the land was the inheritance of his fathers. He could not simply hand off an inheritance that was given to him. -

Ahab went home heavy and displeased, laid down on his bed, turned away his face, and would eat no bread. He threw a fit and sulked because he could not get his way, angry that a subject would not surrender his inheritance.

Jezebel came to Ahab and asked why his spirit was so sad that he would not eat, and he told her Naboth's refusal. Jezebel mocked his weakness, telling him he was king and should let his heart be merry, and she promised to get the vineyard of Naboth for him.

Jezebel wrote letters in Ahab's name and sealed them with his seal, sending them to the elders and nobles of Naboth's city. The seal was a signet, an official mark of the king's authority, so the letters carried royal weight as if Ahab himself had written them. She commanded them to proclaim a fast, set Naboth on high, and set two sons of Belial before him to bear false witness that he blasphemed God and the king, then stone him. This was evil counsel and a murderous plot. -

The elders and nobles obeyed Jezebel's letters, proclaimed a fast, and set Naboth on high among the people. Two children of Belial, children of the devil, sat before Naboth and falsely witnessed that he had blasphemed God and the king. They carried Naboth out and stoned him to death, then sent word to Jezebel that he was dead.

When Jezebel heard Naboth was dead, she told Ahab to arise and take possession of the vineyard he had been refused. Ahab rose up and went down to take the vineyard. This is extortion, seizing what another has by violence and force. Ahab shares the guilt. He sat by and let Jezebel commit the crime because he coveted the field, then turned his face from the evil and went to claim the reward. -

The word of the Lord came to Elijah the Tishbite to go down and meet Ahab in the vineyard of Naboth. Elijah was to declare, Thus saith the Lord, hast thou killed and also taken possession, and in the place where dogs licked the blood of Naboth, dogs would lick Ahab's own blood.

Ahab called Elijah his enemy, and Elijah answered that he had found him because Ahab had sold himself to work evil in the sight of the Lord. The Most High would bring evil on Ahab, cut off every male of his house, and make his house like the house of Jeroboam and the house of Baasha because of the provocation by which he made Israel to sin. The phrase him that pisseth against the wall refers to the males, whom the Most High said he would cut off entirely. -

The Most High declared that the dogs would eat Jezebel by the wall of Jezreel. Any of Ahab's house dying in the city the dogs would eat, and any dying in the field the fowls of the air would eat, matching the curses spoken in the law. -

There was none like Ahab, who sold himself to work wickedness in the sight of the Lord, stirred up by Jezebel his wife. He did very abominably in following idols, as did the Amorites whom the Most High cast out before the children of Israel.

When Ahab heard these words he rent his clothes, put on sackcloth, fasted, and went softly, humbling himself before the Most High. Because Ahab humbled himself, the Most High told Elijah he would not bring the evil in Ahab's own days but would bring it upon his house in his son's days. The judgment was not cancelled but delayed and transferred to the next generation, showing that genuine humbling before the Most High moves his hand. --- Topics: [Idolatry](/encyclopedia/idolatry) · [Sacrifice and Atonement](/encyclopedia/sacrifice-and-atonement)

Elisha sends one of the children of the prophets to Ramoth-gilead to anoint Jehu king over Israel, pour the oil on his head, and flee. Jehu is charged to smite the house of Ahab to avenge the blood of the prophets and of the servants of the Most High shed at the hand of Jezebel, whose work was to kill the prophets while weak Ahab let it continue. The word declares the whole house of Ahab shall perish, and the dogs shall eat Jezebel in the portion of Jezreel with none to bury her.

Jehu's fellow captains ask why the mad fellow came, and when he tells them the prophet anointed him king, they hasten to put their garments under him and blow the trumpets, proclaiming Jehu king. Jehu conspires against Jehoram and charges that none escape the city to carry the news to Jezreel. He rides toward Jezreel where Jehoram lay wounded, and Ahaziah king of Judah had come down to see him.

A watchman spies Jehu's company, and two horsemen sent to ask if it is peace are each told to turn behind him and do not return, for the driving is furious like the driving of Jehu. Jehoram himself goes out and asks if it is peace, and Jehu answers that there can be no peace while the whoredoms and witchcrafts of his mother Jezebel are so many. Jehu draws his bow with full strength and smites Jehoram through the heart, then casts him into the portion of Naboth the Jezreelite according to the word of the Most High.

Ahaziah king of Judah flees but Jehu pursues and has him smitten in his chariot; he flees to Megiddo and dies there. His servants carry him to Jerusalem and bury him in the sepulchre of his fathers in the city of David.

Jezebel paints her face and tires her head, returning to her seductive ways as Jehu enters the gate. Jehu calls out for who is on his side, and two or three eunuchs look out. At Jehu's word they throw her down, her blood is sprinkled on the wall and the horses, and he treads her under foot. When they go to bury her they find only the skull, the feet, and the palms of her hands, fulfilling the word spoken by Elijah that dogs would eat the flesh of Jezebel and her carcass would be as dung upon the field.

name: Hiel the Bethelite
charge: Rebuilding Jericho under the oath Joshua swore before the Lord
summary: When Jericho fell, Joshua adjured Israel: cursed be the man that riseth up and buildeth this city; he shall lay the foundation in his firstborn and set up the gates in his youngest son. Generations later, in the days of Ahab, Hiel rebuilt it at the cost of Abiram his firstborn and Segub his youngest son.
offense: After Jericho fell, Joshua pronounced a curse before the Lord upon the man who would rise to rebuild it: he would lay the foundation in his firstborn and set up the gates in his youngest son (Joshua 6:26). The destroyed city stood under a word that placed a limit upon a future builder's ambition. In Ahab's days Hiel of Bethel rebuilt it (1 Kings 16:34). The account places the undertaking beside Ahab's establishment of Baal worship and his exceeding provocation of the Lord. The kingdom's departure was visible not only at an altar but also in a building work that crossed a boundary spoken generations earlier. The passage of years did not make Joshua's word an empty saying. A man might see walls to be raised and gates to be fitted while overlooking the charge that governed the place. The land could not be measured only by what could be built upon it. Its history included the Lord's judgment as well as the builder's opportunity.
judgment: Hiel laid the foundation in Abiram his firstborn and set up the gates in Segub his youngest son, according to the word the Lord had spoken by Joshua (1 Kings 16:34). The two ends of the undertaking answered the two parts of the curse. The names of the sons preserve the cost beside the report that the city was built. The judgment was not cancelled by the successful completion of the structure. Gates could stand while the household mourned. Outward accomplishment was therefore no proof that the work had been undertaken with the Lord's approval. Joshua 23:14 declares that not one good thing spoken by the Lord had failed. Hiel's history shows that the word of warning was no less certain. The generation that heard Joshua had passed, but the Lord who spoke through him had not forgotten the boundary. What was old to the builder remained binding before God.

entries.commentary: Jericho was straitly shut up because of the children of Israel: none went out and none came in. Jericho had a military, and a garrison, a military base, was built there, with the walls shut so nobody could enter or leave. The Lord said unto Joshua, See, I have given into thine hand Jericho, and the king thereof, and the mighty men of valour: the battle was already decided.

The battle plan came from the Lord: compass the city with all the men of war once a day for six days, seven priests bearing seven trumpets of rams' horns before the ark; on the seventh day compass the city seven times, and at the long blast all the people shout with a great shout, and the wall shall fall down flat. The blowing of the trumpets activates the armies of the Lord, the angels, to help in battle. Remember Elisha's servant: when his eyes were opened he saw the host of angels that were there warring and protecting Israel. This is the spirit behind the men of Israel rehearsing the righteous acts with trumpets and shofars today, at the camps and at the new moons; it is spiritual and an act of faith.

Joshua called the priests and gave the order: seven priests bear seven trumpets before the ark, the armed men pass on before the ark, and the rereward, the guards in the rear, came after the ark. Joshua commanded the people, Ye shall not shout, nor make any noise with your voice, neither shall any word proceed out of your mouth, until the day I bid you shout; then shall ye shout. The ark of the Lord compassed the city once, and they came into the camp and lodged there.

They repeated the act six days back to back, rising early, the priests bearing the ark and blowing the trumpets, the armed men before and the rereward after, one compass of the city each day. Every army in the world stole this from the Israelites: the pass and review of the militaries, with their battalions and units, their guidons with the eagle on the tip of the spear, marching round the field sounding off with cadences and trumpets, is patterned after what Israel did here.

On the seventh day they rose about the dawning of the day and compassed the city seven times. There is something about the number seven that the Lord loves; you read about it in Revelation. At the seventh time, when the priests blew with the trumpets, Joshua said unto the people, Shout; for the Lord hath given you the city. The men apply [Joshua 6](/bible/joshua/6) to this day: when a scoffer will not hear the word and thinks to outcry the truth, the brothers say the scripture together with one mind, one body, one spirit. That unity is spiritual, a rehearsal of the righteous acts. Unity and order are what the enemies fear: not gangs and drug dealing, but the so-called Black man, Hispanic man, and Native American man unified in the order of a military, with structure and organization. That is what puts fear in the nations.

The city shall be accursed, even it and all that are therein, to the Lord: only Rahab the harlot shall live, she and all that are with her in the house, because she hid the messengers. She made a covenant with the spies: she would conceal them and assist Israel, knowing the Lord was with Israel, as long as her family was saved when the city fell. Rahab was a Canaanite, a heathen, yet the heathen can be blessed when they do it to benefit Israel; blessed is he that blesseth thee. Rahab is the scripture's own example that a man is justified by works and not by faith only: faith and works go hand in hand, for your actions prove whether you believe. Was not Rahab the harlot justified by works, when she had received the messengers and sent them out another way? As the body without the spirit is dead, so faith without works is dead also. Works by the Bible's own dictionary is keeping his commandments: set your hope in God, forget not his works, but keep his commandments. Words say a lot, but actions always speak louder, and by him actions are weighed. Keep yourselves from the accursed thing, lest ye make yourselves accursed and make the camp of Israel a curse, and trouble it: your individual sins affect the whole nation of Israel, your brothers, your sisters, and the children. That is why we must examine ourselves whether we be in the faith. All the silver and gold and vessels of brass and iron were consecrated unto the Lord, separated and sanctified for his treasury alone: nobody was to gain personally from this war.

The people shouted when the priests blew with the trumpets, and the wall fell down flat. That shout is [Isaiah 58:1](/bible/isaiah/58#v1) in action, cry aloud and spare not: the sound coming out of their mouths with the trumpets broke everything down, like thousands of lions roaring at once. The people went up into the city, every man straight before him, and they took the city and utterly destroyed all that was in it, both man and woman, young and old, ox, sheep, and ass, with the edge of the sword.

Joshua sent the two spies into the harlot's house to bring out Rahab and all that she had, as they sware unto her; they brought out her father, mother, brethren, and all her kindred, and left them without the camp of Israel. They burnt the city with fire and all that was therein; only the silver, gold, and vessels of brass and iron went into the treasury of the house of the Lord. Joshua saved Rahab the harlot alive and her father's household, and she dwelleth in Israel even unto this day, because she hid the messengers. She helped the nation of Israel toward rulership, and that is the only help Israel wants from the other nations: not food stamps, welfare, or reparations, but tell our people who they are, the Israelites the Bible speaks of, the so-called Blacks, Hispanics, and Native Americans, and that we must keep the commandments of the Most High. Whoever does that will receive mercy just as Rahab did.

Joshua adjured them at that time: cursed be the man before the Lord that riseth up and buildeth this city Jericho; he shall lay the foundation thereof in his firstborn, and in his youngest son shall he set up the gates of it. The city was not to be rebuilt. So the Lord was with Joshua, and his fame was noised throughout all the country.

The word of the Most High comes to Jehu son of Hanani against Baasha, because though he was exalted out of the dust and made prince over Israel, he walked in the way of Jeroboam and made Israel sin. Therefore the Most High will make his house like the house of Jeroboam, and those who die in the city the dogs will eat and those in the field the fowls will eat. The same judgment falls because the same sin is repeated, just as descendants keep the pattern of their fathers though they saw the ruin it brought.

Elah son of Baasha reigns two years, and his servant Zimri, captain of half his chariots, conspires against him while he is drunk in a steward's house and kills him. Zimri, on taking the throne, slays all the house of Baasha, leaving not one male, according to the word spoken by Jehu against Baasha. All of it comes for the sins of Baasha and Elah, who provoked the Most High to anger with their vanities. -

Zimri reigns only seven days in Tirzah. When the people encamped against Gibbethon hear he has slain the king, they make Omri, captain of the host, king over Israel. Omri and Israel go up and besiege Tirzah, and when Zimri sees the city taken, he burns the king's house over himself and dies. His death comes for his sins in walking in the way of Jeroboam, and his treason is recorded, treason being punishable by death in that time.

Israel is divided: half follow Tibni son of Ginath and half follow Omri, but Omri's followers prevail, Tibni dies, and Omri reigns. Omri buys the hill Samaria from Shemer for two talents of silver, builds the city, and names it after Shemer. Omri does worse than all before him, walking in the way of Jeroboam, then sleeps with his fathers, and Ahab his son reigns in his place.

Ahab son of Omri reigns twenty-two years in Samaria and does evil above all that were before him. As if walking in Jeroboam's sins were a light thing, he takes Jezebel daughter of Ethbaal king of the Zidonians to wife and serves and worships Baal, rearing an altar and a grove, provoking the Most High more than all the kings before him. This mirrors Solomon, who followed Ashtoreth the goddess of the Zidonians, and the marrying outside the people that the law forbids because it turns the heart to other gods. In his days Hiel of Bethel rebuilds Jericho, laying its foundation in his firstborn Abiram and setting up its gates in his youngest Segub, according to the word spoken by Joshua. -

If a man vow a vow unto the Lord, or swear an oath to bind his soul with a bond, he shall not break his word; he shall do according to all that proceedeth out of his mouth. A vow is promising the Lord you will do a thing. Say a man vows, Lord, if you bring this to pass I will never eat swine again; he must keep that vow, and he cannot go back on it and simply ask forgiveness afterward. If thou shalt forbear to vow, it shall be no sin in thee; but that which is gone out of thy lips thou shalt keep and perform. Do not suffer thy mouth to cause thy flesh to sin, and do not say before the angel that it was an error.

A daughter in her father's house in her youth who vows a vow is under her father's covering. If her father hears her vow and holds his peace, all her vows stand and every bond wherewith she hath bound her soul stands. But if her father disallow her in the day that he heareth, not any of her vows or bonds shall stand, and the Lord shall forgive her, because her father disallowed her. That shows the power the Most High put in the man of the house: a father can hear his daughter bind herself and say no, and the Lord releases her.

The same covering passes to the husband. If a woman with a husband vows, or utters ought out of her lips wherewith she binds her soul, and her husband hears it and holds his peace in the day that he hears it, her vows stand. But if her husband disallow her on the day that he heard it, he makes her vow of none effect, and the Lord shall forgive her. A wife could be binding herself to something she cannot perform, and her husband can step in and say, Lord, do not hear that vow, and the Most High releases her because of her husband. That is the power of the head of the house: the husband keeping the commandments stands between his wife and a bond that would jack her up. That is a reason to love your hedge, not to despise it.

Every vow of a widow, and of her that is divorced, wherewith they have bound their souls, shall stand against her. She has no father or husband to disallow it, so what she vows she must perform. The husband is a hedge of protection; where no hedge is, the possession is spoiled. The married woman has a covering that the widow and the divorced woman do not have.

If a wife vowed in her husband's house and her husband heard it and held his peace and disallowed her not, then all her vows stand. Her husband may establish every vow and every binding oath to afflict the soul, or her husband may make it void. If he altogether holds his peace at her from day to day, then he establishes all her vows and confirms all her bonds, because he held his peace in the day that he heard them. Holding your peace is confirming it. But if he shall any ways make them void after that he hath heard them, then he shall bear her iniquity. He cannot hear her vow, hold his peace day after day, and then come later to void it; he had the power to stop it and did not, so the iniquity falls to him. And this runs one way: a wife cannot disallow or nullify her husband's vow. This is the order of the house: the husband is the head of the wife, even as Christ is the head of the church, and he is the saviour of the body; so let the wives be subject to their own husbands in every thing, even in what is vowed in prayer.

These are the statutes which the Lord commanded Moses, between a man and his wife, and between the father and his daughter, being yet in her youth in her father's house. The whole chapter is the government of vows inside the house of Israel. --- Topics: [Clean and Unclean Meats](/encyclopedia/clean-and-unclean-meats) · [Sacrifice and Atonement](/encyclopedia/sacrifice-and-atonement) · [The Covenant](/encyclopedia/the-covenant) · [The Feasts of the Most High](/encyclopedia/the-feasts-of-the-most-high) · [The Priesthood](/encyclopedia/the-priesthood) · [The Sabbath](/encyclopedia/the-sabbath)

A man's wisdom makes his face to shine, and the boldness of his face is changed; the counsel is to keep the king's commandment in regard of the oath of the Most High. The king spoken of here is the Most High Himself, for verse 3 says He does whatsoever pleases Him; therefore keeping the king's commandment is keeping the Lord's commandment, and where the word of the king is, there is power.

Whoso keeps the commandment shall feel no evil thing, and a wise man's heart discerns both time and judgment, for to every purpose there is a time and judgment. No man has power over the spirit to retain the spirit, nor power in the day of death; there is no discharge in that war, and wickedness will not deliver those given to it.

Solomon applied his heart to every work done under the sun and saw one man rule over another to his own hurt. He saw the wicked buried and then forgotten in the place where they had done their evil, and because sentence against an evil work is not executed speedily, the hearts of the sons of men are fully set to do evil.

Though a sinner do evil a hundred times and his days be prolonged, Solomon knows it shall be well with those that fear the Most High. It shall not be well with the wicked, and he shall not prolong his days, which are as a shadow, because he fears not before the Most High; the meaning is that the wicked do not inherit the kingdom and do not have the everlasting life the righteous receive.

There is a vanity done upon the earth, that just men are treated according to the work of the wicked and wicked men according to the work of the righteous. Solomon commends mirth, for a man has no better thing under the sun than to eat, drink, and be merry in his labor; yet a man cannot find out the work of the Most High done under the sun, and though he labor to seek it out, he shall not find it.

name: Elijah
charge: Standing alone against the prophets of Baal, and running before the king in the power of the Lord
summary: Elijah announced the drought to Ahab, received provision at Cherith and Zarephath, and called Israel back to the Lord at Carmel. After Jezebel threatened him, the Lord sustained him in the wilderness and gave him further work, a successor, and assurance that seven thousand had not bowed to Baal. He was later taken up by a whirlwind, and Elisha received his mantle.
offense: Elijah stood before Ahab and declared that there would be neither dew nor rain except according to his word. His authority was expressed in the confession that he stood before the Lord God of Israel (1 Kings 17:1). He did not stand before the king to obtain permission to speak. The king himself was beneath the word he brought. The same word that sent him to announce the drought directed his preservation within it. He went to Cherith, where ravens brought bread and flesh and he drank from the brook. When the brook dried, he went to Zarephath as commanded (1 Kings 17:2-9). Obedience did not keep the brook from drying; it kept him ready to follow the next instruction. The Lord's provision was not confined to one place or one means. When he returned to Ahab, he refused the accusation that he troubled Israel. The trouble arose from forsaking the commandments and following Baalim (1 Kings 18:17-18). At Carmel he called the people to cease halting between two opinions. Their silence could not remain an answer when the question was whom they would serve. He repaired the Lord's altar with twelve stones according to the tribes of Israel, laid the sacrifice in order, and had water poured over it three times. His prayer asked that the people know the Lord was God, that he was the Lord's servant, and that he had done these things at his word (1 Kings 18:30-37). The sign was not sought to establish an independent greatness for the prophet. It was sought to turn the people's hearts back.

He repaired the Lord's altar with twelve stones according to the tribes of Israel, laid the sacrifice in order, and had water poured over it three times. name: The widow of Zarephath
charge: Making the prophet's cake first, out of the last handful of meal
summary: A Gentile widow gathering two sticks to cook a last meal for herself and her son was asked by a stranger to feed him first from it, on a promise from the God of Israel. She did. The barrel of meal did not waste and the cruse of oil did not fail until the rain came, and when her son died the prophet raised him.
offense: As the Lord thy God liveth, I have not a cake, but an handful of meal in a barrel, and a little oil in a cruse: and, behold, I am gathering two sticks, that I may go in and dress it for me and my son, that we may eat it, and die. Elijah said, Fear not; go and do as thou hast said: but make me thereof a little cake first, and bring it unto me, and after make for thee and for thy son. And she went and did according to the saying of Elijah. Christ named her against Nazareth: unto none of the widows of Israel was Elias sent, save unto Sarepta.
judgment: For thus saith the Lord God of Israel, The barrel of meal shall not waste, neither shall the cruse of oil fail, until the day that the Lord sendeth rain upon the earth. And she, and he, and her house, did eat many days. When her son fell sick and there was no breath left in him, Elijah stretched himself upon the child three times and cried unto the Lord, and the Lord heard the voice of Elijah; and the soul of the child came into him again, and he revived. The woman said, Now by this I know that thou art a man of God, and that the word of the Lord in thy mouth is truth.

entries.commentary: Elijah the Tishbite, of the inhabitants of Gilead, said unto Ahab that as the Lord God of Israel liveth, before whom he stands, there shall not be dew nor rain these years but according to his word. Elijah prayed and it was no rain. The teaching opens by framing the whole session on the power of the Most High: he has power over everything, the animals and all creation, and he set that power on display through his prophet.

The word of the Lord sent Elijah eastward to hide by the brook Cherith before Jordan, and there he drank of the brook and the ravens brought him bread and flesh in the morning and in the evening. This shows the power of the Most High over the animals: he can command the ravens to bring a man food if it be his will, just as he did Elijah.

The brook dried up for want of rain, and the Lord sent Elijah all the way across the land to Zarephath, which belongeth to Zidon on the coast, where he had commanded a widow woman to sustain him. From the east side by Jordan to the west by Sidon was a hard walk of a Sabbath day's journey or more, with no water anywhere. Coming to the gate, Elijah asked the widow for water and a morsel of bread, and she answered that she had but a handful of meal in a barrel and a little oil in a cruise, gathering two sticks to dress a last meal for herself and her son that they might eat it and die. Elijah told her to make him a little cake first and after that for herself and her son, for the Lord God of Israel said the barrel of meal would not waste nor the cruise of oil fail until the day the Lord sent rain. She obeyed, and she and Elijah and her house did eat many days. For trusting in the Lord and obeying, she was sustained. The instruction to feed the man of God first is a precept: the man eats first. Sisters must trust in the Lord when he tells them to reverence their husbands and be submissive in all things, and not lean to their own understanding.

After these things the widow's son fell sick, and his sickness was so sore that there was no breath left in him. She said unto Elijah, Art thou come to call my sin to remembrance and to slay my son? Her thought was that the child was paying for the parent's sins. Elijah took the child up to the loft, laid him on his own bed, and cried unto the Lord, stretching himself upon the child three times and praying that the child's soul come into him again. The Lord heard the voice of Elijah, and the soul of the child came into him again and he revived. Elijah delivered the living child to his mother, and she said, Now by this I know that thou art a man of God and that the word of the Lord in thy mouth is truth. All praises that Elijah was there to call upon the Lord, for it was not the young man's time to go. A man's days are determined and appointed, and he cannot pass the bound the Most High has set; because it was not the child's time, the Lord let his soul return.

Being full of the Holy Ghost he is led by the Spirit into the wilderness, forty days tempted of the devil, and in those days he did eat nothing. He answers with the law: man shall not live by bread alone, but by every word of God.

The devil shows him all the kingdoms of the world in a moment of time. No man can do that, which settles who was standing there. All this power will I give thee, for that is delivered unto me, and to whomsoever I will I give it. The offer is real, and the price is worship. Get thee behind me, Satan: for it is written, Thou shalt worship the Lord thy God, and him only shalt thou serve. Again the answer is a commandment.

Set on a pinnacle of the temple and answered with scripture, he replies, It is said, Thou shalt not tempt the Lord thy God. When the devil had ended all the temptation, he departed from him for a season. The whole battle was fought with the word, and that is the only way it is won.

As his custom was, he went into the synagogue on the sabbath day, and stood up for to read. He reads from Esaias: The Spirit of the Lord is upon me, because he hath anointed me to preach the gospel to the poor, to preach deliverance to the captives. This day is this scripture fulfilled in your ears.

They wonder at the gracious words, and then ask, Is not this Joseph's son? No prophet is accepted in his own country. He names the widow of Sarepta and Naaman the Syrian, and they are filled with wrath, thrust him out of the city, and lead him to the brow of the hill to cast him down headlong, but he passes through the midst of them.

In the synagogue there was a man which had a spirit of an unclean devil, and it cried out, I know thee who thou art; the Holy One of God. That spirit was sitting in the house of worship, and it knew exactly who he was. Knowing who he is and doing what he says are two different things.

He rebukes the fever in Simon's wife's mother and it leaves her, and he lays his hands on every one of the sick brought to him. I must preach the kingdom of God to other cities also: for therefore am I sent. He went where the people were, and some received the word and some did not.

Christ calls the twelve and gives them power against unclean spirits and to heal all manner of sickness and disease, the same works he was doing himself. The twelve are named here, ending with Judas Iscariot, who also betrayed him.

Go not into the way of the Gentiles, and into any city of the Samaritans enter ye not, but go rather to the lost sheep of the house of Israel. The twelve go to the southern kingdom first, before the gospel goes to the northern kingdom.
Preach that the kingdom of heaven is at hand, heal the sick, cleanse the lepers, raise the dead, cast out devils. Freely ye have received, freely give.
They are to carry no gold, silver or brass, no scrip, no second coat, no shoes, no staves, for the workman is worthy of his meat.
In every city they are to enquire who in it is worthy, and to let their peace rest on a worthy house and return to them from one that is not.
Where they are not received they shake off the dust of their feet, and it shall be more tolerable for Sodom and Gomorrha in the day of judgment than for that city.

Behold, I send you forth as sheep in the midst of wolves: be ye therefore wise as serpents, and harmless as doves. This is a word for a people living in captivity. There is only so much that can be said and done on another man's ground, and wisdom is required alongside harmlessness.

They will be delivered up to the councils and scourged in the synagogues, which is what the Pharisees had the power to do. They are brought before governors and kings for a testimony against them and the Gentiles: against their own people who turned on Christ, and against the rulers of that time.
Take no thought how or what ye shall speak, for it shall be given you in that same hour. It is not you that speak, but the Spirit of your Father which speaketh in you.

The brother shall deliver up the brother to death, and the father the child. Serving the Most High brings division, and it comes first inside your own house. Ye shall be hated of all men for my name's sake: but he that endureth to the end shall be saved.
When they persecute you in this city, flee ye into another.
The disciple is not above his master. If they have called the master of the house Beelzebub, they will call them of his household worse.
There is nothing covered that shall not be revealed. What is told in darkness is to be spoken in light, and what is heard in the ear preached upon the housetops.
Fear not them which kill the body but are not able to kill the soul, but rather fear him which is able to destroy both soul and body in hell.
Not one sparrow falls to the ground without your Father, and the very hairs of your head are all numbered. That is not written for decoration; it is how closely he holds his own.
Whosoever shall confess me before men, him will I confess also before my Father; and whosoever shall deny me before men, him will I also deny.
I came not to send peace, but a sword. A man's foes shall be they of his own household.

He that loveth father or mother more than me is not worthy of me. This is not forbidding natural love for your family; it is forbidding the trimming of your ways to keep peace with them. That is how the pagan holidays come back in. A brother in the truth goes to see family he has not seen in a long while, and he sits down in the feast to keep them comfortable.

He that taketh not his cross and followeth after me is not worthy of me. He that findeth his life shall lose it, and he that loseth his life for my sake shall find it. What is given up is the sin that was being lived in. That old man is put to death, and the life that is found is coming out of the congregation of the dead.

He that receiveth you receiveth me, and he that receiveth me receiveth him that sent me. Even a cup of cold water given in the name of a disciple does not lose its reward, and the reward in view is the kingdom.
