Before Ahaziah, Elijah repeated the sentence: because he had sent to Ekron, he would not come down from his bed but would die. He died according to the word, and Jehoram succeeded him because he had no son (2 Kings 1:16-17). Bringing the prophet before the throne had not brought the judgment under the throne's control.

entries.commentary: Moab rebels against Israel after the death of Ahab. Nations that had been subdued under David and brought under tribute begin to break away, because Israel no longer walks in the blessing that came from serving the Most High. -

Ahaziah falls down through a lattice in his upper chamber and is sick, and sends messengers to inquire of Beelzebub, the god of Ekron, the lord of the flies, whether he shall recover. He turns to an idol rather than to the Most High for his answer. The angel of the Lord sends Elijah the Tishbite to meet the messengers and ask whether it is because there is no God in Israel that they go to inquire of Beelzebub. The word of the Lord is that Ahaziah shall not come down from his bed but shall surely die. When the messengers describe the hairy man girt with a girdle of leather who met them, the king knows it is Elijah. Ahaziah should have known the history that would have kept him from trusting the god of Ekron. -

The king sends a captain of fifty with his fifty to Elijah, who sits on the top of a hill, and the captain commands the man of God to come down. Elijah answers that if he is a man of God, let fire come down from heaven and consume him and his fifty, and it does. A second captain of fifty is sent and speaks the same way, and fire from heaven consumes him and his fifty as well. The third captain goes up, falls on his knees, and pleads that his life and the lives of his fifty be precious in Elijah's sight. The angel of the Lord tells Elijah to go down with the third captain and not to fear him. Elijah delivers to the king the same word, that because he sent to inquire of Beelzebub as though there were no God in Israel, he shall surely die.

Ahaziah dies according to the word of the Lord that Elijah had spoken, and Jehoram reigns in his stead because Ahaziah had no son. The rest of the acts of Ahaziah are written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel.

Ye shall be holy, for I the Lord your God am holy; this word went to all the congregation of the children of Israel. Fear every man his mother and his father goes back to the commandment, honour thy father and thy mother. Honour can be kept even at a distance: show respect, and do nothing that would bring shame on your mother. But there is a balance; if she asks for what is against the commandments of the Most High, the commandments come first. Keep my sabbaths: the feast days are Sabbaths also. The Passover, the first and last days of the feast of Tabernacles, the day of atonement, and the memorial of blowing of trumpets are all Sabbaths; no servile work, no buying and selling, though cooking is permitted on the feast days.
Turn not unto idols, nor make molten gods; this is the commandment against making any graven image.

The peace offering was eaten the same day it was offered or on the morrow; whatever remained to the third day was burnt. Eaten on the third day it is abominable, and the eater bears his iniquity, for he has profaned the hallowed thing of the Lord.

The corners of the field, the gleanings of the harvest, and the leavings of the vineyard belonged to the poor and the stranger. The Most High is teaching, do not be selfish; love thy neighbour as thyself and look out for the poor of your people. He that provides not for his own, and specially for those of his own house, has denied the faith. Those of his own house are his wife and children; his own is his nation. Care for your people. Charge them that are rich that they be not highminded, but ready to distribute, willing to communicate. Most of us today have no fields or vineyards, but some have good jobs and blessed incomes; you cannot take it with you, so give of your substance. The scriptures also say no good can come to him that gives no alms.

Dealing falsely is any dishonesty: skewing the truth to get your way, or cheating. Be honest. Have an honest job so you do not steal; run an honest business so you do not cheat people with foul practices, selling goods you know will fail or charging a customer for repairs he does not need. That honesty is owed even to the other nations.

Do not swear by His name falsely. Saying I swear to God over a lie profanes the name of the Most High. Christ said swear not at all, neither by heaven, nor by the earth, nor by thy head; let your communication be yea, yea and nay, nay. The only reason a man swears is that he has lied before and no one believes him; in your repentance take swearing out of your speech, and do not put oaths on your own head or your family either.

The wages of him that is hired shall not abide with thee all night until the morning: when a man works for you, pay him that same day. Holding back the wage is defrauding thy neighbour, so businesses in Israel should pay their people the way the scriptures say. If both parties agree beforehand to payment the next day, that agreement is between you, the Lord, and that man; the scripture states the standard.

Curse not the deaf, put no stumblingblock before the blind, but fear thy God. Do no unrighteousness in judgment; respect not the person of the poor nor honour the person of the mighty. The courts of this land do the opposite: our people receive far harsher sentences than others for the same crime with the same priors, sometimes before the very same judge.

A talebearer revealeth secrets, but he that is of a faithful spirit concealeth the matter. What a brother or sister tells you in confidence is not yours to spread; carrying it to the next person is talebearing, and it happens even in this truth. Where no wood is, there the fire goeth out: much strife and contention comes from messy people. Repent of that messy spirit; it has no place in Israel.

Hate not thy brother in thine heart; rebuke thy neighbour and suffer not sin upon him. If you love your brother or sister you correct them when they are going off into sin; that is real love. Love thy neighbour as thyself: thy neighbour is the children of thy people. Get that right, against the teaching that makes the neighbour everybody.
Keep the statutes: no gendering cattle with a diverse kind, no sowing the field with mingled seed, and no garment mingled of linen and woollen; that is the law against mixed fabrics.

The bondmaid betrothed to an husband and not redeemed was scourged, not put to death, because she was not free; the man brought a ram for a trespass offering, and the priest made atonement, and the sin was forgiven him.

Fruit of a newly planted tree was counted as uncircumcised for three years and not eaten; in the fourth year all the fruit was holy to praise the Lord withal; only in the fifth year could the fruit be eaten, that it might yield its increase.

Eat nothing with the blood: cook the blood out of the meat. No rare or bloody meat, none of the raw-meat customs of the other nations. Use no enchantments nor observe times; that goes into the horoscopes, astrology, and the rest of that nonsense. Leave it alone.

Round not the corners of your head, meaning do not bald your head; mar not the corners of thy beard, meaning do not shave off the beard. This is written to all the children of Israel, not to the priests only.

No cuttings in the flesh for the dead, nor any marks printed upon you: that is the tattoo. The RIP tattoo for a dead family member is both a cutting in the flesh for the dead and a mark printed upon you. If you came into this truth already carrying tattoos, repent, ask the Most High for forgiveness, and get no more. Ear and nose piercings are not forbidden by this verse; the cutting forbidden here is the cutting in the flesh for the dead.

Prostituting your daughter to cause her to be a whore takes several forms: letting her dress immodestly, letting a little girl wear makeup and grown attire, and letting her have a boyfriend. There are no boyfriends and girlfriends in the scriptures. The father waketh for the daughter: his charge is to watch over her, know her clothes, her phone, her friends and their parents, and keep her under supervision, lest she pass away the flower of her age, which is her virginity being taken. Keeping a sure watch over her is not being too hard on her; it is the commandment, lest she make thee a laughingstock to thine enemies. Many daughters go the way of the mother, as the proverb says, as is the mother, so is her daughter; but Israel is teaching the sisters self-respect again, with the scriptures on modest apparel and on not wearing that which pertaineth to a man. When daughters are left without watch, the land falls into whoredom and fills with wickedness; the state of the community today shows the fruit of neglecting this law.

Keep my sabbaths and reverence my sanctuary. Regard not them that have familiar spirits, neither seek after wizards to be defiled by them. Rise up before the hoary head and honour the face of the old man: show respect unto your elders.

Vex not the stranger that sojourns with thee in the land; he shall be as one born among you, and thou shalt love him as thyself, for ye were strangers in the land of Egypt. The stranger of this law is an Israelite of another tribe sojourning outside the allotment of his own tribe: a man of Judah dwelling in the land of Benjamin is a stranger to that land, because that was not the allotment the Most High gave him. When your brother the stranger falls into decay, relieve him and let him sojourn with you; give him work to deliver him out of his low state until he can stand again. The bondmen laws show the contrast in how the word stranger is used. The bondmen and bondmaids were to be of the heathen round about, and in that context the children of the strangers sojourning among you are the heathen, a possession and an inheritance; but over your brethren the children of Israel ye shall not rule with rigour. Then the sojourner or stranger that waxeth rich by thee returns to the Israelite stranger, for the bondservant of the heathen did not wax rich.

Just balances, just weights, a just ephah and a just hin. Falsifying the balance is rigging the scale so that one pound weighs out as two and the buyer pays double; our people were doing that wickedness, and the Most High requires honest measure. Therefore observe all my statutes and all my judgments and do them: the Lord which brought Israel out of the land of Egypt requires it.
The Most High told Isaiah to take a great roll and write in it with a man's pen concerning Maher-shalal-hash-baz, meaning quick to the plunder, swift to the spoil.

Isaiah took faithful witnesses to record, Uriah the priest and Zechariah the son of Jeberechiah, then went to the prophetess, who conceived and bare a son. The Most High said to call his name Maher-shalal-hash-baz, for before the child shall have knowledge to cry, "My father, and my mother," the riches of Damascus and the spoil of Samaria shall be taken away before the king of Assyria. This ties to [Isaiah 7:16](/bible/isaiah/7#v16), "before the child shall know to refuse evil and choose the good"; both point to the fall of the lands of Rezin and Pekah.

Because the people refuse the waters of Shiloah that go softly and rejoice in Rezin and Remaliah's son, the Most High brings upon them the waters of the river strong and many, the king of Assyria and all his glory, rising over all his channels and banks. He shall pass through Judah and overflow, reaching even to the neck, and the stretching out of his wings shall fill the breadth of the land, O Immanuel, which means God with us.

"Associate yourselves, O ye people, and ye shall be broken in pieces." Though the far countries gird themselves, they shall be broken; take counsel together and it shall come to nought, speak the word and it shall not stand, for God is with us. If the counsel is from man it will fall, but if it is from the Most High it cannot be overthrown, and men would only end up fighting against God. -

The Most High spoke with a strong hand, instructing Isaiah not to walk in the way of this people, and not to say "a confederacy" to all them to whom this people says a confederacy, nor to fear their fear. "Sanctify the LORD of hosts himself; and let him be your fear, and let him be your dread."

He shall be for a sanctuary, but also a stone of stumbling and a rock of offence to both the houses of Israel, and a gin and snare to the inhabitants of Jerusalem. He is a sanctuary for his people, a little sanctuary in the places where they are scattered, but a stone of stumbling to those who reject him. The word became a snare upon the leadership because the understanding is given precept upon precept, in another tongue, so that those without it stumble and fall. -
Many among them shall stumble, fall, be broken, snared, and taken.

"Bind up the testimony, seal the law among my disciples." Knowing the law is knowing what the mark truly is, instead of thinking of a microchip and being snared and taken by every wind, like the trees moved with the wind.

"I will wait upon the LORD, that hideth his face from the house of Jacob, and I will look for him." Behold, Isaiah and the children the Most High gave him are for signs and wonders in Israel, from the Lord of hosts which dwelleth in mount Zion.

When they say to seek unto them that have familiar spirits, and wizards that peep and mutter, the answer is: should not a people seek unto their God? For the living to the dead? "To the law and to the testimony: if they speak not according to this word, it is because there is no light in them." Christians say Jesus is the word and go to [John 17:17](/bible/john/17#v17), "thy word is truth," but the word spoken of is the law; no law means no light, which is why there is no light in christianity. -

They shall pass through it hardly bestead and hungry, fret themselves, and curse their king and their God, looking upward and to the earth. They shall behold trouble and darkness, dimness of anguish, and be driven to darkness.

name: The young mockers of Bethel
charge: Mocking the prophet of the Lord
summary: As Elisha went up to Bethel, the seat of Jeroboam's calf, a company came out of the city mocking him: go up, thou bald head. He cursed them in the name of the Lord, and two she-bears came out of the wood and tore forty-two of them.
offense: As Elisha went toward Bethel, a group came out of the city and mocked him, repeatedly calling him bald and telling him to go up (2 Kings 2:23). Their common voice turned the prophet's passage into an occasion of public contempt. The encounter follows the recognition that Elijah's spirit rested upon Elisha and the healing of Jericho's waters (2 Kings 2:15, 19-22). One community brought its need before the man of God; these mockers met him with derision. The difference lay not in the prophet's appearance, but in how his presence was received.
judgment: Elisha turned, looked upon them, and cursed them in the name of the Lord. Two she-bears came from the wood and tore forty-two of the group (2 Kings 2:24). The sentence interrupted the mockery with a calamity far beyond what the speakers had reckoned upon. Leviticus 26:21-22 warns Israel of wild beasts among the judgments of resisting the Lord. At Bethel, the injury is recorded plainly without a count of deaths. Elisha continued to Carmel and Samaria (2 Kings 2:25). The company that presumed to dismiss him could not prevent his ministry from going forward, and its contempt did not remain without consequence.

entries.commentary: When the Most High is about to take up Elijah into heaven by a whirlwind, Elijah goes with Elisha from Gilgal and tells him to tarry, but Elisha refuses to leave him. At Bethel and at Jericho the sons of the prophets tell Elisha that his master will be taken from him today, and each time he answers that he knows it and bids them hold their peace. The sons of the prophets are a prophetic order or company, not the literal blood sons of the prophets. Fifty of them stand afar off to view as Elijah and Elisha come to the Jordan. Elijah takes his mantle, wraps it together, and smites the waters, which divide so the two go over on dry ground. Elijah asks what he shall do for Elisha before he is taken, and Elisha asks for a double portion of his spirit; Elijah says it is a hard thing, granted only if Elisha sees him taken. A chariot of fire and horses of fire part them, and Elijah goes up by a whirlwind into heaven.

Elisha sees it and cries, my father, my father, the chariot of Israel and the horsemen thereof, and sees him no more. He takes hold of his own clothes and rends them in two pieces and takes up the mantle of Elijah that fell from him. Elisha returns and smites the waters of Jordan with the mantle, asking, where is the Lord God of Elijah, and the waters part so he goes over. The sons of the prophets at Jericho see it and say the spirit of Elijah rests on Elisha, and they bow themselves to the ground before him.

The sons of the prophets press Elisha to let fifty strong men go and seek his master, in case the spirit of the Lord has cast him upon some mountain or valley. Elisha tells them not to send. They urge him until he is ashamed, and he lets them go, but after three days they do not find Elijah. When they return, he reminds them that he told them not to go.

The men of Jericho tell Elisha that the city is pleasant but the water is bad and the ground barren. Elisha calls for a new cruse with salt in it, casts the salt into the spring, and says, thus saith the Lord, I have healed these waters; there shall not be from thence any more death or barren land. The waters are healed to this day according to the saying of Elisha. The sign shows that the spirit that was on Elijah now works through Elisha.

As Elisha goes up to Bethel, little children come out of the city and mock him, saying, go up, thou bald head. He turns back, looks on them, and curses them in the name of the Lord. Two she bears come out of the wood and tear forty and two of the children. Elisha goes on from there to Carmel and returns to Samaria. --- Topics: [Idolatry](/encyclopedia/idolatry)

The children of Israel are to make no idols nor graven images, rear up no standing image, and set up no image of stone in the land to bow down to it. That covers the images bowed to today: the cobblestone of Islam, the cross, and the relics and Egyptian heads that egyptologists worship. The Israelites are not to do that.

Keep the sabbaths of the Most High and reverence His sanctuary. When you came into the sanctuary you had better come with respect, because the Most High was putting men to death over it. Nadab and Abihu, the sons of Aaron, offered strange fire before the Lord which He commanded them not, and fire went out from the Lord and devoured them; that is what reverencing the sanctuary means.

These are the blessings for walking in the statutes and keeping the commandments, the same blessings and curses read in Deuteronomy the 28th chapter. If Israel kept the commandments there would be no famine: rain in due season, the crops continually growing, the harvest coming in on time, and rain in the land even in a drought.

The threshing is the corn and the vintage is the grapes for the wine. The threshing reaching to the vintage and the vintage to the sowing time means one season's plenty would carry into the next. Israel would never be without wine, without crops, without food; each harvest would reach to the next season, and the bread would be eaten to the full in safety.

The Most High would give peace in the land: no enemies able to come against Israel, no war in the land, no one making the people afraid. That was fulfilled in the days of king Solomon, when there was rest on every side. That is also how you know the people in the land of Israel today are not the real Jews: this prophecy of rest is not fulfilled on them. When the Most High saves Israel from captivity it will be the same again, and none shall make him afraid.

Israel would chase their enemies, and the enemies would fall before them by the sword; the nations feared Israel when the nation kept this covenant, as the book of Joshua shows. Five would chase an hundred, and an hundred put ten thousand to flight: that is how much power the Most High was going to bestow on His people, having respect unto them, making them fruitful, and establishing His covenant with them and their children.

Eating the old store and bringing forth the old because of the new means the storehouses would be so full that the old crop would have to be carried out to make room for the new; that is how plenteous the land would be. The Most High would set His tabernacle among the people, walk among them, and be their God; He brought them out of Egypt so they should not be bondmen, and broke the bands of their yoke.

This is the flip side. If Israel would not hearken but despised the statutes and broke the covenant, the Most High would walk contrary to the people, standing in exact opposition so that nothing would prosper. Terror is the terrorism lived under every single day: terrorized by wicked corrupt officers, by our own brothers and sisters, by the nations. Consumption is being consumed in the land, with diseases, oppression, financial mishaps, and the prison system; the burning ague goes into disease, harm to the eyes, and sorrow of heart in the mind. Sowing seed in vain: vineyards planted that the enemies eat, and children sown in vain, born only to be killed, incarcerated, or raised up under the curse.

The Most High set His face against Israel, and the people are slain before their enemies; you see that every single day. They that hate you shall reign over you: that is the clear explanation of why no laws will be passed to deliver this people and why there will be no reparations. No political party, Democratic or Republican, will be beneficial, because the curse stands and they that hate us now reign over us; and we flee when none pursueth.

Seven times more punishment for the sins, and the pride of Israel's power broken: the very power promised in the blessings, when enemies would flee, was taken away. That is the explanation of how the slave masters could bring Israel into slavery: they are not bigger or stronger nations, but it was divine intervention; the Most High broke our power and took our strength so the enemies could prevail. We outnumbered them many times in the cotton fields, yet could do nothing. The heaven as iron and the earth as brass also goes into the shackles on the neck and on the feet; and the strength is spent in vain, for the land yields no increase.

Walking contrary still brings seven times more plagues according to the sins. Wild beasts sent among the people to rob them of their children, destroy their cattle, and make them few in number: wolves, coyotes, bears, whatever the Most High would allow to come upon the people for their wickedness. That is real evil brought for real rebellion. It also goes into the pestilences and diseases loosed among the people in these last days, as [Revelation 6](/bible/revelation/6) bears out with death by sword, hunger, and the beasts of the earth.

If the people would not be reformed by these things, the Most High would punish yet seven times more and bring a sword to avenge the quarrel of His covenant; gathered into their cities, the pestilence would be sent among them and they would be delivered into the hand of the enemy. Breaking the staff of bread, with ten women baking bread in one oven and delivering bread again by weight, is straight poverty: a lack of resources and food. Many of us grew up literally knocking on the neighbor's door to borrow sugar, borrow the iron, borrow bread, use the grill at such and such house because our appliances did not work; that is this verse, the same thing to this day, eating and not being satisfied.

The Most High said He would walk contrary in fury, and He would be the one doing it: He would use the enemies, but it would be Him behind it. That is heavy. Eating the flesh of sons and daughters goes into 70 AD, and it also happened in the days of the kings when the city was besieged and there was such famine that a woman's son was boiled and eaten.

The high places destroyed, the images cut down, and the carcasses of the people cast upon the carcasses of their idols: our people dying in the christian church with a cross around the neck, our people dying up against the cobblestone, still worshipping while they die. Even the high places themselves fall in judgment, as when a storm brought a church down on the congregation in Africa during a so-called easter program; that is what this verse reads about.

The Most High made the cities waste and brought the sanctuaries to desolation, and would not smell the savour of the sweet odours: He was not accepting the sacrifices, and He used the enemy to destroy the sanctuary. The Babylonians destroyed the temple, then the Greeks, then the Romans. When Babylon came against Jerusalem, Esau stood on the side cheering it on to the foundation, as [Psalms 137](/bible/psalms/137) records. Scattered among the heathen with a sword drawn out after them: not only the scattering, but death and anguish sent among the people in the lands of the captivity.

Then shall the land enjoy her sabbaths as long as it lieth desolate. The land was to rest every seventh year, and the sabbaths were not kept: no cooking or tilling on the sabbath, the land resting every seven years, none of it. The Most High said the land could not rest while the people dwelt on it doing evil, so He rid the people out of the land so that the land could enjoy her sabbaths while it lay desolate without them.

Upon them that are left alive a faintness is sent into their hearts in the lands of their enemies, so that the sound of a shaken leaf chases them; the same trembling heart, failing of eyes, and sorrow of mind that [Deuteronomy 28](/bible/deuteronomy/28) describes for the land of the enemies. Falling one upon another as it were before a sword when none pursueth: even at these protests, when the rubber bullets, the tear gas, the water hoses, and the dogs come out, the people stumble and fall over one another trying to get away. Still to this day the same thing. And ye shall perish among the heathen: many of us die in this land and in all the lands where we are scattered, and the land of the enemies eats the people up in oppression.

They that are left pine away in their iniquity in the enemies' land, and in the iniquities of their fathers. You see people just decay in their sickness: the Most High may not judge a man right away but gives him space to repent, yet he keeps eating the defiled food, smoking his weed, doping, in and out of jail, and slowly pines away. It is a miserable life to live; we have to get right with the Most High.

Confessing the iniquity of the fathers and their own trespass, with the uncircumcised heart humbled, is exactly what is being done right now: repenting, confessing the sins, remembering that the sins of the forefathers are ours, and turning the uncircumcised mind back to the Father. Accepting the punishment of the iniquity means going through the trials without fighting the sentence: not marching for reparations or so-called equality, but accepting the punishment for the iniquities committed against the Most High.

When the people repent and turn back, the Most High remembers His covenant with Jacob, with Isaac, and with Abraham, the covenant passed down to their children, the children of Israel; and He remembers the land. The land enjoys her sabbaths while she lieth desolate without them, and the people must accept that they were evil and wicked against the Most High, because they despised His judgments and their soul abhorred His statutes.

Yet for all that, in the land of their enemies the Most High will not cast the people away, neither abhor them to destroy them utterly and break His covenant. He sent Israel into captivity not for all to die, but to be afflicted until they finally turn back to the Lord God of Israel. So when you hear people say the Israelites are done away, that is a lie: the Most High promised He would not destroy the seed of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, but would give them a chance to repent and would remember the covenant of their ancestors whom He brought out of Egypt in the sight of the heathen. It also carries into the future tense.

These are the statutes and judgments and laws which the Most High made between Him and the children of Israel in mount Sinai by the hand of Moses. The quick recap of the chapter: these are the blessings and the curses that come upon the children of Israel for obedience or disobedience, and the chapter runs parallel with Deuteronomy the 28th chapter.

If a man steal an ox or a sheep and kill it or sell it, he restores five oxen for an ox and four sheep for a sheep. We are in a different situation where we do not keep oxen and sheep, but the principle of restitution still applies among brothers and sisters in the body: if something is stolen, the law written here governs the payback. Do not be stealing.

If a thief be found breaking up means breaking in. He entered your home and you defended yourself and he died: that is what is called self-defense today, and no blood is shed for him, meaning there is no judgment. The judgment was already passed in the breaking in. If the sun be risen upon him, the thief got away, and there shall be blood shed for him means there shall be a judgment; then the verse gives the judgment. He makes full restitution, and if he have nothing he is sold for his theft: not sold into slavery, but into work servitude until he pays off the debt of what he stole. If the theft be found in his hand alive, he restores double. Verse three covers the thief who already got rid of what he stole; verse four covers the one still holding it.

These are self-explanatory: if a man lets his beast feed in another man's field or vineyard, he makes restitution of the best of his own field and vineyard; and he that kindles a fire that consumes another man's corn surely makes restitution.

If a man deliver money or stuff to his neighbor to keep and it be stolen, the thief found pays double. If the thief be not found, the master of the house is brought unto the judges, to see whether he put his hand unto his neighbor's goods, whether he was part of a scheme to deceive the owner out of his goods. For all manner of trespass, whether for ox, ass, sheep, raiment, or any lost thing, both parties come before the judges, and whom the judges condemn pays double unto his neighbor.

If a beast delivered to a neighbor to keep die or be hurt or driven away, no man seeing it, an oath of the Lord is between them both. In layman's terms he swears: I did not take the stuff, I did not set you up, I do not know where it is. The owner accepts the oath and the matter ends there; it is not to be spoken of again. Paul uses this civil law to show how the Most High is unchangeable. An oath for confirmation is the end of all strife; God confirmed his counsel by an oath, and by two immutable things, that it is impossible for God to lie and that he will not take back what went out of his mouth, we have strong consolation. The same way, once the oath of this law is applied, the matter is over.

If the thing kept be stolen from him, he makes restitution; if it be torn in pieces, he brings it for witness and does not make it good. If a man borrow ought of his neighbor, ought meaning anything, and it be hurt or die with the owner not present, he surely makes it good. You borrowed it, it got messed up, you owe the man. But if the owner be with it, or if it be an hired thing, it came for its hire. If you came to plow a man's field for ten shekels with your own donkey and your donkey breaks his leg, you cannot expect the owner to pay for your own faulty equipment; the same as a business loan today, the property owner is not liable when your own equipment breaks down.

If a man entice a maid that is not betrothed and lie with her, he shall surely endow her to be his wife; he has to sign the papers. He is at fault for not going through the proper channels of marriage, and she is at fault for being enticed and laying down. The proper channel was that the father married off the daughter. To marry thy daughter is to perform a weighty matter, for the father gives her over to that man for the rest of her life and is out of all watching over her; so she is to be given to a man of understanding, one keeping the commandments as a wise man. In our own land the daughter went from her father's house to a husband's house with the blessing of the father.

Thou shalt not suffer a witch to live: witchcraft goes into horoscopes, palm readings, and all things of that nature. Whosoever lieth with a beast, bestiality, shall surely be put to death. He that sacrificeth unto any god save unto the Lord only shall be utterly destroyed.

This is twofold, and first and foremost the stranger is your brother from a different area, our own people. [Leviticus 25](/bible/leviticus/25) shows it: if thy brother be waxen poor, though he be a stranger or a sojourner, sojourn meaning travel, thou shalt relieve him that he may live with thee. A brother of another tribe who falls on hard times and travels down to live with you is that stranger; neither vex him nor oppress him, for ye were strangers in the land of Egypt.

Ye shall not afflict any widow or fatherless child. A wife without a husband already has a hard life, and a son or daughter without a father the same; do not make their life harder than it already is. If thou afflict them in any wise and they cry unto the Most High, he will surely hear their cry, and his wrath shall wax hot: he will kill you with the sword, and your own wives shall be widows and your children fatherless. That is the Lord's plain warning against mistreating those less fortunate.

Usury means interest. You cannot charge your brother or sister interest: if you lend twenty dollars, you get twenty dollars back, nothing more, nothing less; no little bit more off the top. This is the same law read in [Leviticus 25:36-37](/bible/leviticus/25#v36).

If thou take thy neighbor's raiment to pledge, deliver it unto him by that the sun goeth down, for that is his covering only; wherein shall he sleep? The tunics and overcoats worn then were also sleeping garments to keep a man warm at night, especially the poor. A well-off man does not have to work for you; this speaks of the less fortunate who extend their services for money and give what is most valuable to them, their raiment, as the pledge. If he cries unto the Most High, he will hear, for he is gracious.

Thou shalt not revile the gods means do not hate or speak evil of your leaders. The word gods here is the leaders over you: the Most High says in the psalm, I have said, Ye are gods, and all of you are children of the Most High, speaking of us. [Acts 23](/bible/acts/23) is the example: when Paul spoke against the high priest, they that stood by said, Revilest thou God's high priest? And Paul answered, I wist not, brethren, that he was the high priest: for it is written, Thou shalt not speak evil of the ruler of thy people, quoting this very verse.

Thou shalt not delay to offer the first of thy ripe fruits and of thy liquors, and the firstborn of thy sons shalt thou give unto me. The firstborn sons that opened the matrix were consecrated unto the Lord, and the father redeemed them back from the priest with shekels. Likewise with the oxen and the sheep: seven days the firstling stayed with his dam, his mother, and on the eighth day it was given. The Lord did not want it too young, taken as soon as it popped out; it had to be its appointed time with the mother, then brought to the priest.

Ye shall be holy men unto me: neither shall ye eat any flesh that is torn of beasts in the field; ye shall cast it to the dogs. This is twofold, and the dogs are the strangers of other nations, the aliens and foreigners. Always get the context of the law, because sometimes the stranger is your brother and sometimes it is literally the other nations. [Deuteronomy 14:21](/bible/deuteronomy/14#v21) doubles this law: that which dieth of itself thou shalt give unto the stranger that is in thy gates, or sell it unto an alien, for thou art an holy people unto the Lord thy God. Cast the torn flesh to the other nations; ye shall not eat it, because ye are holy people.

Ye shall be holy, for I the Lord your God am holy; this word went to all the congregation of the children of Israel. Fear every man his mother and his father goes back to the commandment, honour thy father and thy mother. Honour can be kept even at a distance: show respect, and do nothing that would bring shame on your mother. But there is a balance; if she asks for what is against the commandments of the Most High, the commandments come first. Keep my sabbaths: the feast days are Sabbaths also. The Passover, the first and last days of the feast of Tabernacles, the day of atonement, and the memorial of blowing of trumpets are all Sabbaths; no servile work, no buying and selling, though cooking is permitted on the feast days.
Turn not unto idols, nor make molten gods; this is the commandment against making any graven image.

The peace offering was eaten the same day it was offered or on the morrow; whatever remained to the third day was burnt. Eaten on the third day it is abominable, and the eater bears his iniquity, for he has profaned the hallowed thing of the Lord.

The corners of the field, the gleanings of the harvest, and the leavings of the vineyard belonged to the poor and the stranger. The Most High is teaching, do not be selfish; love thy neighbour as thyself and look out for the poor of your people. He that provides not for his own, and specially for those of his own house, has denied the faith. Those of his own house are his wife and children; his own is his nation. Care for your people. Charge them that are rich that they be not highminded, but ready to distribute, willing to communicate. Most of us today have no fields or vineyards, but some have good jobs and blessed incomes; you cannot take it with you, so give of your substance. The scriptures also say no good can come to him that gives no alms.

Dealing falsely is any dishonesty: skewing the truth to get your way, or cheating. Be honest. Have an honest job so you do not steal; run an honest business so you do not cheat people with foul practices, selling goods you know will fail or charging a customer for repairs he does not need. That honesty is owed even to the other nations.

Do not swear by His name falsely. Saying I swear to God over a lie profanes the name of the Most High. Christ said swear not at all, neither by heaven, nor by the earth, nor by thy head; let your communication be yea, yea and nay, nay. The only reason a man swears is that he has lied before and no one believes him; in your repentance take swearing out of your speech, and do not put oaths on your own head or your family either.

The wages of him that is hired shall not abide with thee all night until the morning: when a man works for you, pay him that same day. Holding back the wage is defrauding thy neighbour, so businesses in Israel should pay their people the way the scriptures say. If both parties agree beforehand to payment the next day, that agreement is between you, the Lord, and that man; the scripture states the standard.

Curse not the deaf, put no stumblingblock before the blind, but fear thy God. Do no unrighteousness in judgment; respect not the person of the poor nor honour the person of the mighty. The courts of this land do the opposite: our people receive far harsher sentences than others for the same crime with the same priors, sometimes before the very same judge.

A talebearer revealeth secrets, but he that is of a faithful spirit concealeth the matter. What a brother or sister tells you in confidence is not yours to spread; carrying it to the next person is talebearing, and it happens even in this truth. Where no wood is, there the fire goeth out: much strife and contention comes from messy people. Repent of that messy spirit; it has no place in Israel.

Hate not thy brother in thine heart; rebuke thy neighbour and suffer not sin upon him. If you love your brother or sister you correct them when they are going off into sin; that is real love. Love thy neighbour as thyself: thy neighbour is the children of thy people. Get that right, against the teaching that makes the neighbour everybody.
Keep the statutes: no gendering cattle with a diverse kind, no sowing the field with mingled seed, and no garment mingled of linen and woollen; that is the law against mixed fabrics.

The bondmaid betrothed to an husband and not redeemed was scourged, not put to death, because she was not free; the man brought a ram for a trespass offering, and the priest made atonement, and the sin was forgiven him.

Fruit of a newly planted tree was counted as uncircumcised for three years and not eaten; in the fourth year all the fruit was holy to praise the Lord withal; only in the fifth year could the fruit be eaten, that it might yield its increase.

Eat nothing with the blood: cook the blood out of the meat. No rare or bloody meat, none of the raw-meat customs of the other nations. Use no enchantments nor observe times; that goes into the horoscopes, astrology, and the rest of that nonsense. Leave it alone.

Round not the corners of your head, meaning do not bald your head; mar not the corners of thy beard, meaning do not shave off the beard. This is written to all the children of Israel, not to the priests only.

No cuttings in the flesh for the dead, nor any marks printed upon you: that is the tattoo. The RIP tattoo for a dead family member is both a cutting in the flesh for the dead and a mark printed upon you. If you came into this truth already carrying tattoos, repent, ask the Most High for forgiveness, and get no more. Ear and nose piercings are not forbidden by this verse; the cutting forbidden here is the cutting in the flesh for the dead.

Prostituting your daughter to cause her to be a whore takes several forms: letting her dress immodestly, letting a little girl wear makeup and grown attire, and letting her have a boyfriend. There are no boyfriends and girlfriends in the scriptures. The father waketh for the daughter: his charge is to watch over her, know her clothes, her phone, her friends and their parents, and keep her under supervision, lest she pass away the flower of her age, which is her virginity being taken. Keeping a sure watch over her is not being too hard on her; it is the commandment, lest she make thee a laughingstock to thine enemies. Many daughters go the way of the mother, as the proverb says, as is the mother, so is her daughter; but Israel is teaching the sisters self-respect again, with the scriptures on modest apparel and on not wearing that which pertaineth to a man. When daughters are left without watch, the land falls into whoredom and fills with wickedness; the state of the community today shows the fruit of neglecting this law.

Keep my sabbaths and reverence my sanctuary. Regard not them that have familiar spirits, neither seek after wizards to be defiled by them. Rise up before the hoary head and honour the face of the old man: show respect unto your elders.

Vex not the stranger that sojourns with thee in the land; he shall be as one born among you, and thou shalt love him as thyself, for ye were strangers in the land of Egypt. The stranger of this law is an Israelite of another tribe sojourning outside the allotment of his own tribe: a man of Judah dwelling in the land of Benjamin is a stranger to that land, because that was not the allotment the Most High gave him. When your brother the stranger falls into decay, relieve him and let him sojourn with you; give him work to deliver him out of his low state until he can stand again. The bondmen laws show the contrast in how the word stranger is used. The bondmen and bondmaids were to be of the heathen round about, and in that context the children of the strangers sojourning among you are the heathen, a possession and an inheritance; but over your brethren the children of Israel ye shall not rule with rigour. Then the sojourner or stranger that waxeth rich by thee returns to the Israelite stranger, for the bondservant of the heathen did not wax rich.

Just balances, just weights, a just ephah and a just hin. Falsifying the balance is rigging the scale so that one pound weighs out as two and the buyer pays double; our people were doing that wickedness, and the Most High requires honest measure. Therefore observe all my statutes and all my judgments and do them: the Lord which brought Israel out of the land of Egypt requires it.

The people of the land take Jehoahaz the son of Josiah and make him king in Jerusalem; he is twenty three years old and reigns three months. The king of Egypt puts him down, condemns the land in a hundred talents of silver and a talent of gold, and makes Eliakim his brother king, turning his name to Jehoiakim, and carries Jehoahaz to Egypt.

Jehoiakim is twenty five years old when he begins to reign and reigns eleven years in Jerusalem, doing evil in the sight of the Lord his God, so Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon comes up against him and binds him in fetters to carry him to Babylon. Nebuchadnezzar also carries off the vessels of the house of the Lord to Babylon and puts them in his temple. The Most High set a wicked king over the land because his own people would not do what he said. The power of the earth is in the hand of the Most High, and in due time he sets over it one that is profitable. When Israel will not rule in righteousness, he raises a Nebuchadnezzar; Israel's purpose was never to be wicked and rule at the same time. -

Jehoiachin is eight years old when he begins to reign and reigns three months and ten days in Jerusalem, and he does that which is evil in the sight of the Lord. When the year is expired, Nebuchadnezzar sends and brings him to Babylon with the goodly vessels of the house of the Lord, and makes Zedekiah his brother king over Judah.

Zedekiah is twenty one years old when he begins to reign and reigns eleven years, and he does evil in the sight of the Lord his God and humbles not himself before Jeremiah the prophet speaking from the mouth of the Lord. He rebels against Nebuchadnezzar who had made him swear by God, and stiffens his neck and hardens his heart from turning to the Lord God of Israel. The chief priests and people transgress very much after all the abominations of the heathen and pollute the house of the Lord. The Most High sends to them by his messengers, rising up early and sending because he had compassion, but they mock the messengers, despise his words, and misuse his prophets until the wrath of the Lord arises and there is no remedy. -

The Most High brings upon them the king of the Chaldees, who slays their young men with the sword in the house of their sanctuary and has no compassion upon young man or maiden, old man or him that stooped for age. He gives them all into Nebuchadnezzar's hand, and all the vessels of the house of God, great and small, and the treasures of the house of the Lord and of the king and his princes are brought to Babylon. They burn the house of God, break down the walls of Jerusalem, burn its palaces, and destroy all the goodly vessels, exactly the fierce nation the curses warned of. -

Those who escape the sword are carried away to Babylon, where they are servants to Nebuchadnezzar and his sons until the reign of the kingdom of Persia. This fulfills the word of the Lord by the mouth of Jeremiah, that the land would enjoy her sabbaths and lie desolate to fulfill threescore and ten years.

In the first year of Cyrus king of Persia, that the word of the Lord by Jeremiah might be accomplished, the Most High stirs up the spirit of Cyrus to make a proclamation throughout all his kingdom. Cyrus declares that the Lord God of heaven has given him all the kingdoms of the earth and charged him to build him a house in Jerusalem, and calls any of the Lord's people to go up, showing again that the Most High sets over the earth one that is profitable for his purpose. --- Topics: [Clean and Unclean Meats](/encyclopedia/clean-and-unclean-meats) · [Idolatry](/encyclopedia/idolatry) · [Sacrifice and Atonement](/encyclopedia/sacrifice-and-atonement) · [The Covenant](/encyclopedia/the-covenant) · [The Feasts of the Most High](/encyclopedia/the-feasts-of-the-most-high) · [The Priesthood](/encyclopedia/the-priesthood) · [The Sabbath](/encyclopedia/the-sabbath)

name: The prophet's widow, and the pot of oil
charge: Borrowing not a few vessels, as the prophet said, and shutting the door
summary: A widow of the sons of the prophets had a creditor coming to take her two sons for bondmen and one pot of oil in the house. Elisha told her to borrow empty vessels, not a few, shut the door, and pour. The oil stopped when the vessels did. She paid the debt and lived on the rest.
offense: A widow appealed to Elisha because her creditor was coming to take her two sons as bondmen. Her husband had feared the Lord, but his death had left an obligation her household could not meet. She possessed only a pot of oil (2 Kings 4:1-2). The need was both immediate and practical: the debt threatened the family that remained. Elisha told her to borrow empty vessels from her neighbours, not a few, and shut the door upon herself and her sons. She was to pour into the vessels and set aside those filled (2 Kings 4:3-4). Her preparation answered the word before the supply had multiplied. The sons whose removal she feared now helped bring the vessels to her.
judgment: She poured until every available vessel was full. When her son said there was no vessel more, the oil stayed (2 Kings 4:5-6). The account connects the extent of the filling with the vessels brought, without making the widow's poverty a limit upon the Lord's provision. Elisha directed her to sell the oil, pay the debt, and live with her children upon the rest (2 Kings 4:7). Deliverance did not mean pretending the debt had never existed. It supplied the means to discharge it and sustain the household afterward. The blessing reached the creditor's claim and the family's continuing need together, preserving the sons without exchanging one unresolved burden for another.

Her husband had feared the Lord, but his death had left an obligation her household could not meet. She possessed only a pot of oil (2 Kings 4:1-2). Elisha told her to borrow empty vessels from her neighbours, not a few, and shut the door upon herself and her sons. She was to pour into the vessels and set aside those filled (2 Kings 4:3-4). verses.text: 1Now there cried a certain woman of the wives of the sons of the prophets unto Elisha, saying, Thy servant my husband is dead; and thou knowest that thy servant did fear the Lord: and the creditor is come to take unto him my two sons to be bondmen. 2And Elisha said unto her, What shall I do for thee? tell me, what hast thou in the house? And she said, Thine handmaid hath not any thing in the house, save a pot of oil. 3Then he said, Go, borrow thee vessels abroad of all thy neighbours, even empty vessels; borrow not a few. 4And when thou art come in, thou shalt shut the door upon thee and upon thy sons, and shalt pour out into all those vessels, and thou shalt set aside that which is full.

entries.commentary: A certain woman of the wives of the sons of the prophets cries to Elisha that her husband is dead, that her husband feared the Lord, and that the creditor has come to take her two sons to be bondmen. Because the husband died in debt, the creditor comes to take the sons to work off what is owed. Elisha asks what she has in the house, and she says nothing but a pot of oil. He tells her to borrow empty vessels from all her neighbors, not a few, then shut the door upon herself and her sons and pour oil into all the vessels. She pours out, and the oil continues until every vessel is full, and only then does the oil stay. Elisha tells her to sell the oil, pay her debt, and live with her children on the rest. The empty vessels she borrowed from her people, the children of Israel, were filled through the spirit of the Lord.

Elisha passes through Shunem, where a great woman constrains him to eat bread, and as often as he passes by he turns in there to eat. She perceives that he is a holy man of God and tells her husband to make a little chamber on the wall with a bed, a table, a stool, and a candlestick, so he may turn in whenever he comes. On a day when he rests in the chamber, Elisha wants to bless her and sends Gehazi to ask what may be done for her, whether she would be spoken for to the king or the captain of the host. She answers that she dwells among her own people. Gehazi tells Elisha the woman has no child and her husband is old. Elisha tells her that about this season, according to the time of life, she shall embrace a son. Like our mother Sarah, she does not believe it and tells the man of God not to lie to his handmaid, yet she conceives and bears a son at that season. -

When the child is grown, he goes out to his father to the reapers and cries, my head, my head. His father has a lad carry him to his mother, and he sits on her knees till noon and then dies, from what seemed only a headache. She carries the child up and lays him on the bed of the man of God, the bed in the chamber she had made for Elisha, shuts the door, and goes out. She calls to her husband for a young man and an ass so she may run to the man of God, and though he asks why, since it is neither new moon nor sabbath, she answers, it shall be well. She rides to Elisha at Carmel, and when the man of God sees her afar off, he sends Gehazi to ask whether it is well with her, her husband, and the child, and she answers, it is well.

When she comes to Elisha at the hill, she catches him by the feet, and Gehazi comes near to thrust her away, but the man of God says let her alone, for her soul is vexed within her and the Lord has hid it from him. She says, did I desire a son of my lord, did I not say do not deceive me. Elisha tells Gehazi to gird up his loins, take his staff, greet no man on the way, and lay the staff on the face of the child. The mother says, as the Lord liveth and as thy soul liveth, I will not leave thee, so Elisha rises and follows her. Gehazi goes on before them and lays the staff on the face of the child, but there is neither voice nor hearing. He returns to tell Elisha the child is not awake.

When Elisha comes to the house, the child is dead, laid upon his bed. He goes in, shuts the door upon them both, and prays to the Lord. He goes up and lies upon the child, putting his mouth on his mouth, his eyes on his eyes, and his hands on his hands, and stretches himself upon the child, and the flesh of the child grows warm. He walks in the house to and fro, goes up and stretches himself upon him again, and the child sneezes seven times and opens his eyes. Elisha calls Gehazi to call the Shunammite, and when she comes he tells her to take up her son. She falls at his feet, bows to the ground, takes up her son, and goes out. This is another act of the Most High through Elisha, restoring the child to life.

Elisha comes again to Gilgal, where there is a dearth in the land, and the sons of the prophets sit before him. He tells his servant to set on the great pot and seethe pottage for them. One goes out into the field to gather herbs, finds a wild vine, and gathers his lap full of wild gourds, shredding them into the pot, for they knew them not. As the men eat, they cry out, O thou man of God, there is death in the pot, and they cannot eat. Elisha tells them to bring meal, casts it into the pot, and says pour out for the people that they may eat, and there is no harm in the pot. He cures the poisoned food so the men may eat safely.

A man comes from Baal-shalisha and brings the man of God bread of the firstfruits, twenty loaves of barley and full ears of corn in the husk. Elisha says, give to the people that they may eat. His servant asks how he should set this before a hundred men, but Elisha says again, give to the people, for thus saith the Lord, they shall eat and shall leave thereof. He sets it before them, and they eat and leave some, according to the word of the Lord.

When ye come into the land which I give you, six years thou shalt sow thy field and prune thy vineyard, but in the seventh year shall be a sabbath of rest unto the land, a sabbath for the Lord: no sowing, no pruning, no reaping of that which groweth of its own accord. As we rest on the seventh day, the land rests the seventh year. Letting the land rest is harmony and balance on the earth, and the sabbath of the land is meat for thee, thy servants, the stranger, thy cattle, and the beasts in thy land. These land laws were given for the land of Israel; land bought in this captivity is not under the seventh year rest.

Thou shalt number seven sabbaths of years, seven times seven years, forty and nine years; then shall thou cause the trumpet of the jubile to sound on the tenth day of the seventh month, in the day of atonement, throughout all your land. Ye shall hallow the fiftieth year, and proclaim liberty throughout all the land unto all the inhabitants thereof: it shall be a jubile unto you, and ye shall return every man unto his possession, and every man unto his family. Neither sow, nor reap that which groweth of itself, for it is the jubile; it shall be holy unto you.

If thou sell ought unto thy neighbour, or buyest ought of thy neighbour's hand, ye shall not oppress one another: according to the number of years after the jubile thou shalt buy, and according unto the fewness of years thou shalt diminish the price, for according to the number of the years of the fruits doth he sell unto thee. Thou shalt fear thy God, for I am the Lord your God; the price was reckoned honestly to the jubile so no man was oppressed.

Wherefore ye shall do my statutes and keep my judgments, and ye shall dwell in the land in safety, and the land shall yield her fruit, and ye shall eat your fill. If ye shall say, What shall we eat the seventh year? behold, we shall not sow nor gather in our increase: then I will command my blessing upon you in the sixth year, and it shall bring forth fruit for three years. The Most High answered the lack before it came: the sixth year would bring forth enough until the harvests of the ninth year came in, and ye shall sow the eighth year and eat yet of old fruit.

The land shall not be sold for ever, for the land is mine; for ye are strangers and sojourners with me. Israel was not able to sell away any of the land for ever, because it is the holy land of the Most High, and in all the land of your possession ye shall grant a redemption for the land. If thy brother be waxen poor and hath sold away some of his possession, and any of his kin come to redeem it, then shall he redeem that which his brother sold; or if the man himself be able, he may redeem it, or it goes out in the jubile and he returns to his possession. Redeem and buy are interchangeable words here: his kin come to redeem it meaning to buy it back. This is the prime example to reference for the curse that says no man shall buy you: no man shall redeem you. The other nations never came to say, we want to redeem Israel out of slavery and set them back to freedom; Israel has been in slavery for hundreds of years and no nation did that.

If a man sell a dwelling house in a walled city, he may redeem it within a whole year after it is sold; if it be not redeemed within the space of a full year, the house in the walled city is established for ever to him that bought it. But the houses of the villages which have no wall are counted as the fields of the country: they may be redeemed, and they go out in the jubile. Notwithstanding, the cities of the Levites, the houses of the cities of their possession, may the Levites redeem at any time, for the houses of the cities of the Levites are their possession among the children of Israel. Levi was not given any land; his portion was the offerings of the Lord, and the fields of the suburbs of their cities are their perpetual possession and may not be sold.

If thy brother be waxen poor and fallen in decay with thee, then thou shalt relieve him, yea, though he be a stranger or a sojourner, that he may live with thee. The word stranger does not always mean a heathen; sometimes it is your own brother sojourning away from his land, and the context of the verse tells you which. Thy brother is thy neighbour and the children of thy people: thou shalt not hate thy brother in thine heart, nor bear any grudge against the children of thy people, but thou shalt love thy neighbour as thyself. Brother, neighbour, and children of thy people all mean the same thing. Take thou no usury of him, or increase, but fear thy God, that thy brother may live with thee. Usury is interest, a fee accumulating over time; thou shalt not give him thy money upon usury, nor lend him thy victuals for increase. Lending for the opportunity to make a profit off your own people is evil. I am the Lord your God, which brought you forth out of the land of Egypt, to give you the land of Canaan. The Most High is not the God of everybody: to bring Israel out He judged Egypt, and to give Israel Canaan He cast out the seven nations, greater and mightier than Israel, delivered them before Israel to be smitten, with no covenant and no mercy shewed, during that time period.

If thy brother that dwelleth by thee be waxen poor and be sold unto thee, thou shalt not compel him to serve as a bondservant, but as an hired servant and as a sojourner he shall be with thee, and shall serve thee unto the year of jubile; then shall he depart from thee, both he and his children with him, and shall return unto his own family and unto the possession of his fathers. The Hebrew servant serves six years, and in the seventh he goes out free for nothing; if he came in by himself he goes out by himself, and if he were married his wife goes out with him. That seventh year of release is that servant's jubile: a servant taken in 2012 goes out free in 2019, and one taken in 2019 goes out free in 2026. For they are my servants, which I brought forth out of the land of Egypt: they shall not be sold as bondmen. Thou shalt not rule over him with rigour, but shalt fear thy God; deal with him properly, for the Most High judges both the poor man and the one he serves.

Both thy bondmen and thy bondmaids, which thou shalt have, shall be of the heathen that are round about you; of them shall ye buy bondmen and bondmaids, and of the children of the strangers that do sojourn among you, and they shall be your possession. Ye shall take them as an inheritance for your children after you, to inherit them for a possession; they shall be your bondmen for ever. But over your brethren the children of Israel, ye shall not rule one over another with rigour.

If a sojourner or stranger wax rich by thee, and thy brother that dwelleth by him wax poor and sell himself unto the stranger, after that he is sold he may be redeemed again: one of his brethren may redeem him, either his uncle, or his uncle's son, or any that is nigh of kin unto him of his family; or if he be able, he may redeem himself, working as an hired servant and earning the price of his own freedom. Here again redeem means buy, as in buying a man out of slavery back to the position of freedom; and the price of his redemption was reckoned with him that bought him, according to the number of years from the year he was sold unto the year of jubile, as the time of an hired servant. If he be not redeemed in these years, then he shall go out in the year of jubile, both he and his children with him. For unto me the children of Israel are servants; they are my servants whom I brought forth out of the land of Egypt: I am the Lord your God. Everybody is not the servant of the Most High; the children of Israel are His servants, and this teaching identifies them today as the so-called Blacks, Hispanics, and Native Americans. --- Topics: [Clean and Unclean Meats](/encyclopedia/clean-and-unclean-meats) · [Sacrifice and Atonement](/encyclopedia/sacrifice-and-atonement) · [The Covenant](/encyclopedia/the-covenant) · [The Feasts of the Most High](/encyclopedia/the-feasts-of-the-most-high) · [The Priesthood](/encyclopedia/the-priesthood) · [The Sabbath](/encyclopedia/the-sabbath)

Hew thee two tables of stone like unto the first, and make thee an ark of wood; Moses made the ark of shittim wood and went up with the two tables in his hand. He wrote on the tables, according to the first writing, the ten commandments: twice the record says God wrote them, in [Deuteronomy 9:10](/bible/deuteronomy/9#v10) written with the finger of God and here again. That is why the law is so important; these are not merely the commandments of Moses, they are the laws of God, and breaking them brings judgment if you do not repent. We have to repent, keep the commandments, and be found blameless before the Lord when Christ returns. Moses put the tables in the ark which he had made, and there they be, as the Lord commanded.

Aaron died and was buried, and Eleazar his son ministered in the priest's office in his stead. At that time the Lord separated the tribe of Levi, to bear the ark of the covenant, to stand before the Lord to minister unto him, and to bless in his name; wherefore Levi hath no part nor inheritance with his brethren, the Lord is his inheritance. Levi ate well through the sacrifices the Lord set up: the Levites dwelt in the best areas, the suburbs, and lived in castles, because the Lord was their provider. All they had to do was teach Israel the commandments of God. But they corrupted the covenant of Levi, left off teaching the law, and were partial in it, so the Lord gave them a swift and mighty judgment. Now you understand why Levi, identified in the land of Haiti, has been the poorest in the western hemisphere and catches hell to this day: their provider was the Lord, and they departed out of the way.

Moses stayed in the mount, according to the first time, forty days and forty nights, and the Lord hearkened unto him at that time also, and the Lord would not destroy thee. Arise, take thy journey before the people, that they may go in and possess the land which I sware unto their fathers.

And now, Israel, what doth the Lord thy God require of thee: here is your purpose in life, the stipulations for the body the Most High gave you, and what you must do to please him as the children of Israel. Fear the Lord thy God, walk in all his ways, love him, and serve him with all thy heart and with all thy soul: it all boils down to keeping the commandments of the Lord and his statutes, which he commands thee for thy good. That is how you love and serve God until the day we return to the dust or he sends his son to redeem us from the land of our captivity. Do not just say you love God, put action behind it. Sisters, come out of the pants and mini skirts and put on a modest dress, and be in subjection to your own husbands; brothers, put on your fringes, stop dyeing your hair, and marry the mother of your children instead of leaving her a baby mama. When you will not do what he told you to do, no words out of your mouth can make you love him; your actions show you actually hate him.

Behold, the heaven and the heaven of heavens is the Lord's thy God, the earth also; yet only the Lord had a delight in thy fathers to love them, and he chose their seed after them, even you above all people, as it is this day. No other nation can lay claim to this: our forefather Abraham was the friend of God, and the Most High took Israel from the chief men of the earth, for Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob were the best men walking the face of the earth when he made us a nation. Heavy scriptures right there.

Circumcise therefore the foreskin of your heart, and be no more stiffnecked. For the Lord your God is God of gods, and Lord of lords, a great God, a mighty, and a terrible, which regardeth not persons, nor taketh reward: that is what needs to be taught in the church, who we are really dealing with. Christ described his father the same way and forewarned us plainly: the Most High can destroy both the flesh and the spirit, disintegrate the spirit with no second chance at life, so make sure you are walking correct and keeping these laws before you come before him.

He doth execute the judgment of the fatherless and widow, and loveth the stranger, in giving him food and raiment; love ye therefore the stranger, for ye were strangers in the land of Egypt. Which stranger is Moses telling Israel to love? He is prophesying of the day Israel's own brother would become a stranger: when the northern kingdom was cut off, the brother became the stranger who would come back. Love them, because they are coming back into the covenant. The stranger of this commandment is thy brother fallen into decay, whom thou shalt relieve, not the nations Israel was commanded to drive out.

Thou shalt fear the Lord thy God; him shalt thou serve, and to him shalt thou cleave, and swear by his name. He is thy praise, and he is thy God, that hath done for thee these great and terrible things which thine eyes have seen. Thy fathers went down into Egypt with threescore and ten persons, and now the Lord thy God hath made thee as the stars of heaven for multitude. --- Topics: [Esau and Edom](/encyclopedia/esau-and-edom) · [Idolatry](/encyclopedia/idolatry) · [Sacrifice and Atonement](/encyclopedia/sacrifice-and-atonement) · [The Covenant](/encyclopedia/the-covenant) · [The Feasts of the Most High](/encyclopedia/the-feasts-of-the-most-high) · [The Priesthood](/encyclopedia/the-priesthood)

The cry is for the Most High to arise so His enemies are scattered and those that hate Him flee before Him. As smoke is driven away, so drive them away; as wax melts before the fire, so let the wicked perish at the presence of God. This is going into the blessing again. Today people say they are blessed as an individual, but we understood that the blessings of God are in [Deuteronomy 28](/bible/deuteronomy/28), and they refer to our condition as a nation of people. Our enemies fleeing from us is part of that blessing. -

Let the righteous, those keeping the commandments, be glad and rejoice exceedingly before God. We are going to rejoice on our feast days, not oppressed by the enemy, serving the Lord without fear in the Kingdom. Sing praises to His name, extol Him that rideth upon the heavens by His name Yah, and rejoice before Him. The Lord has many titles as you read the scriptures. He is a father of the fatherless and a judge of the widows; He sets the solitary in families and brings out those bound with chains, but the rebellious dwell in a dry land.

When the Most High went forth before His people and marched through the wilderness, the earth shook and the heavens dropped at His presence, and even Sinai itself was moved. Just as when we came out of Egypt, the Most High went before us in the wilderness and in the chariot; He always went before us. The scriptures talk about how when the Most High comes, the hailstorms come, the mountains tremble, and thunder and lightning appear. We serve the only true God, the God of Israel, the God of everybody. He sent a plentiful rain to confirm His inheritance when it was weary, and prepared of His goodness for the poor.

The Lord gave the word, and great was the company of those that published it. That is why you have different books of people that the Lord spoke to: Ezekiel, Jeremiah, and all the prophets in the company of Israel that published what God said. Kings of armies did flee, and she that tarried at home divided the spoil. Though they lay among the pots, yet shall they be as the wings of a dove covered with silver. -

The hill of Bashan is a high hill, but this is the hill which God desired to dwell in; yea, the Lord will dwell in it forever. The Most High dwells in Zion, in Jerusalem. That is why Christ said a city on a hill cannot be hidden; that is the city Jerusalem where the Lord dwells. The chariots of God are twenty thousand, even thousands of angels, the Lord among them as in Sinai. That is why in [Isaiah 66:15](/bible/isaiah/66#v15) He is coming back with the whirlwind. He has ascended on high, led captivity captive, and received gifts for men, even for the rebellious, that the Lord God might dwell among them.

Blessed be the Lord who daily loadeth us with benefits, even the God of our salvation. As it says in [Lamentations 3](/bible/lamentations/3), His mercy is renewed every morning. He that is our God is the God of salvation, and unto God the Lord belong the issues of death. There is something we must understand: to the Lord belong the issues of death. That is why you see people get shot many times and still live, or go through things people wonder how they survived. When it is not your time you are not going, and when it is your time you are not staying. -

The Lord said He will bring His people again from Bashan and from the depths of the sea, that thy foot may be dipped in the blood of thine enemies. This is going into treading the winepress of the wrath of God, what you hear in the scriptures about treading grapes. The Lord said we are going to walk in the blood of our enemies, because the Lord is a man of war. Israel really does not know war in the sense we are in now; the scriptures talk about how the Lord is going to teach us to know war again.

They have seen the goings of the Most High, the goings of my God my king in the sanctuary. The singers went before, the players on instruments followed after, and among them were the damsels playing with timbrels, like a marching band with women playing instruments. Bless ye God in the congregations, even the Lord from the fountain of Israel. There is little Benjamin with their ruler, the princes of Judah and their council, the princes of Zebulun and the princes of Naphtali. These are the tribes of Israel, the sons of Jacob whose name was changed to Israel. -

Thy God hath commanded thy strength; strengthen, O God, that which Thou hast wrought for us because of Thy temple at Jerusalem, and kings shall bring presents unto thee. Rebuke the company of the spearmen, the multitude of the bulls, till everyone submit himself with pieces of silver; scatter the people that delight in war. Until they submit, paying taxes to us, we are going to make them submit and pay tribute. Princes shall come out of Egypt, and Ethiopia shall soon stretch out her hands unto God.

Sing unto God ye kingdoms of the earth, to Him that rideth upon the heavens, who sends out His voice, and that a mighty voice. This is why in Revelation you hear the voice of many waters. God has a strong voice; His prophets have a strong voice. As men we speak with authority. On the streets the scripture says cry aloud, spare not, lift up thy voice like a trumpet. Ascribe strength unto God; His excellency is over Israel and His strength is in the clouds. The God of Israel gives strength and power unto His people. Blessed be God.

In his own country they are astonished at his wisdom and his mighty works, and then are offended at him because they know his family. A prophet is not without honour, but in his own country, and among his own kin, and in his own house. What was done to him is done to those teaching today: men who knew you before you repented ask who you think you are.

He could there do no mighty work, save that he laid his hands upon a few sick folk and healed them, and he marvelled because of their unbelief. Consider what that means. The unbelief of his own people was such that it made the son of the Most High marvel.

He sends them forth by two and two with power over unclean spirits, taking nothing for the journey but a staff. Whosoever will not receive you nor hear you, shake off the dust under your feet for a testimony against them. The word goes out whether they hear or whether they forbear, and that shaking of the dust seals the judgment.

Herod hears of him and says it is John, whom he beheaded, risen from the dead. John had told Herod plainly, It is not lawful for thee to have thy brother's wife. Herod knew the law well enough to be accused by it, because those rulers were schooled in the customs of Israel.

Herodias had a quarrel against John and would have killed him, but could not, for Herod feared him, knowing that he was a just man and an holy. When the oath is made, the daughter asks her mother what to ask, and is told, The head of John the Baptist. The king was exceeding sorry, but for his oath's sake he sent the executioner.

He was moved with compassion toward them, because they were as sheep not having a shepherd, and he began to teach them many things. Five loaves and two fishes feed five thousand men, and twelve baskets of fragments are taken up. He made them sit down by companies, in ranks by hundreds and by fifties. No man argued about where he was placed. The Most High is a God of order, and the eating came after the order.

He comes to them walking upon the sea, and they suppose it had been a spirit and cry out. These were fishermen; they knew what water does. They were sore amazed, for they considered not the miracle of the loaves, for their heart was hardened. Men can watch a thing done in front of them and still not take it to heart.
Wherever he entered, they laid the sick in the streets and besought him that they might touch if it were but the border of his garment, and as many as touched him were made whole.
