name: Asa in his first years
charge: Taking away the strange altars and the high places; commanding Judah to seek the Lord and do the law; crying to the Lord against a million Ethiopians
summary: Before the failure that is its own case, Asa did thirty-five years of what a king was for. He removed the idols, removed his own mother from being queen for her grove, made Judah swear to seek the Lord with all their heart, and when Zerah came against him with a million men he prayed one prayer and won.
offense: Asa removed the strange altars and images and commanded Judah to seek the Lord and do His law. He used the years of quiet to strengthen the cities, acknowledging that their rest came from seeking God. When Zerah came against him with an overwhelming army, Asa did not measure deliverance by numbers. He cried to the Lord, with whom it is nothing to help with many or with those who have no power. After the victory, Azariah called the king and people to continued faithfulness: the Lord would be with them while they were with Him. Asa took courage, renewed the altar, and gathered the people into a covenant to seek God with all their heart. He removed Maachah from being queen because of her idol, allowing neither family position nor royal privilege to shelter the abomination.
judgment: The Lord defeated the Ethiopians before Asa, and Judah returned with spoil. Others gathered to Asa when they saw that the Lord was with him. The people rejoiced in the oath they had made, sought God with their whole desire, and found Him. He gave them rest round about. The strength of this beginning lay in dependence upon God, not simply in fortified walls or military success. The same word that encouraged Asa also warned him that forsaking the Lord would have consequences.

entries.commentary: Abijah sleeps with his fathers and Asa his son reigns; the land is quiet ten years. Asa does that which is good and right, taking away the altars of the strange gods, the high places, the images, and the groves. Asa commands Judah to seek the Most High and to do the law and the commandment. The pattern of Rehoboam warns what happens when a strong king forsakes that law. -

Asa builds fenced cities because the land has rest and no war, for the Most High has given him rest. Rest is not idleness; while the land is before them they build walls, towers, gates, and bars. Asa has an army of 300,000 of Judah and 280,000 of Benjamin, all mighty men of valor. -

Zerah the Ethiopian, a Cushite, comes out with a host of a thousand thousand and three hundred chariots. Asa cries unto the Most High that it is nothing for him to help with many or with them that have no power. The Most High smites the Ethiopians before Asa; they flee and are destroyed, and Judah carries away very much spoil. Faith in the Most High, not the numbers of the enemy, wins the battle. -

The fear of the Most High comes on all the cities round about Gerar, and Judah spoils them, for there was exceeding much spoil in them. They smite the tents of cattle and carry away sheep and camels in abundance, then return to Jerusalem.

The Spirit of God comes on Azariah the son of Oded, who meets Asa and says the Most High is with them while they are with him; if they seek him he will be found, but if they forsake him he will forsake them. Israel had long been without the true God, a teaching priest, and law, but when in their trouble they turned to the Most High, he was found of them. Azariah charges Asa to be strong, for his work shall be rewarded.

When Asa hears these words and the prophecy of Oded, he takes courage, puts away the abominable idols out of Judah, Benjamin, and the cities he took from mount Ephraim, and renews the altar of the Most High. Hearing the word gives courage still, for we teach our people who they are, that the Israelites and the Christ are black. Faith comes by hearing. -

Asa gathers Judah, Benjamin, and the strangers out of Ephraim, Manasseh, and Simeon, who fell to him in abundance when they saw the Most High was with him. These strangers are Israelites whose hearts turned back. In the fifteenth year of Asa they enter a covenant to seek the Most High with all their heart and soul, that whosoever would not seek him should be put to death. They swear with a loud voice, and the Most High gives them rest round about.

Asa removes Maachah his mother from being queen because she made an idol in a grove; he cuts it down, stamps it, and burns it at the brook Kidron. Though the high places are not all taken away, the heart of Asa is perfect all his days. He brings the dedicated silver, gold, and vessels into the house of God, and there is no more war until the thirty and fifth year of his reign.

Abijam reigns three years in Jerusalem and walks in all the sins of his father, his heart not perfect with the Most High as David's was. The children did what they saw their fathers do, not merely what was said, which is why the Most High teaches His people to be different. Yet for David's sake the Most High gives him a lamp in Jerusalem, because David did right all his days save only in the matter of Uriah the Hittite, a wrong from which David repented. -

After Abijam dies, Asa his son reigns forty-one years and does right in the eyes of the Most High as David his father did. Asa takes the sodomites out of the land, removes the idols his fathers made, and even removes his own mother Maachah from being queen because she made an idol in a grove, which he destroys and burns at the brook Kidron. Though the high places are not removed, Asa's heart is perfect with the Most High all his days, and he brings dedicated silver, gold, and vessels into the house of the Most High.

There is war between Asa and Baasha king of Israel, who builds Ramah to cut off passage to and from Asa. Asa takes silver and gold from the house of the Most High and the king's house and sends it to Benhadad of Syria to break his league with Baasha, and Benhadad smites cities of Israel so Baasha stops building Ramah. Asa uses the stones and timber of Ramah to build Geba and Mizpah. In his old age he is diseased in his feet, then sleeps with his fathers, and Jehoshaphat his son reigns in his place.

Nadab son of Jeroboam reigns over Israel two years and does evil, walking in the way and sin of his father. Baasha conspires against him, kills him, and reigns in his place, then smites all the house of Jeroboam, leaving none that breathed, according to the word spoken by Ahijah the Shilonite. This fulfills, years later, the judgment that Jeroboam's descendants would be destroyed for the sins by which he made Israel to sin.

Baasha reigns twenty-four years in Tirzah and does evil, walking in the way of Jeroboam and in the sin by which he made Israel to sin. The pattern continues: each king who follows takes up the sin of the one before, and the same judgments keep coming.

name: Asa in his latter years
charge: Hiring the king of Syria against Israel; imprisoning the seer who reproved him; seeking to the physicians and not to the Lord
summary: For thirty-five years Asa was one of Judah's best kings. Then Baasha fortified Ramah, and Asa emptied the temple treasury to buy Ben-hadad's help instead of relying on the Lord who had given him the Ethiopians. Rebuked, he put the seer in the stocks; diseased, he sought physicians; and he died in the forty-first year of his reign.
offense: When Baasha fortified Ramah, Asa took silver and gold from the house of the Lord and the king's house and hired Ben-hadad to break his agreement with Israel. The plan relieved the immediate pressure, but Asa had relied upon the king of Syria instead of the Lord who had delivered him from the Ethiopians. Hanani exposed the difference between a successful maneuver and a faithful heart. Asa answered the rebuke with anger, imprisoned the seer, and oppressed some of the people. Later, when disease afflicted his feet, he sought the physicians but not the Lord. The charge is his neglect of God; the passage does not make the use of physicians itself the offense.
judgment: Hanani declared that the Syrian host had escaped Asa's hand and that he would have wars. Asa had purchased temporary relief while losing the greater deliverance that reliance upon God would have brought. His disease became exceedingly severe, and he died in the forty-first year of his reign. He received an honorable burial, but the honor shown at his death did not erase the rebuke recorded against his latter years. The king who once cried to God against an immense army resisted correction when his own policy was challenged.

name: Jehoshaphat
charge: Seeking the Lord and walking in his commandments; sending Levites to teach the book of the law through all the cities of Judah; setting the battle in array with singers
summary: He sent princes and Levites round Judah with the book of the law to teach it, and the fear of the Lord fell on the kingdoms round about. When Moab, Ammon and Edom came against him he proclaimed a fast, prayed in the congregation, and put the singers in front of the army. They came to the watchtower and found only dead bodies. His alliances with Ahab's house are their own case.
offense: Jehoshaphat sought the God of his father and sent princes, Levites, and priests through Judah with the book of the law. The people were to be taught what the Lord required, not merely governed by royal command. He appointed judges and charged them to judge for the Lord, without partiality or gifts. Their authority did not place them above the judgment they administered. When a great multitude came against Judah, Jehoshaphat feared, proclaimed a fast, and gathered the people to seek the Lord. His prayer rested upon God's rule, covenant, and sanctuary. He confessed that they had neither might against the company nor knowledge of what to do: their eyes were upon God. At Jahaziel's word, they went out, placing singers before the army to praise the beauty of holiness.
judgment: Therefore the Lord stablished the kingdom in his hand; and all Judah brought to Jehoshaphat presents; and he had riches and honour in abundance. And the fear of the Lord fell upon all the kingdoms of the lands that were round about Judah, so that they made no war against Jehoshaphat. Ye shall not need to fight in this battle: set yourselves, stand ye still, and see the salvation of the Lord with you. When they began to sing and to praise, the Lord set ambushments, and they were smitten. They were three days in gathering of the spoil, it was so much. So the realm of Jehoshaphat was quiet: for his God gave him rest round about.
offenseFull: Jehoshaphat sought the God of his father and sent princes, Levites, and priests through Judah with the book of the law. The people were to be taught what the Lord required, not merely governed by royal command. He appointed judges and charged them to judge for the Lord, without partiality or gifts. Their authority did not place them above the judgment they administered.

When a great multitude came against Judah, Jehoshaphat feared, proclaimed a fast, and gathered the people to seek the Lord. His prayer rested upon God's rule, covenant, and sanctuary. He confessed that they had neither might against the company nor knowledge of what to do: their eyes were upon God. At Jahaziel's word, they went out, placing singers before the army to praise the beauty of holiness.
judgmentFull: The Lord established the kingdom, and the fear of God restrained surrounding kingdoms. In the wilderness battle, the enemies turned against one another. Judah found the multitude fallen and spent three days gathering spoil. On the fourth day they blessed the Lord in the valley of Berachah and returned to Jerusalem with joy.
God gave Jehoshaphat rest round about. His victory joined prayer with obedience: the people stood where God directed and trusted the word He had sent before they saw the deliverance.

verses.text: 3And the Lord was with Jehoshaphat, because he walked in the first ways of his father David, and sought not unto Baalim; 4But sought to the Lord God of his father, and walked in his commandments, and not after the doings of Israel. 5Therefore the Lord stablished the kingdom in his hand; and all Judah brought to Jehoshaphat presents; and he had riches and honour in abundance. 6And his heart was lifted up in the ways of the Lord: moreover he took away the high places and groves out of Judah.

entries.commentary: Jehoshaphat reigned in the place of his father Asa, taking the throne after him. He strengthened himself against Israel, setting himself apart from the northern kingdom's ways. -
He placed forces and garrisons in the fenced cities of Judah and in the cities of Ephraim that Asa had taken. A diligent king secures the land and prepares before trouble comes.

The Most High was with Jehoshaphat because he walked in the first ways of his father David and sought not unto Baal. David was a man after the Most High's own heart because he kept the commandments and charged Solomon to keep them.
Jehoshaphat sought the Lord God of his fathers and walked in his commandments, not after the doings of Israel. The way we must walk is defined by the ordinances and laws we are taught. -
Because he obeyed, the Most High established the kingdom in his hand. All Judah brought presents, and he had riches, honor, and abundance.
His heart was lifted up in the ways of the Lord, not in pride but in devotion. He removed the high places and the groves out of Judah, tearing down false worship.

In the third year of his reign he sent princes and Levites to teach in the cities of Judah, and they carried the book of the Law of the Lord with them. They went throughout all the cities and taught the people, the same pattern we follow, going out into the streets to teach. -
The fear of the Lord fell upon all the kingdoms round about Judah so that they made no war against Jehoshaphat. Teaching the Law had a real effect on the nations; wisdom disarmed his enemies. -
Some of the Philistines brought presents and tribute silver, and the Arabians brought him flocks of rams and he goats. His obedience brought increase even from surrounding peoples.

Jehoshaphat waxed great exceedingly and built castles and cities of store in Judah. Cities of store are cities of provision, like Egypt's storehouses under Joseph in the years of plenty; in captivity our people had neither building nor closet, but the diligent tend to plenty.

He had much business in the cities of Judah, and mighty men of valor were mustered in Jerusalem by the house of their fathers. The captains numbered hundreds of thousands of ready men, prepared for war, waiting on the king beside those set in the fenced cities.

These are the commandments, the statutes, and the judgments, commanded to be taught, that thou mightest fear the Lord thy God: the fear always comes up first, thou, and thy son, and thy son's son, all the days of thy life. Hear therefore, O Israel, and observe to do it, that ye may increase mightily. Increase and power are the desire of the people, and keeping the commandments is the one thing our people have not tried; assimilation, the gods of the nations, and politics, liberal or conservative, have all been tried and none of it has worked. The land that floweth with milk and honey is the true riches: cattle, vegetation, agriculture, land to cultivate, the gift that keeps on giving.

Hear, O Israel: the Lord our God is one Lord: and thou shalt love the Lord thy God with all thine heart, and with all thy soul, and with all thy might. Thou shalt teach them diligently unto thy children: diligently means you do not miss a beat. The children are not to be taught the dance challenges, halloween, and the satanic birthdays, and remember that you teach by your actions, so you fix yourself first. Talk of them when thou sittest in thine house: go through the scriptures at home, the histories of Samson, Joseph, Solomon, and David. When thou walkest by the way: when you run into each other, ask, are you keeping the laws, what four chapters did you read today? When thou liest down, and when thou risest up: the bedtime stories are biblical, the ten plagues of Egypt rather than the fairy tales, prayer before they sleep and when they rise, and even the coloring books painting the images brown, bringing it back to its true course.

Thou shalt bind them for a sign upon thine hand, and they shall be as frontlets between thine eyes: bind them in your mind. The commandments are the light, the torch that guides you and leads you in the correct path. And thou shalt write them upon the posts of thy house, and on thy gates.

When the Lord brings thee into great and goodly cities which thou buildedst not, houses full of all good things which thou filledst not, wells digged which thou diggedst not, and thou shalt have eaten and be full, then beware lest thou forget the Lord which brought thee forth out of the house of bondage. Thou shalt fear the Lord thy God, and serve him, and shalt swear by his name; ye shall not go after the gods of the people round about you, for the Lord thy God is a jealous God, lest his anger be kindled and destroy thee from off the face of the earth. Ye shall not tempt the Lord your God, as ye tempted him in Massah.

Ye shall diligently keep the commandments of the Lord your God, and his testimonies, and his statutes. Testimony is one of the trigger words that confuses our people: the laws are what Moses gave, and the testimonies are the history of the forefathers and foremothers, what they went through and how it was handled according to the laws. Everything correlates: when king David had Uriah killed, that goes back to thou shalt not kill, thou shalt not covet, and bearing false witness; he was dealing with much sin in that one matter. That is how you go precept upon precept, line upon line, to the law and to the testimony. A personal testimony that cannot come back to the Bible is not biblical; if they speak not according to this word, it is because there is no light, no truth, in them. Thou shalt do that which is right and good in the sight of the Lord: not by personal standards of what feels good in the heart, but by the standard set before us, for the scripture says plainly that the law is good. The reward is to go in and possess the good land, the real wealth, not the bags and rings and sneakers, which are vanity.

When thy son asketh thee in time to come, saying, what mean the testimonies, and the statutes, and the judgments? The children will ask why David did what he did, why Samson, why Miriam was judged, why Moses was barred; the answer starts with the history. Then thou shalt say unto thy son, we were Pharaoh's bondmen in Egypt, and the Lord brought us out with a mighty hand, and shewed signs and wonders upon Egypt and upon Pharaoh; he brought us out that he might bring us in, to give us the land which he sware unto our fathers. The Most High always keeps his covenant; he is not a man, that he should lie. The Lord commanded us to do all these statutes, to fear the Lord our God, for our good always, that he might preserve us alive: the fear again stands first, and the commandments are for Israel's good and preservation, obligated and not optional, with punishment for breaking and reward for keeping. And it shall be our righteousness, if we observe to do all these commandments: keeping the commandments is what makes you righteous, and righteousness is kept at all times, the fringes worn seven days a week and not on the sabbath only. Words like testimony, righteousness, grace, and faith must be defined out of the scripture itself: the Bible is a dictionary within itself. Egypt means slavery, righteousness means keeping the laws, and going by the Bible's own definitions destroys the private interpretations of the religions.

name: Jehoshaphat's alliances
charge: Joining affinity with Ahab; going to Ramoth-gilead with him; joining with Ahaziah to make ships
summary: A king who sought the Lord and taught the law through Judah kept making common cause with the house of Ahab. He nearly died at Ramoth-gilead in Ahab's place, was told by Jehu the seer that wrath was upon him for helping the ungodly, and later lost a whole fleet at Ezion-geber for the same fault.
offense: Jehoshaphat joined himself to Ahab by affinity and went with him to Ramoth-gilead. Though he asked for a prophet of the Lord, he still accompanied Ahab after Micaiah announced disaster. Seeking a true word did not excuse proceeding against it. The alliance placed a king who sought the Lord beside a king who hated the prophet's correction. Afterward Jehoshaphat joined Ahaziah in making ships. This partnership again joined his work to a wicked king. A profitable undertaking could not make the association acceptable to God.
judgment: At Ramoth-gilead, Jehoshaphat was surrounded by the Syrian captains. He cried out, and the Lord helped him and moved them away. His rescue was mercy, not approval of the alliance. Jehu the son of Hanani met him with the question whether he should help the ungodly and love those who hated the Lord. Wrath was upon him, although God also acknowledged the good found in him. Eliezer later declared that because Jehoshaphat had joined Ahaziah, the Lord had broken his works. The ships were broken and could not go to Tarshish. Both accounts distinguish God's regard for the king's obedience from His rejection of particular choices.

Afterward Jehoshaphat joined Ahaziah in making ships. This partnership again joined his work to a wicked king. A profitable undertaking could not make the association acceptable to God.

verses.text: 1Now Jehoshaphat had riches and honour in abundance, and joined affinity with Ahab. 2And after certain years he went down to Ahab to Samaria. And Ahab killed sheep and oxen for him in abundance, and for the people that he had with him, and persuaded him to go up with him to Ramoth–gilead. 3And Ahab king of Israel said unto Jehoshaphat king of Judah, Wilt thou go with me to Ramoth–gilead? And he answered him, I am as thou art, and my people as thy people; and we will be with thee in the war.

entries.commentary: Jehoshaphat had riches and honor and abundance, and joined affinity with Ahab through marriage. Ahab feasted him and persuaded him to go up to Ramoth Gilead, and Jehoshaphat answered, I am as thou art, my people as thy people, we will be with thee in the war. His bond with Ahab was a joining together, like the spirit that witnesses with the spirit: what is mine is yours.

Jehoshaphat asked to inquire at the word of the Lord before going to battle. The king of Israel gathered four hundred prophets who all said go up and prosper, telling the king only what he wanted to hear.

Jehoshaphat asked if there was not still a prophet of the Lord to inquire of. Ahab said there was one man, Micaiah, but he hated him because he never prophesied good, only evil, meaning he told the truth. -

The king called for Micaiah while the two kings sat in their robes at the gate of Samaria. Zedekiah made horns of iron and all the prophets prophesied victory, making a tangible sign to push their false word.
The messenger urged Micaiah to speak good like the other prophets, with one assent. Micaiah answered, as the Lord liveth, even what my God saith, that will I speak. -

Micaiah first answered sarcastically, go up and prosper, until the king adjured him to speak nothing but the truth in the name of the Lord. Then he told the real word: he saw all Israel scattered upon the mountains as sheep with no shepherd, and the Lord said these have no master, let them return to their houses in peace.

*1 And Jehoshaphat the king of Judah returned to his house in peace to Jerusalem. 2 And Jehu the son of Hanani the seer went out to meet him, and said to king Jehoshaphat, Shouldest thou help the ungodly, and love them that hate the LORD? therefore is wrath upon thee from before the LORD. 3 Nevertheless there are good things found in thee, in that thou hast taken away the groves out of the land, and hast prepared thine heart to seek God. 4 And Jehoshaphat dwelt at Jerusalem: and he went out again through the people from Beer-sheba to mount Ephraim, and brought them back unto the LORD God of their fathers. 5 And he set judges in the land throughout all the fenced cities of Judah, city by city, 6 And said to the judges, Take heed what ye do: for ye judge not for man, but for the LORD, who is with you in the judgment. 7 Wherefore now let the fear of the LORD be upon you; take heed and do it: for there is no iniquity with the LORD our God, nor respect of persons, nor taking of gifts. 8 Moreover in Jerusalem did Jehoshaphat set of the Levites, and of the priests, and of the chief of the fathers of Israel, for the judgment of the LORD, and for controversies, when they returned to Jerusalem. 9 And he charged them, saying, Thus shall ye do in the fear of the LORD, faithfully, and with a perfect heart. 10 And what cause soever shall come to you of your brethren that dwell in their cities, between blood and blood, between law and commandment, statutes and judgments, ye shall even warn them that they trespass not against the LORD, and so wrath come upon you, and upon your brethren: this do, and ye shall not trespass. 11 And, behold, Amariah the chief priest is over you in all matters of the LORD; and Zebadiah the son of Ishmael, the ruler of the house of Judah, for all the king’s matters: also the Levites shall be officers before you. Deal courageously, and the LORD shall be with the good.*

After three years without war between Syria and Israel, Jehoshaphat king of Judah comes down to the king of Israel. Ahab reminds his servants that Ramoth in Gilead belongs to Israel, yet they sit still and do not take it out of the hand of the king of Syria. Ahab asks Jehoshaphat to go with him to battle, and Jehoshaphat answers that he is as Ahab is, his people and horses as Ahab's, but first asks that they inquire at the word of the Lord. Ahab gathers about four hundred prophets, who all say with one mouth, go up, for the Lord shall deliver it into the hand of the king. This is the setting for a division that ran between the northern kingdom and the southern kingdom. After the split, the northern kingdom fell into idolatry and forsook the Levites, so a prophet of the Most High would want nothing to do with their manner of worship. -

Jehoshaphat is not moved by four hundred prophets speaking the same thing, and asks whether there is not yet a prophet of the Lord that they may inquire of him. He wants to hear from a true prophet of the Most High, not from prophets who serve the king. Ahab answers that there is one man, Micaiah the son of Imlah, but he hates him because Micaiah does not prophesy good concerning him, but evil. Jehoshaphat rebukes him, saying, let not the king say so.

The king of Israel calls an officer to hasten Micaiah, while Ahab and Jehoshaphat sit each on his throne in their robes at the entrance of the gate of Samaria, and all the prophets prophesy before them. Zedekiah the son of Chenaanah makes horns of iron and says, thus saith the Lord, with these shalt thou push the Syrians until thou have consumed them. Here again a man claims to speak for the Most High while the whole company presses Ahab to go up and prosper.

The messenger tells Micaiah that all the prophets declare good to the king with one mouth, and urges him to speak likewise. Micaiah answers that whatever the Lord saith unto him, that will he speak, and at first he echoes the others, prompting the king to adjure him to tell nothing but the truth. Micaiah then reveals what he saw, all Israel scattered on the hills as sheep having no shepherd, and the Lord saying these have no master. He saw the Lord on his throne with all the host of heaven, and a spirit that offered to be a lying spirit in the mouth of all Ahab's prophets to persuade him to fall at Ramoth-gilead. The Most High put a lying spirit in the mouth of these prophets and spoke evil concerning Ahab. The deceiver as well as the deceived are under the hand of the Most High, who uses the lie to bring the judgment he has already declared. -

Zedekiah the son of Chenaanah smites Micaiah on the cheek and asks which way the spirit of the Lord went from him to speak to Micaiah, defending his own false prophecy. The king of Israel orders Micaiah taken back and put in prison, fed with bread and water of affliction until Ahab returns in peace. Micaiah answers that if Ahab returns at all in peace, the Lord has not spoken by him, and calls all the people to hearken. His word stands as the test of who truly spoke for the Most High.

The king of Israel and Jehoshaphat go up to Ramoth-gilead. Ahab disguises himself and tells Jehoshaphat to wear his robes, hoping to escape the word spoken against him, while the king of Syria commands his captains to fight only against the king of Israel. The captains pursue Jehoshaphat until they perceive he is not the king of Israel and turn back. A certain man draws a bow at a venture and smites Ahab between the joints of the harness, and the king is held up in his chariot until he dies at even, the blood running into the chariot. When they wash the chariot in the pool of Samaria, the dogs lick up his blood according to the word of the Lord. The judgment pronounced earlier against Ahab and his house begins to be fulfilled exactly as spoken.

The rest of the acts of Ahab, the ivory house he made and the cities he built, are written in the book of the Chronicles of the kings of Israel. Ahab sleeps with his fathers, and Ahaziah his son reigns in his stead.

Jehoshaphat the son of Asa begins to reign over Judah in the fourth year of Ahab, at thirty-five years old, and reigns twenty-five years in Jerusalem. He walks in the ways of Asa his father, doing right in the eyes of the Lord, though the high places are not taken away and the people still burn incense there. Jehoshaphat makes peace with the king of Israel and puts the remnant of the sodomites out of the land. There is then no king in Edom but a deputy, because Edom had been subdued and had not yet revolted. -

Ahaziah the son of Ahab begins to reign over Israel in Samaria in the seventeenth year of Jehoshaphat and reigns two years. He does evil in the sight of the Lord and walks in the way of his father and his mother and in the way of Jeroboam the son of Nebat, who made Israel to sin. He serves Baal and worships him and provokes the Lord God of Israel to anger, according to all that his father had done. The sin of the house of Ahab continues into the next generation. --- Topics: [Esau and Edom](/encyclopedia/esau-and-edom) · [Idolatry](/encyclopedia/idolatry) · [The Priesthood](/encyclopedia/the-priesthood)

name: Jehoram of Judah
charge: Slaying all his brethren with the sword; walking in the way of the house of Ahab; making high places and compelling Judah to fornication
summary: Jehoshaphat's eldest son married Ahab's daughter, killed his six brothers to secure the throne, and led Judah to the high places. A writing came to him from Elijah naming the sentence: a great plague on his people, his children and his wives, and a disease of the bowels that would take two years to kill him.
offense: Jehoram strengthened himself upon the throne and killed his brothers, together with princes of Israel. He walked in the ways of Ahab's house, made high places, and caused Judah to commit fornication. Royal power became an instrument for bloodshed and for leading the people away from God. Elijah's writing named both offenses: Jehoram had followed the corrupt kings of Israel and killed brothers better than himself. His marriage into Ahab's house did not diminish his responsibility for the course he chose.
judgment: Edom and Libnah revolted. The Philistines and Arabians invaded, carried away the substance of the king's house, and took his sons and wives, leaving only his youngest son. The Lord then struck Jehoram with an incurable disease of the bowels. After two years he died in grievous suffering. The people made no burning for him as they had for his fathers, and he departed without being desired. He was buried in the city of David, but not in the sepulchres of the kings. Yet the Lord did not destroy David's house, because of His covenant. The preservation of that house displayed God's faithfulness, not Jehoram's innocence.
offenseFull: Jehoram strengthened himself upon the throne and killed his brothers, together with princes of Israel. He walked in the ways of Ahab's house, made high places, and caused Judah to commit fornication. Royal power became an instrument for bloodshed and for leading the people away from God.

Elijah's writing named both offenses: Jehoram had followed the corrupt kings of Israel and killed brothers better than himself. His marriage into Ahab's house did not diminish his responsibility for the course he chose.

The people made no burning for him as they had for his fathers, and he departed without being desired. He was buried in the city of David, but not in the sepulchres of the kings. Yet the Lord did not destroy David's house, because of His covenant. The preservation of that house displayed God's faithfulness, not Jehoram's innocence.

verses.text: 4Now when Jehoram was risen up to the kingdom of his father, he strengthened himself, and slew all his brethren with the sword, and divers also of the princes of Israel. 5Jehoram was thirty and two years old when he began to reign, and he reigned eight years in Jerusalem. 6And he walked in the way of the kings of Israel, like as did the house of Ahab: for he had the daughter of Ahab to wife: and he wrought that which was evil in the eyes of the Lord. 7Howbeit the Lord would not destroy the house of David, because of the covenant that he had made with David, and as he promised to give a light to him and to his sons for ever.

entries.commentary: Jehoshaphat slept with his fathers and was buried in the city of David, and Jehoram his son reigned in his stead. Jehoshaphat had given his sons great gifts of silver, gold, and precious things with fenced cities, but he gave the kingdom to Jehoram because he was the firstborn. As soon as Jehoram was risen up and strengthened himself, he slew all his brethren with the sword, along with divers of the princes of Israel. This is a pattern to watch: as soon as some among Israel get power, they turn and hurt everyone around them; the moment he got the throne he killed his own brothers.

Jehoram was thirty and two years old when he began to reign, and he reigned eight years in Jerusalem. He walked in the way of the kings of Israel, as did the house of Ahab, meaning he was wicked; Israel's kings were all wicked, and he had the daughter of Ahab to wife. Yet the Most High would not destroy the house of David, because of the covenant He had made with David, promising to give a light to him and to his sons forever. The Most High keeps His promises. Just as He did not break His word to David, He did not break His promise to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob; those promises were made to the Israelites and stand to this day, and we have plenty of proof of it.

In Jehoram's days Edom revolted from under the dominion of Judah and made themselves a king, and Libnah revolted at the same time because he had forsaken the Most High. When we obey the Most High the nations are subject to us; when we come out from under the commandments, that is when the other nations rise up and revolt against us and keep us in sin. Jehoram made high places in the mountains of Judah and caused the inhabitants of Jerusalem to commit fornication and compelled Judah thereto. Dealing with other gods is spiritual fornication, but physical fornication is built into these false worships; the pagan holidays passed down to our people, whatever the season, are built on fornication, and that is what draws the people to follow them. -

There came a writing to Jehoram from Elijah the prophet, telling him he had not walked in the ways of Jehoshaphat his father nor in the ways of Asa king of Judah, but in the way of the kings of Israel. Elijah charged him with making Judah and Jerusalem go a whoring like the whoredoms of the house of Ahab, and with slaying his brethren who were better than himself. The Most High declared He would smite his people, his children, his wives, and his goods with a great plague. His own body would be struck: he would have great sickness by disease of his bowels, until his bowels fell out by reason of the sickness day by day. This is what it looks like to mess with the Most High. -

The Most High stirred up against Jehoram the spirit of the Philistines and the Arabians that were near the Ethiopians, and they came up into Judah and carried away all his substance, his sons, and his wives, leaving only Jehoahaz his youngest. Because of his disobedience his whole family was carried into captivity by the Philistines, the Arabs, and the Ethiopians, the same peoples who later held our people in the trans-Saharan slave trade. After all this the Most High smote him in his bowels with an incurable disease, and at the end of two years his bowels fell out and he died of sore diseases. He reigned eight years and departed without being desired; many were glad to see him go. They made no burning for him and buried him in the city of David but not in the sepulchres of the kings. A good name is better than precious ointment; a man cannot rule wickedly and shame the people and then expect them to stand by him when disease comes. It is a fearful thing to fall into the hands of the Most High.

Elisha warns the Shunammite woman whose son he restored to flee the coming seven year famine, and she sojourns in the land of the Philistines. When she returns to appeal to the king for her house and land, Gehazi is at that moment telling the king how Elisha restored a dead body to life. The timing is of the Most High, so the king restores all that was hers and the fruits of the field from the day she left.

Ben-hadad king of Syria, sick, sends Hazael to inquire of Elisha whether he will recover, for the word of a prophet, also called a seer, was precious in those days. Elisha tells Hazael the king may recover but the Most High has shown that he shall surely die, then weeps because he sees the evil Hazael will do to Israel: burning strongholds, slaying young men, and ripping up women with child. Elisha tells Hazael he will be king over Syria, revealing that leadership can discern spirits at work in a man that the man does not see in himself. Hazael returns and smothers the king with a wet cloth and reigns in his place.

Jehoram son of Jehoshaphat begins to reign over Judah and walks in the way of the kings of Israel because the daughter of Ahab was his wife. He does evil in the sight of the Most High, yet Judah is not destroyed for David his servant's sake, according to the promise.

In Jehoram's days Edom revolts from under the hand of Judah and makes a king over itself, breaking the subjection Edom had been under from the days of David and Solomon. This revolt fulfills the word spoken to Esau, that when he gained the dominion he would break the yoke from off his neck, a pattern reaching to Edom's later rise. Jehoram sleeps with his fathers and is buried in the city of David, and Ahaziah his son reigns in his place. -

Ahaziah son of Jehoram begins to reign over Judah and walks in the way of the house of Ahab, being the son-in-law of that house, a picture of the generational curse passed from father to son. He goes with Jehoram son of Ahab to war against Hazael king of Syria, and the Syrians wound Jehoram at Ramah. Jehoram returns to Jezreel to be healed, and Ahaziah goes down to see him, setting the stage for both kings to meet Jehu's judgment.

If thou shalt hearken diligently unto the voice of the Lord thy God to observe and to do all his commandments, the Most High will set thee on high above all nations of the earth. Diligent means characterized by steady, earnest, and energetic effort. You have to be on fire for the laws of the Most High, standing fast. You cannot be one foot in and one foot out, lukewarm, yawning through the classes. You cannot be tired of the word of the Lord; be excited to hear it.
All these blessings shall come on thee and overtake thee, if thou shalt hearken unto the voice of the Lord thy God. Hearken means to listen.

Blessed in the city and blessed in the field; blessed shall be the fruit of thy body, which is your children, and the fruit of thy ground and cattle. Blessed shall be thy basket and thy store: that is going into your surplus. Blessed when thou comest in and blessed when thou goest out: it is twofold, but it is going into coming in and out of Jerusalem.

The enemies that rise up against thee shall flee before thee seven ways; the blessing is commanded on thy storehouses and on all thou settest thine hand unto. The Most High shall establish thee an holy people unto himself, and all the people of the earth shall see that thou art called by the name of the Lord and be afraid of thee. Thou shalt lend unto many nations and not borrow; the Lord shall make thee the head and not the tail, above only and not beneath, if thou hearken to the commandments and turn not aside after other gods. Isaiah sums up [Deuteronomy 28:1-14](/bible/deuteronomy/28#v1): we possessed it but a little while. Israel had the blessings to a point when they went into the land, but only about eighty years at the full level, under David and Solomon. How Solomon abounded in gold, ships, and plenty of food you can read in 1 Kings.

But if thou wilt not hearken unto the voice of the Lord thy God to observe to do all his commandments and his statutes, all these curses shall come upon thee and overtake thee. Now we do some precepting, word by word. The voice of the Lord is his commandments; to hearken unto his voice means to keep his commandments. Observe to DO all his commandments: do is the action word. The Most High is a God of doing, and by him actions are weighed. Do not talk proudly and arrogantly, saying God loves me no matter what and God knows my heart; he had a personal relationship with a few men like Abraham, Isaac, Jacob, Samuel, and David, and talking like you are one of them is arrogancy coming out of your mouth. Curses means evil: the Lord said, I will bring evil upon this people because they have not hearkened unto my words. Overtake thee means you shall not be able to escape them, and though they cry unto him, he will not hearken.

Cursed shalt thou be in the city: as when police fired on a car of siblings as young as nine years old in Georgia after the children panicked when a cruiser followed their vehicle. That is cursed in the city. Cursed shalt thou be in the field: we came off the slave ship and went right to the field, picking cotton from sunup to sundown. We know that one.

Cursed shall be thy basket and thy store: that goes into your businesses and your holdings. It is hard enough for a black man or woman to start a business; we are left with side hustles while the major trades, the ships, the metals, and the timber belong to Esau. These curses are on us as a nation. It is not about us individually; keep that in mind.

Cursed shall be the fruit of thy body: your children. The same children panicking in front of police, and the dozens of children killed by youth gun violence in Chicago in a matter of months. Cursed shall be the fruit of thy land, thy kine, and thy sheep: the food we eat is cursed. Fast food fills our neighborhoods, and where there is no fast food there is a corner store selling unclean meat that causes diseases in us. Ezekiel says it plainly: the children of Israel eat their defiled bread among the Gentiles. Others may eat that food, but it is foul for us because we are supposed to eat the best food on the planet, for we are an holy people as [Deuteronomy 14](/bible/deuteronomy/14) says.

Cursed shalt thou be when thou comest in and cursed when thou goest out. He is talking about Jerusalem, but it is twofold: it is coming in and going out of life itself. Ecclesiasticus, for you newer people in the Apocrypha, spells it out: we are born under the curses and we die still living under them.

The Lord shall send upon thee cursing, vexation, and rebuke in all that thou settest thine hand unto, until thou be destroyed. Rebuke means sharp disapproval or criticism because of your behavior: no matter what you do, nobody will see the silver lining in it; even what you mean for good turns out bad. Vexation means the state of being annoyed or a thing that causes annoyance: among these nations they do not love you, they tolerate you. Your marching for equal rights annoys them; they ask why you will not just accept what you were given.

The Lord shall make the pestilence cleave unto thee: diseases. He shall smite thee with a consumption, a fever, an inflammation, an extreme burning, the sword, blasting, and mildew. Amos shows what the blasting and mildew go into: famine, pestilence after the manner of Egypt, young men slain with the sword, death and destruction.

Thy heaven over thy head shall be brass, and the earth under thee iron. It is twofold: rain not coming down and crops not coming up. It also goes into the chains above your head and the shackles of iron on your feet. Look up the images of slavery and you see whose neck the chains were on. The rain of thy land shall be powder and dust from heaven until thou be destroyed.

Thou shalt go out one way against thine enemies and flee seven ways before them, and shalt be removed into all the kingdoms of the earth: 1492 and 1619. Thy carcase shall be meat unto the fowls of the air and the beasts of the earth, and no man shall fray them away. Look up Wounded Knee, where the United States cavalry killed the Native Americans, who are Gad in the Bible, and left their bodies in the snow.

The Lord will smite thee with the botch of Egypt, the emerods, the scab, and the itch, whereof thou canst not be healed. The itch that cannot be healed: look up who has the highest rates of sexually transmitted diseases right now. It is us.

The Lord shall smite thee with madness, blindness, and astonishment of heart, and thou shalt grope at noonday as the blind gropeth in darkness. Thou shalt not prosper in thy ways, and thou shalt be only oppressed and spoiled evermore, and no man shall save thee: going back into bondage. Hosea shows the wandering of the blind: we fled from the Most High, we return but not to the Most High, and the end of it is derision in the land of Egypt, which means captivity.

Thou shalt betroth a wife and another man shall lie with her: our wives were taken away, raped, robbed, and murdered in the captivity. Thou shalt build an house and not dwell therein: we built the master's house, we built the White House, and to this day our people frame the roofs of suburban houses they will never live in. Thou shalt plant a vineyard and not gather the grapes: down south our people and the Haitians, who are Levi, are still in the fields picking beans and oranges, and none of it comes back to them; it is packaged and shipped somewhere else. Thine ass shall be violently taken away from before thy face and shall not be restored to thee: no reparations. They just pulled the okey-doke in North Carolina, promising reparations and then saying it would not be paid in money but in infrastructure. The Most High said it would not be restored.

Thy sons and thy daughters shall be given unto another people, and thine eyes shall look and fail with longing for them all the day long, and there shall be no might in thine hand. The slave narratives collected in When I Was a Slave back it up: slaves were treated like cattle, a speculator went about the country buying them up, and it was pitiful to see children taken from the mother's breast, mothers sold from children, husbands sold from wives. Another narrative: slavery days were hell; babies were snatched from their mother's breast and sold to speculators, children separated from sisters and brothers and never saw each other again. The Bible is a true book, and our ancestors backed it up.

The fruit of thy land and all thy labours shall a nation which thou knowest not eat up, and thou shalt be only oppressed and crushed alway. The record of the conquistadors says one Spaniard ate enough for seven of the Indians, the northern kingdom. They literally ate up the fruit of the land. Thou shalt be mad for the sight of thine eyes which thou shalt see.

The Lord shall bring thee and thy king unto a nation which neither thou nor thy fathers have known, and there shalt thou serve other gods, wood and stone. Thou shalt become an astonishment, a proverb, and a byword among all nations: Puerto Rican, Dominican, Haitian, Jamaican, African American, gentile. We lost our name and left it for a curse, like it says in Isaiah, while others wear the name and cry anti-Semitic.

Thou shalt carry much seed out into the field and gather but little in; thou shalt plant vineyards but neither drink the wine nor gather the grapes; olive trees through all thy coasts, but no oil to anoint thyself. Thou shalt beget sons and daughters, but thou shalt not enjoy them, for they shall go into captivity: the same story the slave narratives tell. It happened before the ships too. When we ruled in Spain, in what they call the Dark Ages, a shipload of our people cast out on the African coast had the men and youths sold into slavery, the defenseless women ravished, and the aged, the sick, and the infants tortured and murdered by the thousands. That is recorded in The Jews and Moors in Spain; get that book if you do not have it.

All thy trees and the fruit of thy land shall the locust consume. The stranger that is within thee shall get up above thee very high, and thou shalt come down very low; he shall lend to thee, and thou shalt not lend to him; he shall be the head, and thou shalt be the tail. Basically, you will always be oppressed. Their own book, New World Jewry, says the Jewish converts were so disseminated through all the trading parts of the world that they became the pegs and nails that keep the whole frame of commerce together, back in the 1600s. But the curse says Israel comes down very low and borrows from the stranger. The lender at the top of world trade and the cursed borrower cannot be the same people; somebody is lying, and now we caught it.

All these curses shall pursue thee and overtake thee till thou be destroyed, because thou hearkenedst not unto the voice of the Lord thy God. They shall be upon thee for a sign and for a wonder, and upon thy seed for ever. There is no time limit on this thing; that is how we know we are the real Israelites, because these curses are still hitting us all over the earth in some shape, form, or fashion to this day. The Most High said you would be the bottom, and he meant it until the kingdom comes. That is why they do not want to go to [Deuteronomy 28](/bible/deuteronomy/28).

Because thou servedst not the Lord thy God with joyfulness and with gladness of heart for the abundance of all things: we have to be happy keeping these commandments. That means joyful at the new moon, joyful on the sabbath, joyful in the classes. The lack of joy in keeping the commandments is the very reason the captivity came. Sisters, that includes the commandment to be obedient and in subjection to your husband. Do not act like it is bondage; your husband cannot save you on the day of judgment, and you must work out your own salvation and stand before Christ with a joyful spirit in the commandments.

Therefore shalt thou serve thine enemies in hunger, in thirst, in nakedness, and in want of all things, and he shall put a yoke of iron upon thy neck until he have destroyed thee. Here is one way we stay destroyed: Juneteenth. The slave narrative records the master telling his slaves, this is military law, but I am forced to tell you this law says you are now free; I cannot make you stay unless you want to. That June 19th announcement of the master's law is what is still celebrated in Texas. Our people celebrate Juneteenth like it is something to be proud of, but it is the slave master's holiday, and we are still slaves under the curses.

The Lord shall bring a nation against thee from far, from the end of the earth, as swift as the eagle flieth: the eagle is the symbol of Esau's nation. A nation whose tongue thou shalt not understand: we did not speak English, and our brothers in the islands and South America did not speak Spanish when the ships came. New World Jewry itself records that many slaves were called ladino, which in that context means a negro slave who could speak Spanish. So the northern kingdom brother who says he is not black is simply a negro that speaks Spanish; welcome home, you are our brother. A nation of fierce countenance, which shall not regard the person of the old nor shew favour to the young: they worked the old to death in the cotton fields, and today an old man dies with a knee held on his neck for over eight minutes, and children get fired on by police. Neither old nor young is spared.

He shall eat the fruit of thy cattle and the fruit of thy land until thou be destroyed, leaving thee neither corn, wine, nor oil. The Native Americans lived off the land, following the buffalo and the deer and making coats of skins. Now Reuben stays by the casino and Gad lives on reservation lands like barren wasteland where nothing grows, with outdoor plumbing, and it has never been restored. Reparations is not a casino, and it is not being called sovereign while occupied by another nation.

He shall besiege thee in all thy gates until thy high and fenced walls come down. Verse 52 onward is going into the siege of Jerusalem by Babylon and by Rome, and Assyria did this also. This is NOT talking about black-on-black violence; do not use it for that. Thou shalt eat the fruit of thine own body, the flesh of thy sons and daughters, in the siege and in the straitness wherewith thine enemies shall distress thee. The Most High starved our people out in the siege until they boiled and ate their own children. The proof it is not street violence is in the text itself: the tender man's eye shall be evil toward the wife of his bosom and toward the remnant of his children, because he has nothing left in the siege. It describes a good, caring, delicate man broken by famine, not violence in the neighborhood. The tender and delicate woman, which would not set the sole of her foot upon the ground for delicateness: our sisters have fallen a long way from that standard of tenderness and delicateness, and they need to return to it.

If thou wilt not observe to do all the words of this law written in this book, that thou mayest fear this glorious and fearful name, THE LORD THY GOD, then he will make thy plagues wonderful, plagues of thy seed, of long continuance, and sore sicknesses. Verse 59 is saying the Most High will make up diseases to keep punishing you; he will even have Esau create them in a laboratory and make them affect you more than anybody else. He will bring upon thee all the diseases of Egypt which thou wast afraid of, and also every sickness and every plague which is NOT written in the book of this law, until thou be destroyed.

Ye shall be left few in number, whereas ye were as the stars of heaven for multitude, because thou wouldest not obey the voice of the Lord thy God. As the Lord rejoiced over you to do you good and to multiply you, so the Lord will rejoice over you to destroy you. We have to understand who we are dealing with: he is happy to bless you and happy to destroy you for breaking the commandments. That is the God this Christianity needs to be teaching, to put some fear back in our people.

The Lord shall scatter thee among all people from the one end of the earth even unto the other, and there thou shalt serve other gods which neither thou nor thy fathers have known, even wood and stone: that is talking about Christianity and Islam. The Handbook of Denominations records that as early as 1700 white slaveholders in the south provided religious teaching for their slaves, and the slaves identified with the faith of their owners: if your slave master was Baptist you were Baptist; if he was Catholic you were Catholic. The same book says black Baptist doctrine runs quite parallel to that of white Baptist churches: it is the same exact thing, the slave master's religion with a black face on it. The Most High is saying: wherever I scatter you, you will not know me; you will be caught up thinking you serve me, but you do not know me. The only time you will know him is when he puts his spirit back on the earth and reveals it in the last days. That is why there is so much turmoil in our life, because we were not serving God right.

Among these nations shalt thou find no ease, neither shall the sole of thy foot have rest, but the Lord shall give thee there a trembling heart, and failing of eyes, and sorrow of mind. No ease: the northern kingdom is catching it right now, with migrant children taken from their families and detained in hotels not even registered with the government before deportation, and thousands of those children cannot be found.

Thy life shall hang in doubt before thee, and thou shalt fear day and night, and shalt have none assurance of thy life. That is why those children panicked when the police car pulled up behind them: no assurance of thy life. In the morning thou shalt say, Would God it were even, and at even, Would God it were morning, for the fear of thine heart and the sight of thine eyes.

Here is the nail in the coffin: the Lord shall bring thee into Egypt again with ships. Egypt means bondage; the scripture defines it right in [Deuteronomy 5](/bible/deuteronomy/5), the land of Egypt, the house of bondage. He is saying: I will bring you into slavery again, with ships. It is not the literal land of Egypt, because you can walk to Egypt; Isaiah shows Israel walked down to Egypt. The false pastors who say we were shipped back across the Red Sea are wrong; the ships went to a spiritual Egypt. Revelation names it: the great city which spiritually is called Sodom and Egypt. The greatest country on the face of the earth, America, Babylon the great, is the Egypt we were carried into with ships. Even their own scholarship confirms who was there the first time: a treatise on physical geography admits that negroes existed in Egypt in the days of Rameses with the same national features they have now. The Bible says the negroes go INTO Egypt, bondage, AGAIN. There ye shall be sold unto your enemies for bondmen and bondwomen, and no man shall buy you: buy means redeem. Under the servitude laws a poor brother sold to a stranger could be redeemed by his uncle, his uncle's son, or any of his kin; but in this captivity none of your brothers can redeem you, because they are in bondage right along with you, as verse 29 already said: no man shall save thee.
Thou shalt be only oppressed and spoiled evermore, and no man shall save thee; the quick precept for no man shall buy you.

name: Ahaziah of Judah
charge: Walking in the ways of the house of Ahab, his mother being his counsellor to do wickedly
summary: Ahaziah followed the counsel of his mother and Ahab's house. He joined Joram in war and visited him at Jezreel. His coming to Joram brought him into the judgment executed by Jehu. He was killed, and those who buried him remembered the faithfulness of his forefather Jehoshaphat.
offense: Ahaziah followed the counsel of his mother and the house of Ahab. Those who should have guided the young king toward the Lord became his counselors to his destruction. He joined Joram of Israel in war against Hazael and afterward went to visit the wounded king at Jezreel. His connection to Jehoshaphat did not make his own conduct righteous. He chose the ways of Ahab's house and joined its cause when judgment was approaching it.
judgment: Chronicles declares that Ahaziah's destruction was of God in coming to Joram. He went out with him against Jehu, whom the Lord had anointed to cut off Ahab's house. Jehu's men also killed the princes of Judah and Ahaziah's relatives who attended him. Ahaziah was sought out and killed. Those who buried him remembered Jehoshaphat, his forefather, who had sought the Lord with all his heart. That remembered faithfulness secured a measure of regard at his burial, but it had not sheltered Ahaziah from the consequences of his own alliance. His house was left without strength to retain the kingdom.
offenseFull: Ahaziah followed the counsel of his mother and the house of Ahab. Those who should have guided the young king toward the Lord became his counselors to his destruction. He joined Joram of Israel in war against Hazael and afterward went to visit the wounded king at Jezreel.
His connection to Jehoshaphat did not make his own conduct righteous. He chose the ways of Ahab's house and joined its cause when judgment was approaching it.
judgmentFull: Chronicles declares that Ahaziah's destruction was of God in coming to Joram. He went out with him against Jehu, whom the Lord had anointed to cut off Ahab's house. Jehu's men also killed the princes of Judah and Ahaziah's relatives who attended him.

Ahaziah was sought out and killed. Those who buried him remembered Jehoshaphat, his forefather, who had sought the Lord with all his heart. That remembered faithfulness secured a measure of regard at his burial, but it had not sheltered Ahaziah from the consequences of his own alliance. His house was left without strength to retain the kingdom.

verses.text: 1And the inhabitants of Jerusalem made Ahaziah his youngest son king in his stead: for the band of men that came with the Arabians to the camp had slain all the eldest. So Ahaziah the son of Jehoram king of Judah reigned. 2Forty and two years old was Ahaziah when he began to reign, and he reigned one year in Jerusalem. His mother’s name also was Athaliah the daughter of Omri. 3He also walked in the ways of the house of Ahab: for his mother was his counsellor to do wickedly. 4Wherefore he did evil in the sight of the Lord like the house of Ahab: for they were his counsellors after the death of his father to his destruction. 5He walked also after their counsel, and went with Jehoram the son of Ahab king of Israel to war against Hazael king of Syria at Ramoth–gilead: and the Syrians smote Joram. 6And he returned to be healed in Jezreel because of the wounds which were given him at Ramah, when he fought with Hazael king of Syria. And Azariah the son of Jehoram king of Judah went down to see Jehoram the son of Ahab at Jezreel, because he was sick.

7And the destruction of Ahaziah was of God by coming to Joram: for when he was come, he went out with Jehoram against Jehu the son of Nimshi, whom the Lord had anointed to cut off the house of Ahab. 8And it came to pass, that, when Jehu was executing judgment upon the house of Ahab, and found the princes of Judah, and the sons of the brethren of Ahaziah, that ministered to Ahaziah, he slew them. 9And he sought Ahaziah: and they caught him, (for he was hid in Samaria,) and brought him to Jehu: and when they had slain him, they buried him: Because, said they, he is the son of Jehoshaphat, who sought the Lord with all his heart. So the house of Ahaziah had no power to keep still the kingdom.

entries.commentary: The inhabitants of Jerusalem made Ahaziah, Jehoram's youngest son, king in his stead, for the band of Arabians had slain all the elder sons. Ahaziah was forty and two years old when he began to reign and reigned one year in Jerusalem, and his mother's name was Athaliah the daughter of Omri. He walked in the ways of the house of Ahab, for his mother was his counsellor to do wickedly, and the house of Ahab were his counsellors after his father died, to his destruction. This is a warning against being ruled by the wrong counsel: instead of going to the priests and the judges, he went to his mother, and she counselled him into ruin. A woman with a grudge can rule a kingdom through her son, and that is what Athaliah did.

Ahaziah walked after their counsel and went with Jehoram son of Ahab to war against Hazael king of Syria at Ramoth-gilead, where Jehoram was wounded. He went down to see the wounded Jehoram at Jezreel, and the destruction of Ahaziah was of the Most High, for by going he came into the path of Jehu, whom the Most High had anointed to cut off the house of Ahab. That same Jehu who killed the seventy sons of Ahab found the princes of Judah and the sons of Ahaziah's brethren and slew them, then sought and caught Ahaziah, who was hid in Samaria. They buried Ahaziah for the sake of Jehoshaphat his forefather who sought the Most High with all his heart; but the house of Ahaziah had no power to keep the kingdom, so the wicked king was cut off by the same hand the Most High anointed to avenge Israel.

When Athaliah saw that her son was dead, she arose and destroyed all the seed royal of the house of Judah, killing the king's sons. But Jehoshabeath the daughter of king Jehoram, wife of Jehoiada the priest and sister of Ahaziah, took Joash the son of Ahaziah and stole him from among the king's sons that were slain, hiding him and his nurse in a bedchamber. She hid the child in the house of God six years while Athaliah reigned over the land, showing that Athaliah was ruling in the position of the son she had lost. Athaliah did not carry out this slaughter alone; she had weak men helping her run over everything, which is how she seized and held the throne.

Elisha warns the Shunammite woman whose son he restored to flee the coming seven year famine, and she sojourns in the land of the Philistines. When she returns to appeal to the king for her house and land, Gehazi is at that moment telling the king how Elisha restored a dead body to life. The timing is of the Most High, so the king restores all that was hers and the fruits of the field from the day she left.

Ben-hadad king of Syria, sick, sends Hazael to inquire of Elisha whether he will recover, for the word of a prophet, also called a seer, was precious in those days. Elisha tells Hazael the king may recover but the Most High has shown that he shall surely die, then weeps because he sees the evil Hazael will do to Israel: burning strongholds, slaying young men, and ripping up women with child. Elisha tells Hazael he will be king over Syria, revealing that leadership can discern spirits at work in a man that the man does not see in himself. Hazael returns and smothers the king with a wet cloth and reigns in his place.

Jehoram son of Jehoshaphat begins to reign over Judah and walks in the way of the kings of Israel because the daughter of Ahab was his wife. He does evil in the sight of the Most High, yet Judah is not destroyed for David his servant's sake, according to the promise.

In Jehoram's days Edom revolts from under the hand of Judah and makes a king over itself, breaking the subjection Edom had been under from the days of David and Solomon. This revolt fulfills the word spoken to Esau, that when he gained the dominion he would break the yoke from off his neck, a pattern reaching to Edom's later rise. Jehoram sleeps with his fathers and is buried in the city of David, and Ahaziah his son reigns in his place. -

Ahaziah son of Jehoram begins to reign over Judah and walks in the way of the house of Ahab, being the son-in-law of that house, a picture of the generational curse passed from father to son. He goes with Jehoram son of Ahab to war against Hazael king of Syria, and the Syrians wound Jehoram at Ramah. Jehoram returns to Jezreel to be healed, and Ahaziah goes down to see him, setting the stage for both kings to meet Jehu's judgment.

Elisha sends one of the children of the prophets to Ramoth-gilead to anoint Jehu king over Israel, pour the oil on his head, and flee. Jehu is charged to smite the house of Ahab to avenge the blood of the prophets and of the servants of the Most High shed at the hand of Jezebel, whose work was to kill the prophets while weak Ahab let it continue. The word declares the whole house of Ahab shall perish, and the dogs shall eat Jezebel in the portion of Jezreel with none to bury her.

Jehu's fellow captains ask why the mad fellow came, and when he tells them the prophet anointed him king, they hasten to put their garments under him and blow the trumpets, proclaiming Jehu king. Jehu conspires against Jehoram and charges that none escape the city to carry the news to Jezreel. He rides toward Jezreel where Jehoram lay wounded, and Ahaziah king of Judah had come down to see him.

A watchman spies Jehu's company, and two horsemen sent to ask if it is peace are each told to turn behind him and do not return, for the driving is furious like the driving of Jehu. Jehoram himself goes out and asks if it is peace, and Jehu answers that there can be no peace while the whoredoms and witchcrafts of his mother Jezebel are so many. Jehu draws his bow with full strength and smites Jehoram through the heart, then casts him into the portion of Naboth the Jezreelite according to the word of the Most High.

Ahaziah king of Judah flees but Jehu pursues and has him smitten in his chariot; he flees to Megiddo and dies there. His servants carry him to Jerusalem and bury him in the sepulchre of his fathers in the city of David.

Jezebel paints her face and tires her head, returning to her seductive ways as Jehu enters the gate. Jehu calls out for who is on his side, and two or three eunuchs look out. At Jehu's word they throw her down, her blood is sprinkled on the wall and the horses, and he treads her under foot. When they go to bury her they find only the skull, the feet, and the palms of her hands, fulfilling the word spoken by Elijah that dogs would eat the flesh of Jezebel and her carcass would be as dung upon the field.

A wise son takes his father's instruction, but a scorner will not even hear rebuke. What you do with correction marks whether you are wise or a scorner. The scriptures constantly tell you to watch your mouth. Everything you say you will give account for, so he that guards his mouth keeps his life while the one who opens his lips wide brings destruction.

The lazy soul desires and has nothing, but the diligent soul is made fat. Desire without labor stays empty. The righteous man hates lying, but the wicked is loathsome and comes to shame. Righteousness keeps the upright, while wickedness overthrows the sinner.

Some make themselves rich yet have nothing, and some make themselves poor yet have great riches. This is the man who forsakes things when he comes into the truth, giving up sponsorships and possessions, yet he still has great riches because the kingdom of heaven is coming to him. A man's riches may be the ransom of his life, but the poor does not even hear rebuke.

The light of the righteous rejoices, but the lamp of the wicked is put out. Only by pride comes contention, but with the well-advised is wisdom, which points to seeking counsel at all times. Wealth gotten by vanity is diminished, but he that gathers by labor increases. Those chasing the fast dollar and fast money will see all those riches diminish.

Hope deferred makes the heart sick, but when the desire comes it is a tree of life. Whoever despises the word is destroyed, but he that fears the commandment is rewarded. The law of the wise is a fountain of life to depart from the snares of death.

Good understanding gives favor, but the way of transgressors is hard. Every prudent man deals with knowledge, but a fool lays his folly open for all to see. A wicked messenger falls into mischief, but a faithful ambassador is health.

Poverty and shame come to the one who refuses instruction, but he that regards reproof is honored. He that walks with wise men shall be wise, but a companion of fools is destroyed. Every beast cleaves to its like: around fools you become a fool, around wise men you become wise.

Evil pursues sinners, but the righteous are repaid with good. A good man leaves an inheritance to his children's children, and the wealth of the sinner is laid up for the just. This is powerful for us as a nation. A lot of black people do not like to talk about death, but get your life insurance and leave an inheritance to your children's children. That is how far ahead we have to think.

He that spares his rod hates his son, but he that loves him disciplines him early. Discipline your children. Esau has set it up so no one wants anyone to discipline our kids, but the discipline is a bullet. The righteous eats to the satisfying of his soul, but the belly of the wicked shall want.

name: Jehoiada the priest
charge: Hiding the king's son six years from Athaliah; making a covenant between the Lord, the king, and the people; doing good in Israel, both toward God and toward his house
summary: When Athaliah killed the seed royal, Jehoiada's wife stole the baby Joash out of the slaughter and the priest hid him in the house of the Lord six years. In the seventh he armed the Levites, crowned the boy, had Athaliah taken out and slain, tore down the house of Baal, and set the temple in order. He was buried among the kings.
offense: While Athaliah destroyed the royal seed, Jehoshabeath rescued Joash and hid him in the house of God. Jehoiada guarded the child through the years of concealment. In the seventh year he gathered the captains, Levites, and fathers of Israel into a covenant and brought forth the king's son according to the Lord's promise concerning David. He ordered the guards, kept the holy place from unauthorized entry, and gave Joash the crown and testimony. He made a covenant that the king and people should be the Lord's people. The house of Baal was broken down, and the service of the Lord's house was restored according to its appointed order.
judgment: And all the people of the land rejoiced: and the city was quiet, after that they had slain Athaliah with the sword. And Joash did that which was right in the sight of the Lord all the days of Jehoiada the priest. Jehoiada waxed old, and was full of days when he died; an hundred and thirty years old was he when he died. And they buried him in the city of David among the kings, because he had done good in Israel, both toward God, and toward his house. What Joash did after Jehoiada died is his own case.
offenseFull: While Athaliah destroyed the royal seed, Jehoshabeath rescued Joash and hid him in the house of God. Jehoiada guarded the child through the years of concealment. In the seventh year he gathered the captains, Levites, and fathers of Israel into a covenant and brought forth the king's son according to the Lord's promise concerning David.

He ordered the guards, kept the holy place from unauthorized entry, and gave Joash the crown and testimony. He made a covenant that the king and people should be the Lord's people. The house of Baal was broken down, and the service of the Lord's house was restored according to its appointed order.
judgmentFull: Joash was established upon the throne, the people rejoiced, and the city was quiet after Athaliah was put to death outside the house of the Lord. Joash did right in the sight of the Lord during Jehoiada's lifetime.

Jehoiada lived to be a hundred and thirty years old. He was buried among the kings because he had done good in Israel, toward God and His house. His honor was not founded on possessing the crown, but on faithfully preserving the king and restoring the people's covenant obligations.

verses.text: 10But when Athaliah the mother of Ahaziah saw that her son was dead, she arose and destroyed all the seed royal of the house of Judah. 11But Jehoshabeath, the daughter of the king, took Joash the son of Ahaziah, and stole him from among the king’s sons that were slain, and put him and his nurse in a bedchamber. So Jehoshabeath, the daughter of king Jehoram, the wife of Jehoiada the priest, (for she was the sister of Ahaziah,) hid him from Athaliah, so that she slew him not. 12And he was with them hid in the house of God six years: and Athaliah reigned over the land.

1And in the seventh year Jehoiada strengthened himself, and took the captains of hundreds, Azariah the son of Jeroham, and Ishmael the son of Jehohanan, and Azariah the son of Obed, and Maaseiah the son of Adaiah, and Elishaphat the son of Zichri, into covenant with him. 2And they went about in Judah, and gathered the Levites out of all the cities of Judah, and the chief of the fathers of Israel, and they came to Jerusalem. 3And all the congregation made a covenant with the king in the house of God.
