name: Josiah at Megiddo
charge: Going to battle against Necho without inquiring of the Lord
summary: The reformer king, promised he would be gathered to his grave in peace, went out against Pharaoh Necho, who was marching to Carchemish and had no quarrel with Judah. Necho sent word that God had commanded him to make haste and that Josiah should not meddle with God, who was with him. Josiah disguised himself and fought anyway.
offense: After Josiah had prepared the temple, Pharaoh Necho came to fight at Carchemish. Josiah went out against him. Necho sent word that his quarrel was not with Judah and warned Josiah not to oppose the God who had commanded him to make haste. Josiah would not turn away. He disguised himself and entered the battle at Megiddo. Chronicles expressly says that he did not listen to the words of Necho from the mouth of God. The king's earlier reforms and devotion to the law did not make this later decision right.
judgment: Archers hit him in the valley of Megiddo; his servants carried him to Jerusalem and he died. Jeremiah lamented for him, and the lament became an ordinance in Israel. The promise of a peaceful grave was kept in the sense that he did not see the evil that followed.
offenseFull: After Josiah had prepared the temple, Pharaoh Necho came to fight at Carchemish. Josiah went out against him. Necho sent word that his quarrel was not with Judah and warned Josiah not to oppose the God who had commanded him to make haste.

Josiah would not turn away. He disguised himself and entered the battle at Megiddo. Chronicles expressly says that he did not listen to the words of Necho from the mouth of God. The king's earlier reforms and devotion to the law did not make this later decision right.

entries.commentary: Josiah keeps a Passover unto the Lord in Jerusalem, and they kill the Passover on the fourteenth day of the first month, keeping the laws pertaining to the Passover. He sets the priests in their charges, encourages them to the service of the house of the Lord, and tells the Levites to put the holy ark in the house Solomon built and to serve the Lord and his people Israel. He commands them to prepare themselves by their courses and stand in the holy place, then kill the Passover, sanctify themselves, and prepare their brethren to do according to the word of the Lord by the hand of Moses. -

Josiah gives the people thirty thousand lambs and kids and three thousand bullocks for the Passover offerings, and his princes give willingly to the people, the priests, and the Levites. The service is prepared, the priests stand in their place and the Levites in their courses, they kill the Passover, sprinkle the blood, flay the offerings, and roast the Passover with fire according to the ordinance. The singers, the sons of Asaph, are in their place according to the commandment of David, and the porters wait at every gate so they need not depart from their service.

All the service of the Lord is prepared the same day to keep the Passover and offer burnt offerings on the altar according to the commandment of king Josiah. The children of Israel present keep the Passover and the feast of unleavened bread seven days, and there was no Passover like it kept in Israel from the days of Samuel the prophet; none of the kings of Israel kept such a Passover as Josiah kept in his eighteenth year.

After this, Necho king of Egypt comes up to fight at Carchemish by Euphrates, and Josiah goes out against him though Necho sends word that his war is not with Josiah and that God had commanded him to make haste. Josiah will not turn his face but disguises himself to fight, hearkening not to the words of Necho from the mouth of God, and the archers shoot him in the valley of Megiddo. His servants take him from the chariot and bring him to Jerusalem, where he dies and is buried, and all Judah and Jerusalem mourn, and Jeremiah laments for Josiah, written in the Lamentations, a book of the Bible.
The rest of the acts of Josiah and his goodness, according to that which is written in the law of the Lord, and his deeds first and last, are written in the book of the kings of Israel and Judah.

Josiah gathered all the elders of Judah and Jerusalem, went up to the house of the Most High with the priests, the prophets, and all the people both small and great, and read in their ears all the words of the book of the covenant that was found there. Our forefathers had the Bible; the king read it openly, then stood by a pillar and made a covenant before the Lord to walk after him and keep his commandments, testimonies, and statutes with all their heart and soul. All the people stood to the covenant to perform the words written in the book. -

The king commanded Hilkiah and the priests to bring out of the temple all the vessels made for Baal, for the grove, and for all the host of heaven, and he burned them in the fields of Kidron and carried their ashes to Bethel. He put down the idolatrous priests whom the kings of Judah had ordained to burn incense in the high places and around Jerusalem, and those that burnt incense to Baal, to the sun, the moon, the planets, and all the host of heaven. When Josiah read the law the fear of the Lord came upon him and he saw why the nation was under judgment, just as a person is cut when they first hear the truth and realize what they have been doing wrong. -

He brought the grove out of the house of the Lord to the brook Kidron, burned it, stamped it to powder, and cast the powder on the graves of the children of the people. He broke down the houses of the sodomites that were by the house of the Lord, where the women wove hangings for the grove; there should be no sodomite among the sons of Israel, yet they had grown so bold as to do this wickedness right beside the temple. He brought all the priests out of the cities of Judah and defiled the high places where they had burnt incense, and though the priests of the high places did not come up to the altar, they still ate of the unleavened bread among their brethren.

Josiah defiled Topheth in the valley of the children of Hinnom so that no man might make his son or daughter pass through the fire to Molech. Topheth was the place where the people sacrificed their children, and it had to be defiled because Israel would not stop the evil on its own. -

He took away the horses the kings of Judah had given to the sun and burnt the chariots of the sun with fire. He beat down the altars on the roof of Ahaz's chamber and the altars Manasseh had made in the two courts of the house of the Lord, and cast their dust into the brook Kidron. He defiled the high places Solomon had built for Ashtoreth, Chemosh, and Milcom, the abominations of the Zidonians, Moabites, and Ammonites, and broke in pieces the images, cut down the groves, and filled their places with the bones of men. This is repentance in action: cleaning house, getting rid of every idol and evil that causes a people to go off from the Lord and to fall under punishment. -

Josiah also destroyed the altar and high place at Bethel that Jeroboam had made when he set up the golden calves, burning it and stamping it small to powder. Turning himself, he spied the sepulchres in the mount, took out the bones, and burnt them upon the altar to pollute it, according to the word the man of God had proclaimed. When told which sepulchre belonged to the man of God who prophesied these things, he said to let him alone and let no man move his bones. -

Josiah also took away all the houses of the high places in the cities of Samaria, which the kings of Israel had made to provoke the Lord to anger, and did to them as he had done at Bethel. The northern kingdom had already been carried into captivity by Assyria, so most of the people were gone, yet the idolatrous houses remained. He slew all the priests of the high places upon their altars, burnt men's bones upon them, and returned to Jerusalem.

The king commanded all the people to keep the Passover to the Lord their God as it is written in the book of this covenant. Such a Passover had not been held from the days of the judges nor in all the days of the kings of Israel and Judah, but in the eighteenth year of Josiah this Passover was held in Jerusalem. Reading the book of the law brought the nation back to keeping the appointed feasts in order, just as the feast is kept in order today. -

Josiah also put away the workers with familiar spirits, the wizards, the images, the idols, and all the abominations spied in Judah and Jerusalem, that he might perform the words of the law found by Hilkiah. There was no king before or after him that turned to the Lord with all his heart, soul, and might according to all the law of Moses; he put things in order like a true leader. Nevertheless the Lord did not turn from the fierceness of his great wrath because of the provocations of Manasseh, and said he would remove Judah out of his sight as he had removed Israel and cast off Jerusalem.

Pharaohnechoh king of Egypt went up against the king of Assyria to the river Euphrates, and Josiah went against him and was slain at Megiddo. Josiah got involved in a matter that did not concern him and lost his life in it, a warning not to enter into quarrels that are not one's own. His servants carried him dead in a chariot from Megiddo to Jerusalem and buried him, and the people took Jehoahaz his son and anointed him king in his father's place.

Jehoahaz was twenty three years old and reigned three months in Jerusalem, and did evil in the sight of the Lord according to all his fathers had done. Pharaohnechoh bound him at Riblah so he might not reign, put the land to a tribute of silver and gold, and made Eliakim the son of Josiah king, turning his name to Jehoiakim. Jehoiakim taxed the people to pay Pharaoh, exacting the silver and gold of every man of the land, and he also did evil in the sight of the Lord like his forefathers, not like his father Josiah.

Josiah begins to reign at eight years old and reigns thirty-one years, doing that which is right in the sight of the Most High and walking in all the way of David, turning neither to the right nor the left. In his eighteenth year he sends Shaphan the scribe to Hilkiah the priest to gather the silver brought to the house of the Most High and deliver it to the workmen for repairs. The money is given to carpenters, builders, and masons and for timber and hewn stone, and no reckoning is made with them because they dealt faithfully. Josiah rebuilds and reestablishes what Manasseh and Amon destroyed, and he makes sure the workmen are paid, for by the law the workman is worthy of his hire.

Hilkiah the high priest finds the book of the law in the house of the Most High and gives it to Shaphan, who reads it. Manasseh and Amon were so wicked the very book of the law had been lost. Shaphan reports to the king about the money and the workmen, then tells him Hilkiah delivered him a book, and reads it before the king. When the king hears the words of the book of the law he rends his clothes, for the king was meant to read the law before all the people, which the wicked kings had not done. Josiah commands Hilkiah and his servants to inquire of the Most High for him and the people, for great is the wrath kindled against them because their fathers did not hearken to this book. -

Hilkiah and the king's men go to Huldah the prophetess, who dwells in Jerusalem in the college; there were women among the people who were prophetesses, known by their works. Huldah returns the word of the Most High: He will bring evil upon this place and its inhabitants, all the words of the book, because they forsook Him and burned incense to other gods, and His wrath shall not be quenched. But to Josiah, because his heart was tender and he humbled himself and wept before the Most High, the word is that he shall be gathered to his fathers and to his grave in peace, and his eyes shall not see the evil to come. Because Josiah was righteous, repaired the temple, found the book, and began to keep the commandments again, he found mercy; yet the word spoken against Israel for its sin would still come to pass. --- Topics: [Idolatry](/encyclopedia/idolatry) · [The Feasts of the Most High](/encyclopedia/the-feasts-of-the-most-high) · [The Priesthood](/encyclopedia/the-priesthood)

Josiah is eight years old when he begins to reign and reigns thirty one years in Jerusalem, and he does that which is right in the sight of the Lord and walks in the ways of David his father, declining neither to the right hand nor to the left. Comparing the ages shows the point: Manasseh began at twelve, Amon at twenty two, and Josiah at eight, yet the youngest was the wisest. Better is a poor and wise child than an old and foolish king who will no more be admonished. In the eighth year of his reign, while yet young, he begins to seek after the God of David, and in the twelfth year he begins to purge Judah and Jerusalem of the high places, groves, and images. -

They break down the altars of Baal in his presence, cut down the images and groves, and break the carved and molten images to powder, strowing the dust upon the graves of those who had sacrificed to them. He burns the bones of the priests upon their altars and cleanses Judah and Jerusalem, and does the same in the cities of Manasseh, Ephraim, and Simeon, then returns to Jerusalem. -

In the eighteenth year of his reign, when he has purged the land and the house, Josiah sends Shaphan, Maaseiah, and Joah to repair the house of the Lord his God. The money the Levites had gathered from Manasseh, Ephraim, and all the remnant of Israel and Judah is put into the hands of the workmen, who buy hewn stone and timber for couplings and to floor the houses the kings of Judah had destroyed. The men do the work faithfully under overseers of the Levites, with scribes, officers, and porters, that is security, set over the burdens and the service.

When they bring out the money, Hilkiah the priest finds a book of the law of the Lord given by Moses, the very Bible, and delivers it to Shaphan the scribe. Shaphan carries the book to the king and reads it before him, reporting that all committed to the servants is being done and the money delivered to the workmen. -

When the king hears the words of the law, he rends his clothes and commands Hilkiah, Ahikam, Abdon, Shaphan, and Asaiah to go inquire of the Lord for him and for the remnant left in Israel and Judah. He knows great is the wrath of the Lord poured out because the fathers had not kept the word of the Lord to do all that is written in the book. To inquire of the Lord, one must go to a saint, a chosen prophet who has the word. -

Hilkiah and the men go to Huldah the prophetess, wife of Shallum, who dwells in the college in Jerusalem, and she declares the word of the Lord God of Israel. She says the Most High will bring evil and all the curses written in the book upon this place, because they forsook him and burned incense to other gods to provoke him to anger. But because Josiah's heart was tender and he humbled himself, wept, and rent his clothes, the Most High will gather him to his fathers in peace so his eyes will not see the evil to come. -

Josiah gathers all the elders, priests, Levites, and all the people great and small, and reads in their ears all the words of the book of the covenant found in the house of the Lord. He stands in his place and makes a covenant before the Lord to walk after him and keep his commandments, testimonies, and statutes with all his heart and soul, and causes all present to stand to it. Josiah takes away all the abominations out of all the countries belonging to the children of Israel and makes all present serve the Lord their God, and they depart not from following him all his days. All wisdom is the performance of the law.

The burden of the word of the Lord for Israel, saith the Lord, which stretcheth forth the heavens, and layeth the foundation of the earth, and formeth the spirit of man within him. Behold, I will make Jerusalem a cup of trembling unto all the people round about, when they shall be in the siege both against Judah and against Jerusalem. In that day will I make Jerusalem a burdensome stone for all people: all that burden themselves with it shall be cut in pieces, though all the people of the earth be gathered together against it. In that day I will smite every horse with astonishment, and his rider with madness; and I will open mine eyes upon the house of Judah. In that day will I make the governors of Judah like an hearth of fire among the wood, and like a torch of fire in a sheaf; and they shall devour all the people round about, on the right hand and on the left.

The Lord also shall save the tents of Judah first, that the glory of the house of David and the glory of the inhabitants of Jerusalem do not magnify themselves against Judah. In that day shall the Lord defend the inhabitants of Jerusalem; and he that is feeble among them at that day shall be as David; and the house of David shall be as God, as the angel of the Lord before them. It shall come to pass in that day, that I will seek to destroy all the nations that come against Jerusalem.

I will pour upon the house of David, and upon the inhabitants of Jerusalem, the spirit of grace and of supplications: and they shall look upon me whom they have pierced, and they shall mourn for him, as one mourneth for his only son. In that day shall there be a great mourning in Jerusalem, as the mourning of Hadadrimmon in the valley of Megiddon. The land shall mourn, every family apart: the house of David apart, the house of Nathan apart, the house of Levi apart, the family of Shimei apart, and all the families that remain, every family apart, and their wives apart.

name: Zedekiah
charge: Breaking his oath to Nebuchadnezzar; stiffening his neck against the Lord's word by Jeremiah
summary: Sworn by God to serve Babylon, Zedekiah rebelled against Nebuchadnezzar and would not humble himself before Jeremiah speaking from the mouth of the Lord. Warned to the last that surrender would save the city and his life, he feared the Jews who had defected more than he feared the word.
offense: Zedekiah did evil and would not humble himself before Jeremiah. He also rebelled against Nebuchadnezzar, who had made him swear by God. Ezekiel exposed the broken covenant through the figure of the vine that turned toward another eagle, seeking Egyptian help. The oath was not made harmless by the fact that it had been sworn to a foreign king. Jeremiah told Zedekiah that surrender would preserve his life and prevent the city from being burned. Zedekiah feared that the Jews who had already fallen to the Chaldeans would abuse him. The prophet assured him that they would not and urged him to obey. The king nevertheless refused the way of escape set before him.
judgment: The city was besieged until famine prevailed. Zedekiah fled by night, but the Chaldeans overtook him in the plains of Jericho and brought him to Riblah. His sons were killed before his eyes; then his eyes were put out, and he was bound and taken to Babylon. Jerusalem was burned as Jeremiah had warned. The king who feared the humiliation of surrender suffered a far greater calamity through resistance. God's warning had included mercy, but Zedekiah would not submit to receive it.

Jerusalem was burned as Jeremiah had warned. The king who feared the humiliation of surrender suffered a far greater calamity through resistance. God's warning had included mercy, but Zedekiah would not submit to receive it.

verses.text: 11Zedekiah was one and twenty years old when he began to reign, and reigned eleven years in Jerusalem. 12And he did that which was evil in the sight of the Lord his God, and humbled not himself before Jeremiah the prophet speaking from the mouth of the Lord. 13And he also rebelled against king Nebuchadnezzar, who had made him swear by God: but he stiffened his neck, and hardened his heart from turning unto the Lord God of Israel.

entries.commentary: The people of the land take Jehoahaz the son of Josiah and make him king in Jerusalem; he is twenty three years old and reigns three months. The king of Egypt puts him down, condemns the land in a hundred talents of silver and a talent of gold, and makes Eliakim his brother king, turning his name to Jehoiakim, and carries Jehoahaz to Egypt.

Jehoiakim is twenty five years old when he begins to reign and reigns eleven years in Jerusalem, doing evil in the sight of the Lord his God, so Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon comes up against him and binds him in fetters to carry him to Babylon. Nebuchadnezzar also carries off the vessels of the house of the Lord to Babylon and puts them in his temple. The Most High set a wicked king over the land because his own people would not do what he said. The power of the earth is in the hand of the Most High, and in due time he sets over it one that is profitable. When Israel will not rule in righteousness, he raises a Nebuchadnezzar; Israel's purpose was never to be wicked and rule at the same time. -

Jehoiachin is eight years old when he begins to reign and reigns three months and ten days in Jerusalem, and he does that which is evil in the sight of the Lord. When the year is expired, Nebuchadnezzar sends and brings him to Babylon with the goodly vessels of the house of the Lord, and makes Zedekiah his brother king over Judah.

Zedekiah is twenty one years old when he begins to reign and reigns eleven years, and he does evil in the sight of the Lord his God and humbles not himself before Jeremiah the prophet speaking from the mouth of the Lord. He rebels against Nebuchadnezzar who had made him swear by God, and stiffens his neck and hardens his heart from turning to the Lord God of Israel. The chief priests and people transgress very much after all the abominations of the heathen and pollute the house of the Lord. The Most High sends to them by his messengers, rising up early and sending because he had compassion, but they mock the messengers, despise his words, and misuse his prophets until the wrath of the Lord arises and there is no remedy. -

The Most High brings upon them the king of the Chaldees, who slays their young men with the sword in the house of their sanctuary and has no compassion upon young man or maiden, old man or him that stooped for age. He gives them all into Nebuchadnezzar's hand, and all the vessels of the house of God, great and small, and the treasures of the house of the Lord and of the king and his princes are brought to Babylon. They burn the house of God, break down the walls of Jerusalem, burn its palaces, and destroy all the goodly vessels, exactly the fierce nation the curses warned of. -

Those who escape the sword are carried away to Babylon, where they are servants to Nebuchadnezzar and his sons until the reign of the kingdom of Persia. This fulfills the word of the Lord by the mouth of Jeremiah, that the land would enjoy her sabbaths and lie desolate to fulfill threescore and ten years.

In the first year of Cyrus king of Persia, that the word of the Lord by Jeremiah might be accomplished, the Most High stirs up the spirit of Cyrus to make a proclamation throughout all his kingdom. Cyrus declares that the Lord God of heaven has given him all the kingdoms of the earth and charged him to build him a house in Jerusalem, and calls any of the Lord's people to go up, showing again that the Most High sets over the earth one that is profitable for his purpose. --- Topics: [Clean and Unclean Meats](/encyclopedia/clean-and-unclean-meats) · [Idolatry](/encyclopedia/idolatry) · [Sacrifice and Atonement](/encyclopedia/sacrifice-and-atonement) · [The Covenant](/encyclopedia/the-covenant) · [The Feasts of the Most High](/encyclopedia/the-feasts-of-the-most-high) · [The Priesthood](/encyclopedia/the-priesthood) · [The Sabbath](/encyclopedia/the-sabbath)

In the ninth year of Zedekiah's reign Nebuchadnezzar came with all his host against Jerusalem, pitched against it, and built forts round about it. The city was besieged until the eleventh year of Zedekiah, and the famine prevailed in the city. Because the city was besieged no food, water, or goods could get in, so there was no bread for the people of the land.

The city was broken up and the men of war fled by night by the way of the gate between two walls by the king's garden, while the Chaldeans were round about the city. The army pursued the king, overtook him in the plains of Jericho, and his army was scattered from him, and they took him to the king of Babylon at Riblah, where judgment was given upon him. They slew Zedekiah's sons before his eyes, then put out his eyes, bound him with fetters of brass, and carried him to Babylon, just as Jeremiah had warned him.

In the fifth month of the nineteenth year of Nebuchadnezzar, Nebuzaradan the captain of the guard came to Jerusalem. He burnt the house of the Lord, the king's house, and every great man's house, and the army broke down the walls of Jerusalem round about. He carried away the rest of the people and the fugitives, but left the poor of the land to be vinedressers and husbandmen, since the poor could not fend for themselves.

The Chaldeans broke in pieces the pillars of brass, the bases, and the brasen sea that were in the house of the Lord, and carried the brass to Babylon because it was valuable. They took away the pots, shovels, snuffers, spoons, and vessels of brass, and the firepans and bowls of gold and silver the captain of the guard took away. The two pillars, one sea, and the bases Solomon had made were of brass without weight, the one pillar eighteen cubits high with a brasen chapiter, wreathen work, and pomegranates round about.

The captain of the guard took Seraiah the chief priest, Zephaniah the second priest, and the three keepers of the door. He took an officer over the men of war, five men in the king's presence, the principal scribe of the host, and threescore men of the people found in the city. Nebuzaradan brought them to the king of Babylon at Riblah, and the king smote and slew them there; so Judah was carried away out of their land.

Over the people left in the land Nebuchadnezzar made Gedaliah the son of Ahikam, the son of Shaphan, governor. Gedaliah counselled the captains and their men not to fear to serve the Chaldeans but to dwell in the land and serve the king of Babylon, and it would be well with them. But Ishmael the son of Nethaniah, of the royal seed, came with ten men and smote Gedaliah and the Jews and Chaldeans with him, and the people fled to Egypt for fear of the Chaldeans, killing a man who gave wise counsel.

In the thirty seventh year of the captivity of Jehoiachin, Evilmerodach king of Babylon lifted up his head out of prison and spake kindly to him. He set his throne above the thrones of the other kings in Babylon, changed his prison garments, and let him eat bread continually before him all the days of his life. Jehoiachin was given a continual daily allowance for the rest of his life, a mercy shown at the very end of the account. --- Topics: [Idolatry](/encyclopedia/idolatry) · [Sacrifice and Atonement](/encyclopedia/sacrifice-and-atonement) · [The Covenant](/encyclopedia/the-covenant) · [The Feasts of the Most High](/encyclopedia/the-feasts-of-the-most-high) · [The Priesthood](/encyclopedia/the-priesthood)

King Zedekiah the son of Josiah reigns in place of Coniah, whom Nebuchadnezzar made king in the land of Judah, but neither he nor his servants nor the people hearken to the words of the Most High spoken by Jeremiah. Zedekiah sends men to ask Jeremiah to pray to the Most High for them, while Jeremiah is still going in and out among the people, not yet put into prison. Pharaoh's army comes out of Egypt, and when the Chaldeans besieging Jerusalem hear of it, they depart from the city.

The word of the Most High comes to Jeremiah for the king of Judah: Pharaoh's army that came to help shall return to Egypt into their own land. The Chaldeans shall come again, fight against this city, take it, and burn it with fire; the people are not to deceive themselves that the Chaldeans have surely departed. Even if they smote the whole Chaldean army so that only wounded men remained, those men would rise up in their tents and burn the city with fire.

When the Chaldean army breaks up from Jerusalem for fear of Pharaoh's army, Jeremiah goes forth toward the land of Benjamin to separate himself among the people. At the gate of Benjamin a captain of the ward named Irijah seizes him, charging that he is falling away to the Chaldeans; Jeremiah answers that it is false, but Irijah will not hear him. Irijah brings Jeremiah to the princes, who are wroth with him, smite him, and put him in prison in the house of Jonathan the scribe.

After Jeremiah has remained many days in the dungeon and its cells, Zedekiah secretly sends for him and asks if there is any word from the Most High; Jeremiah answers there is, that the king shall be delivered into the hand of the king of Babylon. Jeremiah asks what he has offended against the king, his servants, or the people that they have put him in prison, and where now are the prophets who prophesied that the king of Babylon would not come. He pleads not to be sent back to the house of Jonathan the scribe lest he die there; Zedekiah commands he be kept in the court of the prison and given a daily piece of bread out of the bakers' street until all the bread in the city is spent.

Shephatiah, Gedaliah, Jucal, and Pashur hear Jeremiah telling the people that whoever remains in the city shall die by sword, famine, and pestilence, but whoever goes forth to the Chaldeans shall live and have his life for a prey. The princes tell the king that Jeremiah must be put to death because he weakens the hands of the men of war and seeks not the welfare of the people but their hurt; the king answers that he is in their hand and the king can do nothing against them. They cast Jeremiah into the dungeon of Malchiah in the court of the prison, letting him down with cords into a place with no water but mire, and Jeremiah sinks in the mire.

Abedmelech the Ethiopian, one of the eunuchs in the king's house, hears that Jeremiah has been put in the dungeon while the king sits in the gate of Benjamin. Abedmelech goes to the king and says these men have done evil in all they have done to Jeremiah, who is likely to die of hunger where he is, for there is no more bread in the city; the king commands him to take thirty men and lift the prophet out before he dies. Abedmelech takes old cast clouts and rotten rags, lets them down by cords, and tells Jeremiah to put them under his armholes under the cords; they draw him up out of the dungeon, and Jeremiah remains in the court of the prison.

Zedekiah sends for Jeremiah into the third entry of the house of the Most High and asks him to hide nothing; Jeremiah answers that if he declares it the king will surely put him to death, and if he counsels him the king will not hearken. The king swears secretly that as the Most High liveth he will not put him to death nor give him into the hand of those who seek his life. Jeremiah tells him that if he goes forth to the king of Babylon's princes his soul shall live and the city shall not be burned, but if he will not go forth the city shall be given to the Chaldeans and burned; the king says he is afraid of the Jews already fallen to the Chaldeans, and Jeremiah urges him to obey the voice of the Most High that it may be well with him.

If the king refuses to go forth, Jeremiah shows him that all the women left in the king's house shall be brought out to the king of Babylon's princes, saying his friends have prevailed against him and his feet are sunk in the mire and turned away back. All his wives and children shall be brought to the Chaldeans, and he shall not escape but be taken by the hand of the king of Babylon and cause the city to be burned with fire. Zedekiah charges Jeremiah to let no man know their words, and to tell the princes only that he presented his supplication not to be returned to Jonathan's house; the princes come and ask, Jeremiah answers as the king commanded, and he abides in the court of the prison until the day Jerusalem is taken.

Zedekiah was twenty-one years old when he began to reign and reigned eleven years in Jerusalem, and his mother was Hamutal the daughter of Jeremiah of Libnah. Zedekiah was not of the royal lineage per se, and Zedekiah was not really his name; to see how he became king we go back to when Babylon took the real king away. -

He did that which was evil in the eyes of the Most High as Jehoiakim had done, and through the anger of the Most High against Jerusalem and Judah, Zedekiah rebelled against the king of Babylon. The Most High had told through Jeremiah that the people would have to serve Babylon seventy years, but Zedekiah decided to rebel against it instead of submitting to the prophecy. -

In the ninth year of his reign Nebuchadnezzar and all his army came against Jerusalem, pitched against it, and built forts round about, and the city was besieged until the eleventh year of Zedekiah. By the fourth month the famine was so sore in the city that there was no bread for the people of the land. This should sound familiar; the same siege and famine came on us again under the Romans in 70 A.D. These are generational curses that fall on multiple generations when we break the Most High's commandments. -

When the city was broken up the men of war fled by night by the gate between the two walls, but the army of the Chaldeans pursued the king and overtook Zedekiah in the plains of Jericho, his army scattered from him. They brought Zedekiah to the king of Babylon at Riblah, where he gave judgment upon him, and the king of Babylon slew Zedekiah's sons before his eyes and slew all the princes of Judah. Then they put out Zedekiah's eyes, so the last thing he would ever see was his sons put to death in his face, and they bound him in chains, carried him to Babylon, and kept him in prison till the day of his death; the Most High allowed these heathen to bring hell into Jerusalem. -

In the fifth month Nebuzaradan the captain of the guard came to Jerusalem and burned the house of the Most High, the king's house, and all the houses of the great men with fire. The Chaldeans birthed this destruction, but Edom, the so-called white man, took part in it; Esau loves burning things, which is ironic since he is destined to burn forever, wasted away by the same fire he loved to waste these nations with. Edom were Babylon's personal cheerleaders, calling for Jerusalem and the temple to be razed to the foundation; the daughter of Babylon that Edom cheered on became the mother of harlots, Babylon the great, which is to be destroyed. -

Nebuzaradan carried away captive certain of the poor of the people, the residue in the city, and those that had fallen to the king of Babylon, but left certain of the poor of the land to be vinedressers and husbandmen. The Chaldeans broke the pillars of brass, the bases, and the brazen sea in the house of the Most High and carried all the brass to Babylon, along with the caldrons, shovels, snuffers, bowls, spoons, and every vessel of brass, gold, and silver. This was a billion dollar heist of the temple's gold, brass, and silver, and it too was prophecy; it fulfilled what was foretold to Hezekiah when he foolishly showed Babylon all his treasures. -

The captain of the guard took Seraiah the chief priest, Zephaniah the second priest, the three keepers of the door, the eunuch over the men of war, seven of the king's counselors, the principal scribe, and threescore men of the people found in the city. He brought them to the king of Babylon at Riblah, where the king smote them and put them to death, and thus Judah was carried away captive out of his own land. Babylon made sure to put our mighty men to death, the same tactic the oppressor always used in slavery and segregation, killing the mightiest men to destroy the people's hope so they would no longer rise up against the enemy. -

These are the numbers Nebuchadnezzar carried away captive: in the seventh year 3,023 Jews, in the eighteenth year 832 persons from Jerusalem, and in the twenty-third year Nebuzaradan carried away 745 persons, four thousand and six hundred in all.

In the thirty-seventh year of the captivity of Jehoiachin king of Judah, Evilmerodach king of Babylon in the first year of his reign lifted up his head, brought him out of prison, and spake kindly to him. He set Jehoiachin's throne above the thrones of the other kings in Babylon, changed his prison garments, and gave him a continual daily allowance of food all the days of his life. Jehoiachin was the real king carried captive earlier in Second Kings 24, and after his long imprisonment he found favor; his lineage became the line through which Christ came. --- Topics: [Esau and Edom](/encyclopedia/esau-and-edom) · [Idolatry](/encyclopedia/idolatry) · [The Priesthood](/encyclopedia/the-priesthood)

The word of the Most High came to Ezekiel to put forth a riddle and speak a parable unto the house of Israel. A great eagle with great wings and divers colors came unto Lebanon, took the highest branch of the cedar, cropped off the top of his young twigs, and carried it into a land of traffic and a city of merchants. He took also of the seed of the land, planted it in a fruitful field by great waters, and it grew into a spreading vine of low stature whose branches turned toward him.

There was another great eagle with great wings and many feathers, and this vine bent her roots and shot forth her branches toward him that he might water it, though it was already planted in good soil by great waters. The Most High asks whether it shall prosper; He shall pull up the roots and cut off the fruit that it wither, and when the east wind touches it, it shall utterly wither in the furrows where it grew.

The Most High tells the rebellious house what these things mean: the king of Babylon came to Jerusalem, took the king and princes to Babylon, took of the king's seed, made a covenant and took an oath of him, and also took the mighty of the land. The enemy takes the mighty of the land, the best and brightest, and turns them against their people by giving them the mind of the oppressor, so the kingdom might be base and not lift itself up. When our people do well financially, get a good education, and buy into the pick-yourself-up-by-the-bootstraps idea that everyone has the same opportunity, the smart ones are removed from the ghetto so they will not be there to cause the uprising. -

The king rebelled against Babylon and sent ambassadors into Egypt for horses and much people; the Most High asks shall he prosper, shall he escape, or shall he break the covenant and be delivered. Because he despised the oath and broke the covenant after giving his hand, he shall die in the midst of Babylon, and Pharaoh with his mighty army shall not help him in the war. The Most High will spread His net upon him, take him in His snare, bring him to Babylon, and plead with him there; his fugitives shall fall by the sword and the remnant be scattered, and they shall know that He is the Lord.

The Most High will Himself take of the highest branch of the high cedar, crop off a tender twig, and plant it upon the high mountain in the height of Israel. It shall bring forth boughs, bear fruit, and be a goodly cedar under which all fowl of every wing shall dwell, and all the trees of the field shall know that He has brought down the high tree and exalted the low tree. If the Most High has declared it, it shall come to pass, for the scripture cannot be broken. -

The word of the Most High comes to Ezekiel to set his face toward Jerusalem, drop his word toward the holy places, and prophesy against the land of Israel. The Most High is against her and will draw forth His sword out of his sheath to cut off the righteous and the wicked, the sword being the nations He sends. He judges us as a nation, so the righteous and the wicked all get judged together; the sword goes forth against all flesh from the south to the north and shall not return.

Ezekiel is told to sigh with the breaking of his loins and with bitterness before their eyes. When they ask why he sighs he is to answer that it is for the tidings that come, because every heart shall melt, all hands be feeble, every spirit faint, and all knees be weak as water.

A sword is sharpened and furbished, meaning polished, sharpened to make a sore slaughter and furbished that it may glitter. It contemneth the rod of His son, and Judah is that rod; the sword is given to be furbished into the hand of the slayer. Ezekiel is to cry and howl, for the sword shall be upon His people and upon all the princes of Israel; it is a trial, a sword that has already been tested by other nations that the Lord uses.

Ezekiel is to smite his hands together and let the sword be doubled the third time, the sword of the slain that enters even into their private chambers so there is no escape. The point of the sword is set against all their gates, and that point is Babylon pointing at all the gates of Jerusalem. The sword goes one way or the other, to the right hand or the left, whichever way it turns to seek judgment and destruction upon Jerusalem, and the Most High's fury shall rest there.

The word of the Most High comes again to appoint two ways for the sword of the king of Babylon to come, both out of one land. One way points to Rabbath of the Ammonites and the other to Judah in fenced Jerusalem, and the king of Babylon stands at the parting of the ways to use divination, which is witchcraft. He makes his arrows bright, consults with images, and looks in the liver, and at his right hand the divination points for Jerusalem to appoint captains and set battering rams against the gates.

Because their iniquity is remembered and their transgressions discovered so that their sins appear, they shall be taken with the hand. To the profane wicked prince of Israel whose day is come, He says remove the diadem and take off the crown, exalt him that is low and abase him that is high. He will overturn, overturn, overturn it, and it shall be no more until he come whose right it is, and He will give it to him.

Concerning the Ammonites and their reproach, the sword is drawn and furbished to consume because of the glittering. While the diviners see vanity and divine a lie, the sword will bring them upon the necks of the slain whose day is come. He will judge them in the place where they were created, in the land of their nativity, pour out His indignation, blow against them in the fire of His wrath, and deliver them into the hand of brutish men skilful to destroy; they shall be for fuel to the fire and be no more remembered.

name: The captivity of Judah
charge: Polluting the house of the Lord; mocking the messengers of God; refusing the Sabbath and the land's sabbaths
summary: All the chief of the priests and the people transgressed very much after all the abominations of the heathen and polluted the house of the Lord. The Lord sent messengers because he had compassion; they mocked them, despised his words, and misused his prophets until there was no remedy.
offense: Judah's fall followed persistent transgression among rulers, priests, prophets, and people. They polluted the Lord's house, shed blood, practiced oppression, and failed to distinguish the holy from the profane. False prophets strengthened the corruption by speaking visions God had not given. The Lord sent His messengers repeatedly because He had compassion on His people and His dwelling place. They mocked the messengers, despised His words, and misused His prophets until there was no remedy. The sentence did not come without warning or opportunity to turn.
judgment: The Chaldeans killed within the sanctuary, carried away its treasures, burned the house of God, and broke down Jerusalem's wall. Those who escaped the sword were carried to Babylon and served there until the Persian kingdom. The land lay desolate and enjoyed its sabbaths, fulfilling the word of the Lord by Jeremiah concerning seventy years. The captivity was not the end of God's word to Israel. In the first year of Cyrus, the Lord stirred the king to proclaim the rebuilding of His house at Jerusalem. The same account that records Judah's removal closes with an opening for return, showing that judgment did not annul God's faithfulness.

verses.text: 14Moreover all the chief of the priests, and the people, transgressed very much after all the abominations of the heathen; and polluted the house of the Lord which he had hallowed in Jerusalem. 15And the Lord God of their fathers sent to them by his messengers, rising up betimes, and sending; because he had compassion on his people, and on his dwelling place: 16But they mocked the messengers of God, and despised his words, and misused his prophets, until the wrath of the Lord arose against his people, till there was no remedy. 17Therefore he brought upon them the king of the Chaldees, who slew their young men with the sword in the house of their sanctuary, and had no compassion upon young man or maiden, old man, or him that stooped for age: he gave them all into his hand. 18And all the vessels of the house of God, great and small, and the treasures of the house of the Lord, and the treasures of the king, and of his princes; all these he brought to Babylon. 19And they burnt the house of God, and brake down the wall of Jerusalem, and burnt all the palaces thereof with fire, and destroyed all the goodly vessels thereof. 20And them that had escaped from the sword carried he away to Babylon; where they were servants to him and his sons until the reign of the kingdom of Persia: 21To fulfil the word of the Lord by the mouth of Jeremiah, until the land had enjoyed her sabbaths: for as long as she lay desolate she kept sabbath, to fulfil threescore and ten years.

4And the Lord hath sent unto you all his servants the prophets, rising early and sending them; but ye have not hearkened, nor inclined your ear to hear. 5They said, Turn ye again now every one from his evil way, and from the evil of your doings, and dwell in the land that the Lord hath given unto you and to your fathers for ever and ever: 6And go not after other gods to serve them, and to worship them, and provoke me not to anger with the works of your hands; and I will do you no hurt. 7Yet ye have not hearkened unto me, saith the Lord; that ye might provoke me to anger with the works of your hands to your own hurt. 8Therefore thus saith the Lord of hosts; Because ye have not heard my words, 9Behold, I will send and take all the families of the north, saith the Lord, and Nebuchadrezzar the king of

entries.commentary: The people of the land take Jehoahaz the son of Josiah and make him king in Jerusalem; he is twenty three years old and reigns three months. The king of Egypt puts him down, condemns the land in a hundred talents of silver and a talent of gold, and makes Eliakim his brother king, turning his name to Jehoiakim, and carries Jehoahaz to Egypt.

Jehoiakim is twenty five years old when he begins to reign and reigns eleven years in Jerusalem, doing evil in the sight of the Lord his God, so Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon comes up against him and binds him in fetters to carry him to Babylon. Nebuchadnezzar also carries off the vessels of the house of the Lord to Babylon and puts them in his temple. The Most High set a wicked king over the land because his own people would not do what he said. The power of the earth is in the hand of the Most High, and in due time he sets over it one that is profitable. When Israel will not rule in righteousness, he raises a Nebuchadnezzar; Israel's purpose was never to be wicked and rule at the same time. -

Jehoiachin is eight years old when he begins to reign and reigns three months and ten days in Jerusalem, and he does that which is evil in the sight of the Lord. When the year is expired, Nebuchadnezzar sends and brings him to Babylon with the goodly vessels of the house of the Lord, and makes Zedekiah his brother king over Judah.

Zedekiah is twenty one years old when he begins to reign and reigns eleven years, and he does evil in the sight of the Lord his God and humbles not himself before Jeremiah the prophet speaking from the mouth of the Lord. He rebels against Nebuchadnezzar who had made him swear by God, and stiffens his neck and hardens his heart from turning to the Lord God of Israel. The chief priests and people transgress very much after all the abominations of the heathen and pollute the house of the Lord. The Most High sends to them by his messengers, rising up early and sending because he had compassion, but they mock the messengers, despise his words, and misuse his prophets until the wrath of the Lord arises and there is no remedy. -

The Most High brings upon them the king of the Chaldees, who slays their young men with the sword in the house of their sanctuary and has no compassion upon young man or maiden, old man or him that stooped for age. He gives them all into Nebuchadnezzar's hand, and all the vessels of the house of God, great and small, and the treasures of the house of the Lord and of the king and his princes are brought to Babylon. They burn the house of God, break down the walls of Jerusalem, burn its palaces, and destroy all the goodly vessels, exactly the fierce nation the curses warned of. -

Those who escape the sword are carried away to Babylon, where they are servants to Nebuchadnezzar and his sons until the reign of the kingdom of Persia. This fulfills the word of the Lord by the mouth of Jeremiah, that the land would enjoy her sabbaths and lie desolate to fulfill threescore and ten years.

In the first year of Cyrus king of Persia, that the word of the Lord by Jeremiah might be accomplished, the Most High stirs up the spirit of Cyrus to make a proclamation throughout all his kingdom. Cyrus declares that the Lord God of heaven has given him all the kingdoms of the earth and charged him to build him a house in Jerusalem, and calls any of the Lord's people to go up, showing again that the Most High sets over the earth one that is profitable for his purpose. --- Topics: [Clean and Unclean Meats](/encyclopedia/clean-and-unclean-meats) · [Idolatry](/encyclopedia/idolatry) · [Sacrifice and Atonement](/encyclopedia/sacrifice-and-atonement) · [The Covenant](/encyclopedia/the-covenant) · [The Feasts of the Most High](/encyclopedia/the-feasts-of-the-most-high) · [The Priesthood](/encyclopedia/the-priesthood) · [The Sabbath](/encyclopedia/the-sabbath)

The word came to Jeremiah in the fourth year of Jehoiakim, the first year of Nebuchadnezzar, recounting that for twenty-three years, from the thirteenth year of Josiah, the Most High had risen early and spoken but the people would not hearken. He sent all His servants the prophets to call every man to turn from his evil way and not go after other gods, promising He would do them no hurt, yet they provoked Him to anger with the works of their own hands.

Because they would not hear, the Most High will send and take all the families of the north and Nebuchadnezzar the king of Babylon, His servant, against this land to utterly destroy it and make it a perpetual desolation, an astonishment, and a hissing. He takes from them the voice of mirth and gladness, the voice of the bridegroom and the bride, the sound of the millstones, and the light of the candle; this is the prophecy that these nations shall serve the king of Babylon seventy years.

When the seventy years are accomplished, the Most High will punish the king of Babylon and that nation for their iniquity and make the land of the Chaldeans a perpetual desolation. Even though He may take us down with one kingdom, He then takes that kingdom and punishes it with a new kingdom; the Most High uses people, He used Nebuchadnezzar, He used Cyrus, some of it for our good and some for our punishment. Many nations and great kings shall serve themselves of them, and He will recompense them according to their deeds and the works of their own hands.

The Most High gives Jeremiah the wine cup of His fury to make all the nations drink, beginning with Jerusalem and the cities of Judah, so they become a desolation, an astonishment, a hissing, and a curse. The cup passes to Egypt, the mingled people, Uz, the Philistines, Edom, Moab, Ammon, Tyrus, Zidon, Dedan, Tema, Buz, Arabia, Zimri, Elam, the Medes, all the kingdoms of the world, and last the king of Sheshach. They shall drink, be drunken, spew, fall, and rise no more; the Most High is bringing evil first on the city called by His name, and none of the inhabitants of the earth shall go unpunished. Just as we went into captivity, were placed under the neck of our enemies, and had all manner of wickedness done to us, they will not escape; we will repent and be back on top, and everything we went through, they will go through.

The Most High will roar from on high against all the inhabitants of the earth, for He has a controversy with the nations and will plead with all flesh and give the wicked to the sword. Evil shall go forth from nation to nation, a great whirlwind is raised up, and the slain of the Most High shall lie from one end of the earth to the other, unlamented and unburied. The shepherds and the principal of the flock are told to howl and wallow in ashes, for the days of their slaughter are accomplished; all the wickedness the nations did to us comes back on them, and they drink of the Most High's fury exactly as we did.

The word of the Most High comes to Ezekiel to judge the bloody city, Jerusalem, and show her all her abominations. She has shed blood in her midst and made idols against herself to defile herself, causing her days to draw near. Because of her idolatry and wickedness, once judgment comes He makes her a reproach unto the heathen and a mocking to all countries, both near and far.

The princes of Israel used their power to shed blood, set light by father and mother, dealt by oppression with the stranger, and vexed the fatherless and the widow. They despised His holy things, profaned His sabbaths, carried tales to shed blood, ate upon the mountains, and committed lewdness in her midst. They broke all manner of the immoral laws of [Leviticus 18](/bible/leviticus/18), committing abomination with a neighbor's wife, defiling a daughter-in-law, and humbling a sister, doing the doings of the other nations. They took gifts to shed blood, being put on the take and paid off to shed a man's blood, took usury and increase, and greedily gained by extortion, and have forgotten Him; these are wicked leaders.

The Most High smites His hand at their dishonest gain and at the blood shed in their midst, asking whether their heart can endure or their hands be strong in the day He deals with them. He will scatter them among the heathen, disperse them in the countries, and consume their filthiness out of them, and they shall know that He is the Lord when they take their inheritance in the sight of the heathen.

The house of Israel is become dross to Him, all brass, tin, iron, and lead, the dross of silver in the midst of the furnace. He will gather them into the midst of Jerusalem as men gather metal into the furnace, and blow the fire of His wrath upon them. They shall be melted in the midst of the furnace as silver is melted, and shall know that He is the Lord who poured out His fury upon them.

The land is not cleansed nor rained upon, and there is a conspiracy of her prophets in her midst, like a roaring lion ravening the prey, devouring souls and making many widows; the leaders of Israel are very corrupt. Her priests violated His law and profaned His holy things, putting no difference between the holy and the profane or the clean and the unclean and hiding their eyes from His sabbaths, just like today where our people put no difference between anything, and it is called Christianity. Her princes are like wolves ravening the prey to shed blood and destroy souls for dishonest gain, and her prophets daub them with untempered mortar, seeing vanity and divining lies, saying thus saith the Lord God when He has not spoken. The people used oppression, exercised robbery, and vexed the poor and needy and the stranger wrongfully, showing the same oppression, robbery, and extortion by the leadership. He sought for a man to make up the hedge and stand in the gap before Him so He would not destroy the land, but He found none, so He poured out His indignation and consumed them with the fire of His wrath. -

The children of Israel are to make no idols nor graven images, rear up no standing image, and set up no image of stone in the land to bow down to it. That covers the images bowed to today: the cobblestone of Islam, the cross, and the relics and Egyptian heads that egyptologists worship. The Israelites are not to do that.

Keep the sabbaths of the Most High and reverence His sanctuary. When you came into the sanctuary you had better come with respect, because the Most High was putting men to death over it. Nadab and Abihu, the sons of Aaron, offered strange fire before the Lord which He commanded them not, and fire went out from the Lord and devoured them; that is what reverencing the sanctuary means.

These are the blessings for walking in the statutes and keeping the commandments, the same blessings and curses read in Deuteronomy the 28th chapter. If Israel kept the commandments there would be no famine: rain in due season, the crops continually growing, the harvest coming in on time, and rain in the land even in a drought.

The threshing is the corn and the vintage is the grapes for the wine. The threshing reaching to the vintage and the vintage to the sowing time means one season's plenty would carry into the next. Israel would never be without wine, without crops, without food; each harvest would reach to the next season, and the bread would be eaten to the full in safety.

The Most High would give peace in the land: no enemies able to come against Israel, no war in the land, no one making the people afraid. That was fulfilled in the days of king Solomon, when there was rest on every side. That is also how you know the people in the land of Israel today are not the real Jews: this prophecy of rest is not fulfilled on them. When the Most High saves Israel from captivity it will be the same again, and none shall make him afraid.

Israel would chase their enemies, and the enemies would fall before them by the sword; the nations feared Israel when the nation kept this covenant, as the book of Joshua shows. Five would chase an hundred, and an hundred put ten thousand to flight: that is how much power the Most High was going to bestow on His people, having respect unto them, making them fruitful, and establishing His covenant with them and their children.

Eating the old store and bringing forth the old because of the new means the storehouses would be so full that the old crop would have to be carried out to make room for the new; that is how plenteous the land would be. The Most High would set His tabernacle among the people, walk among them, and be their God; He brought them out of Egypt so they should not be bondmen, and broke the bands of their yoke.

This is the flip side. If Israel would not hearken but despised the statutes and broke the covenant, the Most High would walk contrary to the people, standing in exact opposition so that nothing would prosper. Terror is the terrorism lived under every single day: terrorized by wicked corrupt officers, by our own brothers and sisters, by the nations. Consumption is being consumed in the land, with diseases, oppression, financial mishaps, and the prison system; the burning ague goes into disease, harm to the eyes, and sorrow of heart in the mind. Sowing seed in vain: vineyards planted that the enemies eat, and children sown in vain, born only to be killed, incarcerated, or raised up under the curse.

The Most High set His face against Israel, and the people are slain before their enemies; you see that every single day. They that hate you shall reign over you: that is the clear explanation of why no laws will be passed to deliver this people and why there will be no reparations. No political party, Democratic or Republican, will be beneficial, because the curse stands and they that hate us now reign over us; and we flee when none pursueth.

Seven times more punishment for the sins, and the pride of Israel's power broken: the very power promised in the blessings, when enemies would flee, was taken away. That is the explanation of how the slave masters could bring Israel into slavery: they are not bigger or stronger nations, but it was divine intervention; the Most High broke our power and took our strength so the enemies could prevail. We outnumbered them many times in the cotton fields, yet could do nothing. The heaven as iron and the earth as brass also goes into the shackles on the neck and on the feet; and the strength is spent in vain, for the land yields no increase.

Walking contrary still brings seven times more plagues according to the sins. Wild beasts sent among the people to rob them of their children, destroy their cattle, and make them few in number: wolves, coyotes, bears, whatever the Most High would allow to come upon the people for their wickedness. That is real evil brought for real rebellion. It also goes into the pestilences and diseases loosed among the people in these last days, as [Revelation 6](/bible/revelation/6) bears out with death by sword, hunger, and the beasts of the earth.

If the people would not be reformed by these things, the Most High would punish yet seven times more and bring a sword to avenge the quarrel of His covenant; gathered into their cities, the pestilence would be sent among them and they would be delivered into the hand of the enemy. Breaking the staff of bread, with ten women baking bread in one oven and delivering bread again by weight, is straight poverty: a lack of resources and food. Many of us grew up literally knocking on the neighbor's door to borrow sugar, borrow the iron, borrow bread, use the grill at such and such house because our appliances did not work; that is this verse, the same thing to this day, eating and not being satisfied.

The Most High said He would walk contrary in fury, and He would be the one doing it: He would use the enemies, but it would be Him behind it. That is heavy. Eating the flesh of sons and daughters goes into 70 AD, and it also happened in the days of the kings when the city was besieged and there was such famine that a woman's son was boiled and eaten.

The high places destroyed, the images cut down, and the carcasses of the people cast upon the carcasses of their idols: our people dying in the christian church with a cross around the neck, our people dying up against the cobblestone, still worshipping while they die. Even the high places themselves fall in judgment, as when a storm brought a church down on the congregation in Africa during a so-called easter program; that is what this verse reads about.

The Most High made the cities waste and brought the sanctuaries to desolation, and would not smell the savour of the sweet odours: He was not accepting the sacrifices, and He used the enemy to destroy the sanctuary. The Babylonians destroyed the temple, then the Greeks, then the Romans. When Babylon came against Jerusalem, Esau stood on the side cheering it on to the foundation, as [Psalms 137](/bible/psalms/137) records. Scattered among the heathen with a sword drawn out after them: not only the scattering, but death and anguish sent among the people in the lands of the captivity.

Then shall the land enjoy her sabbaths as long as it lieth desolate. The land was to rest every seventh year, and the sabbaths were not kept: no cooking or tilling on the sabbath, the land resting every seven years, none of it. The Most High said the land could not rest while the people dwelt on it doing evil, so He rid the people out of the land so that the land could enjoy her sabbaths while it lay desolate without them.

Upon them that are left alive a faintness is sent into their hearts in the lands of their enemies, so that the sound of a shaken leaf chases them; the same trembling heart, failing of eyes, and sorrow of mind that [Deuteronomy 28](/bible/deuteronomy/28) describes for the land of the enemies. Falling one upon another as it were before a sword when none pursueth: even at these protests, when the rubber bullets, the tear gas, the water hoses, and the dogs come out, the people stumble and fall over one another trying to get away. Still to this day the same thing. And ye shall perish among the heathen: many of us die in this land and in all the lands where we are scattered, and the land of the enemies eats the people up in oppression.

They that are left pine away in their iniquity in the enemies' land, and in the iniquities of their fathers. You see people just decay in their sickness: the Most High may not judge a man right away but gives him space to repent, yet he keeps eating the defiled food, smoking his weed, doping, in and out of jail, and slowly pines away. It is a miserable life to live; we have to get right with the Most High.

Confessing the iniquity of the fathers and their own trespass, with the uncircumcised heart humbled, is exactly what is being done right now: repenting, confessing the sins, remembering that the sins of the forefathers are ours, and turning the uncircumcised mind back to the Father. Accepting the punishment of the iniquity means going through the trials without fighting the sentence: not marching for reparations or so-called equality, but accepting the punishment for the iniquities committed against the Most High.

When the people repent and turn back, the Most High remembers His covenant with Jacob, with Isaac, and with Abraham, the covenant passed down to their children, the children of Israel; and He remembers the land. The land enjoys her sabbaths while she lieth desolate without them, and the people must accept that they were evil and wicked against the Most High, because they despised His judgments and their soul abhorred His statutes.

Yet for all that, in the land of their enemies the Most High will not cast the people away, neither abhor them to destroy them utterly and break His covenant. He sent Israel into captivity not for all to die, but to be afflicted until they finally turn back to the Lord God of Israel. So when you hear people say the Israelites are done away, that is a lie: the Most High promised He would not destroy the seed of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, but would give them a chance to repent and would remember the covenant of their ancestors whom He brought out of Egypt in the sight of the heathen. It also carries into the future tense.

These are the statutes and judgments and laws which the Most High made between Him and the children of Israel in mount Sinai by the hand of Moses. The quick recap of the chapter: these are the blessings and the curses that come upon the children of Israel for obedience or disobedience, and the chapter runs parallel with Deuteronomy the 28th chapter.

In the first year of Darius the son of Ahasuerus, of the seed of the Medes, made king over the realm of the Chaldeans, Daniel understood by the books the seventy years of the desolations of Jerusalem spoken to Jeremiah. This is the same Darius dealt with when the Persians and Medes were shown in chapters 7 and 8.

Daniel set his face unto the Most High to seek him by prayer and supplications, with fasting, sackcloth, and ashes, confessing that the people had sinned, committed iniquity, done wickedly, and rebelled, departing from his precepts and judgments. They had not hearkened unto the prophets who spake in his name to their kings, princes, fathers, and all the people of the land.

Righteousness belongs to the Most High, but confusion of faces to the people of Judah, the inhabitants of Jerusalem, and all Israel, near and far off, driven through all the countries because of their trespasses. Our people were scattered everywhere because of our transgressions, exactly as the law warned. -

All Israel transgressed the law by departing, so the curse was poured upon them and the oath written in the law of Moses, because they had sinned against him. The oath that was written is [Deuteronomy 28](/bible/deuteronomy/28), verses 1 through 68. -

Daniel appealed to the Most High who brought his people out of Egypt with a mighty hand, confessing they had sinned and done wickedly, and asking that his anger and fury be turned away from his city Jerusalem, his holy mountain. He pleaded for the Most High to hear, forgive, hearken, and do, not for their righteousness but for his great mercies, since the city and the people are called by his name.

While Daniel was speaking, praying, and confessing his sin and the sin of his people Israel, the man Gabriel, whom he had seen in the vision, was caused to fly swiftly and touched him about the time of the evening oblation. Gabriel came to give him skill and understanding, for at the beginning of his supplications the commandment came forth, and Daniel was greatly beloved.

Seventy weeks are determined upon the people and the holy city to finish the transgression, make an end of sins, make reconciliation for iniquity, bring in everlasting righteousness, seal up the vision, and anoint the most Holy. From the going forth of the commandment to restore and build Jerusalem unto Messiah the Prince shall be seven weeks and threescore and two weeks, the street built again even in troublous times. After threescore and two weeks Messiah is cut off, but not for himself, and the people of the prince that shall come destroy the city and the sanctuary. He confirms the covenant with many for one week, and in the midst of the week causes the sacrifice and oblation to cease. Daniel was given the four beasts first, then this further vision of the seventy weeks by Gabriel in the midst of his prayer and supplications. The bishop's class on the seventy weeks opens this up in full.

The city that was full of people now sits solitary as a widow; she that was great among the nations and a princess among the provinces has become tributary. Jerusalem that used to be jumping, the nation of the chosen people, is now a desolate, empty land. She weeps sore in the night with tears on her cheeks, and among all her lovers she has none to comfort her, for all her friends dealt treacherously and became her enemies. Israel's lovers and friends were other nations serving other gods, and when it got real they turned their backs, just as the Most High warned. -

Judah has gone into captivity because of affliction and great servitude; she dwells among the heathen and finds no rest, and all her persecutors overtook her between the straits. No servitude in history compares to ours; the scriptures say they had dominion over our bodies, which is beyond the Irish indentured servants and beyond the holocaust of the fake jews with the Germans. The ways of Zion mourn because none come to the solemn feasts, her adversaries are the chief and her enemies prosper, for the Most High afflicted her for the multitude of her transgressions, and her children are gone into captivity before the enemy. We went from a nation others looked up to and envied, called the perfection of beauty, to a people whose enemies are now the head and prosper, exactly as the curses of [Deuteronomy 28](/bible/deuteronomy/28) and [Leviticus 26](/bible/leviticus/26) foretold.

Jerusalem remembered in the days of her affliction all the pleasant things she had of old, when her people fell into the enemy's hand and none did help her, and the adversaries mocked at her sabbaths. Jerusalem grievously sinned, so she is removed; her filthiness is in her skirts, she remembered not her last end, and she has no comforter, for the heathen entered her sanctuary, whom the Most High commanded should not enter His congregation. All her people sigh and seek bread, and they gave their pleasant things for meat to relieve the soul; when things get that serious, people give up whatever they once thought they could not live without. -

She calls to all who pass by to see if there is any sorrow like her sorrow, which the Most High afflicted in the day of His fierce anger, sending fire into her bones and spreading a net for her feet. The yoke of her transgressions is bound by His hand upon her neck, and the Most High trod underfoot all her mighty men in the midst of her and called an assembly to crush her young men, the leaders taken out first. She weeps because the comforter that should relieve her soul is far from her; there was oppression but no comforter to relieve them. -

Zion spreads forth her hands and there is none to comfort her; the Most High commanded that Jacob's adversaries should be round about him, and Jerusalem is as a menstruous woman among them. The Most High is righteous, for Jerusalem rebelled against His commandment; it takes a spiritual mind to be in great distress and still confess that the Most High is right in His judgment, because we have committed fornication against Him. She called for her lovers but they deceived her, and her priests and elders gave up the ghost in the city while they sought meat to relieve their souls. **The Three Holy Children 3-5**  *3 Blessed art thou, O Lord God of our fathers: thy name is worthy to be praised and glorified for evermore: 4 For thou art righteous in all the things that thou hast done to us: yea, true are all thy works, thy ways are right, and all thy judgments truth. 5 In all the things that thou hast brought upon us, and upon the holy city of our fathers, even Jerusalem, thou hast executed true judgment, for according to truth and judgment didst thou bring all these things upon us because of our sins.*  The three holy children confessed the Most High was righteous in all He brought upon Jerusalem because of their sins.

She cries that she is in distress, her bowels troubled and her heart turned within her, for she grievously rebelled; abroad the sword bereaves and at home there is death. Her enemies heard of her trouble and are glad that the Most High has done it, and she prays that He would bring the day He has called, that they would be like her. Even in judgment our forefathers still prayed for the destruction of the enemy, asking the Most High to render to them all their wickedness and do to them as He had done to Jerusalem. -
