verses.text: 24Thus shalt thou also speak to Shemaiah the Nehelamite, saying, 25Thus speaketh the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel, saying, Because thou hast sent letters in thy name unto all the people that are at Jerusalem, and to Zephaniah the son of Maaseiah the priest, and to all the priests, saying, 26The Lord hath made thee priest in the stead of Jehoiada the priest, that ye should be officers in the house of the Lord, for every man that is mad, and maketh himself a prophet, that thou shouldest put him in prison, and in the stocks. 27Now therefore why hast thou not reproved Jeremiah of Anathoth, which maketh himself a prophet to you? 28For therefore he sent unto us in Babylon, saying, This captivity is long: build ye houses, and dwell in them; and plant gardens, and eat the fruit of them. 29And Zephaniah the priest read this letter in the ears of Jeremiah the prophet.

30Then came the word of the Lord unto Jeremiah, saying, 31Send to all them of the captivity, saying, Thus saith the Lord concerning Shemaiah the Nehelamite; Because that Shemaiah hath prophesied unto you, and I sent him not, and he caused you to trust in a lie: 32Therefore thus saith the Lord; Behold, I will punish Shemaiah the Nehelamite, and his seed: he shall not have a man to dwell among this people; neither shall he behold the good that I will do for my people, saith the Lord; because he hath taught rebellion against the Lord.

8For thus saith the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel; Let not your prophets and your diviners, that be in the midst of you, deceive you, neither hearken to your dreams which ye cause to be dreamed. 9For they prophesy falsely unto you in my name: I have not sent them, saith the Lord.

entries.commentary: Jeremiah sent a letter from Jerusalem to the residue of the elders, the priests, the prophets, and all the people whom Nebuchadnezzar had carried captive to Babylon, after Jeconiah, the queen, the eunuchs, the princes, the carpenters, and the smiths had departed. Just like in this captivity, our people still carried those talents and skills; we had carpenters and we had blacksmiths.

The Most High tells the captives that even in their captivity they should build houses and dwell in them, buy homes, plant gardens and eat the fruit of them. They are to take wives and beget sons and daughters, take wives for their sons and husbands for their daughters, that they may be increased and not diminished, and seek the peace of the city where He caused them to be carried away, for in the peace thereof they shall have peace. -

Let not the false prophets and diviners in the midst of the people deceive them, nor their dreams; today Christianity has so-called prophets and Islam has so-called prophecy, but they deceive people because that is not the right way to serve the right God. After seventy years are accomplished at Babylon the Most High will visit them and perform His good word to return them, for His thoughts toward them are of peace and not of evil, to give them an expected end; the same is happening today, knowledge is being increased, we are finding out who we are and coming back to God's laws to be saved out of this captivity. When they call upon Him, seek Him, and search for Him with all their heart, He will be found of them and turn away their captivity, gathering them from all the nations and places whither He drove them; this is why the leadership goes out and teaches in the four corners of the earth, because all our people have been driven to the four corners.

Because they said the Lord had raised them up prophets in Babylon, the Most High declares He will send the sword, the famine, and the pestilence upon them and make them like vile figs that cannot be eaten, and deliver them to be a curse, an astonishment, a hissing, and a reproach among all the nations. This is because they had not hearkened to His words, which He sent by His servants the prophets, rising up early; so it behooves us to follow God's laws, for the prophets today are the ones going out teaching on the corners every Sabbath and seven days a week. The Most High never comes down here Himself to speak to the people; He speaks through His servants the prophets. -

Concerning Ahab the son of Kolaiah and Zedekiah the son of Maaseiah, who prophesied a lie in His name, the Most High would deliver them into the hand of Nebuchadnezzar to be slain before the captives' eyes. They would become a curse, the Lord make thee like Zedekiah and like Ahab whom the king of Babylon roasted in the fire, because they committed villainy in Israel, committed adultery with their brothers' wives, and spoke lying words in His name. -

To Shemaiah the Nehelamite: because he sent letters in his own name to all the people at Jerusalem and to Zephaniah the priest, claiming the Lord had made Zephaniah priest in the stead of Jehoiada to put every man that makes himself a prophet in prison and the stocks, and asking why he had not reproved Jeremiah for telling the captives their captivity was long and to build houses. Zephaniah read the letter in the ears of Jeremiah, and the word of the Lord came to Jeremiah, for the Lord was dealing with Jeremiah, that was the difference. Because Shemaiah prophesied when the Lord sent him not and caused the people to trust in a lie, the Most High would punish him and his seed; he shall not have a man to dwell among the people nor behold the good the Lord will do, because he taught rebellion against the Lord.

Pashur the priest, chief governor in the house of the Most High, hears Jeremiah prophesy, smites him, and puts him in the stocks in the high gate of Benjamin. When he is let out the next day, Jeremiah tells him the Most High has renamed him Magor-missabib, a terror to himself and all his friends, for they shall fall by the sword of the king of Babylon. All Judah, all the strength and treasures of the city, and Pashur's whole household will be carried captive to Babylon, and Pashur will die there and be buried there with all the friends to whom he prophesied lies.

Jeremiah is going through it so bad, mocked and reproached daily, that he says he will not make mention of the Most High nor speak any more in His name. Just like us when we go out to camp, if somebody does not speak evil of us every time we do something big, there is a hater or somebody trying to demonize us. But the word was in his heart like a burning fire shut up in his bones; he was weary with holding it in and could not stay, he had to blast them, he could not hold it.

Jeremiah hears the defaming of many and his familiar friends watching for his stumbling, hoping to be enticed against him and take their revenge. The Most High is with him as a mighty terrible one, so his persecutors will stumble, not prevail, and be greatly ashamed in an everlasting confusion that will never be forgotten. He commits his cause to the Most High who tries the righteous and sees the reins and the heart, and sings praise because He delivers the soul of the poor from the hand of evildoers.

Crushed by the persecution, Jeremiah curses the day he was born and the man who brought his father the news of a man child, wishing that man to be like the cities the Most High overthrew. He asks why he came forth out of the womb only to see labor and sorrow and to have his days consumed with shame.

The prophet or dreamer of dreams who speaks to turn you away from the Lord your God was put to death under the kingdom. Today Israel is in the land of its oppressors and cannot exact that judgment, and no kind of violence is advocated; the deceived and the deceiver are his, and the judgment belongs to the Most High. What is done today: mark them which cause divisions and offences contrary to the doctrine which ye have learned, and avoid them. The doctrine learned is the law, for I give you good doctrine, forsake ye not my law. Going contrary to the laws of marriage, of the sabbath, of raising children righteously, or of going to thy brother alone when there is an ought between you, and secretly enticing others to follow, is how one turns people away from the Lord; those men and those women have to be put out from among the body.

If thy brother, thy son, thy daughter, the wife of thy bosom, or thy friend which is as thine own soul entice thee secretly to serve other gods: these are the people closest to you, the ones that can have influence on you. Thou shalt not consent, nor hearken, nor pity, nor spare, neither shalt thou conceal him, meaning hide him; when wickedness is concealed, the whole nation is put in jeopardy. Trust in a person is no cover for your soul: when someone you love and trust has the devil on them, they will lead you astray. Nobody can make you do anything, but they can influence you; do not give anyone that credit and let them cause you to lose your crown. This is why [Leviticus 5:1](/bible/leviticus/5#v1) is opened at the start of class: if you know of anything, you are supposed to utter it. Many grew up on snitches get stitches, but in repentance we have to understand that concealing sin is part of why Israel is in the condition it is in, and we have to teach righteousness. It is that simple.

If certain men, the children of Belial, withdraw the inhabitants of a city, saying, let us go and serve other gods: inquire, make search, and ask diligently, and if it be truth and the thing certain, that city was smitten with the edge of the sword, gathered into the midst of the street, and burnt with fire, an heap for ever, not to be built again. Achan is the example of this kind of judgment: Israel committed a trespass in the accursed thing, and one man's folly kindled the anger of the Lord against all Israel. Wars Israel had been winning without losing a man began to be lost, and Joshua had to search and seek out who had committed the crime in Israel. All Israel stoned Achan with stones and burned him with fire in the valley of Achor, and the Lord turned from the fierceness of his anger; righteous judgment lifted the wrath and the people were able to move forward.

name: Jonadab and the Rechabites
charge: Obeying the commandment of Jonadab their father for over two hundred years: no wine, no house, no vineyard, no field
summary: The Lord had Jeremiah set wine before a whole clan in a chamber of the temple. They refused it: their father Jonadab had commanded them to drink none, build no house and sow no seed, and they had kept it all their days. The Lord held them up against Judah, who would not obey him though he rose early and spoke, and promised Jonadab a man before him for ever.
offense: The Rechabites refused the wine Jeremiah set before them in a chamber of the Lord's house. Jonadab their father had commanded them not to drink wine, build houses, sow seed, or plant vineyards, but to dwell in tents. They had kept his charge through their generations. Their presence in Jerusalem was explained by their flight from the invading armies, not by a claim that their ancestral way had been abandoned. Their refusal supplied the contrast God intended. The descendants of Jonadab observed their father's command, while Judah would not hear the Lord despite His repeated sending of prophets. The lesson did not make wine forbidden to everyone; it exposed Judah's refusal to obey the God who had spoken to them.
judgment: Jeremiah announced that Jonadab the son of Rechab would not lack a man to stand before the Lord for ever, because his children had kept his commandment and done all he had charged them. At the same time, God declared the announced evil upon Judah and Jerusalem because He had spoken and they had not heard. The faithful household and the disobedient nation stood side by side, making clear that repeated access to God's word was no substitute for doing it.

entries.commentary: In the days of Jehoiakim the Most High sent Jeremiah to the house of the Rechabites to bring them into the temple chambers and set wine before them to drink. Jaazaniah and the whole house of the Rechabites refused, saying Jonadab the son of Rechab their father commanded them to drink no wine, build no house, sow no seed, and plant no vineyard, but dwell in tents all their days that they might live long in the land. They had obeyed the voice of Jonadab in all things, dwelling in tents, and only came to Jerusalem for fear of the army of the Chaldeans and the Syrians.

The Most High tells Jeremiah to point Judah to the Rechabites: the sons of Jonadab kept their father's command to drink no wine to this day, but this people would not hearken to Him though He rose early and spoke. He sent all His servants the prophets calling every man to return from his evil way, amend his doings, and go not after other gods, promising they would dwell in the land, yet they would not incline their ear. Because the Rechabites obeyed the commandment of their father, Jonadab shall not want a man to stand before Him for ever; but because Judah would not hear or answer, He will bring upon them all the evil He pronounced. --- Topics: [Idolatry](/encyclopedia/idolatry) · [Sacrifice and Atonement](/encyclopedia/sacrifice-and-atonement) · [The Covenant](/encyclopedia/the-covenant) · [The Feasts of the Most High](/encyclopedia/the-feasts-of-the-most-high) · [The Priesthood](/encyclopedia/the-priesthood)

Jehu writes to the rulers of Jezreel who kept Ahab's seventy sons, challenging them to set up a son and fight, but they are exceedingly afraid because two kings could not stand before him. They submit as his servants, and Jehu's second letter commands them to take the heads of Ahab's seventy sons and bring them to Jezreel by the next day. The heads are laid in two heaps at the gate, and Jehu slays all that remained of the house of Ahab, his great men, kinsfolk, and priests, until none remained, according to the word spoken by Elijah.

Jehu meets the brethren of Ahaziah going to salute the king's children and has all forty-two of them slain at the pit of the shearing house, guilty by association with the house of Ahab. He takes up Jehonadab the son of Rechab, whose heart is right with his, into the chariot to see his zeal for the Most High. At Samaria Jehu slays all that remained unto Ahab, destroying him according to the saying of the Most High spoken to Elijah.

Jehu gathers all the worshippers of Baal by pretending he will serve Baal much more than Ahab did, doing it in subtilty to destroy them. He fills the house of Baal, brings out vestments for every worshipper, and makes sure no servant of the Most High is among them, only Baal worshippers, as with the clergy garments and idolatry seen in false worship today. After the sacrifice he sends in the guard to slay them all, breaks down the images and the house of Baal, and makes it a draught house, so Jehu destroyed Baal out of Israel. -

Though Jehu destroys Baal out of Israel, he does not depart from the golden calves that Jeroboam set up in Bethel and in Dan; hold Dan in mind for later scriptures. The Most High commends Jehu for executing what is right against the house of Ahab and promises his children to the fourth generation shall sit on the throne of Israel. Yet Jehu takes no heed to walk in the law of the Most High with all his heart, showing that a man may do great things and still turn away and stay in sin. -

In those days the Most High begins to cut Israel short, and Hazael smites them in all the coasts from Jordan eastward through Gilead and Bashan. The rest of Jehu's acts are written in the book of the Chronicles of the kings of Israel, and he reigns twenty-eight years in Samaria before Jehoahaz his son reigns in his place. Jehu's life is a warning that the walk is a marathon, not a sprint, and the difference is whether a man gets back up and repents or stays down and departs from the law. --- Topics: [Esau and Edom](/encyclopedia/esau-and-edom) · [Idolatry](/encyclopedia/idolatry) · [Sacrifice and Atonement](/encyclopedia/sacrifice-and-atonement) · [The Priesthood](/encyclopedia/the-priesthood)

name: Baruch the scribe
charge: Writing the roll from the prophet's mouth and reading it in the house of the Lord, and writing it again after the king burned it
summary: He wrote all the words of the Lord from Jeremiah's mouth on a roll, and because the prophet was shut up, he read it in the house of the Lord on a fast day in the ears of all the people. The princes heard it and told him to hide with Jeremiah. Jehoiakim cut the roll with a penknife and burned it leaf by leaf. Baruch wrote it again from Jeremiah's mouth, and many like words were added. He sought great things for himself and was told not to, and given his life for a prey.
offense: Baruch wrote the words Jeremiah dictated and read the roll in the Lord's house when Jeremiah could not go there. He then read it before the princes. The work required more than copying: he publicly delivered a warning that placed both him and the prophet in danger. After Jehoiakim burned the roll, Baruch wrote again at Jeremiah's mouth, preserving all the former words and many like words added. The king's attack did not cause him to abandon the charge. Yet Baruch also knew weariness and grief, crying that the Lord had added sorrow to his pain and that he found no rest.
judgment: The Lord answered Baruch's distress by setting it within the judgment coming upon the land. What God had built He would break down, and what He had planted He would pluck up. Baruch was not to seek great things for himself amid that overthrow. God promised him his life for a prey in all places where he went. Preservation, rather than worldly advancement, was the particular mercy pledged to him. The faithful scribe was not promised freedom from the nation's troubles, but life through them.

judgmentFull: The Lord answered Baruch's distress by setting it within the judgment coming upon the land. What God had built He would break down, and what He had planted He would pluck up. Baruch was not to seek great things for himself amid that overthrow.

God promised him his life for a prey in all places where he went. Preservation, rather than worldly advancement, was the particular mercy pledged to him. The faithful scribe was not promised freedom from the nation's troubles, but life through them.

verses.text: 4Then Jeremiah called Baruch the son of Neriah: and Baruch wrote from the mouth of Jeremiah all the words of the Lord, which he had spoken unto him, upon a roll of a book. 5And Jeremiah commanded Baruch, saying, I am shut up; I cannot go into the house of the Lord: 6Therefore go thou, and read in the roll, which thou hast written from my mouth, the words of the Lord in the ears of the people in the Lord’s house upon the fasting day: and also thou shalt read them in the ears of all Judah that come out of their cities. 7It may be they will present their supplication before the Lord, and will return every one from his evil way: for great is the anger and the fury that the Lord hath pronounced against this people. 8And Baruch the son of Neriah did according to all that Jeremiah the prophet commanded him, reading in the book the words of the Lord in the Lord’s house.

entries.commentary: In the fourth year of Jehoiakim, the Most High tells Jeremiah to take a roll of a book and write in it all the words He has spoken against Israel, against Judah, and against all the nations, from the days of Josiah until that day. The purpose is that the house of Judah, hearing all the evil purposed against them, might return every man from his evil way so that He would forgive their iniquity and their sin.

Jeremiah calls Baruch the son of Neriah, who writes from Jeremiah's mouth all the words of the Most High upon the roll. Because Jeremiah is shut up and cannot go into the house of the Most High, he sends Baruch to read the roll in the ears of the people on the fasting day, that they might present their supplication and turn from their evil way, for great is the anger and fury pronounced against this people. Baruch does all that the prophet commanded, reading the book of the words of the Most High in the Most High's house.

In the fifth year of Jehoiakim, in the ninth month, a fast is proclaimed before the Most High to all the people in Jerusalem and those who came from the cities of Judah. Baruch reads the words of Jeremiah in the temple in the chamber of Gemariah, in the ears of all the people. Michaiah the son of Gemariah, having heard the words, goes down into the king's house to the scribe's chamber where all the princes are sitting, and declares to them all he had heard when Baruch read.

The princes send Jehudi to bring Baruch with the roll, and they ask him to sit and read it in their ears. When they hear all the words they are afraid, both one and another, and say they will surely tell the king; they ask Baruch how he wrote all these words, and he answers that Jeremiah pronounced them with his mouth while Baruch wrote them with ink in the book. The princes tell Baruch to go hide himself and Jeremiah, and to let no man know where they are.

The princes lay up the roll in the chamber of Elishama the scribe and tell all the words in the ears of the king, who sends Jehudi to fetch it and read it before him and the princes. The king sits in the winter house in the ninth month with a fire burning on the hearth; as Jehudi reads three or four leaves, the king cuts them with a penknife and casts them into the fire until the whole roll is consumed. Neither the king nor his servants are afraid nor rend their garments; though Elnathan, Delaiah, and Gemariah make intercession that he not burn the roll, he will not hear, and he commands that Baruch and Jeremiah be seized, but the Most High hides them.

After the king burns the roll, the word of the Most High comes to Jeremiah to take another roll and write all the former words that Jehoiakim had burned. Against Jehoiakim He pronounces that he shall have none to sit upon the throne of David, his dead body shall be cast out to the heat by day and the frost by night, and He will punish him, his seed, and his servants for their iniquity. Jeremiah gives a second roll to Baruch, who writes from Jeremiah's mouth all the words of the burned book, and many like words are added besides.

name: Ebed-melech the Ethiopian
charge: Going to the king for Jeremiah, and drawing him up out of the dungeon with old cast clouts and rotten rags
summary: The princes had put Jeremiah in a dungeon of mire to die. A eunuch of the king's house, an Ethiopian, went out to Zedekiah at the gate and told him the prophet was likely to die of hunger where he was. The king gave him thirty men and he drew Jeremiah up with rags under his armholes. Before the city fell the Lord sent him his own word: thy life for a prey, because thou hast put thy trust in me.
offense: Ebed-melech, the Ethiopian eunuch in the king's house, heard that Jeremiah had been lowered into the dungeon and was sinking in the mire. He went to the king and plainly called the princes' action evil, warning that the prophet would die where he had been cast. With the king's permission, he took men and ropes to draw Jeremiah out. He also gathered old cast clouts and rotten rags and instructed Jeremiah to place them under his arms beneath the cords. His intervention joined courage before authority with careful treatment of the man being rescued.
judgment: Go and speak to Ebed-melech the Ethiopian, saying, Thus saith the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel; Behold, I will bring my words upon this city for evil, and not for good; and they shall be accomplished in that day before thee. But I will deliver thee in that day, saith the Lord: and thou shalt not be given into the hand of the men of whom thou art afraid. For I will surely deliver thee, and thou shalt not fall by the sword, but thy life shall be for a prey unto thee: because thou hast put thy trust in me, saith the Lord.
offenseFull: Ebed-melech, the Ethiopian eunuch in the king's house, heard that Jeremiah had been lowered into the dungeon and was sinking in the mire. He went to the king and plainly called the princes' action evil, warning that the prophet would die where he had been cast.

With the king's permission, he took men and ropes to draw Jeremiah out. He also gathered old cast clouts and rotten rags and instructed Jeremiah to place them under his arms beneath the cords. His intervention joined courage before authority with careful treatment of the man being rescued.
judgmentFull: While Jeremiah remained in the court of the prison, the Lord sent him a promise for Ebed-melech. The announced evil would come upon Jerusalem, but Ebed-melech would not be delivered into the hands of the men he feared. God would deliver him, and his life would be for a prey because he had put his trust in the Lord.
The approaching fall of the city did not prevent God from distinguishing the man who trusted Him. Ebed-melech's place in the royal household did not keep him silent when its princes acted wickedly.

verses.text: 4Therefore the princes said unto the king, We beseech thee, let this man be put to death: for thus he weakeneth the hands of the men of war that remain in this city, and the hands of all the people, in speaking such words unto them: for this man seeketh not the welfare of this people, but the hurt. 5Then Zedekiah the king said, Behold, he is in your hand: for the king is not he that can do any thing against you. 6Then took they Jeremiah, and cast him into the dungeon of Malchiah the son of Hammelech, that was in the court of the prison: and they let down Jeremiah with cords. And in the dungeon there was no water, but mire: so Jeremiah sunk in the mire.

entries.commentary: Shephatiah, Gedaliah, Jucal, and Pashur hear Jeremiah telling the people that whoever remains in the city shall die by sword, famine, and pestilence, but whoever goes forth to the Chaldeans shall live and have his life for a prey. The princes tell the king that Jeremiah must be put to death because he weakens the hands of the men of war and seeks not the welfare of the people but their hurt; the king answers that he is in their hand and the king can do nothing against them. They cast Jeremiah into the dungeon of Malchiah in the court of the prison, letting him down with cords into a place with no water but mire, and Jeremiah sinks in the mire.

Abedmelech the Ethiopian, one of the eunuchs in the king's house, hears that Jeremiah has been put in the dungeon while the king sits in the gate of Benjamin. Abedmelech goes to the king and says these men have done evil in all they have done to Jeremiah, who is likely to die of hunger where he is, for there is no more bread in the city; the king commands him to take thirty men and lift the prophet out before he dies. Abedmelech takes old cast clouts and rotten rags, lets them down by cords, and tells Jeremiah to put them under his armholes under the cords; they draw him up out of the dungeon, and Jeremiah remains in the court of the prison.

Zedekiah sends for Jeremiah into the third entry of the house of the Most High and asks him to hide nothing; Jeremiah answers that if he declares it the king will surely put him to death, and if he counsels him the king will not hearken. The king swears secretly that as the Most High liveth he will not put him to death nor give him into the hand of those who seek his life. Jeremiah tells him that if he goes forth to the king of Babylon's princes his soul shall live and the city shall not be burned, but if he will not go forth the city shall be given to the Chaldeans and burned; the king says he is afraid of the Jews already fallen to the Chaldeans, and Jeremiah urges him to obey the voice of the Most High that it may be well with him.

If the king refuses to go forth, Jeremiah shows him that all the women left in the king's house shall be brought out to the king of Babylon's princes, saying his friends have prevailed against him and his feet are sunk in the mire and turned away back. All his wives and children shall be brought to the Chaldeans, and he shall not escape but be taken by the hand of the king of Babylon and cause the city to be burned with fire. Zedekiah charges Jeremiah to let no man know their words, and to tell the princes only that he presented his supplication not to be returned to Jonathan's house; the princes come and ask, Jeremiah answers as the king commanded, and he abides in the court of the prison until the day Jerusalem is taken.

In the ninth year of Zedekiah, in the tenth month, Nebuchadnezzar and all his army come against Jerusalem and besiege it, and in the eleventh year, the fourth month, the ninth day, the city is broken up. The princes of the king of Babylon come in and sit in the middle gate; when Zedekiah and the men of war see them, they flee by night by the way of the king's garden through the gate between the two walls toward the plain. The Chaldean army pursues and overtakes Zedekiah in the plains of Jericho, and they bring him up to Nebuchadnezzar at Riblah, where the king of Babylon slays Zedekiah's sons and all the nobles of Judah before his eyes, then puts out Zedekiah's eyes, binds him with chains for Babylon, and burns the king's house and the houses of the people, breaking down the walls of Jerusalem.

Nebuzaradan the captain of the guard carries away captive to Babylon the remnant of the people that remained in the city, those who fell away to him, and the rest, but leaves the poor of the people who had nothing in the land of Judah and gives them vineyards and fields. Nebuchadnezzar gives charge concerning Jeremiah that he be taken, looked to well, and done no harm, but treated as he himself shall say. The princes of Babylon send and take Jeremiah out of the court of the prison and commit him to Gedaliah the son of Ahikam to carry him home, so he dwells among the people.

While Jeremiah is still shut up in the court of the prison, the word of the Most High comes to him for Abedmelech the Ethiopian, declaring that He will bring His words upon this city for evil and not for good, and they shall be accomplished in that day. But in that day He will deliver Abedmelech, who shall not be given into the hand of the men he is afraid of, and shall not fall by the sword, because he has put his trust in the Most High; the Most High deals with the Ethiopian because he was used to help Jeremiah, sent to take the prophet up out of the dungeon before he died. -

Be not envious against evil men, neither desire to be with them, for their heart studies destruction and their lips talk of mischief. Through wisdom a house is built, by understanding it is established, and by knowledge the chambers are filled with precious and pleasant riches.

A wise man is strong; a man of knowledge increases strength. By wise counsel you make your war, and in the multitude of counselors there is safety. Something other nations use that black people have not figured out yet starts with an "m": mentorship. People freestyle without a plan and it does not work out. Other nations have mentors who already accomplished what they are trying to do and get counsel, which is advice, on how to reach that level. Some black people are too prideful to ask for help. Wisdom is too high for a fool; he opens not his mouth in the gate.

He that devises to do evil will be called a mischievous person. The thought of foolishness is sin, and the scorner is an abomination to men. The thought of foolishness is sin. We have thoughts we cannot control that pop up, and we have to rebuke them and say that is the devil. All of us have some perverse thoughts, and you have to rebuke them. If you faint in the day of adversity your strength is small.

If you forbear to deliver them that are drawn to death and ready to be slain, and say you knew it not, does not he that ponders the heart consider it and render to every man according to his works? Eat honey because it is good, and the honeycomb which is sweet; so is the knowledge of wisdom to your soul. When you find it there is a reward and your expectation will not be cut off. Cherish knowledge, wisdom, and understanding. Always be in a position to learn and see the lessons in life. Often a regular situation holds a life lesson and you miss it because your antennas are not up.

Lay not wait against the dwelling of the righteous, for a just man falls seven times and rises up again, but the wicked fall into mischief. Certain brothers come into the truth and make mistakes, but each mistake they learn from and rise up again. He respects brothers who make mistakes and get back in the fight, unlike those too embarrassed to admit they were wrong who run like a little girl. Rejoice not when your enemy falls, and let not your heart be glad when he stumbles, lest the Most High see it and turn away his wrath from him.

Fret not yourself because of evil men, neither be envious of the wicked, for there is no reward to the evil man and the candle of the wicked will be put out. Whatever the wicked have going on, or riches gotten by wickedness, do not stress over it. The Most High is going to judge them and deal with them, so keep it moving. Fear the Most High and the king, and meddle not with them given to change, for their calamity rises suddenly.

It is not good to have respect of persons in judgment. He that says to the wicked, you are righteous, the people will curse and nations abhor him, but to them that rebuke him will be delight and a good blessing. Every man will kiss his lips that gives a right answer.

Prepare your work outside and make it fit in the field, and afterward build your house. Be not a witness against your neighbor without cause, and deceive not with your lips. Say not, I will do to him as he has done to me. This is where turning the other cheek comes from; you have to take the high road instead of getting vengeance. His neighbor drunkenly scratched his car while parking her sister's car, and it took everything in him not to get revenge. He let it go and took the high road.

He went by the field of the slothful and the vineyard of the man void of understanding, and it was all grown over with thorns and nettles, its stone wall broken down. He considered it well and received instruction: yet a little sleep, a little slumber, a little folding of the hands to sleep, so your poverty comes as one that travels and your want as an armed man. These chapters deal with wisdom, raising children, avoiding sin, and laziness. These are things we need to put into our character. Proverbs is a very good character-building book that should be read often. --- Topics: [Clean and Unclean Meats](/encyclopedia/clean-and-unclean-meats) · [Esau and Edom](/encyclopedia/esau-and-edom) · [Sacrifice and Atonement](/encyclopedia/sacrifice-and-atonement)

Five were wise and five were foolish. The foolish took their lamps and took no oil with them; the wise took oil in their vessels with their lamps. The oil is the wisdom of the scriptures. The foolish come afterward saying, Lord, Lord, open to us, and are answered, Verily I say unto you, I know you not. Calling on his name while breaking the commandments is exactly this. Men bless what the law calls an abomination and still say Lord, Lord.

Every man received according to his several ability, and the two who traded were told, Well done, thou good and faithful servant. The one who hid his talent blamed his lord and called him a hard man, and was answered, Thou wicked and slothful servant. That fearful spirit is not of the Most High, and a man should examine himself for it. Unto every one that hath shall be given, and he shall have abundance; but from him that hath not shall be taken away even that which he hath. Knowledge that is not used is knowledge that is lost.

He separates them one from another, as a shepherd divideth his sheep from the goats, and says to those on the right hand, Inherit the kingdom prepared for you from the foundation of the world. Inasmuch as ye have done it unto one of the least of these my brethren, ye have done it unto me. Meeting the need of a brother or sister in the body is counted as done to Christ himself. Those on the left hand are answered with the same measure: inasmuch as ye did it not to one of the least of these, ye did it not to me. --- Topics: [Clean and Unclean Meats](/encyclopedia/clean-and-unclean-meats) · [The Feasts of the Most High](/encyclopedia/the-feasts-of-the-most-high) · [The Priesthood](/encyclopedia/the-priesthood) · [The Sabbath](/encyclopedia/the-sabbath)

Keep judgment and do justice, for His salvation is near to come and His righteousness to be revealed. Blessed is the man that does this and lays hold on it, that keeps the Sabbath from polluting it and keeps his hand from doing any evil.

The son of the stranger that has joined himself to the Most High is not to say the Lord has utterly separated him from His people, and the eunuch is not to say he is a dry tree. These strangers spoken of are Israel; the whole passage is the Most High speaking to Israel. To the eunuchs that keep His Sabbaths and take hold of His covenant, He gives a place and a name in His house better than of sons and daughters, an everlasting name that will not be cut off. The sons of the stranger that join themselves to Him, keep the Sabbath, and take hold of His covenant, He will bring to His holy mountain and make joyful in His house of prayer; their offerings will be accepted, for His house will be called a house of prayer for all people. The Lord God who gathers the outcasts of Israel says He will yet gather others to Him besides those already gathered.

All the beasts of the field and forest are called to devour. Judgment is turned on the failed leadership. The watchmen are blind and ignorant, dumb dogs that cannot bark, sleeping and loving to slumber. They are greedy dogs that never have enough, shepherds that cannot understand. They all look to their own way, every one for his gain, saying they will fetch wine and fill themselves with strong drink, and tomorrow will be as this day and much more abundant.

name: Ishmael the son of Nethaniah
charge: Murder of Gedaliah the governor at his own table; slaughter of the Jews and Chaldeans with him, and of seventy pilgrims
summary: Of the seed royal, hired by the king of the Ammonites, Ishmael ate bread with Gedaliah at Mizpah and killed him, then killed the men with him, then killed seventy mourners on their way to the house of the Lord and threw them in a pit. He escaped to Ammon with eight men. Scripture records no sentence on him; it records what his deed cost the remnant.
offense: Ishmael came with ten men to Gedaliah at Mizpah and ate with him. During that hospitality he rose up and killed the governor appointed over the remnant, together with Jews and Chaldeans there. Gedaliah had previously refused to believe the warning of a plot against his life. Ishmael then went out weeping to meet eighty men coming with offerings to the house of the Lord. He drew them into Mizpah and killed seventy, casting their bodies into a pit. Ten were spared when they offered hidden stores of food. He took the remaining people captive and set out toward the Ammonites. His tears concealed violence, and the prospect of supplies determined whom he spared.
judgment: Johanan and the captains pursued Ishmael. The captives rejoiced when they saw them and returned with Johanan, while Ishmael escaped to the Ammonites with eight men. The account records the breaking of his hold over the captives, but not his eventual death or a further punishment. His bloodshed left the remnant afraid of Babylonian retaliation and helped set the stage for their flight toward Egypt. His escape did not make his murders lawful, nor did it erase the injury done to a people already reduced by war.

But Gedaliah the son of Ahikam believed them not. 15Then Johanan the son of Kareah spake to Gedaliah in Mizpah secretly, saying, Let me go, I pray thee, and I will slay Ishmael the son of Nethaniah, and no man shall know it: wherefore should he slay thee, that all the Jews which are gathered unto thee should be scattered, and the remnant in Judah perish? 16But Gedaliah the son of Ahikam said unto Johanan the son of Kareah, Thou shalt not do this thing: for thou speakest falsely of Ishmael.

entries.commentary: The word came to Jeremiah after Nebuzaradan the captain of the guard let him go from Ramah, where he had been bound in chains among all the captives of Jerusalem and Judah being carried away to Babylon; Jeremiah was let go when Jerusalem was seized. The captain, a heathen, told Jeremiah that the Most High had pronounced this evil upon the place because the people sinned against Him and would not obey His voice, so this thing had come upon them. The nations always knew why we went into captivity; it is sin, the breaking of the Most High's laws, that becomes our weakness and how we are overcome. -

The captain loosed Jeremiah from the chains on his hands and gave him an ultimatum, either to come with him to Babylon where he would be looked after well, or to remain in the land as he pleased. He directed Jeremiah to Gedaliah the son of Ahikam, whom the king of Babylon had made governor over the cities of Judah, gave him food and a reward, and let him go; Gedaliah was one of Jeremiah's good friends. Jeremiah went to Gedaliah at Mizpah and dwelt with him among the people left in the land.

When all the captains of the forces in the fields heard that the king of Babylon had made Gedaliah governor and had committed to him the men, women, children, and the poor of the land who were not carried away, they came together to him at Mizpah. Gedaliah swore to them not to fear serving the Chaldeans but to dwell in the land, gather wine and summer fruits and oil, and serve the king of Babylon, and it would be well with them; the war was over and they were already conquered. All the Jews scattered in Moab, Ammon, Edom, and the other countries heard of the remnant left under Gedaliah and returned to the land of Judah, gathering wine and summer fruits in abundance.

Johanan the son of Kareah and the captains of the forces came to Gedaliah at Mizpah and warned him that Baalis the king of the Ammonites had sent Ishmael the son of Nethaniah to slay him, but Gedaliah believed them not. Johanan spoke secretly to Gedaliah, offering to kill Ishmael himself so that Gedaliah would not be slain and the gathered remnant scattered. Gedaliah forbade Johanan to do it, saying he spoke falsely of Ishmael, and refused to believe the plot.

In the seventh month Ishmael the son of Nethaniah, of the royal seed and a prince of the king, came with ten men to Gedaliah at Mizpah, and they ate bread together at a banquet held in Ishmael's honor. Ishmael and his ten men rose up and smote Gedaliah the son of Ahikam with the sword and slew him, the governor the king of Babylon had made over the land. Ishmael also slew all the Jews with Gedaliah at Mizpah and the Chaldeans and men of war that were found there.

The second day after the murder, before anyone knew of it, eighty men came from Shechem, Shiloh, and Samaria with their beards shaven, their clothes rent, and their bodies cut, bringing offerings and incense to the house of the Most High. Ishmael went out from Mizpah weeping as he met them, playing a part, and invited them in to Gedaliah; when they came into the midst of the city he and his men slew them and cast them into a pit. Ten of the eighty were spared when they told Ishmael they had hidden treasures of wheat, barley, oil, and honey in the field. The pit Ishmael filled with the slain was the one Asa the king had made for fear of Baasha king of Israel during the war between them. -

Ishmael carried away captive all the residue of the people at Mizpah, including the king's daughters, whom Nebuzaradan had committed to Gedaliah, and departed toward the Ammonites. When Johanan and the captains heard of all the evil Ishmael had done, not only killing Gedaliah but at least eighty other men, they took their men and went to fight him and found him by the great waters in Gibeon. All the people Ishmael had taken captive were glad to see Johanan, turned about, and returned to him, but Ishmael escaped from Johanan with eight men and went to the Ammonites.

Johanan took the whole remnant he had recovered from Ishmael, the mighty men of war, the women, the children, and the eunuchs, and departed to dwell near Bethlehem on the way toward Egypt. They set out to seek refuge in Egypt because they were afraid of the Chaldeans, since Ishmael had slain Gedaliah whom the king of Babylon had made governor; with Gedaliah dead they felt they had no reason to stay.

In the ninth year of Zedekiah's reign Nebuchadnezzar came with all his host against Jerusalem, pitched against it, and built forts round about it. The city was besieged until the eleventh year of Zedekiah, and the famine prevailed in the city. Because the city was besieged no food, water, or goods could get in, so there was no bread for the people of the land.

The city was broken up and the men of war fled by night by the way of the gate between two walls by the king's garden, while the Chaldeans were round about the city. The army pursued the king, overtook him in the plains of Jericho, and his army was scattered from him, and they took him to the king of Babylon at Riblah, where judgment was given upon him. They slew Zedekiah's sons before his eyes, then put out his eyes, bound him with fetters of brass, and carried him to Babylon, just as Jeremiah had warned him.

In the fifth month of the nineteenth year of Nebuchadnezzar, Nebuzaradan the captain of the guard came to Jerusalem. He burnt the house of the Lord, the king's house, and every great man's house, and the army broke down the walls of Jerusalem round about. He carried away the rest of the people and the fugitives, but left the poor of the land to be vinedressers and husbandmen, since the poor could not fend for themselves.

The Chaldeans broke in pieces the pillars of brass, the bases, and the brasen sea that were in the house of the Lord, and carried the brass to Babylon because it was valuable. They took away the pots, shovels, snuffers, spoons, and vessels of brass, and the firepans and bowls of gold and silver the captain of the guard took away. The two pillars, one sea, and the bases Solomon had made were of brass without weight, the one pillar eighteen cubits high with a brasen chapiter, wreathen work, and pomegranates round about.

The captain of the guard took Seraiah the chief priest, Zephaniah the second priest, and the three keepers of the door. He took an officer over the men of war, five men in the king's presence, the principal scribe of the host, and threescore men of the people found in the city. Nebuzaradan brought them to the king of Babylon at Riblah, and the king smote and slew them there; so Judah was carried away out of their land.

Over the people left in the land Nebuchadnezzar made Gedaliah the son of Ahikam, the son of Shaphan, governor. Gedaliah counselled the captains and their men not to fear to serve the Chaldeans but to dwell in the land and serve the king of Babylon, and it would be well with them. But Ishmael the son of Nethaniah, of the royal seed, came with ten men and smote Gedaliah and the Jews and Chaldeans with him, and the people fled to Egypt for fear of the Chaldeans, killing a man who gave wise counsel.

In the thirty seventh year of the captivity of Jehoiachin, Evilmerodach king of Babylon lifted up his head out of prison and spake kindly to him. He set his throne above the thrones of the other kings in Babylon, changed his prison garments, and let him eat bread continually before him all the days of his life. Jehoiachin was given a continual daily allowance for the rest of his life, a mercy shown at the very end of the account. --- Topics: [Idolatry](/encyclopedia/idolatry) · [Sacrifice and Atonement](/encyclopedia/sacrifice-and-atonement) · [The Covenant](/encyclopedia/the-covenant) · [The Feasts of the Most High](/encyclopedia/the-feasts-of-the-most-high) · [The Priesthood](/encyclopedia/the-priesthood)
Noah and his sons were told to replenish the earth after the flood, and the earth is replenished with righteous children; a multitude of ungodly children profits nothing.
The fear and dread of man upon the beasts is not how it was in the beginning, and not how it will remain; the original relationship between man and the animals will be restored.

This is the introduction of man eating meat. The Most High did not give man a new stomach; the body was already made for it and it lay dormant until after the flood. Having the liberty to eat meat does not mean eating without balance; be not too greedy upon meats, for excess of meats brings sickness. The law of what may be eaten was already understood; you could not eat everything. The doctrine that says you can pray over anything and eat it is a seducing spirit and a doctrine of devils. Fish is meat; all flesh is not the same flesh, but the flesh of beasts, of fishes, and of birds are all flesh. Every creature of God is good for what it was made for, and it is sanctified by the word of God, and the word that sanctifies what may be eaten is the dietary law.
The law against eating flesh with the blood was given to Adam and is still in place with Noah; the word is true from the beginning.

The Most High requiring blood at the hand of every beast is animal sacrifice, still in place with Noah, passed down generation to generation. The judgment for sin has always been death. When Eve sinned and caused Adam to sin, either they had to die, or something had to stand in their place; the blood of the animal stood in for them. That is the scapegoat: it takes the wrongdoings, mistakes, and faults of others and places them on the animal. That is why Cain and Abel were bringing offerings, because they knew of the sacrifice from [Genesis 3](/bible/genesis/3).

Whoso sheddeth man's blood, by man shall his blood be shed: life for life. This law is way before Moses, so it cannot be dismissed as the law of Moses. The laws were never done away with; Christ came not to destroy the law but to fulfil, and not one jot or tittle passes from the law.

The covenant established here is with Noah, his seed, and every living creature: all flesh shall never again be cut off by the waters of a flood. This is a general covenant with all flesh. The covenant with Israel is found in [Jeremiah 31](/bible/jeremiah/31).

The bow in the cloud, the rainbow, is the token of the covenant between the Most High and the earth; it compasses the heaven about with a glorious circle, and His hands bended it. The world has taken that same bow, the token of the covenant, and turned it into the symbol of sodomy. The spiritual eyes will see what that means: the great city is spiritually called Sodom and Egypt.
The waters shall no more become a flood to destroy all flesh. The next time the destruction is not water but fire, when the day of the Lord comes and the elements melt with fervent heat.

Shem, Ham, and Japheth went forth out of the ark and the whole earth was overspread from them. Ham dwelt in what is called Africa; Shem in the land mass toward Arabia; Japheth went into Europe. Ham is the father of Canaan, and Canaan dwelt in the land later called the land of Israel. That is how you know the land of Israel is a part of Africa; the maps separate Israel from Africa so that the connection is not made.

Noah was still perfect and righteous. A just man falleth seven times and riseth up again; one fall does not undo righteousness. Understand Noah's heart: he preached repentance for around a hundred years, and everyone he knew outside his house drowned. Strong drink is for him that is ready to perish and wine for those of heavy hearts; Noah drank too much, but he remained righteous in the eyes of the Most High. Ham saw the nakedness of his father and did not cover him; Shem and Japheth went backward and covered their father without looking. The commandments concerning nakedness were being applied; [Leviticus 18](/bible/leviticus/18) opens those laws.

Noah was asleep, so how did he know what his younger son had done? The Most High speaks to man in a dream, in a vision of the night, and reveals His secret unto His servants the prophets; Noah was a preacher of righteousness, and the Lord told him. Cursed be Canaan: a servant of servants unto his brethren. Blessed be the Lord God of Shem: it was revealed that the Messiah and the righteous seed would come through Shem.

name: Johanan and the remnant that went down to Egypt
charge: Asking the word of the Lord, swearing to obey it, and refusing it; burning incense to the queen of heaven in Egypt
summary: The remnant asked Jeremiah to pray for direction and swore to obey whatever the Lord said. Ten days later the answer came: stay in the land and I will build you; go to Egypt and the sword you fear will overtake you there. They called the prophet a liar, took him with them to Egypt, and there openly returned to the queen of heaven.
offense: Ye dissembled in your hearts, when ye sent me unto the Lord your God, saying, Pray for us unto the Lord our God; and according unto all that the Lord our God shall say, so declare unto us, and we will do it. In Egypt the men who knew their wives burned incense to other gods answered Jeremiah: we will certainly do whatsoever thing goeth forth out of our own mouth, to burn incense unto the queen of heaven, as we did in the cities of Judah; for then had we plenty of victuals.
judgment: Then it shall come to pass, that the sword, which ye feared, shall overtake you there in the land of Egypt, and the famine, whereof ye were afraid, shall follow close after you there in Egypt; and there ye shall die. I will take the remnant of Judah, that have set their faces to go into the land of Egypt, and they shall all be consumed, and fall in the land of Egypt; none shall return but such as shall escape. The sign given was Pharaoh-hophra delivered into the hand of his enemies, as Zedekiah had been.

entries.commentary: All the captains, Johanan, Jezaniah, and all the people from the least to the greatest came to Jeremiah the prophet before going into Egypt and begged him to pray to the Most High for them, that they might know the way to walk and what to do. Jeremiah agreed to pray and promised to declare everything the Most High answered, keeping nothing back. They swore the Most High would be a true and faithful witness against them if they did not obey His voice, whether good or evil, so that it might be well with them.

After ten days the word of the Most High came to Jeremiah, and he called Johanan and all the people to hear the answer. The Most High told them that if they would still abide in the land He would build them and not pull them down, plant them and not pluck them up, for He repented of the evil He had done to them; He does not desire evil against His people, He only wants His laws kept. He told them not to be afraid of the king of Babylon of whom they were afraid, for He was with them to save them, deliver them from his hand, and show them mercies so they could return to their own land.

If instead they refused to dwell in the land and said they would go into Egypt to see no war, hear no trumpet, and hunger for no bread, then the sword they feared would overtake them there and the famine would follow close after them, and there they would die. All the men who set their faces to go into Egypt would die by the sword, the famine, and the pestilence, and none would remain or escape the evil He would bring; the Most High set before them life or death and told them to choose life. As His anger was poured out on the inhabitants of Jerusalem, so His fury would be poured out on them when they entered Egypt, and they would become an execration, an astonishment, a curse, and a reproach, and see the land no more.

The Most High plainly told the remnant of Judah to go not into Egypt, and Jeremiah warned them He had admonished them that day. They had dissembled in their hearts when they sent him to pray, giving a false appearance and concealing that they did not truly mean to obey; some people speak words they do not believe. Because they had not obeyed His voice, they would certainly die by the sword, the famine, and the pestilence in the very place they desired to go; we are these same people, quick to say we will not do what the Most High commands, though now that we understand who we are in these last days many of us want to keep His laws.

When Jeremiah finished speaking all the words of the Most High, Azariah the son of Hoshaiah, Johanan the son of Kareah, and all the proud men told him he spoke falsely and called him a lying prophet; pride is destruction according to the scriptures. They accused Baruch the son of Neriah of setting Jeremiah against them to deliver them into the hand of the Chaldeans, to be put to death or carried captive to Babylon. Many people ask for counsel while already having their own minds made up; when the counsel is not what they want to hear they go looking for someone who will tell them what they want, and so these men obeyed not the voice of the Most High to dwell in Judah.

Johanan and all the captains took the whole remnant of Judah, the men, women, children, and the king's daughters that Nebuzaradan had left with Gedaliah, along with Jeremiah the prophet and Baruch. They came into the land of Egypt as far as Tahpanhes because they obeyed not the voice of the Most High.

The word of the Most High came to Jeremiah in Tahpanhes to take great stones and hide them in the clay of the brick kiln at the entry of Pharaoh's house, in the sight of the men of Judah. The Most High declared He would send for Nebuchadnezzar the king of Babylon, His servant, set his throne upon those hidden stones, spread his royal pavilion over them, and smite the land of Egypt. When Nebuchadnezzar came he would deliver such as were for death to death, such as were for captivity to captivity, and such as were for the sword to the sword; in war each person already has an appointed end that the Most High has set. He would kindle a fire in the houses of the gods of Egypt, array himself with the land of Egypt as a shepherd puts on his garment so that none escape, break the images of Bethshemesh, and burn the houses of the gods of the Egyptians with fire. --- Topics: [Esau and Edom](/encyclopedia/esau-and-edom) · [Sacrifice and Atonement](/encyclopedia/sacrifice-and-atonement) · [The Feasts of the Most High](/encyclopedia/the-feasts-of-the-most-high)

The word came to Jeremiah concerning all the Jews dwelling in the land of Egypt and in the country of Pathros; the Most High reminded them of all the evil He had brought on Jerusalem and the cities of Judah, now a desolation where no man dwelt, because of the wickedness they committed provoking Him to anger. They went to burn incense and serve other gods that neither they nor their fathers knew, yet the Most High sent all His servants the prophets, rising early and sending them, pleading with them not to do this abominable thing that He hates. The same work goes on today; we fill up the street corners all over the earth bringing forth the glorious gospel of the one true living God and Christ, the prophets He raised up to give warning. -

They hearkened not nor inclined their ear to turn from their wickedness and burn no incense to other gods, so the Most High's fury and anger was poured forth and kindled in the cities of Judah and the streets of Jerusalem until they were wasted and desolate. He asks why they commit this great evil against their own souls, cutting off man and woman, child and suckling out of Judah, leaving none to remain. They provoke Him to wrath with the works of their hands, burning incense to other gods in the land of Egypt where they had gone to dwell, cutting themselves off to become a curse and a reproach among all the nations of the earth. -

The Most High asks whether they have forgotten the wickedness of their fathers, the kings of Judah, their wives, and their own wickedness committed in the land of Judah and the streets of Jerusalem; they were not humbled even to that day, nor did they fear or walk in His law and statutes. Therefore He will set His face against them for evil, to cut off all Judah, and take the remnant that set their faces to go into Egypt to sojourn there; they shall all be consumed and fall by the sword and the famine, from the least to the greatest. They shall become an execration, an astonishment, a curse, and a reproach; only a small number escaping the sword shall return, for none shall return to Judah though they have a desire to dwell there. -

All the men who knew their wives had burned incense to other gods, and all the women, a great multitude in Egypt and Pathros, answered Jeremiah defiantly. These men did not rule their houses well and had no authority over their households; their wives were in the midst of idolatry, the same disorder we see in this place spiritually called Egypt, in Babylon the great today. They said they would not hearken to the word spoken in the name of the Most High but would perform their vows to burn incense to the queen of heaven and pour out drink offerings, claiming they had plenty of victuals and saw no evil until they left off, and then wanted all things and were consumed by the sword and famine. The women declared they made their cakes to worship her and poured out drink offerings without their men; the times women gather together without their men, such as baby showers with cakes and drinks and partying, are burning incense to other gods to keep in mind.

Jeremiah answered all the people, men and women, that the incense they burned in the cities of Judah and the streets of Jerusalem, they and their fathers, kings, and princes, the Most High remembered and it came into His mind. The Most High could no longer bear the evil of their doings and the abominations they committed, therefore their land became a desolation, an astonishment, and a curse without an inhabitant as at that day. This evil happened to them because they burned incense and sinned against the Most High and did not obey His voice nor walk in His law, statutes, and testimonies.

Jeremiah told all the people and all the women that they and their wives had both spoken with their mouths and fulfilled with their hands their vows to burn incense to the queen of heaven, and would surely accomplish them. Therefore the Most High swore by His great name that His name shall no more be named in the mouth of any man of Judah in all Egypt, saying "The Lord GOD liveth"; He will watch over them for evil and not for good until they are consumed by the sword and famine. Only a small number escaping the sword shall return out of Egypt into Judah, and all the remnant that went to Egypt shall know whose words shall stand, His or theirs.

The Most High gives a sign that He will punish them in that place so they may know His words shall surely stand against them for evil; He will give Pharaoh-hophra king of Egypt into the hand of his enemies as He gave Zedekiah king of Judah into the hand of Nebuchadnezzar. Evil does not come merely by chance; the Most High brings that evil upon us when we turn from Him and follow our own mind, sinning against the one true living God in Christ. -

Woe to the rebellious children who take counsel but not of the Most High, and who go down into Egypt without asking at his mouth. This is the same rebellion named at the start of the book. Leaning to Pharaoh's strength instead of the Most High turns their trust into shame and confusion. There were times kings sought the Most High, and times they sought heathen kings to fight their battles for them. -

The riches carried down to Egypt on asses and camels buy help that profits nothing, for the Egyptians shall help in vain. The same thing happened in the Babylonian captivity, and the same thing is happening to us today. The Most High tells Isaiah to write it in a table and note it in a book for a time to come forever, because these things were written for our learning. -

This is a rebellious, lying people that will not hear the law of the Most High, telling the seers to prophesy smooth things and deceits. Our pastors do the same today, teaching that the laws are done away with. They want the Holy One of Israel to cease from before them because they love their oppression and the ways of their slave masters. That iniquity becomes a breach ready to fall, breaking suddenly like a potter's vessel that cannot be spared.

In returning and rest, in quietness and confidence, is our salvation and strength, but the people would not have it. Instead they say they will flee upon horses. Because they trust their own swiftness, one thousand will flee at the rebuke of one, until they are left as a lonely beacon on a hill.

The Most High waits to be gracious and exalts himself to have mercy, for he is a God of judgment: blessed are all they that wait for him. Waiting means holding patience through the trials and tribulations. People will come, even family members, saying no one is coming to save you and you must save yourself with guns. You must stay steadfast and answer the Most High's cry with patience. -

Though the Most High gives the bread of adversity and the water of affliction, our teachers will no longer be removed into a corner; our eyes shall see our teachers. We see this now on these platforms, in the daily bread classes, radio shows, the Sabbath, and the street corners. The ear hears a word behind saying "This is the way, walk ye in it," because the men are out teaching. Then the people defile and cast away their idols of silver and gold as a menstruous cloth, as we have watched brothers cast off crosses and ankhs at camp.

Then the Most High gives rain for the seed, bread of the increase, fat and plenteous pasture, and rivers on every high hill in the day of the great slaughter when the towers fall. The light of the moon shall be as the sun, and the sun sevenfold, in the day he binds up the breach of his people and heals the stroke of their wound.

The name of the Most High comes from far, burning with anger, his tongue a devouring fire, sifting the nations with the sieve of vanity. His people shall have a song and gladness of heart as when one comes to the mountain of the Most High. Like King David dancing before the ark until Michal despised him, we will be joyful in that day when we no longer fear being shot in the street, having our doors kicked in, or losing our homes. Through the voice of the Most High the Assyrian is beaten down, for Tophet is ordained of old and its fire kindled by the breath of the Most High.
