name: Moab and Ammon
charge: Magnifying themselves against the Lord and against his people; rejoicing over the sanctuary when it was profaned
summary: Lot's two sons, neighbours to Israel from the wilderness on, are judged in Isaiah, Jeremiah, Ezekiel, Amos and Zephaniah for one long habit: pride against the Lord and gladness at Judah's ruin. Ammon ripped up the women with child of Gilead to enlarge its border; Moab said, Aha, against the house of Judah.
offense: We have heard of the pride of Moab; he is very proud: of his loftiness, and his arrogancy, and his pride, and the haughtiness of his heart. He shall be no more praised, because he hath magnified himself against the Lord. Of Ammon: because thou saidst, Aha, against my sanctuary, when it was profaned; and against the land of Israel, when it was desolate; and against the house of Judah, when they went into captivity. Amos: they have ripped up the women with child of Gilead, that they might enlarge their border.
judgment: Moab shall be destroyed from being a people, because he hath magnified himself against the Lord. Yet will I bring again the captivity of Moab in the latter days. Of Ammon: I will deliver thee to the men of the east for a possession, and Rabbah shall be a stable for camels; Zephaniah: Moab shall be as Sodom, and the children of Ammon as Gomorrah, even the breeding of nettles, and saltpits, and a perpetual desolation. Nebuchadnezzar came through both.

entries.commentary: This is the word of the Most High against Moab. Woe unto Nebo, for it is spoiled; Kiriathaim is confounded and taken. There shall be no more praise of Moab. In Heshbon they have devised evil against it: come, let us cut it off from being a nation. These are the Moabites, and God calls the so-called Chinese by that name.

A voice of crying goes up from Horonaim, spoiling and great destruction. Moab is destroyed, and her little ones cause a cry to be heard. Flee, save your lives, and be like the heath in the wilderness. There is no standing against the judgment that is coming.

Because thou hast trusted in thy works and in thy treasures, thou shalt also be taken. Chemosh their god goes into captivity with his priests and princes together. The spoiler comes upon every city, and no city escapes. The valley perishes and the plain is destroyed, as the Most High has spoken.
Cursed be he that doeth the work of the Lord deceitfully, and cursed be he that keepeth back his sword from blood. The work of the Most High is not to be done half-heartedly.

Moab has been at ease from his youth and settled on his lees, never emptied from vessel to vessel, never gone into captivity. Therefore his taste remained in him and his scent is not changed. The Most High will send wanderers to empty his vessels and break their bottles, and Moab shall be ashamed of Chemosh as the house of Israel was ashamed of Bethel.

How say ye, we are mighty and strong men for the war? Moab is spoiled, and his chosen young men are gone down to the slaughter, saith the King, whose name is the Lord of hosts. The calamity of Moab is near to come and his affliction hastens fast. All that know his name are to bemoan how the strong staff is broken.

The daughter that inhabits Dibon is told to come down from her glory and sit in thirst, for the spoiler of Moab comes upon her. The inhabitant of Aroer is to stand by the way and ask the one who flees, what is done. Moab is confounded, for it is broken down. Howl and cry, and tell it in Arnon that Moab is spoiled.

Judgment comes on the whole plain country, city by city, from Holon and Jahazah to Dibon, Nebo, Kiriathaim, Kerioth, and Bozrah, upon all the cities of Moab, far or near. The horn of Moab is cut off and her arm is broken. The strength of the nation is taken away by the Most High.

Make Moab drunken, for he magnified himself against the Lord, and he shall wallow in his own vomit and be in derision. The Most High asks, was not Israel a derision unto thee? Did the Lord not punish his own children? Then what makes the heathen think their time is not going to come? He punishes his own, so he will surely punish the wicked.

The pride of Moab is called out: exceedingly proud, his loftiness, his arrogance, and the haughtiness of his heart. For all that pride, these Moabites will go back to their proper place and serve the nation of Israel for what they have done. The wickedness of Moab against the children of God is real history the American Board of Education does not teach: enslaving us during the Tang Dynasty, feeding the ghettos, and building whole industries off our people. All of it will be manifested and answered for. -

The Most High declares he will howl and mourn for Moab, for the men of Kir-heres and the vine of Sibmah, because the spoiler is fallen upon the summer fruits and the vintage. Joy and gladness is taken from the plentiful field. He will cause to cease in Moab him that offereth in the high places and him that burneth incense to his gods. The idolatry is cut off with the people.

The heart of the Most High sounds like pipes for Moab, because the riches he has gotten are perished. Every head shall be bald and every beard clipped, with cutting upon the hands and sackcloth upon the loins. A good majority of Moab bald their heads and shave their faces rather than keep their beards, the same as the Mongolians right next door to them. There shall be lamenting generally upon the housetops of Moab.

Moab is broken like a vessel wherein is no pleasure. They howl, asking how it is broken down, and Moab becomes a derision and a dismay to all around him. He that judges shall fly as an eagle and spread his wings over Moab. The mighty men's hearts that day shall be as the heart of a woman in her pains, and Moab shall be destroyed from being a people because he magnified himself against the Lord.

Fear, the pit, and the snare are upon the inhabitants of Moab. He that flees the fear falls into the pit, and he that climbs out of the pit is taken in the snare; there is no escape from the years of their visitation. A fire comes forth out of Heshbon and devours the corner of Moab. Woe unto Moab, for thy sons and thy daughters are taken captives.

Yet the Most High will bring again the captivity of Moab in the latter days. This has not happened yet, but it will come to pass, for he has spoken it and his word shall not return. Thus far is the judgment of Moab.

The word of the Most High comes against the Ammonites, the so-called Japanese, because they said Aha against His sanctuary when it was profaned, against the land of Israel when it was desolate, and against the house of Judah when they went into captivity. Because they clapped their hands, stamped their feet, and rejoiced in heart with all their despite against Israel, cheering our destruction, He will deliver them to the men of the east for a possession, cut them off from the people, and cause them to perish, that they may know He is the Lord.

Because Moab, the so-called Chinese, and Seir say that the house of Judah is like unto all the heathen, claiming Judah is no longer the Most High's chosen people, judgment is pronounced against them. The Most High will open the side of Moab from his frontier cities, the glory of the country, and deliver them to the men of the east along with the Ammonites so that the Ammonites be not remembered among the nations, and He will execute judgments upon Moab.

Because Edom, the so-called white man, dealt against the house of Judah by taking vengeance and greatly offended, the Most High will stretch out His hand upon Edom, cut off man and beast, and make it desolate from Teman, and they of Dedan shall fall by the sword. He will lay His vengeance upon Edom by the hand of His people Israel, and they shall do in Edom according to His anger and His fury. This is future prophecy that has not yet come to pass, for the Most High must first change our minds to act according to His anger to perform righteous recompense with our own hands. -

Because the Philistines dealt by revenge and took vengeance with a despiteful heart to destroy for the old hatred, never letting the feud go the way they always warred with us from the days of the judges, Samuel, Saul, and David, judgment comes upon them. The Most High will stretch out His hand upon the Philistines, cut off the Cherethims, destroy the remnant of the sea coast, and execute great vengeance with furious rebukes, that they may know He is the Lord when He lays His vengeance upon them.

The words of Amos, who was among the herdmen of Tekoa, which he saw concerning Israel in the days of Uzziah king of Judah and Jeroboam the son of Joash king of Israel, two years before the earthquake. The Lord roars from Zion and utters his voice from Jerusalem, so that the habitations of the shepherds mourn and the top of Carmel withers. This chapter was read straight through without going precept upon precept.

For three transgressions of Damascus and for four, the Most High will not turn away the punishment, because they threshed Gilead with threshing instruments of iron. He will send a fire into the house of Hazael that shall devour the palaces of Benhadad, break the bar of Damascus, cut off the inhabitants of the plain of Aven and the sceptre from the house of Eden, and the people of Syria shall go into captivity unto Kir.

For three transgressions of Gaza and for four, the Most High will not turn away the punishment, because they carried away the whole captivity to deliver them up to Edom. He will send a fire on the wall of Gaza that shall devour its palaces, cut off the inhabitant from Ashdod and the sceptre from Ashkelon, turn his hand against Ekron, and the remnant of the Philistines shall perish.

For three transgressions of Tyrus and for four, the Most High will not turn away the punishment, because they delivered up the whole captivity to Edom and did not remember the brotherly covenant. He will send a fire on the wall of Tyrus that shall devour its palaces.

For three transgressions of Edom and for four, the Most High will not turn away the punishment, because Edom pursued his brother with the sword, cast off all pity, and kept his wrath forever. He will send a fire upon Teman that shall devour the palaces of Bozrah.

For three transgressions of the children of Ammon and for four, the Most High will not turn away the punishment, because they ripped up the women with child of Gilead to enlarge their border. He will kindle a fire in the wall of Rabbah that shall devour its palaces, with shouting in the day of battle and a tempest in the day of the whirlwind, and their king shall go into captivity, he and his princes together. --- Topics: [Esau and Edom](/encyclopedia/esau-and-edom) · [The Covenant](/encyclopedia/the-covenant)

For three transgressions of Moab and for four, the Most High will not turn away the punishment, because he burned the bones of the king of Edom into lime. Moab today is the Chinese. He will send a fire upon Moab that shall devour the palaces of Kerioth, and Moab shall die with tumult, with shouting, and with the sound of the trumpet, and he will cut off the judge and slay all the princes with him.

For three transgressions of Judah and for four, the Most High will not turn away the punishment, because they despised the law of the Lord, did not keep his commandments, and their lies caused them to err after which their fathers walked. This is the reason we are in captivity even today. Going back to the Assyrian captivity, our forefathers were rebellious against the Most High's laws, did not want to keep the commandments, and wanted to worship idols. He will send a fire upon Judah that shall devour the palaces of Jerusalem.

For three transgressions of Israel and for four, the Most High will not turn away the punishment, because they sold the righteous for silver and the poor for a pair of shoes. That goes into oppression, and just like in today's time nobody wants to hear the righteous words of the Most High and keep the commandments; when you bring out the commandments you hear "what, I can't wear pants." They pant after the dust of the earth on the head of the poor, turn aside the way of the meek, and a man and his father go in unto the same maid to profane the Most High's holy name. There were men even in that time going in unto their father's wife, and you may find a TV show today promoting that behavior. They lay themselves down upon clothes laid to pledge by every altar and drink the wine of the condemned in the house of their god. -

Yet the Most High destroyed the Amorite before them, whose height was like the height of the cedar and who was strong as the oaks; he destroyed his fruit from above and his roots from beneath. The Amorite is another heathen nation. He brought Israel up from the land of Egypt, led them forty years through the wilderness to possess the land of the Amorite, and raised up their sons for prophets and their young men for Nazirites. You can use this to show that the children of Israel are the prophets of the Most High. But they gave the Nazirites wine to drink and commanded the prophets saying, prophesy not. That goes into lies and deceit, doing anything to stop the word of the Most High.

The Most High is pressed under them as a cart is pressed that is full of sheaves; therefore the flight shall perish from the swift, the strong shall not strengthen his force, and the mighty shall not deliver himself, because Israel will be in captivity. He that is courageous among the mighty shall flee away naked in that day; every possession you had will be stripped from you as you flee, the same way a robber coming to a bank strips everybody down and takes the goods.

Gather yourselves together, yea, gather together, O nation not desired; before the decree bring forth, before the fierce anger of the Lord come upon you. Seek ye the Lord, all ye meek of the earth, which have wrought his judgment; seek righteousness, seek meekness: it may be ye shall be hid in the day of the Lord's anger.

Gaza shall be forsaken, and Ashkelon a desolation: they shall drive out Ashdod at the noon day, and Ekron shall be rooted up. The word of the Lord is against you; O Canaan, the land of the Philistines, I will even destroy thee, that there shall be no inhabitant. The coast shall be for the remnant of the house of Judah; they shall feed thereupon: for the Lord their God shall visit them, and turn away their captivity.

I have heard the reproach of Moab, and the revilings of the children of Ammon, whereby they have reproached my people, and magnified themselves against their border. Surely Moab shall be as Sodom, and the children of Ammon as Gomorrah: the residue of my people shall spoil them, and the remnant of my people shall possess them. This shall they have for their pride, because they have reproached and magnified themselves against the people of the Lord of hosts. He will stretch out his hand against the north, and destroy Assyria; and will make Nineveh a desolation, and dry like a wilderness. This is the rejoicing city that dwelt carelessly, that said in her heart, I am, and there is none beside me: how is she become a desolation!

Send the lamb to the ruler of the land from Sela to the wilderness, unto the mount of the daughter of Zion, for the daughters of Moab shall be at the fords of Arnon as a wandering bird cast out of the nest. Moab is told to take counsel, execute judgment, make her shadow as the night in the midst of the noonday, hide the outcasts, and not betray the one that wanders. She is asked to be a covert to the outcasts from the face of the spoiler. When the extortioner and spoiler are consumed out of the land, the throne shall be established in mercy, and one shall sit upon it in truth in the tabernacle of David, judging and seeking judgment and hasting righteousness.

We have heard of the pride of Moab, that he is very proud, of his haughtiness and pride and wrath, but his lies shall not be so. Therefore Moab shall howl for Moab, everyone shall howl. For the foundations of Kirhareseth they shall mourn, surely they are stricken. The fields of Heshbon languish and the vine of Sibmah, whose principal plants the lords of the heathen have broken down; her branches are stretched out, gone over the sea.

The prophet bewails the vine of Sibmah with weeping and waters Heshbon and Elealeh with his tears, for the shouting over the summer fruits and harvest is fallen. Gladness and joy are taken away out of the plentiful field; in the vineyards there is no singing nor shouting, and the treaders tread out no wine in their presses, for the Most High has made the vintage shouting to cease. The prophet's inward parts sound like a harp for Moab and for Kirharesh, and when Moab wearies himself upon the high place and comes to his sanctuary to pray, he shall not prevail.

This is the word the Most High has spoken concerning Moab since that time. But now the Most High speaks, saying that within three years, as the years of a hireling, the glory of Moab shall be contemned with all that great multitude, and the remnant shall be very small and feeble.

He that is wounded in the stones or hath his privy member cut off shall not enter into the congregation of the Lord. This law repeats what was already given: the priests' law in Leviticus lists the same blemishes that barred a man from approaching to offer the bread of his God, including him that hath his stones broken.

A bastard shall not enter into the congregation of the Lord, even to his tenth generation: the children begotten of forbidden unions with the nations were shut out of the congregation. The prophets tie the bastard to Ashdod: a bastard shall dwell in Ashdod. Ashdod was one of the cities given to the tribe of Judah in the inheritance, but Israel did not drive out all the inhabitants and lost it. In the days of Nehemiah, Jews had married wives of Ashdod, of Ammon, and of Moab, and their children spake half in the speech of Ashdod and could not speak in the Jews' language. Why is that? Because the mothers do the raising of the children.

An Ammonite or Moabite shall not enter into the congregation of the Lord, even to their tenth generation, for ever. In the time of Nehemiah this very law was read out of the book of Moses in the audience of the people, and when they heard it our people separated from Israel all the mixed multitude whom they had intermarried with and had children with.

The reason for the ban: Ammon and Moab met not Israel with bread and with water in the way when they came forth out of Egypt, and hired Balaam the son of Beor of Pethor to curse them. The history is in Numbers: Balak the son of Zippor, king of Moab, was sore afraid because the people were many, and sent the elders of Moab and Midian with the rewards of divination to call Balaam to curse Israel. Nevertheless the Lord thy God would not hearken unto Balaam, but turned the curse into a blessing, because the Lord thy God loveth thee; therefore Israel was never to seek their peace nor their prosperity.

Thou shalt not abhor an Edomite, for he is thy brother: this was a temporary law. Edom broke the brotherly covenant; he did pursue his brother with the sword, did cast off all pity, his anger did tear perpetually, and he kept his wrath for ever. Edom's hatred is a perpetual hatred: he shed the blood of the children of Israel by the force of the sword in the time of their calamity, and as we see our people being slaughtered by Esau, that anger continues even to this very day. Thou shalt not abhor an Egyptian, because thou wast a stranger in his land: many brothers and sisters do not want to deal with that part and only want to deal with Edom, but Egypt likewise came under judgment for the violence against the children of Judah, because they shed innocent blood in their land.

When the host goeth forth against thine enemies, then keep thee from every wicked thing: when Israel went to war, they were to keep themselves from every wicked thing. The example is Achan: Israel was warned in any wise to keep from the accursed thing, lest they make the camp of Israel a curse and trouble it, and Achan the son of Carmi of the tribe of Judah took of the accursed thing, the Babylonish garment, and the anger of the Lord was kindled against the children of Israel. Because of that trespass Israel could not stand before their enemies but turned their backs, for they were accursed; the Lord would not be with them any more except they destroyed the accursed from among them, and Achan and his family and all that belonged to him were destroyed and burned, and a heap set upon them, because he broke the covenant.

Any man that was not clean by reason of uncleanness that chanceth him by night went abroad out of the camp; when evening came he washed himself with water, and when the sun was down he came into the camp again.

There was a place without the camp to go forth abroad, and a paddle upon the weapon to dig and cover that which cometh from thee: to make it plain, if you had to ease yourself, you went outside the camp to do it. Verse 14 explains why: the Lord thy God walketh in the midst of thy camp, to deliver thee and to give up thine enemies before thee; therefore shall thy camp be holy, that he see no unclean thing in thee and turn away from thee. That is what we just read happened with Achan the son of Carmi: he brought an unclean thing into the camp, and the Most High turned from Israel in battle. God says he is in the midst of Israel and none else; the Lord would go before us and fight our battles, and that is why he wanted no unclean thing in the camp, for we are holy and the camp was to be holy.

There shall be no whore of the daughters of Israel, nor a sodomite of the sons of Israel. A sodomite is the biblical word for a homosexual, and the whore of the daughters of Israel here is the same sin in the daughters, what we today would call lesbians. There is a heavy push in the world today for our men to be homosexuals and our sisters to be lesbians; popular entertainers are used to influence the younger generation to sin, just as young rappers were dressed in skirts and dresses until it became cool to be gay. This is what we have to bring our people back from: by being an example, the men being an example, the sisters being an example in the way they dress and carry themselves, and by having families, reinstituting a father and a mother in the divine order the Most High God established. Thou shalt not bring the hire of a whore or the price of a dog into the house of the Lord thy God, for even both these are abomination unto the Lord. Without are dogs: that is not the four-legged barking kind, but the other nations. Christ told a woman of another nation it is not meet to take the children's bread and cast it to dogs, and she said, Truth, Lord; and four-legged dogs did not pierce Christ's hands and feet, for the dogs that compassed him were the other nations, in that case the Romans.

Thou shalt not lend upon usury to thy brother, usury of money, of victuals, of any thing: when you read the definition of usury, that is interest. We are not to charge interest to each other when we loan each other anything. Unto a stranger thou mayest lend upon usury: the blessing is that Israel shall lend unto many nations and shall not borrow, the head and not the tail. That is our rightful place on the earth when we keep these commandments: we should lend unto them and may take usury upon what we lend to them, but we should not do that to our own people. The same law was already read in Exodus: if thou lend money to any of my people that is poor by thee, thou shalt not be to him as an usurer.

name: Babylon, the lady of kingdoms
charge: Showing no mercy to the captives; saying, I am, and none else beside me; trusting in her sorceries
summary: Babylon was the Lord's hammer against Judah, and was judged for how she swung it: without mercy, laying a heavy yoke on the ancient, and saying in her heart, I shall be a lady for ever. Isaiah and Jeremiah both name the end before the beginning: the Medes, the sudden fall, the perpetual desolation.
offense: I was wroth with my people, I have polluted mine inheritance, and given them into thine hand: thou didst shew them no mercy; upon the ancient hast thou very heavily laid thy yoke. And thou saidst, I shall be a lady for ever. Thou hast trusted in thy wickedness: thou hast said, None seeth me. Thy wisdom and thy knowledge, it hath perverted thee; and thou hast said in thine heart, I am, and none else beside me. Jeremiah adds the account: they have devoured Israel; the violence done to me and to my flesh be upon Babylon, shall the inhabitant of Zion say.
judgment: The Lord commanded her to sit in the dust and announced the loss of her former honor. Widowhood and loss of children would come suddenly despite her enchantments. An evil she could not ward off would expose the weakness of the wisdom in which she trusted. The astrologers would be as stubble before fire, unable to deliver even themselves. Those with whom she had labored would wander away, leaving none to save her. The oracle reverses Babylon's confidence at every point: power, learning, commerce, and sorcery could not exempt her from the God whose people she had oppressed.
offenseFull: Babylon said that she would be a lady for ever. Though the Lord had delivered His people into her hand, she showed no mercy and laid a heavy yoke upon the aged. Permission to conquer was not permission for limitless cruelty.

She trusted in wickedness, saying that none saw her, and let wisdom and knowledge turn her aside. Her boast, “I am, and none else beside me,” joined self-exaltation with confidence that she would never know widowhood or the loss of children. Sorceries and astrologers were summoned to secure a future she would not consider humbly.
judgmentFull: The Lord commanded her to sit in the dust and announced the loss of her former honor. Widowhood and loss of children would come suddenly despite her enchantments. An evil she could not ward off would expose the weakness of the wisdom in which she trusted.

The oracle reverses Babylon's confidence at every point: power, learning, commerce, and sorcery could not exempt her from the God whose people she had oppressed.

entries.commentary: The burden of Babylon which Isaiah the son of Amoz did see: lift up a banner upon the high mountain, exalt the voice, shake the hand that they may go into the gates of the nobles. The banner is the Bible. The Most High has commanded His sanctified ones and called His mighty ones for His anger. There is the noise of a multitude in the mountains, kingdoms of nations gathered together; the Most High of hosts musters the host of the battle. They come from a far country, from the end of heaven, the Most High and the weapons of His indignation, to destroy the whole land. Those nukes are not just sitting there for nothing; they will be used.

Howl, for the day of the Most High is at hand; it comes as a destruction from the Almighty. Every hand faints, every heart melts, and pain and sorrow take hold of them. If you study this Bible, you understand the prophecies and what is to come, so you prepare your mind. The ones who should be afraid are those who do not know what is coming to pass. They shall be amazed one at another, their faces as flames. Esau's face is going to be as flames, meaning it is going to be red. The day of the Most High comes cruel with wrath and fierce anger to lay the land desolate and destroy the sinners out of it, those not keeping His laws, which is why the remnant keeping His law escapes and is recovered the second time.

The stars of heaven and the constellations, the satellites, shall not give their light; the sun is darkened and the moon does not shine. The Most High will punish the world for their evil and the wicked for their iniquity, and cause the arrogancy of the proud to cease. The arrogant one is Esau, a very proud nation. The Most High will make a man more precious than fine gold, even a man than the golden wedge of Ophir. This is the Israelite man made precious as fine gold. He shakes the heavens, and the earth removes out of her place off its axis, and what removes it is nuclear destruction, in the day of His fierce anger. Every man turns to his own people and flees into his own land; that is a word against interracial marriage. Everyone found with the other nations, especially Edom, shall be thrust through, everyone joined to them shall fall by the sword, their children dashed to pieces before their eyes, their houses spoiled and their wives ravished. This is not talking about us; it is about these other nations.

The Most High stirs up the Medes against them, who do not regard silver nor delight in gold. Their bows dash the young men to pieces; they have no pity on the fruit of the womb and their eye does not spare children. Babylon, the glory of kingdoms, the beauty of the Chaldees' excellency, shall be as when the Most High overthrew Sodom and Gomorrah. That is how the United States of Babylon is going to be. It shall never be inhabited from generation to generation; no Arabian pitches a tent there, no shepherd folds there, but wild beasts, owls, satyrs, and dragons dwell in the desolate houses and pleasant palaces. Her time is near to come and her days shall not be prolonged. We do not have that much time, Israel; we have to gather ourselves together, a nation that is not desired. --- Topics: [Esau and Edom](/encyclopedia/esau-and-edom) · [Idolatry](/encyclopedia/idolatry)

The Most High will have mercy on Jacob and will yet choose Israel and set them in their own land, and the stranger shall be joined with them and cleave to the house of Jacob. The people that took Israel captive shall be taken by Israel, and the house of Israel shall possess them in the Most High's land for servants and handmaids. Those who once held Israel as captives will become their captives, and Israel shall rule over their oppressors.

In the day the Most High gives Israel rest from sorrow, fear, and the hard bondage in which they were made to serve, they shall take up this proverb against the king of Babylon: How has the oppressor ceased, and the golden city ceased. The Most High has broken the staff of the wicked and the scepter of the rulers, the one who smote the people in wrath with a continual stroke and ruled the nations in anger. Now the whole earth is at rest and quiet and breaks forth into singing. Even the fir trees and the cedars of Lebanon rejoice, saying that since the oppressor is laid down, no feller is come up against them.

Hell from beneath is moved to meet the king of Babylon at his coming; it stirs up the dead for him, even the chief ones of the earth, and raises up from their thrones all the kings of the nations. They speak and say to him, Are you also become weak as we are, are you become like us. His pomp is brought down to the grave and the noise of his viols, the worm is spread under him, and the worms cover him.

How is he fallen from heaven, O Lucifer, son of the morning, cut down to the ground, he that weakened the nations. He said in his heart that he would ascend into heaven, exalt his throne above the stars of God, sit upon the mount of the congregation in the sides of the north, ascend above the heights of the clouds, and be like the Most High. For all that pride, he shall be brought down to hell, to the sides of the pit.

They that see him shall look narrowly upon him and consider him, saying, Is this the man that made the earth to tremble, that did shake kingdoms. This is the one that made the world as a wilderness, destroyed the cities thereof, and opened not the house of his prisoners.

All the kings of the nations lie in glory, every one in his own house, but this king is cast out of his grave like an abominable branch, as the raiment of those that are slain, thrust through with a sword, going down to the stones of the pit as a carcass trodden under feet. He shall not be joined with them in burial because he destroyed his land and slew his people; the seed of evildoers shall never be renowned.

Prepare slaughter for his children for the iniquity of their fathers, that they do not rise, possess the land, nor fill the face of the world with cities. The Most High of hosts will rise up against Babylon and cut off the name and remnant, and son and nephew. He will make it a possession for the bittern and pools of water and sweep it with the besom of destruction. The besom is a broom made of twigs tied around a stick; sweeping Babylon with the besom of destruction means sweeping it away with the broom of destruction, wiped out completely.

The Most High of hosts has sworn that as He has thought, so shall it come to pass, and as He has purposed, so shall it stand: He will break the Assyrian in His land and upon His mountains tread him underfoot. Then the Assyrian's yoke shall depart from off Israel and his burden from off their shoulders. This is the purpose purposed upon the whole earth, and the hand stretched out upon all the nations; when the Most High has purposed, none shall disallow it, and when His hand is stretched out, none shall turn it back.

In the year king Ahaz died came this burden: Palestine is warned not to rejoice because the rod that smote her is broken, for out of the serpent's root shall come a cockatrice, and its fruit a fiery flying serpent. The firstborn of the poor shall feed and the needy lie down in safety, but the Most High will kill Palestine's root with famine and slay her remnant. The whole of Palestine is called to howl, for a smoke comes from the north and none shall be alone in his appointed times. The answer to the messengers of the nation is that the Most High has founded Zion, and the poor of His people shall trust in it.

This is the word the Lord spoke against Babylon and the land of the Chaldeans. Declare among the nations, publish and set up a standard: Babylon is taken, Bel is confounded, and her idols are broken in pieces. Set up a standard means lift up the greatest standard ever placed on earth, the Bible. The laws show us where we are evil and where we can do better; the Bible is our law and our banner. The scriptures are twofold, so this speaks against ancient Babylon and against modern-day Babylon, which is America. -
Out of the north comes a nation against Babylon to make her land desolate. None shall dwell therein; both man and beast remove and depart.

In those days the children of Israel and the children of Judah come together, going and weeping, to seek the Lord their God. Our people only look for the Most High when we are afflicted, not when things are good. They ask the way to Zion with their faces that direction, saying, come and let us join ourselves to the Lord in a perpetual covenant. There will come a day when we stop seeking the white man through protesting, marching, and voting, and are gathered together only by the word of God. -

My people have been lost sheep whose shepherds caused them to go astray. The so-called reverends and prosperity preachers are bald-headed, beardless, and do nothing the Bible says, turning the people from mountain to hill until they forget their resting place. Their adversaries say, we offend not, because they have sinned against the Lord. Our enemies know that when Israel sins the Most High will not fight for us, and to some degree they are right. The word is to remove out of the midst of Babylon and go forth from the land of the Chaldeans, coming out of her ways and her religions and back to the commandments. -

The Most High raises an assembly of great nations from the north country against Babylon, and none of their arrows return in vain. Chaldea becomes a spoil, and all that spoil her are satisfied. Because Babylon was glad and rejoiced as the destroyers of the Most High's heritage, grown fat as a heifer at grass, her mother shall be confounded. This also touches Esau, the daughter of Babylon, who becomes a wilderness and a dry land, astonishing everyone who passes by.

Put yourselves in array against Babylon, all you that bend the bow; spare no arrows, for she has sinned against the Lord. Take vengeance upon her; as she has done, do unto her. Cut off the sower and the reaper from Babylon, for they shall turn every one to his people and flee every one to his own land. The realest place on earth is jail, where whites stay with whites and Asians with Asians, because everyone turns to their own tribe for protection; the Most High created every species and every nation distinct. -

Israel is a scattered sheep the lions have driven away; first the king of Assyria devoured him, and last Nebuchadnezzar of Babylon broke his bones. The Most High will punish the king of Babylon as he punished Assyria. He will bring Israel again to his habitation to feed on Carmel and Bashan. In those days the iniquity of Israel shall be sought for and there shall be none, and the sins of Judah shall not be found, for he will pardon whom he reserves.

Go up against the land of Merathaim and against Pekod; waste and utterly destroy. How is the hammer of the whole earth cut asunder and broken, and Babylon become a desolation among the nations? The Most High laid a snare and Babylon was taken unaware, because she strove against the Lord. He has opened his armory and brought forth the weapons of his indignation. Every missile, nuke, and bomb these nations think they own, the Most High calls his armory. A black man, the Most High God, and his son Christ are the most powerful beings, and all that the nations possess belongs to him. -

Come against her from the utmost border, open her storehouses, and destroy her utterly; slay all her bullocks and let them go to the slaughter, for their day is come. The voice of them that flee out of Babylon declares in Zion the vengeance of the Lord, the vengeance of his temple. Zion is the temple of the Lord, which is his people.

Call together the archers against Babylon; camp against it round about and let none escape. Recompense her according to her work, for she has been proud against the Holy One of Israel. Her young men shall fall in the streets and all her men of war be cut off in that day. There are many teenagers and young men in Esau's army, and this is why so many of their young men are put to death.

Behold, the Most High is against thee, O thou most proud, for thy day is come. The most proud shall stumble and fall, and none shall raise him up, and a fire is kindled in his cities that devours all around him.

The children of Israel and the children of Judah were oppressed together. That is the so-called blacks, Hispanics, and Native Americans, seen together in the ghettos, projects, and slums, last hired and first fired. All that took them captive held them fast and refused to let them go, but their Redeemer is strong; the Lord of hosts is his name, and he will thoroughly plead their cause. The other nations fare well among us because we give them our business, while we own no banks, no Walmarts, and support neither our own businesses nor one another.

A sword is upon the Chaldeans, upon her princes and wise men, upon her liars, her mighty men, her horses and chariots, and upon all the mingled people, the melting pot, and they shall become as women. A sword is upon her treasures and they shall be robbed, and a drought is upon her waters and they shall be dried up, for it is a land of graven images, and they are mad upon their idols.

The wild beasts of the desert and the owl shall dwell there, and it shall be inhabited no more from generation to generation. This is a future prophecy, because ancient Babylon in Iraq still has people living there now. As the Most High overthrew Sodom and Gomorrah and the neighboring cities, so shall no man abide there, neither shall any son of man dwell therein.

A people comes from the north, a great nation and many kings raised up from the coasts of the earth; they are cruel and will not show mercy, set in array like men to the battle against the daughter of Babylon. Who is the daughter of Babylon? It is Edom. The king of Babylon hears the report of them and his hands wax feeble, and anguish takes hold of him as a woman in travail. -

He shall come up like a lion from the swelling of Jordan against the habitation of the strong, but the Most High makes them suddenly run away; who is the chosen man he will appoint over her? Hear the counsel of the Lord against Babylon: surely the least of the flock shall draw them out and make their habitation desolate. At the noise of the taking of Babylon, the earth is moved and the cry is heard among the nations.

The Most High raises against Babylon a destroying wind and sends fanners to fan her and empty her land. Spare not her young men; destroy utterly all her host. The slain fall in the land of the Chaldeans, thrust through in her streets, for Israel has not been forsaken, nor Judah of his God, though their land was filled with sin against the Holy One of Israel.

Israel and Judah have not been forsaken of the Most High. Flee out of the midst of Babylon and deliver every man his soul; do not be cut off in her iniquity, for this is the time of the Lord's vengeance. -

Babylon has been a golden cup in the Lord's hand that made all the earth drunken; the nations drank of her wine and are mad. All the nations partook, and even the children of Israel were made to drink of the cup of our own destruction. Babylon is suddenly fallen and destroyed. We would have healed Babylon, but she is not healed; forsake her, and let everyone go into his own country.
Her judgment reaches unto heaven and is lifted up even to the skies. The Most High has brought forth our righteousness; come, and let us declare in Zion the work of the Lord our God.

Make bright the arrows and gather the shields; the Lord has raised up the spirit of the kings of the Medes, for his device against Babylon is to destroy it, the vengeance of his temple. Set up the standard upon the walls of Babylon, make the watch strong, set the watchmen, and prepare the ambushes. The standard is the Bible, and the men are made ready, for the Most High has both devised and done what he spoke.

Babylon dwells upon many waters, abundant in treasures, but thine end is come. She dwells upon many waters because her embassies reach into every land, from South Africa to Europe to the Philippines; her treasure was built on the backs of the slaves and the stolen Western Hemisphere. The Lord of hosts has sworn to fill her with men as with caterpillars who lift up a shout against her. She is destroyed from within, because being a melting pot, the other nations infiltrate and destroy America from the inside out, the way a caterpillar becomes an infestation that devours a whole land.

He made the earth by his power, established the world by his wisdom, and stretched out the heavens by his understanding; he brings the wind out of his treasures. Every man is brutish in his knowledge, and every founder is confounded by the graven image, for his molten image is falsehood and there is no breath in them. But the portion of Jacob is not like them, for he is the former of all things, and Israel is the rod of his inheritance.

Thou art my battle-ax and weapons of war; with thee the Most High breaks in pieces the nations and destroys kingdoms, the horse and his rider, the chariot and his rider. With thee he breaks in pieces man and woman, old and young, the young man and the maid, the shepherd and his flock, the husbandman and his oxen, and the captains and rulers. The sisters who love feminism had better humble down, because the woman is named right alongside the man. -

The Most High will render unto Babylon and to all the inhabitants of Chaldea all the evil they have done in Zion. Behold, he is against thee, O destroying mountain that destroys all the earth. He will stretch out his hand, roll her down from the rocks, and make her a burnt mountain; they shall take of her no stone for a corner nor foundation, but she shall be desolate forever.

Set up a standard in the land, blow the trumpet among the nations, and prepare the nations against her; call the kingdoms of Ararat, Minni, and Ashkenaz, and appoint a captain against her. Prepare the nations with the king of the Medes, the captains, the rulers, and all the land of his dominion against Babylon.

The land trembles and sorrows, for every purpose of the Lord is performed against Babylon to make it a desolation without inhabitant. The mighty men of Babylon forbear to fight and remain in their holds; their might fails and they become as women. One post runs to meet another to tell the king of Babylon that his city is taken at one end and the passages are stopped. The daughter of Babylon is like a threshing floor; it is time to thresh her, and the time of her harvest shall come.

Nebuchadnezzar has devoured Israel, crushed her, made her an empty vessel, and swallowed her like a dragon. Let the violence done to Zion be upon Babylon, and her blood upon the inhabitants of Chaldea. The Most High will plead Zion's cause, take vengeance for her, and dry up Babylon's sea and springs. Babylon shall become heaps, a dwelling place for dragons, an astonishment and a hissing without inhabitant.

They roar together like lions and yell as lions' whelps. In their heat the Most High makes their feasts and makes them drunken, that they may sleep a perpetual sleep and not wake. He brings them down like lambs to the slaughter, like rams with the he-goats.

How is Sheshach taken, the praise of the whole earth surprised, and Babylon become an astonishment among the nations? The sea is come up upon Babylon, covered with the multitude of its waves. Her cities are a desolation, a dry land and a wilderness, where no man dwells and no son of man passes by.

The Most High will punish Bel in Babylon and bring out of his mouth what he has swallowed, and the wall of Babylon shall fall. My people, go out of the midst of her and deliver every man his soul from the fierce anger of the Lord. A rumor shall come one year and another rumor the next, with violence in the land and ruler against ruler. Do not let your heart faint at the rumor that is heard.

The days come when the Most High does judgment upon the graven images of Babylon, and her whole land is confounded and her slain fall in her midst. Then heaven and earth and all in them sing for Babylon, for the spoiler comes from the north. As Babylon caused the slain of Israel to fall, so at Babylon shall fall the slain of all the earth.

Ye that have escaped the sword, go away, stand not still, remember the Lord afar off, and let Jerusalem come into your mind. We are confounded because strangers have come into the sanctuaries of the Lord's house. Though Babylon should mount up to heaven and fortify the height of her strength, yet from the Most High shall spoilers come unto her.

A cry and great destruction come from Babylon, for the Lord has spoiled her. Her mighty men are taken and their bows broken, and the Lord of recompense shall surely requite. He makes drunk her princes, wise men, captains, rulers, and mighty men, that they sleep a perpetual sleep and not wake. The broad walls of Babylon shall be utterly broken and her high gates burned with fire, and the people shall labor in vain.

Jeremiah commanded Seraiah, when he went with Zedekiah to Babylon, to read all the evil written against Babylon and then declare that the Most High has spoken to cut off this place forever. After reading the book, Seraiah was to bind a stone to it and cast it into the midst of the Euphrates, saying, thus shall Babylon sink and not rise from the evil the Most High brings upon her. Thus far are the words of Jeremiah. Rejoice in the destruction of our enemies, which is the salvation of the righteous. --- Topics: [Esau and Edom](/encyclopedia/esau-and-edom) · [Idolatry](/encyclopedia/idolatry) · [The Covenant](/encyclopedia/the-covenant) · [The Feasts of the Most High](/encyclopedia/the-feasts-of-the-most-high) · [The Priesthood](/encyclopedia/the-priesthood)

I will stand upon my watch, and set me upon the tower, and will watch to see what he will say unto me, and what I shall answer when I am reproved. Write the vision, and make it plain upon tables, that he may run that readeth it. For the vision is yet for an appointed time, but at the end it shall speak, and not lie: though it tarry, wait for it; because it will surely come, it will not tarry. Behold, his soul which is lifted up is not upright in him: but the just shall live by his faith.

Woe to him that increaseth that which is not his! how long? and to him that ladeth himself with thick clay! Because thou hast spoiled many nations, all the remnant of the people shall spoil thee; because of men's blood, and for the violence of the land, of the city, and of all that dwell therein. Woe to him that coveteth an evil covetousness to his house, that he may set his nest on high, that he may be delivered from the power of evil! For the stone shall cry out of the wall, and the beam out of the timber shall answer it.

Woe to him that buildeth a town with blood, and stablisheth a city by iniquity! The people shall labour in the very fire, and the people shall weary themselves for very vanity. For the earth shall be filled with the knowledge of the glory of the Lord, as the waters cover the sea. Woe unto him that giveth his neighbour drink, that puttest thy bottle to him, and makest him drunken also, that thou mayest look on their nakedness! What profiteth the graven image that the maker thereof hath graven it; the molten image, and a teacher of lies, that the maker of his work trusteth therein, to make dumb idols? Woe unto him that saith to the wood, Awake; to the dumb stone, Arise, it shall teach! Behold, it is laid over with gold and silver, and there is no breath at all in the midst of it. But the Lord is in his holy temple: let all the earth keep silence before him. --- Topics: [Idolatry](/encyclopedia/idolatry) · [Sacrifice and Atonement](/encyclopedia/sacrifice-and-atonement) · [The Feasts of the Most High](/encyclopedia/the-feasts-of-the-most-high)

name: The elders with idols in the temple (Ezekiel 8)
charge: The image of jealousy; creeping things on the walls; women weeping for Tammuz; twenty-five men worshipping the sun with their backs to the temple
summary: Carried in vision to Jerusalem, Ezekiel was shown four scenes of greater and greater abomination inside the house of the Lord: an idol at the gate, seventy elders with censers in a chamber of painted beasts, women mourning a pagan god, and men between the porch and the altar bowing east to the sun. The elders said, the Lord seeth us not.
offense: In Ezekiel's vision, the Lord showed him abominations within the precincts of the sanctuary: the image of jealousy, idolatrous pictures in hidden chambers, elders offering incense, women weeping for Tammuz, and men worshipping the sun with their backs toward the temple. Those practicing secret worship said that the Lord did not see and had forsaken the earth. The hidden rites stood beside violence in the land. The sanctuary's location did not sanctify what was being done within it. God brought the prophet through one disclosure after another so that the judgment could not be mistaken for an unprovoked abandonment.
judgment: The executioners in the vision were commanded to begin at the sanctuary. A mark first distinguished those who sighed and cried over the abominations; proximity to the temple was not the distinction that preserved them. Judgment began with the ancient men before the house. Ezekiel also saw the glory of the Lord move from the threshold to the cherubims and stand at the east gate. The presence upon which Jerusalem presumed was departing. The vision exposed both the sins the people thought concealed and the false security they placed in the building they had defiled.

Those practicing secret worship said that the Lord did not see and had forsaken the earth.

The hidden rites stood beside violence in the land. The sanctuary's location did not sanctify what was being done within it. God brought the prophet through one disclosure after another so that the judgment could not be mistaken for an unprovoked abandonment.

verses.text: 5Then said he unto me, Son of man, lift up thine eyes now the way toward the north. So I lifted up mine eyes the way toward the north, and behold northward at the gate of the altar this image of jealousy in the entry. 6He said furthermore unto me, Son of man, seest thou what they do? even the great abominations that the house of Israel committeth here, that I should go far off from my sanctuary? but turn thee yet again, and thou shalt see greater abominations.

entries.commentary: Certain of the elders of Israel came and sat before Ezekiel, and the word of the Lord said these men have set up their idols in their hearts, setting up something above God, and put the stumbling block of their iniquity before their face. The Most High asks whether He should be inquired of at all by them. Every man of the house of Israel that sets up his idols in his heart and comes to the prophet, the Lord will answer according to the multitude of his idols, that He may take the house of Israel in their own heart, because they are all estranged from Him through their idols and spiritual idolatry.

The Most High tells the house of Israel to repent, come back to His laws, and turn themselves from their idols and away from all their abominations. Every one of the house of Israel, or the stranger that sojourns in Israel, who separates himself from Him and sets up idols in his heart and comes to a prophet to inquire, the Lord will answer by Himself and set His face against that man. He will make him a sign and a proverb, meaning a curse, and cut him off from the midst of His people as an example, that they may know He is the Lord.

If a prophet is deceived when he has spoken a thing, the Lord Himself has deceived that prophet; do not try to deceive yourself in this truth, and when we get counsel we should take it and keep it moving. He will stretch out His hand upon that prophet and destroy him from the midst of His people Israel, and both shall bear the punishment of their iniquity. This is so the house of Israel may go no more astray from Him nor be polluted any more with their transgressions, but be His people and He their God. -

The word of the Lord came saying that when a land sins by trespassing grievously, He will stretch out His hand upon it, break the staff of its bread, and send famine to cut off man and beast. Though these three men, Noah, Daniel, and Job, were in it, they should deliver but their own souls by their righteousness. No one can save anyone else; it does not matter who you are or what your status is in Israel, you have to save yourself by your own righteousness.

If He causes noisome beasts to pass through the land and spoil it so that it is desolate and no man may pass through, this is one of His judgments. Though these three men were in it, as the Lord lives they shall deliver neither sons nor daughters; they only shall be delivered by their righteousness, but the land shall be desolate.

If He brings a sword upon that land to cut off man and beast, though these three men were in it, they shall deliver neither sons nor daughters. They only shall deliver themselves by their righteousness.

If He sends a pestilence into the land and pours out His fury upon it in blood to cut off man and beast, though Noah, Daniel, and Job were in it, they shall deliver neither son nor daughter. They shall but deliver their own souls by their righteousness; everyone has to work out their own righteousness in fear and trembling, delivering their own soul by keeping the Most High's commandments. -

How much more when the Most High sends His four sore judgments upon Jerusalem, the sword, the famine, the noisome beast, and the pestilence, to cut off man and beast; and these are not just for back then but for today. Behold, a remnant shall be left, both sons and daughters, that shall be brought forth unto you, and you shall see their ways and their doings. You shall be comforted concerning the evil the Most High brought upon Jerusalem when you see their ways, and you shall know He has not done without cause all that He has done in it. --- Topics: [Esau and Edom](/encyclopedia/esau-and-edom) · [Idolatry](/encyclopedia/idolatry)

Hearken, O Israel: hearken means listen, pay attention, and there is a difference between hearing and listening. The statutes and judgments are taught for to do them; knowing you are an Israelite is only half the battle. The main thing is applying the scriptures, doing what the Most High is telling you to do, that ye may live. The promise is to go in and possess the land, and possessing land is true wealth: your milk and honey, your cattle, your agriculture, where you cultivate and take care of your family. It is not the diamonds, the cars, the sneakers, or the newest phone; a big house with no land is not wealth, and that is why the heathen boxes our people into apartments.

Ye shall not add unto the word, neither diminish ought from it. This was spoken around 1500 BC, and on the last page of the Bible the same charge closes the book: the prophets across millenniums and captivities all speak the same thing, Moses, Isaiah, Jeremiah, Christ, and John, and that consistency proves the Bible is a true book, because twenty people cannot keep one story straight for five minutes. The watered down versions such as the NIV and ESV show what taking away looks like: many of them remove [Matthew 18:11](/bible/matthew/18#v11) and other scriptures, and they have taken out the Apocrypha.

Your eyes have seen what the Lord did because of Baal-peor: all the men that followed Baal-peor were destroyed from among the people, and this recalls the history of Balaam. Balaam was a Midianite, an Ishmaelite. But ye that did cleave unto the Lord your God are alive every one of you this day: those who said they would not go after that foolishness were saved alive. The Bible is that simple, and it destroys the confusion of the world's religions: keep the commandments and live, or break them and die. Follow after the ways of the nations and be put to death; keep the laws, statutes, and commandments and have life.

Keep therefore and do them, for this is your wisdom and your understanding in the sight of the nations. Israel deals with the Almighty; having the omnipotent God on your side is the wisdom the nations do not have, and it is what they are mad at. When Israel keeps the laws it makes them a peculiar nation: peculiar by definition means characteristic of only one person, group, or thing, and different from the usual or normal. The Most High made this people different and set them above the other nations. Royal means of a kingly ancestry, and the King of kings is Christ; but rulership belongs to the lineage only when the laws are kept. When Israel is fallen into sin, the people look worse than the nations instead of wise and understanding. Which shall hear all these statutes and say, surely this great nation is a wise and understanding people: they may not say it out loud today, but when they see Israel united in Christ and in order, that is what rises in their minds.

What nation is there so great, who hath God so nigh unto them? The Most High is near unto Israel in all things they call upon him for, and no nation has statutes and judgments so righteous as this law. When Israel keeps the laws, statutes, and commandments, they are the light of the world; in the days when the brothers and sisters were in order, the nations looked on and marveled at what nation this was, so great and so beautiful.

Take heed to thyself and keep thy soul diligently, lest thou forget the things thine eyes have seen; and teach them thy sons, and thy sons' sons. These are generational commandments: children's children, cousins' cousins, so that no generation misses a beat. Gather me the people together, and I will make them hear my words, that they may learn to fear me all the days that they shall live upon the earth, and that they may teach their children. Why learn to fear the Most High? Verses 3 and 4 of this same chapter answer it: those that followed the idols were destroyed, and those that cleaved to him are alive. Follow after idols, after the nations and their religions, and he will destroy you. Fear is the first spirit required, before love, before confession: fear and respect go hand in hand, and if you fear him you will do what he says, and do it with joyfulness and gladness for the reward no nation can touch.

The mountain burned with fire unto the midst of heaven, and the Most High spake out of the midst of the fire; ye heard the voice of the words, but saw no similitude. He declared his covenant, even ten commandments: the ten are the umbrella over all the other commandments, the sub-laws and sub-statutes beneath them. And he wrote them upon two tables of stone. The laws men call the mosaic laws did not belong to Moses; they were written with the finger of God and given to Israel by Christ, and they endure for ever.

The Most High commanded Moses at that time to teach the statutes and judgments, and Israel is charged to take good heed, for ye saw no manner of similitude on the day the Lord spake in Horeb. No similitude means he spoke plainly and clearly, not in dark speeches: when the commandments were given there was no arguing over what they meant. Fringes on the borders of the garments, no swine, thou shalt not kill; it was simple and easy to understand. Lest ye corrupt yourselves and make a graven image, the similitude of any figure, the likeness of male or female: Israel had come out of Egypt, where graven images filled the land and where the likeness of the female was worshipped. Egypt is where feminism was already incorporated: Hathor the cattle goddess and Qetesh the goddess of beauty were among the idols learned there, so the Most High had to say plainly, no deity male or female. There is no goddess in the scriptures.

The likeness of any beast on the earth goes back to idols like Heqet the frog god and Sobek the god of the river; the likeness of any winged fowl to Horus the falcon; anything that creepeth on the ground to the beetles, flies, and locusts they deified; any fish in the waters to Sobek and to Dagon the fish god of the Babylonians, whose symbolism carries into pagan imagery to this day. The eagle and the falcon symbols of the powers of this world trace back to the gods and goddesses of Egypt, because this present power is spiritual Egypt and takes after her. Lest thou lift up thine eyes unto heaven and be driven to worship the sun, the moon, and the stars: that is Ra the sun god and Nut the sky goddess, and it is also astrology, the zodiac, and witchcraft today. Calling yourself a Gemini or a Taurus is the same star worship; none of it is the way to the kingdom, and it was filth learned in Egypt. Why worship what the Most High created to serve you? The sun, moon, and stars are ordinances that keep their order and do their job, which is why the new moon can be kept; Israel is the one out of order when the commandments are not kept.

The Lord hath taken you and brought you forth out of the iron furnace, even out of Egypt, to be unto him a people of inheritance. Furthermore the Lord was angry with me for your sakes: again Moses lays his barred crossing on the people. It is how the workers feel when they go out to preach truth and catch anger for it; you are not arguing with the messenger, you are mad at the Bible, so speak the oracles and neither add nor diminish to please anybody. Moses must die in this land and not go over Jordan, but ye shall go over and possess that good land; he kept repeating it, longing for what he would not see.

Take heed unto yourselves, lest ye forget the covenant and make a graven image, for the Lord thy God is a consuming fire, even a jealous God. When children's children are begotten and the stay in the land grows long, corruption creeps in; make the graven image and do evil to provoke him, and ye shall soon utterly perish from off the land. Heaven and earth are called to witness against Israel this day; the warning was on record before it ever came to pass.

And the Lord shall scatter you among the nations, and ye shall be left few in number among the heathen: this is future prophecy of the scattering to the four corners of the earth. And there ye shall serve gods, the work of men's hands, wood and stone: the wood is the cross of christianity and the stone is the kaaba stone at Mecca. Israel would fall into the heathen religions, christianity and islam, in the lands of the scattering.

But if from thence thou shalt seek the Lord thy God, thou shalt find him, if thou seek him with all thy heart and with all thy soul; the seeking begins with the spirit of fear, to get right with the Most High. When thou art in tribulation, and all these things are come upon thee, even in the latter days: the latter days began when Christ came, for God who spake in time past by the prophets hath in these last days spoken by his Son. And shalt be obedient unto his voice: the voice of the Most High tells you to keep his commandments. If someone claims God spoke to him in a dream and told him everything but obedience, that is not the voice of the Most High. For the Lord thy God is a merciful God; he will not forsake thee, nor destroy thee, nor forget the covenant of thy fathers.

Ask now of the days that are past, since the day that God created man upon the earth: you are supposed to search out your forefathers and look up your history, and not slavery only, but the reign under David and Solomon and the empires where Israel ruled, and slavery too, because failing to keep the laws is why the people went into it. Did ever people hear the voice of God speaking out of the midst of the fire and live? Hath God assayed to take him a nation from the midst of another nation, by temptations, by signs, and by wonders, and by war, and by a mighty hand? There is no such history anywhere else; the Most High did this for Israel alone. Unto thee it was shewed, that thou mightest know that the Lord he is God; there is none else beside him.

Out of heaven he made thee to hear his voice, that he might instruct thee; and because he loved thy fathers, therefore he chose their seed after them, and brought thee out of Egypt in his sight with his mighty power. To drive out nations from before thee greater and mightier than thou art: they had more economic might and more military power, but the Most High delivered Israel out of their hands, and to this day the twelve tribes are still here. Know therefore this day, and consider it in thine heart, that the Lord he is God in heaven above and upon the earth beneath; there is none else. Consider is the key word: really appreciate all of it, for Israel could have been born of any nation, but the Most High ordained this people, and the way to cash in is simply keeping the commandments.

Thou shalt keep therefore his statutes and his commandments, that it may go well with thee and with thy children after thee, and that thou mayest prolong thy days upon the earth. This is the solution. The voting, protesting, and marching have never worked and never will; trust in the Most High and keep his laws, and he will take care of his people with long days, families, and the land.

Then Moses severed three cities on this side Jordan toward the sunrising, that the slayer which killed his neighbour unawares, and hated him not in times past, might flee thither and live: Bezer in the wilderness for the Reubenites, Ramoth in Gilead for the Gadites, and Golan in Bashan for the Manassites. The chapter closes with the summary: this is the law, the testimonies, the statutes, and the judgments which Moses spake unto the children of Israel after they came forth out of Egypt, in the land of Sihon and of Og, the two kings of the Amorites.

verses.text: 1Moreover the spirit lifted me up, and brought me unto the east gate of the Lord’s house, which looketh eastward: and behold at the door of the gate five and twenty men; among whom I saw Jaazaniah the son of Azur, and Pelatiah the son of Benaiah, princes of the people. 2Then said he unto me, Son of man, these are the men that devise mischief, and give wicked counsel in this city: 3Which say, It is not near; let us build houses: this city is the caldron, and we be the flesh. 4Therefore prophesy against them, prophesy, O son of man.

7Therefore thus saith the Lord God; Your slain whom ye have laid in the midst of it, they are the flesh, and this city is the caldron: but I will bring you forth out of the midst of it. 8Ye have feared the sword; and I will bring a sword upon you, saith the Lord God. 9And I will bring you out of the midst thereof, and deliver you into the hands of strangers, and will execute judgments among you. 10Ye shall fall by the sword; I will judge you in the border of Israel; and ye shall know that I am the Lord. 11This city shall not be your caldron, neither shall ye be the flesh in the midst thereof; but I will judge you in the border of Israel: 12And ye shall know that I am the Lord: for ye have not walked in my statutes, neither

entries.commentary: The spirit lifted Ezekiel up and brought him to the east gate of the Lord's house, where he saw five and twenty men, among whom were Jaazaniah the son of Azur and Pelatiah the son of Benaiah, princes of the people; remember the name Pelatiah. These are the men that devise mischief and give wicked counsel in the city, telling the people it is not near, let us build houses, this city is the cauldron and we are the flesh. Babylon had already carried away the northern kingdom and some of our people were already in captivity, yet the counsel was that Jerusalem, the iron pot, would protect them, giving the people a false sense of security. The Most High tells Ezekiel to prophesy against these twenty-five wicked men.

The spirit of the Most High fell upon Ezekiel and told him to say that He knows the things that come into their minds, every one of them. They had multiplied their slain in the city and filled the streets with the dead, for the land was full of blood and violence. The dead they laid in the midst of the city are the flesh, and the city is the cauldron, but the Most High will bring them forth out of the midst of it. Because they feared the sword, He will bring a sword upon them, meaning He will bring the nations against Jerusalem.

The Most High will deliver them into the hands of strangers, the nations, and execute judgments among them so that they fall by the sword in the border of Israel and know that He is the Lord. This city will not be their cauldron, neither will they be the flesh in the midst of it; He will judge them in the border of Israel. We get judged because we do not keep the Most High's laws, the same then as today; they had not walked in His statutes but had done after the manners of the heathen around about them. -

While Ezekiel was prophesying, Pelatiah the son of Benaiah died, one of the wicked men that had given wicked counsel, put to death by the Most High. Ezekiel fell upon his face and cried with a loud voice, asking if the Most High would make a full end of the remnant of Israel.

The word of the Lord came again, calling them Ezekiel's brethren, the men of his kindred and the house of Israel, unto whom the inhabitants of Jerusalem had said, get you far from the Lord, this land is given to us in possession. Although the Most High has cast them far off among the heathen and scattered them among the countries, He will yet be to them as a little sanctuary in the countries where they come. Everywhere we are scattered the little sanctuaries are a comfort, just like the schools IUIC is setting up in all our scattered lands, where you come and learn the word of God.

The Most High will gather them from the people and assemble them out of the countries where they were scattered and give them the land of Israel, and they shall take away all its detestable things and abominations. He will give them one heart and put a new spirit within them, putting all of us on one accord with the word of God. He will take the stony heart, the rebellious mind that rebels against His laws, out of their flesh and give them a heart of flesh, a future prophecy of what will happen, that they may walk in His statutes and be His people. But as for those whose heart walks after their detestable things, the wicked Israelites who will not do this, He will recompense their way upon their own heads; there is a big payback when you will not keep His laws.

The cherubims lifted up their wings and the wheels beside them, and the glory of the God of Israel was over them above. The glory of the Lord went up from the midst of the city and stood upon the mountain on the east side, then the spirit took Ezekiel up in a vision by the spirit of God into Chaldea, to them of the captivity. The vision went up from Ezekiel, and he spoke unto the captives in Babylon all the things the Most High had showed him. -

The word of the Most High comes to Ezekiel to judge the bloody city, Jerusalem, and show her all her abominations. She has shed blood in her midst and made idols against herself to defile herself, causing her days to draw near. Because of her idolatry and wickedness, once judgment comes He makes her a reproach unto the heathen and a mocking to all countries, both near and far.

The princes of Israel used their power to shed blood, set light by father and mother, dealt by oppression with the stranger, and vexed the fatherless and the widow. They despised His holy things, profaned His sabbaths, carried tales to shed blood, ate upon the mountains, and committed lewdness in her midst. They broke all manner of the immoral laws of [Leviticus 18](/bible/leviticus/18), committing abomination with a neighbor's wife, defiling a daughter-in-law, and humbling a sister, doing the doings of the other nations. They took gifts to shed blood, being put on the take and paid off to shed a man's blood, took usury and increase, and greedily gained by extortion, and have forgotten Him; these are wicked leaders.

The Most High smites His hand at their dishonest gain and at the blood shed in their midst, asking whether their heart can endure or their hands be strong in the day He deals with them. He will scatter them among the heathen, disperse them in the countries, and consume their filthiness out of them, and they shall know that He is the Lord when they take their inheritance in the sight of the heathen.

The house of Israel is become dross to Him, all brass, tin, iron, and lead, the dross of silver in the midst of the furnace. He will gather them into the midst of Jerusalem as men gather metal into the furnace, and blow the fire of His wrath upon them. They shall be melted in the midst of the furnace as silver is melted, and shall know that He is the Lord who poured out His fury upon them.

The land is not cleansed nor rained upon, and there is a conspiracy of her prophets in her midst, like a roaring lion ravening the prey, devouring souls and making many widows; the leaders of Israel are very corrupt. Her priests violated His law and profaned His holy things, putting no difference between the holy and the profane or the clean and the unclean and hiding their eyes from His sabbaths, just like today where our people put no difference between anything, and it is called Christianity. Her princes are like wolves ravening the prey to shed blood and destroy souls for dishonest gain, and her prophets daub them with untempered mortar, seeing vanity and divining lies, saying thus saith the Lord God when He has not spoken. The people used oppression, exercised robbery, and vexed the poor and needy and the stranger wrongfully, showing the same oppression, robbery, and extortion by the leadership. He sought for a man to make up the hedge and stand in the gap before Him so He would not destroy the land, but He found none, so He poured out His indignation and consumed them with the fire of His wrath. -

Hear, I pray you, O heads of Jacob, and ye princes of the house of Israel; Is it not for you to know judgment? Who hate the good, and love the evil; who pluck off their skin from off them, and their flesh from off their bones; who also eat the flesh of my people. Then shall they cry unto the Lord, but he will not hear them: he will even hide his face from them at that time, as they have behaved themselves ill in their doings.

Thus saith the Lord concerning the prophets that make my people err, that bite with their teeth, and cry, Peace; and he that putteth not into their mouths, they even prepare war against him. Night shall be unto you, that ye shall not have a vision; and it shall be dark unto you, that ye shall not divine. Then shall the seers be ashamed, and the diviners confounded, for there is no answer of God. But truly I am full of power by the spirit of the Lord, and of judgment, and of might, to declare unto Jacob his transgression, and to Israel his sin.

Ye heads of the house of Jacob, and princes of the house of Israel, that abhor judgment, and pervert all equity; they build up Zion with blood, and Jerusalem with iniquity. The heads thereof judge for reward, and the priests thereof teach for hire, and the prophets thereof divine for money: yet will they lean upon the Lord, and say, Is not the Lord among us? none evil can come upon us. Therefore shall Zion for your sake be plowed as a field, and Jerusalem shall become heaps, and the mountain of the house as the high places of the forest.
