verses.text: 10For thy violence against thy brother Jacob shame shall cover thee, and thou shalt be cut off for ever. 11In the day that thou stoodest on the other side, in the day that the strangers carried away captive his forces, and foreigners entered into his gates, and cast lots upon Jerusalem, even thou wast as one of them. 12But thou shouldest not have looked on the day of thy brother in the day that he became a stranger; neither shouldest thou have rejoiced over the children of Judah in the day of their destruction; neither shouldest thou have spoken proudly in the day of distress. 13Thou shouldest not have entered into the gate of my people in the day of their calamity; yea, thou shouldest not have looked on their affliction in the day of their calamity, nor have laid hands on their substance in the day of their calamity; 14Neither shouldest thou have stood in the crossway, to cut off those of his that did escape; neither shouldest thou have delivered up those of his that did remain in the day of distress. 15For the day of the Lord is near upon all the heathen: as thou hast done, it shall be done unto thee: thy reward shall return upon thine own head.

18And the house of Jacob shall be a fire, and the house of Joseph a flame, and the house of Esau for stubble, and they shall kindle in them, and devour them; and there shall not be any remaining of the house of Esau; for the Lord hath spoken it.

12Thus saith the Lord God; Because that Edom hath dealt against the house of Judah by taking vengeance, and hath greatly offended, and revenged himself upon them; 13Therefore thus saith the Lord God; I will also stretch out mine hand upon Edom, and will cut off man and beast from it; and I will make it desolate from Teman; and they of Dedan shall fall by the sword. 14And I will lay my vengeance upon Edom by the hand of my people Israel: and they shall do in Edom according to mine anger and according to my fury; and they shall know my vengeance, saith the Lord God.

entries.commentary: The vision of Obadiah, and it is spoken concerning Edom: Arise ye, and let us rise up against her in battle. Behold, I have made thee small among the heathen: thou art greatly despised. The pride of thine heart hath deceived thee, thou that dwellest in the clefts of the rock, that saith in his heart, Who shall bring me down to the ground? Though thou exalt thyself as the eagle, and though thou set thy nest among the stars, thence will I bring thee down, saith the Lord.

If thieves came to thee, if robbers by night, would they not have stolen till they had enough? If the grapegatherers came to thee, would they not leave some grapes? But Esau is searched out, and his hidden things sought up. All the men of thy confederacy have brought thee even to the border; the men that were at peace with thee have deceived thee, and prevailed against thee. They that eat thy bread have laid a wound under thee. Shall I not in that day destroy the wise men out of Edom, and understanding out of the mount of Esau? And thy mighty men, O Teman, shall be dismayed, to the end that every one of the mount of Esau may be cut off by slaughter.

For thy violence against thy brother Jacob shame shall cover thee, and thou shalt be cut off for ever. In the day that the strangers carried away captive his forces, and foreigners entered into his gates, and cast lots upon Jerusalem, even thou wast as one of them. Esau stood on the other side and took part. Thou shouldest not have looked on the day of thy brother in the day that he became a stranger; neither shouldest thou have rejoiced over the children of Judah in the day of their destruction. Thou shouldest not have entered into the gate of my people in the day of their calamity, nor have laid hands on their substance; neither shouldest thou have stood in the crossway to cut off those of his that did escape, nor have delivered up those of his that did remain in the day of distress.

For the day of the Lord is near upon all the heathen: as thou hast done, it shall be done unto thee: thy reward shall return upon thine own head. As ye have drunk upon my holy mountain, so shall all the heathen drink continually; they shall drink, and they shall swallow down, and they shall be as though they had not been.

But upon mount Zion shall be deliverance, and there shall be holiness; and the house of Jacob shall possess their possessions. The house of Jacob shall be a fire, and the house of Joseph a flame, and the house of Esau for stubble; and they shall kindle in them, and devour them; and there shall not be any remaining of the house of Esau, for the Lord hath spoken it. They of the south shall possess the mount of Esau, and they of the plain the Philistines; and they shall possess the fields of Ephraim, and the fields of Samaria; and Benjamin shall possess Gilead. Saviours shall come up on mount Zion to judge the mount of Esau; and the kingdom shall be the Lord's. --- Topics: [Esau and Edom](/encyclopedia/esau-and-edom)

He that is wounded in the stones or hath his privy member cut off shall not enter into the congregation of the Lord. This law repeats what was already given: the priests' law in Leviticus lists the same blemishes that barred a man from approaching to offer the bread of his God, including him that hath his stones broken.

A bastard shall not enter into the congregation of the Lord, even to his tenth generation: the children begotten of forbidden unions with the nations were shut out of the congregation. The prophets tie the bastard to Ashdod: a bastard shall dwell in Ashdod. Ashdod was one of the cities given to the tribe of Judah in the inheritance, but Israel did not drive out all the inhabitants and lost it. In the days of Nehemiah, Jews had married wives of Ashdod, of Ammon, and of Moab, and their children spake half in the speech of Ashdod and could not speak in the Jews' language. Why is that? Because the mothers do the raising of the children.

An Ammonite or Moabite shall not enter into the congregation of the Lord, even to their tenth generation, for ever. In the time of Nehemiah this very law was read out of the book of Moses in the audience of the people, and when they heard it our people separated from Israel all the mixed multitude whom they had intermarried with and had children with.

The reason for the ban: Ammon and Moab met not Israel with bread and with water in the way when they came forth out of Egypt, and hired Balaam the son of Beor of Pethor to curse them. The history is in Numbers: Balak the son of Zippor, king of Moab, was sore afraid because the people were many, and sent the elders of Moab and Midian with the rewards of divination to call Balaam to curse Israel. Nevertheless the Lord thy God would not hearken unto Balaam, but turned the curse into a blessing, because the Lord thy God loveth thee; therefore Israel was never to seek their peace nor their prosperity.

Thou shalt not abhor an Edomite, for he is thy brother: this was a temporary law. Edom broke the brotherly covenant; he did pursue his brother with the sword, did cast off all pity, his anger did tear perpetually, and he kept his wrath for ever. Edom's hatred is a perpetual hatred: he shed the blood of the children of Israel by the force of the sword in the time of their calamity, and as we see our people being slaughtered by Esau, that anger continues even to this very day. Thou shalt not abhor an Egyptian, because thou wast a stranger in his land: many brothers and sisters do not want to deal with that part and only want to deal with Edom, but Egypt likewise came under judgment for the violence against the children of Judah, because they shed innocent blood in their land.

When the host goeth forth against thine enemies, then keep thee from every wicked thing: when Israel went to war, they were to keep themselves from every wicked thing. The example is Achan: Israel was warned in any wise to keep from the accursed thing, lest they make the camp of Israel a curse and trouble it, and Achan the son of Carmi of the tribe of Judah took of the accursed thing, the Babylonish garment, and the anger of the Lord was kindled against the children of Israel. Because of that trespass Israel could not stand before their enemies but turned their backs, for they were accursed; the Lord would not be with them any more except they destroyed the accursed from among them, and Achan and his family and all that belonged to him were destroyed and burned, and a heap set upon them, because he broke the covenant.

Any man that was not clean by reason of uncleanness that chanceth him by night went abroad out of the camp; when evening came he washed himself with water, and when the sun was down he came into the camp again.

There was a place without the camp to go forth abroad, and a paddle upon the weapon to dig and cover that which cometh from thee: to make it plain, if you had to ease yourself, you went outside the camp to do it. Verse 14 explains why: the Lord thy God walketh in the midst of thy camp, to deliver thee and to give up thine enemies before thee; therefore shall thy camp be holy, that he see no unclean thing in thee and turn away from thee. That is what we just read happened with Achan the son of Carmi: he brought an unclean thing into the camp, and the Most High turned from Israel in battle. God says he is in the midst of Israel and none else; the Lord would go before us and fight our battles, and that is why he wanted no unclean thing in the camp, for we are holy and the camp was to be holy.

There shall be no whore of the daughters of Israel, nor a sodomite of the sons of Israel. A sodomite is the biblical word for a homosexual, and the whore of the daughters of Israel here is the same sin in the daughters, what we today would call lesbians. There is a heavy push in the world today for our men to be homosexuals and our sisters to be lesbians; popular entertainers are used to influence the younger generation to sin, just as young rappers were dressed in skirts and dresses until it became cool to be gay. This is what we have to bring our people back from: by being an example, the men being an example, the sisters being an example in the way they dress and carry themselves, and by having families, reinstituting a father and a mother in the divine order the Most High God established. Thou shalt not bring the hire of a whore or the price of a dog into the house of the Lord thy God, for even both these are abomination unto the Lord. Without are dogs: that is not the four-legged barking kind, but the other nations. Christ told a woman of another nation it is not meet to take the children's bread and cast it to dogs, and she said, Truth, Lord; and four-legged dogs did not pierce Christ's hands and feet, for the dogs that compassed him were the other nations, in that case the Romans.

Thou shalt not lend upon usury to thy brother, usury of money, of victuals, of any thing: when you read the definition of usury, that is interest. We are not to charge interest to each other when we loan each other anything. Unto a stranger thou mayest lend upon usury: the blessing is that Israel shall lend unto many nations and shall not borrow, the head and not the tail. That is our rightful place on the earth when we keep these commandments: we should lend unto them and may take usury upon what we lend to them, but we should not do that to our own people. The same law was already read in Exodus: if thou lend money to any of my people that is poor by thee, thou shalt not be to him as an usurer.

The gold has become dim and the most fine gold changed; the stones of the sanctuary are poured out at the top of every street, and the precious sons of Zion, once comparable to fine gold, are now esteemed as earthen pitchers, the work of the potter's hands. Even the sea monsters draw out the breast and give suck to their young, but the daughter of the people is become cruel like the ostrich in the wilderness; the tongue of the suckling cleaves to the roof of his mouth for thirst, and the young children ask bread and no man breaks it to them. They that fed delicately are desolate in the streets, and they that were brought up in scarlet embrace dunghills, for the punishment of the iniquity of the people is greater than the punishment of Sodom, which was overthrown in a moment. The famine of the siege was so severe that a nation once raised in the finest things was reduced to nothing, and their judgment for their sin exceeded even the sin of Sodom.

Her Nazarites were purer than snow, whiter than milk, more ruddy in body than rubies, their polishing of sapphire, but their visage is now blacker than a coal, and they are not known in the streets. The verse says their visage is blacker than a coal, which shows plainly that the Israelites are a black people; the coal is the natural color of the nation and the burning of the famine only made it darker. They that are slain with the sword are better than they that are slain with hunger, for these pine away, stricken through for want of the fruits of the field. The hands of the pitiful women sodden their own children for meat in the destruction of the people, and the Most High accomplished His fury and poured out His fierce anger, kindling a fire in Zion that devoured its foundations.

The kings of the earth and all the inhabitants of the world would not have believed that the adversary and enemy could enter the gates of Jerusalem, but it came to pass for the sins of her prophets and the iniquities of her priests that shed the blood of the just in her midst. They wandered as blind men in the streets, polluted with blood so that men could not touch their garments, and the people cried unto them, Depart, it is unclean, depart. The anger of the Most High divided them and He would no more regard them; they respected not the persons of the priests and favored not the elders, for the leadership that was supposed to guide the people had defiled itself.

Their eyes failed watching for a vain help; they watched for a nation that could not save them, looking to other countries to deliver them instead of to the Most High. Their persecutors were swifter than the eagles of heaven, pursuing them upon the mountains and laying wait for them in the wilderness, so that they could not go in their streets and their end was come. The breath of their nostrils, the anointed of the Most High, was taken in their pits, the very one under whose shadow they thought to live among the heathen.

Edom is told to rejoice and be glad in the land of Uz, but the cup shall pass through unto her also; she shall be drunken and make herself naked, for her turn of judgment is coming. The punishment of the iniquity of Zion is accomplished and the Most High will no more carry her away into captivity, but He will visit the iniquity of Edom and discover her sins.

name: The prince of Tyre
charge: Saying, I am a God, I sit in the seat of God
summary: Ezekiel's word to the ruler of the merchant city: because thine heart is lifted up, and thou hast said, I am a God, in the midst of the seas; yet thou art a man, and not God. Wiser than Daniel, richer by his traffick, and undone by both.
offense: Self-deification on the strength of trade. By the multitude of thy merchandise they have filled the midst of thee with violence, and thou hast sinned. Tyre had also rejoiced at Jerusalem's fall: aha, she is broken, I shall be replenished.
judgment: They shall bring thee down to the pit, and thou shalt die the deaths of them that are slain in the midst of the seas. Wilt thou yet say before him that slayeth thee, I am God? Nebuchadnezzar besieged the mainland city; Alexander finished the island.

entries.commentary: The Most High tells Ezekiel to say to the prince of Tyrus that because his heart is lifted up and he has said, I am a god, I sit in the seat of God in the midst of the seas, yet he is a man and not God. Though he set his heart as the heart of God and was wiser than Daniel, getting riches by his wisdom and traffic, the Most High will bring strangers upon him, the terrible of the nations, to bring him down to the pit and die the deaths of the uncircumcised by the hand of strangers.

Ezekiel takes up a lamentation upon the king of Tyrus, who was full of wisdom and perfect in beauty, in Eden the garden of God, covered with every precious stone, the anointed cherub upon the holy mountain of God, perfect in his ways until iniquity was found in him. By the multitude of his merchandise he was filled with violence and sinned, his heart lifted up because of his beauty; therefore the Most High casts him out as profane, brings forth a fire from the midst of him, and brings him to ashes in the sight of all who behold him.

The word comes against Zidon, that the Most High will be glorified in the midst of her, sending pestilence and blood into her streets and executing judgments, and they shall know that He is the Lord. There shall be no more a pricking briar nor grieving thorn to the house of Israel from those round about who despise them; when the Most High gathers Israel from the people and is sanctified in them, they shall dwell safely in the land given to His servant Jacob, build houses, and plant vineyards.

In the eleventh year, on the first day of the month, the word comes because Tyrus said against Jerusalem, Aha, she that was the gate of the peoples is broken and turned to me, so I shall be replenished now she is laid waste. Tyrus saw our loss of Jerusalem as their come-up and profit. Therefore the Most High is against Tyrus and will cause many nations to come up against her like the sea casting up its waves; they shall destroy her walls, break her towers, scrape her dust, and make her like the top of a rock, a place for spreading nets, and her daughters in the field shall be slain.

The Most High will bring Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon, a king of kings from the north, with horses, chariots, and horsemen, to slay her daughters, build a fort, cast a mount, and set engines of war against her walls and towers. Babylon serves as His sword against the nations that thought our downfall was their gain. His horses shall cover her with dust and tread down her streets; he shall slay her people, spoil her riches, prey on her merchandise, break her walls, destroy her pleasant houses, and lay her stones, timber, and dust in the midst of the water. He will cause the noise of her songs to cease and make her like the top of a rock, a place to spread nets, built no more. -

At the sound of Tyrus's fall the isles shall shake and the wounded cry, and all the princes of the sea shall come down from their thrones, lay away their robes, put off their broidered garments, and clothe themselves with trembling, sitting on the ground astonished. They shall take up a lamentation, asking how she is destroyed, that renowned city inhabited of seafaring men which was strong in the sea and caused terror on all who haunted it. This parallels the fall of the great seafaring city that reflects Esau's nation today. -

The Most High will make Tyrus a desolate city like cities uninhabited, bring up the deep upon her, and cover her with great waters, bringing her down with them that descend into the pit to the low parts of the earth. He is putting the whole island and civilization under water forever. He will make her a terror, and she shall be no more; though she be sought for, she shall never be found again, because she said Aha when we suffered judgment. The city once beautiful and top-notch is wiped out because of how it mocked the judgment of the Most High. --- Topics: [Esau and Edom](/encyclopedia/esau-and-edom) · [Idolatry](/encyclopedia/idolatry) · [Sacrifice and Atonement](/encyclopedia/sacrifice-and-atonement) · [The Covenant](/encyclopedia/the-covenant) · [The Sabbath](/encyclopedia/the-sabbath)

The words of Amos, who was among the herdmen of Tekoa, which he saw concerning Israel in the days of Uzziah king of Judah and Jeroboam the son of Joash king of Israel, two years before the earthquake. The Lord roars from Zion and utters his voice from Jerusalem, so that the habitations of the shepherds mourn and the top of Carmel withers. This chapter was read straight through without going precept upon precept.

For three transgressions of Damascus and for four, the Most High will not turn away the punishment, because they threshed Gilead with threshing instruments of iron. He will send a fire into the house of Hazael that shall devour the palaces of Benhadad, break the bar of Damascus, cut off the inhabitants of the plain of Aven and the sceptre from the house of Eden, and the people of Syria shall go into captivity unto Kir.

For three transgressions of Gaza and for four, the Most High will not turn away the punishment, because they carried away the whole captivity to deliver them up to Edom. He will send a fire on the wall of Gaza that shall devour its palaces, cut off the inhabitant from Ashdod and the sceptre from Ashkelon, turn his hand against Ekron, and the remnant of the Philistines shall perish.

For three transgressions of Tyrus and for four, the Most High will not turn away the punishment, because they delivered up the whole captivity to Edom and did not remember the brotherly covenant. He will send a fire on the wall of Tyrus that shall devour its palaces.

For three transgressions of Edom and for four, the Most High will not turn away the punishment, because Edom pursued his brother with the sword, cast off all pity, and kept his wrath forever. He will send a fire upon Teman that shall devour the palaces of Bozrah.

For three transgressions of the children of Ammon and for four, the Most High will not turn away the punishment, because they ripped up the women with child of Gilead to enlarge their border. He will kindle a fire in the wall of Rabbah that shall devour its palaces, with shouting in the day of battle and a tempest in the day of the whirlwind, and their king shall go into captivity, he and his princes together. --- Topics: [Esau and Edom](/encyclopedia/esau-and-edom) · [The Covenant](/encyclopedia/the-covenant)

The burden of Tyre calls the ships of Tarshish to howl, for the merchant harbor is laid waste with no house and no entering in. The merchants of Zidon who crossed the sea are silenced, the seed of Sihor and the harvest of the river was her revenue, and the report of Tyre brings sorrow as the report concerning Egypt did.

The inhabitants of the isle are told to pass over to Tarshish and howl, for this joyous city of ancient days is brought down, the crowning city whose merchants are princes and whose traffickers are the honourable of the earth. The Most High of hosts has purposed it, to stain the pride of all glory and bring into contempt all the honourable of the earth.

The Most High has stretched out His hand over the sea and shaken the kingdoms, giving a commandment against the merchant city to destroy its strongholds, so the oppressed virgin daughter of Zidon shall no more rejoice. The land of the Chaldeans is set forth as the example, brought to ruin, and again the ships of Tarshish are told to howl, for their strength is laid waste.

Tyre shall be forgotten seventy years, according to the days of one king, and afterward shall sing as a harlot to be remembered, committing fornication with all the kingdoms of the world. Yet at the end her merchandise and her hire shall be holiness to the Most High, not treasured nor laid up, but for them that dwell before Him to eat sufficiently and for durable clothing.

The burden of the word of the Lord in the land of Hadrach, and Damascus shall be the rest thereof: when the eyes of man, as of all the tribes of Israel, shall be toward the Lord. Tyrus did build herself a strong hold, and heaped up silver as the dust, and fine gold as the mire of the streets. Behold, the Lord will cast her out, and he will smite her power in the sea; and she shall be devoured with fire. Ashkelon shall see it, and fear; Gaza also shall see it, and be very sorrowful, and Ekron, for her expectation shall be ashamed; and the king shall perish from Gaza, and Ashkelon shall not be inhabited. These nations are judged for the part they had in the captivity, and they had a part. He that remaineth, even he, shall be for our God, and he shall be as a governor in Judah, and Ekron as a Jebusite. Those that remain are the ones who will reverence Israel and serve.
I will encamp about mine house because of the army, because of him that passeth by, and because of him that returneth: and no oppressor shall pass through them any more.

Rejoice greatly, O daughter of Zion; shout, O daughter of Jerusalem: behold, thy King cometh unto thee: he is just, and having salvation; lowly, and riding upon an ass, and upon a colt the foal of an ass. That is how you know the verse is speaking of Christ, and salvation is what Israel is waiting on him to bring. He shall speak peace unto the heathen: and his dominion shall be from sea even to sea, and from the river even to the ends of the earth.

As for thee also, by the blood of thy covenant I have sent forth thy prisoners out of the pit wherein is no water. Turn you to the strong hold, ye prisoners of hope: even to day do I declare that I will render double unto thee. We are the prisoners of hope even now.

When I have bent Judah for me, filled the bow with Ephraim, and raised up thy sons, O Zion, against thy sons, O Greece, and made thee as the sword of a mighty man. The Lord shall be seen over them, and his arrow shall go forth as the lightning: and the Lord God shall blow the trumpet, and shall go with whirlwinds of the south. The Lord their God shall save them in that day as the flock of his people: for they shall be as the stones of a crown, lifted up as an ensign upon his land.

name: Pharaoh-hophra and Egypt
charge: Saying, My river is mine own, and I have made it for myself; a staff of reed to the house of Israel
summary: Judah leaned on Egypt against Babylon, and Egypt broke under the hand like a reed and ran into it. Ezekiel's word against Pharaoh is against the boast of ownership: the river was his, he had made it. Forty years of desolation were decreed, and Egypt was to be the basest of kingdoms afterward.
offense: The Lord addressed Pharaoh as the great dragon lying in the midst of his rivers, claiming the river as his own and saying that he had made it for himself. Egypt's strength had become a ground for boasting as though its provision came from Pharaoh's own power. Egypt had also been a staff of reed to the house of Israel. When they leaned upon it, it broke and injured them. The promised support encouraged a confidence it could not sustain. The remnant's later flight to Egypt repeated that misplaced reliance after the Lord had commanded them to remain in Judah.
judgment: Ezekiel announced Pharaoh's removal under the image of hooks in the dragon's jaws. The oracle pronounced desolation, scattering, and afterward a regathering in a lowly condition, so that Egypt would no longer be Israel's confidence. These are the terms of the prophetic sentence, including the forty years named in it. Jeremiah gave the remnant a particular sign: Pharaoh Hophra would be delivered to his enemies and those seeking his life, just as Zedekiah had been delivered to Nebuchadnezzar. The kingdom chosen as a refuge was itself under judgment; its ruler could not guarantee the safety he could not secure for himself.
offenseFull: The Lord addressed Pharaoh as the great dragon lying in the midst of his rivers, claiming the river as his own and saying that he had made it for himself. Egypt's strength had become a ground for boasting as though its provision came from Pharaoh's own power.

Egypt had also been a staff of reed to the house of Israel. When they leaned upon it, it broke and injured them. The promised support encouraged a confidence it could not sustain. The remnant's later flight to Egypt repeated that misplaced reliance after the Lord had commanded them to remain in Judah.

entries.commentary: In the tenth year, tenth month, twelfth day, the word came to set Ezekiel's face against Pharaoh king of Egypt, the great dragon that lies in the midst of his rivers and says, My river is mine own, and I have made it for myself. The Most High will put hooks in his jaws, bring him up out of his rivers, and leave him thrown in the wilderness, because Egypt has been a staff of reed to the house of Israel that broke and tore their shoulder when they leaned upon it.

The Most High will bring a sword upon Egypt, cut off man and beast, and make the land utterly waste and desolate from Syene to the border of Ethiopia, uninhabited forty years, scattering the Egyptians among the nations. At the end of forty years He will bring the Egyptians again from where they were scattered into the land of Pathros, but they shall be a base kingdom, the basest of kingdoms, no more to rule over the nations or be the confidence of the house of Israel.

In the twenty-seventh year the word came that Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon caused his army to serve a great service against Tyrus, yet had no wages for it, every head made bald and every shoulder peeled. Therefore the Most High gives the land of Egypt to Nebuchadnezzar as wages for his army, because they wrought for Him; in that day the horn of the house of Israel will bud forth and Ezekiel will be given the opening of the mouth in their midst.

The word came to Jeremiah concerning all the Jews dwelling in the land of Egypt and in the country of Pathros; the Most High reminded them of all the evil He had brought on Jerusalem and the cities of Judah, now a desolation where no man dwelt, because of the wickedness they committed provoking Him to anger. They went to burn incense and serve other gods that neither they nor their fathers knew, yet the Most High sent all His servants the prophets, rising early and sending them, pleading with them not to do this abominable thing that He hates. The same work goes on today; we fill up the street corners all over the earth bringing forth the glorious gospel of the one true living God and Christ, the prophets He raised up to give warning. -

They hearkened not nor inclined their ear to turn from their wickedness and burn no incense to other gods, so the Most High's fury and anger was poured forth and kindled in the cities of Judah and the streets of Jerusalem until they were wasted and desolate. He asks why they commit this great evil against their own souls, cutting off man and woman, child and suckling out of Judah, leaving none to remain. They provoke Him to wrath with the works of their hands, burning incense to other gods in the land of Egypt where they had gone to dwell, cutting themselves off to become a curse and a reproach among all the nations of the earth. -

The Most High asks whether they have forgotten the wickedness of their fathers, the kings of Judah, their wives, and their own wickedness committed in the land of Judah and the streets of Jerusalem; they were not humbled even to that day, nor did they fear or walk in His law and statutes. Therefore He will set His face against them for evil, to cut off all Judah, and take the remnant that set their faces to go into Egypt to sojourn there; they shall all be consumed and fall by the sword and the famine, from the least to the greatest. They shall become an execration, an astonishment, a curse, and a reproach; only a small number escaping the sword shall return, for none shall return to Judah though they have a desire to dwell there. -

All the men who knew their wives had burned incense to other gods, and all the women, a great multitude in Egypt and Pathros, answered Jeremiah defiantly. These men did not rule their houses well and had no authority over their households; their wives were in the midst of idolatry, the same disorder we see in this place spiritually called Egypt, in Babylon the great today. They said they would not hearken to the word spoken in the name of the Most High but would perform their vows to burn incense to the queen of heaven and pour out drink offerings, claiming they had plenty of victuals and saw no evil until they left off, and then wanted all things and were consumed by the sword and famine. The women declared they made their cakes to worship her and poured out drink offerings without their men; the times women gather together without their men, such as baby showers with cakes and drinks and partying, are burning incense to other gods to keep in mind.

Jeremiah answered all the people, men and women, that the incense they burned in the cities of Judah and the streets of Jerusalem, they and their fathers, kings, and princes, the Most High remembered and it came into His mind. The Most High could no longer bear the evil of their doings and the abominations they committed, therefore their land became a desolation, an astonishment, and a curse without an inhabitant as at that day. This evil happened to them because they burned incense and sinned against the Most High and did not obey His voice nor walk in His law, statutes, and testimonies.

Jeremiah told all the people and all the women that they and their wives had both spoken with their mouths and fulfilled with their hands their vows to burn incense to the queen of heaven, and would surely accomplish them. Therefore the Most High swore by His great name that His name shall no more be named in the mouth of any man of Judah in all Egypt, saying "The Lord GOD liveth"; He will watch over them for evil and not for good until they are consumed by the sword and famine. Only a small number escaping the sword shall return out of Egypt into Judah, and all the remnant that went to Egypt shall know whose words shall stand, His or theirs.

The Most High gives a sign that He will punish them in that place so they may know His words shall surely stand against them for evil; He will give Pharaoh-hophra king of Egypt into the hand of his enemies as He gave Zedekiah king of Judah into the hand of Nebuchadnezzar. Evil does not come merely by chance; the Most High brings that evil upon us when we turn from Him and follow our own mind, sinning against the one true living God in Christ. -

The word of the Most High came to Jeremiah against the gentiles, against Egypt and the army of Pharaoh-necho king of Egypt by the river Euphrates at Carchemish, which Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon smote in the fourth year of Jehoiakim. The Egyptians are gentiles and heathens; they are called to order the buckler and shield, draw near to battle, harness the horses, furnish the spears, and put on the brigandines. Yet the Most High has seen them dismayed and turned back, their mighty ones beaten down and fleeing without looking back, for fear was round about; the swift shall not flee away nor the mighty man escape, stumbling and falling toward the north by the river Euphrates.

Egypt rises up like a flood whose waters are moved like the rivers, boasting he will go up and cover the earth and destroy the city and its inhabitants, calling forth his horses, chariots, and mighty men, the Ethiopians, Libyans, and Lydians that handle the shield and bend the bow. But this is the day of the Lord GOD of hosts, a day of vengeance to avenge Him of His adversaries; the sword shall devour and be made drunk with their blood, for the Most High has a sacrifice in the north country by the river Euphrates. The virgin daughter of Egypt is told to go up into Gilead and take balm, but in vain shall she use many medicines, for she shall not be cured; the nations have heard of her shame and her cry filled the land as her mighty men stumbled and fell together.

The Most High spoke to Jeremiah how Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon should come and smite the land of Egypt; the word is to be declared in Migdol, Noph, and Tahpanhes, calling them to stand fast and prepare, for the sword shall devour round about them. Their valiant men are swept away and stand not because the Most High drove them; they fall one upon another and say let us go again to our own people and the land of our nativity from the oppressing sword. Pharaoh king of Egypt is but a noise who has passed the time appointed; as surely as Tabor is among the mountains and Carmel by the sea, so shall the conqueror come, and the daughter dwelling in Egypt must furnish herself to go into captivity, for Noph shall be waste and desolate without inhabitant.

Egypt is like a very fair heifer, but destruction comes out of the north; even her hired men in the midst of her are like fatted bullocks, turned back and fled away together, not standing because the day of their calamity and the time of their visitation was upon them. The voice shall go like a serpent as they march with an army and come against her with axes like hewers of wood to cut down her forest, though it cannot be searched, because they are more than the grasshoppers and are innumerable. The Most High will punish the multitude of No, Pharaoh, and Egypt with their gods and their kings, delivering them into the hand of Nebuchadnezzar and his servants; afterward it shall be inhabited as in the days of old.

The Most High turns to comfort His own, telling Jacob His servant not to fear nor be dismayed, for He will save him from afar off and his seed from the land of their captivity, and Jacob shall return and be in rest and at ease with none to make him afraid. He will make a full end of all the nations where He has driven us, but He will not make a full end of us; He will correct us in measure and will not leave us wholly unpunished, so there is redemption for us but still a reminder of punishment because of our sins.

Woe to them that go down to Egypt for help, staying on horses and trusting chariots, but not looking to the Holy One of Israel. This makes plain what chapter 30 opened with. We honor the Most High with our lips, but when the oppressor offers gifts we turn away and serve our oppressor's will. When Sennacherib's servant Rabshakeh offered Hezekiah two thousand horses, it was the same trick, a gift to pull the heart off the Most High. -

The Most High is also wise, will bring evil, and will not call back his words, but arises against the evildoers and against those who help them. The Egyptians are men and not God, their horses flesh and not spirit. When the Most High stretches out his hand, both the helper and the one helped fall down together. A nation cannot help you when the Most High has decided to punish both.

As a lion is not afraid of the shepherds' voices, so the Lord of hosts comes down to fight for Mount Zion, defending Jerusalem as birds flying. He will deliver, preserve, and pass over it. Therefore turn to him, from whom the children of Israel have deeply revolted; that revolt is the same rebellion of the rebellious children.

In that day every man casts away the idols of silver and gold his own hands made for a sin. Then the Assyrian falls by a sword that is not of man. He flees, his young men are discomfited, and his princes are afraid of the ensign, because the Most High's fire is in Zion and his furnace in Jerusalem. When the Most High brings his judgment, the heathen nations can do nothing, so we wait patiently while he waits for us to get ourselves together.

Ezekiel is to prophesy, Woe worth the day, for the day of the Lord is near, a cloudy day, the time of the heathen; the sword shall come upon Egypt and great pain in Ethiopia when the slain fall. Ethiopia, Libya, Lydia, all the mingled people, and the men of the land that is in league shall fall with them by the sword; those that uphold Egypt shall fall and the pride of her power come down. -
Those "in league" are the peoples in agreement or alliance with Ethiopia, who fall together with Egypt by the sword.

The Most High will make the multitude of Egypt to cease by the hand of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon and the terrible of the nations, who draw their swords against Egypt and fill the land with the slain, drying the rivers and selling the land into the hand of the wicked. He will destroy the idols, cause the images to cease out of Noph, set fire in Egypt, pour His fury upon Sin, cut off the multitude of No, and send the cities of Egypt into captivity, so they shall know that He is the Lord.

In the eleventh year the word came that the Most High has broken the arm of Pharaoh king of Egypt, and it shall not be bound up to be healed or made strong to hold the sword. He will break both Pharaoh's arms, strengthen the arms of the king of Babylon and put His sword in his hand, scatter the Egyptians among the nations, and they shall know that He is the Lord. --- Topics: [Idolatry](/encyclopedia/idolatry)

name: The shepherds of Israel
charge: Feeding themselves and not the flock; scattering the sheep
summary: Ezekiel 34 arraigns the rulers and pastors of Israel as shepherds who ate the fat and clothed themselves with the wool, but did not strengthen the diseased, heal the sick, bind up the broken, bring back the driven away, or seek the lost. The flock was scattered on every hill and became meat to the beasts.
offense: The shepherds of Israel fed themselves instead of the flock. They ate the fat, clothed themselves with the wool, and killed those that were fed, while failing to strengthen the diseased, heal the sick, bind the broken, bring back the driven, or seek the lost. They ruled with force and cruelty. The sheep were scattered and became prey because those entrusted with them sought their own advantage. The Lord also addressed the strong sheep that trampled the remaining pasture, fouled the waters, and pushed the weak aside. Exploitation was not excused merely because it occurred within the flock.
judgment: God declared Himself against the shepherds and required His flock at their hand. He would remove their opportunity to feed themselves upon it and deliver the sheep from their mouths. He would judge between cattle and cattle, between the fat and the lean. The Lord promised to seek His sheep, gather them, feed them in good pasture, and bind what was broken. He would set one shepherd over them, His servant David, and make a covenant of peace. The remedy for abusive rule was not abandonment of the flock, but God's own intervention and the faithful shepherd He appointed.

verses.text: 1And the word of the Lord came unto me, saying, 2Son of man, prophesy against the shepherds of Israel, prophesy, and say unto them, Thus saith the Lord God unto the shepherds; Woe be to the shepherds of Israel that do feed themselves! should not the shepherds feed the flocks? 3Ye eat the fat, and ye clothe you with the wool, ye kill them that are fed: but ye feed not the flock. 4The diseased have ye not strengthened, neither have ye healed that which was sick, neither have ye bound up that which was broken, neither have ye brought again that which was driven away, neither have ye sought that which was lost; but with force and with cruelty have ye ruled them. 5And they were scattered, because there is no shepherd: and they became meat to all the beasts of the field, when they were scattered. 6My sheep wandered through all the mountains, and upon every high hill: yea, my flock was scattered upon all the face of the earth, and

entries.commentary: Woe is pronounced on the pastors that destroy and scatter the sheep of the Most High's pasture and have not visited them, so He will visit upon them the evil of their doings. He will gather the remnant of His flock out of the countries where He drove them, bring them again to their folds, and set up shepherds who will feed them so they fear no more and none are lacking.

The Most High promises to raise unto David a righteous Branch, a King who shall reign, prosper, and execute judgment and justice, in whose days Judah shall be saved and Israel dwell safely. His name is called THE LORD OUR RIGHTEOUSNESS; this is plainly referring to Christ. The day comes when they will no longer swear by the Most High who brought Israel out of Egypt, but by Him who led the seed of the house of Israel out of the north country and all the countries where He had driven them, back to their own land.

Jeremiah's heart is broken and his bones shake like a drunken man because of the prophets and the words of the Most High's holiness, for the land is full of adulterers and mourns under swearing. Both prophet and priest are profane, and the Most High has found their wickedness even in His house, so their way shall be as slippery ways in the darkness where they are driven and fall. The prophets of Samaria prophesied in Baal and caused Israel to err, and the prophets of Jerusalem commit adultery, walk in lies, and strengthen the hands of evildoers so that none return from wickedness, becoming as Sodom and Gomorrah before Him.

The people are told not to hearken to the prophets who make them vain and speak a vision of their own heart, not out of the mouth of the Most High, telling those who despise Him that they shall have peace and no evil shall come. This is like the pastor who says, let me tell you what God told me to tell you, when it is a lie. None of these prophets has stood in the counsel of the Most High; had they stood there and caused the people to hear His words, they would have turned them from their evil way, but instead the whirlwind of His anger will fall grievously upon the head of the wicked in the latter days.

The Most High asks whether He is a God only near and not far off, when He fills heaven and earth and no one can hide in secret places where He cannot see him. He has heard the prophets who prophesy lies in His name saying, I have dreamed, thinking to cause His people to forget His name by their dreams as their fathers forgot it for Baal. Let the prophet with a dream tell a dream, but let him that has His word speak it faithfully, for His word is like a fire and like a hammer that breaks the rock in pieces; He is against those who steal His words and use their own tongues to lie on the Most High.

When the people, prophet, or priest ask what is the burden of the Most High, Jeremiah is to answer, What burden? for He will forsake them, and every man who claims the burden of the Most High He will punish in his house. Instead of saying the burden of the Most High, they are to ask one another what the Most High has answered and spoken, for they have perverted the words of the living God. Because they keep saying the burden of the Most High after being told not to, He will utterly forget them, forsake them, and cast them out of His presence with an everlasting reproach and perpetual shame that shall not be forgotten. --- Topics: [Idolatry](/encyclopedia/idolatry) · [The Covenant](/encyclopedia/the-covenant) · [The Priesthood](/encyclopedia/the-priesthood)

Open thy doors, O Lebanon, that the fire may devour thy cedars. Howl, fir tree; for the cedar is fallen; because the mighty are spoiled. There is a voice of the howling of the shepherds; for their glory is spoiled: a voice of the roaring of young lions; for the pride of Jordan is spoiled.

Feed the flock of the slaughter, whose possessors slay them, and hold themselves not guilty; and they that sell them say, Blessed be the Lord; for I am rich: and their own shepherds pity them not. The verse names a people who were possessed, sold, and slain by those who held themselves not guilty, and whose own shepherds do not pity them. That is Israel, the so-called Blacks, Hispanics, and Native Americans.

I will no more pity the inhabitants of the land, saith the Lord: but lo, I will deliver the men every one into his neighbour's hand, and into the hand of his king: and they shall smite the land, and out of their hand I will not deliver them. I will feed the flock of slaughter, even you, O poor of the flock. And I took unto me two staves; the one I called Beauty, and the other I called Bands; and I fed the flock. Three shepherds also I cut off in one month; and my soul lothed them, and their soul also abhorred me. I will not feed you: that that dieth, let it die; and that that is to be cut off, let it be cut off; and let the rest eat every one the flesh of another. The scripture says plainly what the end of this land is, and it is why keeping the law matters now.

I took my staff, even Beauty, and cut it asunder, that I might break my covenant which I had made with all the people. I said unto them, If ye think good, give me my price; and if not, forbear. So they weighed for my price thirty pieces of silver. The Lord said unto me, Cast it unto the potter: a goodly price that I was prised at of them. And I took the thirty pieces of silver, and cast them to the potter in the house of the Lord. Then I cut asunder mine other staff, even Bands, that I might break the brotherhood between Judah and Israel. That breaking is the split of the southern and northern kingdoms. He broke it, and he also says he will put it back together.

Take unto thee yet the instruments of a foolish shepherd. For lo, I will raise up a shepherd in the land, which shall not visit those that be cut off, neither shall seek the young one, nor heal that that is broken, nor feed that that standeth still: but he shall eat the flesh of the fat, and tear their claws in pieces. Woe to the idol shepherd that leaveth the flock! The sword shall be upon his arm, and upon his right eye: his arm shall be clean dried up, and his right eye shall be utterly darkened. --- Topics: [Idolatry](/encyclopedia/idolatry) · [The Covenant](/encyclopedia/the-covenant) · [The Feasts of the Most High](/encyclopedia/the-feasts-of-the-most-high) · [The Priesthood](/encyclopedia/the-priesthood)

name: Jonah
charge: Fleeing from the presence of the Lord to avoid his commission; anger at God's mercy
summary: Told to go east to Nineveh, Jonah bought passage west to Tarshish. A storm, a lot, and a fish brought him back. He preached, the city repented, and he was angry enough to die because God spared it. A gourd, a worm, and a wind finished the lesson.
offense: Jonah received the command to cry against Nineveh and fled toward Tarshish from the presence of the Lord. He confessed to the mariners that he feared the God who made the sea and dry land, even while his flight contradicted that confession. The storm endangered others as well as himself. After Nineveh repented, Jonah's anger disclosed his resistance to God's mercy. He said that he had fled because he knew the Lord was gracious and would turn from the announced evil. He preferred death to witnessing the sparing of the city he had been sent to warn.
judgment: Jonah was cast into the sea, and the Lord prepared a great fish to swallow him. From that distress he prayed, acknowledging that salvation is of the Lord. God commanded the fish to release him and gave him the commission a second time. After the preaching, God corrected him again through the gourd, the worm, and the vehement east wind. Jonah pitied the plant that had sheltered him, though he had not made it grow. The Lord asked why He should not spare a great city with more than a hundred and twenty thousand persons unable to discern their right hand from their left, and much cattle. The book closes with God's question, not a recorded answer from Jonah.

verses.text: 1Now the word of the Lord came unto Jonah the son of Amittai, saying, 2Arise, go to Nineveh, that great city, and cry against it; for their wickedness is come up before me. 3But Jonah rose up to flee unto Tarshish from the presence of the Lord, and went down to Joppa; and he found a ship going to Tarshish: so he paid the fare thereof, and went down into it, to go with them unto Tarshish from the presence of the Lord. 4But the Lord sent out a great wind into the sea, and there was a mighty tempest in the sea, so that the ship was like to be broken.
12And he said unto them, Take me up, and cast me forth into the sea; so shall the sea be calm unto you: for I know that for my sake this great tempest is upon you.

entries.commentary: The word of the Lord came unto Jonah the son of Amittai, saying, Arise, go to Nineveh, that great city, and cry against it; for their wickedness is come up before me. But Jonah rose up to flee unto Tarshish from the presence of the Lord, went down to Joppa, found a ship going to Tarshish, paid the fare thereof, and went down into it.

The Lord sent out a great wind into the sea, and there was a mighty tempest, so that the ship was like to be broken. The mariners were afraid, and cried every man unto his god, and cast forth the wares into the sea; but Jonah was gone down into the sides of the ship, and lay, and was fast asleep. They cast lots to know for whose cause this evil was upon them, and the lot fell upon Jonah. He answered them, I am an Hebrew; and I fear the Lord, the God of heaven, which hath made the sea and the dry land. Then were the men exceedingly afraid, for they knew that he fled from the presence of the Lord.

Take me up, and cast me forth into the sea; so shall the sea be calm unto you: for I know that for my sake this great tempest is upon you. The men rowed hard to bring it to the land, but they could not, for the sea wrought and was tempestuous against them. They cried unto the Lord, Lay not upon us innocent blood; then they took up Jonah and cast him into the sea, and the sea ceased from her raging, and the men feared the Lord exceedingly. Now the Lord had prepared a great fish to swallow up Jonah; and Jonah was in the belly of the fish three days and three nights.

I cried by reason of mine affliction unto the Lord, and he heard me; out of the belly of hell cried I, and thou heardest my voice. Thou hadst cast me into the deep, in the midst of the seas; and the floods compassed me about: all thy billows and thy waves passed over me. I said, I am cast out of thy sight; yet I will look again toward thy holy temple. I went down to the bottoms of the mountains; the earth with her bars was about me for ever: yet hast thou brought up my life from corruption, O Lord my God.

When my soul fainted within me I remembered the Lord: and my prayer came in unto thee, into thine holy temple. They that observe lying vanities forsake their own mercy. I will sacrifice unto thee with the voice of thanksgiving; I will pay that that I have vowed. Salvation is of the Lord. The Lord spake unto the fish, and it vomited out Jonah upon the dry land.

The word of the Lord came unto Jonah the second time, saying, Arise, go unto Nineveh, that great city, and preach unto it the preaching that I bid thee. Jonah arose and went unto Nineveh according to the word of the Lord; and he cried, Yet forty days, and Nineveh shall be overthrown.

The people of Nineveh believed God, and proclaimed a fast, and put on sackcloth, from the greatest of them even to the least of them. The king arose from his throne, laid his robe from him, covered him with sackcloth, and sat in ashes, and made the decree that neither man nor beast taste anything, but be covered with sackcloth and cry mightily unto God. Let them turn every one from his evil way, and from the violence that is in their hands. God saw their works, that they turned from their evil way; and God repented of the evil that he had said that he would do unto them, and he did it not.

It displeased Jonah exceedingly, and he was very angry. He said, Was not this my saying when I was yet in my country? Therefore I fled before unto Tarshish: for I knew that thou art a gracious God, and merciful, slow to anger, and of great kindness, and repentest thee of the evil. Take, I beseech thee, my life from me; for it is better for me to die than to live. Then said the Lord, Doest thou well to be angry? Jonah went out of the city, and sat on the east side of the city, and made him a booth, and sat under it in the shadow, till he might see what would become of the city.

The Lord God prepared a gourd, and made it to come up over Jonah, to be a shadow over his head, to deliver him from his grief; so Jonah was exceeding glad of the gourd. God prepared a worm when the morning rose the next day, and it smote the gourd that it withered; and he prepared a vehement east wind, and the sun beat upon the head of Jonah, that he fainted. Thou hast had pity on the gourd, for the which thou hast not laboured, neither madest it grow, which came up in a night, and perished in a night. And should not I spare Nineveh, that great city, wherein are more than sixscore thousand persons that cannot discern between their right hand and their left hand; and also much cattle? --- Topics: [Sacrifice and Atonement](/encyclopedia/sacrifice-and-atonement)
The disciples pluck the ears of corn on the sabbath being an hungred, and the Pharisees accuse them of doing that which is not lawful.
Christ answers with what David did: he entered the house of God and ate the shewbread, which was lawful only for the priests, because he was not of Levi.

The priests in the temple profane the sabbath and are blameless, because the service itself is commanded. If ye had known what this meaneth, I will have mercy, and not sacrifice, ye would not have condemned the guiltless. The Son of man is Lord even of the sabbath day.

A man with a withered hand is set before him to see whether he would heal on the sabbath, that they might accuse him. A man will lift his own sheep out of a pit on the sabbath day, and a man is better than a sheep. Wherefore it is lawful to do well on the sabbath days. The distinction is between what falls out and what is planned. A sheep does not fall into a pit by appointment, and spilt milk is cleaned up when it happens. Wilful sin is the thing thought out beforehand.
The hand is restored whole, like as the other.

The Pharisees hold a council how they might destroy him, and he withdraws himself and heals the multitudes, charging them not to make him known. This too was written beforehand: behold my servant, whom I have chosen, and he shall shew judgment to the Gentiles.

One possessed with a devil, blind and dumb, is healed, and the people ask, Is not this the son of David? The Pharisees answer that he casts out devils by Beelzebub, saying his power came from the devil.

Every kingdom divided against itself is brought to desolation. If Satan cast out Satan, his kingdom cannot stand. By whom do your children cast them out? Therefore they shall be your judges. No man enters a strong man's house and spoils his goods except he first bind the strong man. The binding is the taking away of his understanding; then his house can be spoiled.
He that is not with me is against me, and he that gathereth not with me scattereth abroad.

All manner of sin and blasphemy shall be forgiven unto men, but the blasphemy against the Holy Ghost shall not be forgiven. The Holy Ghost is bound to the law, so speaking against it is not only with the mouth. Going back into the world and back into the ways that were left is a man's actions speaking for him.

The tree is known by his fruit, and a man is known by what he brings forth and by those he teaches. Out of the abundance of the heart the mouth speaketh, and every idle word that men shall speak they shall give account thereof in the day of judgment.

The scribes and Pharisees ask for a sign, and no sign is given but the sign of the prophet Jonas: three days and three nights in the heart of the earth. The men of Nineveh repented at the preaching of Jonas, and the queen of the south came from the uttermost parts of the earth to hear the wisdom of Solomon. These men had a greater than both standing in front of them and would not hear.

The unclean spirit returns to a house swept and garnished and brings seven others more wicked than himself, and the last state of that man is worse than the first. That is the end of turning back after knowing.

Who is my mother, and who are my brethren? Whosoever shall do the will of my Father which is in heaven, the same is my brother, and sister, and mother. This does not unmake a man's natural family. It names a second family, made of those keeping the laws of the Most High.

name: Nineveh under Nahum
charge: A bloody city, full of lies and robbery, mistress of witchcrafts
summary: Nahum charged Nineveh with bloodshed, lies, plunder, and the corruption of nations. The Lord who is slow to anger would not acquit the wicked. The city's defenses, commerce, and commanders would fail, and the peoples it had injured would rejoice at its overthrow.
offense: Nahum charged Nineveh as a bloody city, full of lies and robbery, whose prey did not depart. Its power was pictured as a lions' dwelling filled with torn prey. Violence, deceit, and the entangling of nations had enriched the city and spread its injury abroad.
judgment: The gates of the rivers shall be opened, and the palace dissolved. Nineveh is laid waste; who will bemoan her? There is no healing of thy bruise. Tobit records hearing of its destruction by Nebuchadnezzar and Ahasuerus before he died, and rejoicing over it.

entries.commentary: The burden of Nineveh. The book of the vision of Nahum the Elkoshite. God is jealous, and the Lord revengeth; the Lord revengeth, and is furious; the Lord will take vengeance on his adversaries, and he reserveth wrath for his enemies. The Lord is slow to anger, and great in power, and will not at all acquit the wicked: the Lord hath his way in the whirlwind and in the storm, and the clouds are the dust of his feet. The mountains quake at him, and the hills melt, and the earth is burned at his presence, yea, the world, and all that dwell therein. Who can stand before his indignation? and who can abide in the fierceness of his anger? his fury is poured out like fire, and the rocks are thrown down by him.

The Lord is good, a strong hold in the day of trouble; and he knoweth them that trust in him. With an overrunning flood he will make an utter end of the place thereof, and darkness shall pursue his enemies. What do ye imagine against the Lord? he will make an utter end: affliction shall not rise up the second time. There is one come out of thee, that imagineth evil against the Lord, a wicked counsellor.

Though I have afflicted thee, I will afflict thee no more. For now will I break his yoke from off thee, and will burst thy bonds in sunder. The Lord hath given a commandment concerning thee, that no more of thy name be sown: out of the house of thy gods will I cut off the graven image and the molten image. Behold upon the mountains the feet of him that bringeth good tidings, that publisheth peace! O Judah, keep thy solemn feasts, perform thy vows: for the wicked shall no more pass through thee; he is utterly cut off. --- Topics: [Idolatry](/encyclopedia/idolatry) · [The Feasts of the Most High](/encyclopedia/the-feasts-of-the-most-high)

He that dasheth in pieces is come up before thy face: keep the munition, watch the way, make thy loins strong, fortify thy power mightily. For the Lord hath turned away the excellency of Jacob, as the excellency of Israel: for the emptiers have emptied them out, and marred their vine branches. The chariots shall be with flaming torches in the day of his preparation; they shall rage in the streets, they shall justle one against another in the broad ways: they shall seem like torches, they shall run like the lightnings.

The gates of the rivers shall be opened, and the palace shall be dissolved. Nineveh is of old like a pool of water: yet they shall flee away. Stand, stand, shall they cry; but none shall look back. Take ye the spoil of silver, take the spoil of gold: for there is none end of the store and glory out of all the pleasant furniture. She is empty, and void, and waste: and the heart melteth, and the knees smite together, and much pain is in all loins, and the faces of them all gather blackness.

Where is the dwelling of the lions, and the feedingplace of the young lions, where the lion, even the old lion, walked, and none made them afraid? The lion did tear in pieces enough for his whelps, and filled his holes with prey, and his dens with ravin. Behold, I am against thee, saith the Lord of hosts, and I will burn her chariots in the smoke, and the sword shall devour thy young lions: and I will cut off thy prey from the earth, and the voice of thy messengers shall no more be heard.

Woe to the bloody city! it is all full of lies and robbery; the prey departeth not. There is a multitude of slain, and a great number of carcases; and there is none end of their corpses; they stumble upon their corpses. Because of the multitude of the whoredoms of the wellfavoured harlot, the mistress of witchcrafts, that selleth nations through her whoredoms, and families through her witchcrafts. Behold, I am against thee, saith the Lord of hosts; and I will discover thy skirts upon thy face, and I will shew the nations thy nakedness, and the kingdoms thy shame. All they that look upon thee shall flee from thee, and say, Nineveh is laid waste: who will bemoan her? whence shall I seek comforters for thee?

Art thou better than populous No, that was situate among the rivers, whose rampart was the sea, and her wall was from the sea? Ethiopia and Egypt were her strength, and it was infinite; Put and Lubim were thy helpers. Yet was she carried away, she went into captivity: her young children also were dashed in pieces at the top of all the streets, and they cast lots for her honourable men, and all her great men were bound in chains. Thou also shalt be drunken; all thy strong holds shall be like fig trees with the firstripe figs: if they be shaken, they shall even fall into the mouth of the eater. The gates of thy land shall be set wide open unto thine enemies: the fire shall devour thy bars.

Draw thee waters for the siege, fortify thy strong holds: there shall the fire devour thee; the sword shall cut thee off. Thou hast multiplied thy merchants above the stars of heaven: the cankerworm spoileth, and flieth away. Thy shepherds slumber, O king of Assyria: thy nobles shall dwell in the dust: thy people is scattered upon the mountains, and no man gathereth them. There is no healing of thy bruise; thy wound is grievous: all that hear the bruit of thee shall clap the hands over thee: for upon whom hath not thy wickedness passed continually? ---

Gather yourselves together, yea, gather together, O nation not desired; before the decree bring forth, before the fierce anger of the Lord come upon you. Seek ye the Lord, all ye meek of the earth, which have wrought his judgment; seek righteousness, seek meekness: it may be ye shall be hid in the day of the Lord's anger.

Gaza shall be forsaken, and Ashkelon a desolation: they shall drive out Ashdod at the noon day, and Ekron shall be rooted up. The word of the Lord is against you; O Canaan, the land of the Philistines, I will even destroy thee, that there shall be no inhabitant. The coast shall be for the remnant of the house of Judah; they shall feed thereupon: for the Lord their God shall visit them, and turn away their captivity.

I have heard the reproach of Moab, and the revilings of the children of Ammon, whereby they have reproached my people, and magnified themselves against their border. Surely Moab shall be as Sodom, and the children of Ammon as Gomorrah: the residue of my people shall spoil them, and the remnant of my people shall possess them. This shall they have for their pride, because they have reproached and magnified themselves against the people of the Lord of hosts. He will stretch out his hand against the north, and destroy Assyria; and will make Nineveh a desolation, and dry like a wilderness. This is the rejoicing city that dwelt carelessly, that said in her heart, I am, and there is none beside me: how is she become a desolation!

Woe is pronounced on those who decree unrighteous decrees and write grievous laws to turn aside the needy from judgment and take away the right from the poor. That is us: we are the needy, we are the poor. Back then this was the Assyrians doing it to us because of our disobedience. Today it is your friendly neighborhood white man writing unrighteous laws and prescribing them for us to keep. It is a twofold prophecy. The unrighteous decrees rob the widows and the fatherless. The question is put to the oppressor: what will you do in the day of visitation and desolation, to whom will you flee for help, and where will you leave your glory. Without the Most High they bow down under the prisoners and fall under the slain, for His anger is not turned away and His hand is stretched out still.

The Most High calls the Assyrian the rod of His anger, the staff in their hand His indignation. He used nations to punish us. He sends the Assyrian against a hypocritical nation, the people of His wrath, to take the spoil and tread them down like the mire of the streets. The Most High calls us hypocrites because we love to say we love the Most High, but we do not want to do what the Bible says. The Assyrian did not mean it that way; it was in his heart to destroy and cut off nations. He boasted of the kingdoms he conquered and their idols, not realizing the Most High was using him to punish us and the rest of the nations. We had graven images throughout our land, breaking the Most High's laws.

When the Most High has finished His work on Zion and Jerusalem, He will punish the fruit of the stout heart of the king of Assyria and the glory of his high looks. The Assyrian said, "By the strength of my hand I have done it, and by my wisdom, for I am prudent," boasting that he removed the treasures and inhabitants of the people on his own. The Most High asks whether the axe boasts against the one who hews with it, or the saw magnifies itself against the one who shakes it. The Assyrian was only the axe; the Most High used him to cut us down from rulership to captivity. Therefore the Most High sends leanness among the fat ones and kindles a burning fire that devours the thorns and briers in one day and consumes the glory of the forest, both soul and body, until the trees are so few a child may write them.

In that day the remnant of Israel and those who escaped of the house of Jacob shall no more stay upon him that smote them, but stay upon the Most High, the Holy One of Israel, in truth. This is a future prophecy. "Stay" means to rely upon. Just like back then, we still rely upon the ones who smote us, even today under the nation of Edom, trusting in oppression, relying on the very ones still smiting us in the streets. In that day the remnant, those keeping the Most High's commandments in their right mind, will escape and stop leaning on the oppressor. Though Israel be as the sand of the sea, only a remnant shall return. The Most High will make a consumption decreed and overflowing with righteousness in the midst of all the land. -

The Most High tells His people who dwell in Zion not to be afraid of the Assyrian who smites with a rod and lifts up his staff after the manner of Egypt, for in a very little while the indignation will cease and His anger will turn to their destruction. The Most High will stir up a scourge for the Assyrian, and his yoke shall be taken off Israel's neck and destroyed because of the anointing. The chapter traces the invader's march through the towns until he shakes his hand against the mount of the daughter of Zion. Then the Most High of hosts lops the bough with terror, the high ones are hewn down, and Lebanon falls by a mighty one.

name: The adversaries of Judah and Benjamin
charge: Weakening the hands of the people; hiring counsellors against them to frustrate the building of the house of God
summary: The people of the land offered to help build the temple and were refused, and turned to hindrance: hired counsellors, letters to Artaxerxes, and a stop-work order enforced by force and power. The work lay still until the second year of Darius, whose decree turned the tables: whoever altered it would be hanged on timber from his own house.
offense: The adversaries first offered to join the building, claiming to seek the same God. Zerubbabel, Jeshua, and the chief fathers refused, declaring that they would build the house of the Lord according to Cyrus's command. The rejected offer was followed by open obstruction: the people of the land discouraged Judah, troubled the builders, and hired counselors to frustrate the work (Ezra 4:1-5). Ezra also records accusations against Jerusalem under later kings. Rehum and Shimshai represented the city as rebellious and warned that rebuilding would cost the king tribute and dominion. They obtained an order and enforced it by force and power (Ezra 4:11-23). Opposition clothed itself in concern for royal interests while working to weaken the returned people.
judgment: When the temple work resumed under Haggai and Zechariah, the elders continued while the inquiry went to Darius. The eye of their God was upon them (Ezra 5:5). A search recovered Cyrus's decree, and Darius ordered the work left alone and its expenses supplied from the royal tribute (Ezra 6:1-10). His decree threatened severe punishment against anyone who altered it. The account does not record that penalty being executed upon the earlier adversaries. It records their obstruction overcome: the elders built, the house was finished, and the children of the captivity dedicated it with joy. The authority invoked to hinder the work now required that it be supplied.
