name: Mordecai and Esther
charge: Mordecai: bowing not to Haman. Esther: going in to the king against the law, after three days' fast: if I perish, I perish
summary: A Jew in the king's gate would not bow to an Agagite, and the Agagite bought a decree to kill every Jew in the empire. His cousin the queen fasted three days with all the Jews of Shushan and went in to the king uncalled. Haman was hanged on his own gallows, the Jews were given the day, and Mordecai was next unto the king. The feast of Purim keeps it.
offense: All the king's servants bowed, and reverenced Haman: for the king had so commanded concerning him. But Mordecai bowed not, nor did him reverence; for he had told them that he was a Jew. Esther: Go, gather together all the Jews that are present in Shushan, and fast ye for me, and neither eat nor drink three days, night or day: I also and my maidens will fast likewise; and so will I go in unto the king, which is not according to the law: and if I perish, I perish. Mordecai's word to her: who knoweth whether thou art come to the kingdom for such a time as this?
judgment: So they hanged Haman on the gallows that he had prepared for Mordecai. Then was the king's wrath pacified. The king took off his ring, which he had taken from Haman, and gave it unto Mordecai. The Jews had light, and gladness, and joy, and honour. Mordecai the Jew was next unto king Ahasuerus, and great among the Jews, and accepted of the multitude of his brethren, seeking the wealth of his people, and speaking peace to all his seed. The Greek Esther adds Mordecai's dream and the Lord's answer: the Lord hath done wonders for his people.

entries.commentary: After these things the king promoted Haman the son of Hammedatha the Agagite and set his seat above all the princes, and all the king's servants in the king's gate bowed and reverenced him, for the king had so commanded, but Mordecai bowed not nor did him reverence. The servants asked daily why Mordecai transgressed the king's commandment, and he hearkened not, but told them he was a Jew, and they told Haman to see whether Mordecai's matter would stand. We do not bow, the same as the three Hebrew children did not bow to the image in Babylon, for we pledge allegiance to none but the Most High. -

When Haman saw that Mordecai bowed not nor did him reverence, he was full of wrath, and thought scorn to lay hands on Mordecai alone once they had shown him the people of Mordecai. Haman sought to destroy all the Jews throughout the whole kingdom of Ahasuerus, the people of Mordecai, not one man only. Because Mordecai would not bow, Edom's hatred sought a death sentence for the entire nation, seeking to erase us out of history.

In the first month, Nisan, in the twelfth year of the king, they cast Pur, that is the lot, before Haman from day to day and month to month, to the twelfth month, Adar. Haman told the king there was a certain people scattered abroad whose laws were diverse from all people and who kept not the king's laws, and it was not for the king's profit to suffer them, offering ten thousand talents of silver to have them destroyed. The king took his ring and gave it to Haman the Jews' enemy, granting him the silver and the people to do as he pleased. This is putting a hit out on the entire nation of Israel.

On the thirteenth day of the first month the king's scribes wrote according to all Haman commanded, to the king's lieutenants, governors and rulers of every province in the king's name and sealed with the king's ring. Letters were sent by posts to destroy, kill and cause to perish all Jews, young and old, little children and women, in one day, the thirteenth of the twelfth month Adar, and to take the spoil for prey. The copy was published in every province so they should be ready, and the king and Haman sat down to drink while the city Shushan was perplexed.

When Mordecai perceived all that was done he rent his clothes, put on sackcloth with ashes, went out into the midst of the city and cried with a loud and bitter cry, and came before the king's gate, for none might enter it clothed with sackcloth. In every province where the king's commandment and decree came there was great mourning among the Jews, with fasting, weeping and wailing, and many lay in sackcloth and ashes. Imagine a decree today to kill every descendant of Israel, and you begin to feel what they went through.

Esther's maids and chamberlain told her, and the queen was exceedingly grieved and sent raiment to clothe Mordecai and take away his sackcloth, but he received it not. She sent Hatach, appointed to attend her, to learn what it was and why. Mordecai told Hatach all that had happened and of the money Haman promised to pay for the Jews to be destroyed, and gave him a copy of the decree published in Shushan to show Esther, charging her to go in to the king and make supplication for her people.

Esther answered by Hatach that all the king's servants and people knew that whosoever came unto the king in the inner court uncalled, man or woman, there was one law, to be put to death, except the king held out the golden sceptre that he may live. She said she had not been called to come in unto the king these thirty days, and they told Mordecai her words. She made an excuse, though she was the queen the king had chosen and loved above all the women.

Mordecai sent answer that Esther should not think she would escape in the king's house more than all the Jews, for if she altogether held her peace at this time, then enlargement and deliverance would arise to the Jews from another place, but she and her father's house would be destroyed. Who knoweth whether Esther was come to the kingdom for such a time as this. She was put in her position to serve this very purpose, and the deliverance of Israel cannot be held back; she would either help it along or be left behind while it came another way.

Esther returned answer that Mordecai should gather all the Jews in Shushan to fast for her, neither eating nor drinking three days, night or day, and she and her maidens would fast likewise, and so she would go in unto the king not according to the law, and if she perished, she perished. So Mordecai went his way and did according to all Esther commanded him. She had her mind set right, ready to risk her life for her people. -

On the third day Esther put on her royal apparel and stood in the inner court of the king's house over against the king's house, and the king sat on his royal throne over against the gate. When the king saw Esther the queen standing in the court, she obtained favour in his sight, and he held out to her the golden sceptre in his hand, and Esther drew near and touched the top of the sceptre. She was not called by name, yet as soon as he saw her he received her, for a daughter of Israel finds favour in the eyes of a man.

The king asked what would Esther the queen and what was her request, offering even to the half of the kingdom, and Esther asked that the king and Haman come that day to a banquet she had prepared. The king said cause Haman to make haste that he may do as Esther said, so the king and Haman came to the banquet Esther had prepared. When a woman he loves prepares a table for him, the king bends to hear her every request.

At the banquet of wine the king again asked Esther's petition and request, to the half of the kingdom, and Esther answered that if she had found favour and it pleased the king, let the king and Haman come again to the banquet she would prepare on the morrow, and she would do as the king had said. The book of Esther shows both sides, the good side of a woman doing what she should and the wicked side of what she should not, so it puts a check on the spirit that rises up in women to rebel.

Haman went forth that day joyful and glad of heart, but when he saw Mordecai in the king's gate who stood not up nor moved for him, he was full of indignation, yet refrained himself and went home and called for his friends and Zeresh his wife. Haman told them of the glory of his riches, his many children, and all the ways the king had advanced him above the princes, and that Esther had let no man come to the banquet with the king but himself, and he was bidden again on the morrow. Yet all this availed him nothing so long as he saw Mordecai the Jew sitting at the king's gate. Then Zeresh his wife and all his friends counselled that a gallows fifty cubits high be made, and on the morrow he should speak to the king that Mordecai be hanged thereon, and then go merrily to the banquet, and the thing pleased Haman and he caused the gallows to be made. It was the wife's idea, for the enemy's women are in cahoots with the work against Israel. --- Topics: [Esau and Edom](/encyclopedia/esau-and-edom) · [Sacrifice and Atonement](/encyclopedia/sacrifice-and-atonement) · [The Feasts of the Most High](/encyclopedia/the-feasts-of-the-most-high)

At the banquet of wine the king again asked Esther her petition, promising it would be granted even to the half of the kingdom. Esther pleaded for her life and the life of her people, for they had been sold to be destroyed, slain, and to perish, and had it been only bondage she would have held her tongue. The king demanded to know who he was that dared presume in his heart to do such a thing.

Esther named the adversary and enemy as this wicked Haman, and Haman was afraid before the king and the queen. Sitting at the table, Haman could hardly eat, for he had just arrayed Mordecai and just heard his own household warn him he would fall before the Jews, and now he was exposed at the dinner table.

The king rose in his wrath and went into the palace garden, and Haman stood up to make request for his life to Esther, seeing that evil was determined against him. When the king returned, Haman had fallen upon the bed where Esther was, and the king took it as an assault on the queen in his own house. As the word went out of the king's mouth, they covered Haman's face.

Harbonah, a chamberlain, told the king of the gallows fifty cubits high that Haman had made for Mordecai, who had spoken good for the king, standing at Haman's house. The king commanded Haman be hanged on it, and they hanged Haman on the gallows he had prepared for Mordecai, and the king's wrath was pacified. This is the Most High, a man of war, and this is how He moves.

That day the king gave the house of Haman, the Jews' enemy, to Esther, and Mordecai came before the king, for Esther had told what he was to her. The king took off the ring he had taken from Haman and gave it to Mordecai, and Esther set Mordecai over the house of Haman. Everything Haman had was given to Mordecai.

Esther fell down at the king's feet and besought him with tears to put away the mischief of Haman the Agagite and the device he had devised against the Jews. The king held out the golden scepter, and Esther rose and asked that letters be written to reverse the letters Haman devised to destroy the Jews in all the provinces. She asked how she could endure to see the evil that would come upon her people and the destruction of her kindred.

The king told Esther and Mordecai that he had given Esther the house of Haman and had hanged Haman for laying hand upon the Jews. He granted them to write for the Jews in the king's name and seal it with the king's ring, for a writing sealed with the king's ring could no man reverse. Esther and Mordecai were given the king's authority, so the reputation and word of the king stood behind whatever they wrote.

The king's scribes were called in the third month, Sivan, on the twenty-third day, and it was written to the Jews, lieutenants, deputies, and rulers of the provinces from India to Ethiopia, a hundred twenty and seven provinces, each in its own writing and language. This is the span of the Persian empire, and Israel was scattered all through it, from India to Ethiopia, not concentrated in one place but spread out during the captivity, which shows we have history in these lands. -

The king granted the Jews in every city to gather, stand for their life, and destroy any power that would assault them, both little ones and women, and to take the spoil. Everyone who had listened to Haman's proclamation to kill the Jews was now subject to the Jews' revenge upon their enemies. The decree was to be ready upon the thirteenth day of the twelfth month, Adar, the day the Jews would avenge themselves, for nothing pacifies the Most High but vengeance on the enemies of His people. The posts rode out hastened on mules, camels, and dromedaries by the king's commandment.

Mordecai went out from the king in royal apparel of blue and white, a great crown of gold, and a garment of fine linen and purple, and the city of Shushan rejoiced and was glad. The Jews had light, gladness, joy, and honor, and in every province and city where the decree came they had a feast and a good day. Many of the people of the land became Jews, for the fear of the Jews fell upon them, a picture of the future when the fear of Israel will be on all nations and they will serve the Most High.

In the twelfth month Adar, on the thirteenth day, when the enemies of the Jews hoped to have power over them, it was turned to the contrary and the Jews had rule over those that hated them. The Jews gathered in their cities, and no man could withstand them, for the fear of them fell upon all people, and the rulers, lieutenants, deputies, and officers helped the Jews because the fear of Mordecai fell upon them. Mordecai was great in the king's house and his fame went throughout all the provinces, and this man waxed greater and greater. Though Esther was queen, she was still subject to Mordecai, the man of Israel who wrote the edict.

The Jews smote all their enemies with the sword, slaughter, and destruction, and did what they would to those that hated them. In Shushan the palace they slew and destroyed five hundred men, and they slew the ten sons of Haman the son of Hammedatha, the enemy of the Jews. On the spoil they laid not their hands.

The number slain in Shushan was brought before the king, who told Esther the Jews had slain five hundred men and the ten sons of Haman, and asked what more she desired. Esther asked that the Jews in Shushan be granted the next day also according to the decree, and that Haman's ten sons be hanged on the gallows. The king commanded it done, and the Jews in Shushan gathered on the fourteenth day and slew three hundred more, but on the spoil they laid not their hands.

The other Jews in the king's provinces gathered, stood for their lives, had rest from their enemies, and slew of their foes seventy and five thousand, laying not their hands on the prey. This was on the thirteenth day of Adar, and on the fourteenth they rested and made a day of feasting and gladness. The Jews of Shushan rested on the fifteenth day, so the Jews of the unwalled towns made the fourteenth a day of gladness, feasting, and sending portions one to another. This is where the gift giving of Purim comes from.

Mordecai wrote these things and sent letters to all the Jews near and far to establish that they keep the fourteenth and fifteenth days of Adar yearly. These were the days the Jews rested from their enemies, the month turned from sorrow to joy and from mourning to a good day. They were to make them days of feasting, joy, sending portions one to another, and gifts to the poor. This is where the feast of Purim comes from, a feast that commemorates the destruction of Israel's enemies.

The Jews undertook to keep what Mordecai wrote, because Haman the son of Hammedatha the Agagite had devised against the Jews to destroy them and had cast Pur, that is the lot, to consume them. Pur was the Persian custom of casting lots, much like the lot cast for Jonah to see whose fault the storm was. When Esther came before the king, he commanded by letters that Haman's wicked device return upon his own head, and that he and his sons be hanged on the gallows. -

These days were called Purim after the name Pur, and the Jews ordained and took upon themselves and their seed to keep these two days every year. The days were to be remembered and kept throughout every generation, family, province, and city. These days of Purim should not fail from among the Jews nor the memorial of them perish from their seed, which shows Israel still celebrates Purim today.

Esther the queen, the daughter of Abihail, and Mordecai the Jew wrote with all authority to confirm this second letter of Purim. Letters were sent to all the Jews in the hundred twenty and seven provinces with words of peace and truth, to confirm the days of Purim in their appointed times. The decree of Esther confirmed these matters of Purim, and it was written in the book, which is Israel's own book of history. --- Topics: [Esau and Edom](/encyclopedia/esau-and-edom) · [The Feasts of the Most High](/encyclopedia/the-feasts-of-the-most-high)

The king Ahasuerus laid a tribute upon the land and upon the isles of the sea, and all the acts of his power and might, with the declaration of the greatness of Mardocheus whereunto the king advanced him, are written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Media and Persia. Mardocheus the Jew was next unto king Ahasuerus, great among the Jews and accepted of the multitude of his brethren, seeking the wealth of his people and speaking peace to all his seed. The Feast of Purim has now been established, and Mardocheus is lifted up to be number two in the kingdom for the works he did to warn the king and for standing with Esther through everything that led to this day.

At Rephidim there was no water, and the people did chide with Moses: wherefore is this that thou hast brought us up out of Egypt, to kill us and our children and our cattle with thirst? At the first sign of trial the people jumped off the Lord's bandwagon again, the same as we do today when tribulation comes. Moses cried unto the Lord, What shall I do unto this people? they be almost ready to stone me. They were ready to kill the prophet over water, blaming the brother for what only the Most High controls; we have to build our faith up like Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, who trusted the Lord even when trials came.

The Lord stood before Moses upon the rock in Horeb; Moses smote the rock, and water came out of it in the sight of the elders of Israel. He called the place Massah and Meribah, temptation and chiding, because they tempted the Lord, saying, Is the Lord among us, or not? That is wickedness: He had just made Egypt dark, slain their firstborn, and sent His angel in the chariot to guide us, and the people still asked whether He was with them. The mercy of the Most High in bearing that is beyond us.

Then came Amalek, and fought with Israel in Rephidim. Amalek was the first nation to come against Israel after Egypt; Amalek was Esau's grandson, born to Eliphaz of Timna the concubine, a duke in the land of Edom. When Moses held up his hand, Israel prevailed; when he let down his hand, Amalek prevailed. Aaron and Hur stayed up his hands until the going down of the sun. Moses was about eighty years old holding a rod above his head all day; the fathers were mighty men, stronger than we are today. The sign shewed the people whose hand their life was in: Moses is the man to hearken to, so do not speak against him. And Joshua discomfited Amalek with the edge of the sword; Joshua was a mighty warrior even then.

Write this for a memorial in a book, and rehearse it in the ears of Joshua: for I will utterly put out the remembrance of Amalek from under heaven. Moses wrote it, and [Deuteronomy 25](/bible/deuteronomy/25) is that rehearsal: remember what Amalek did unto thee by the way. Amalek smote the hindmost, all that were feeble, when Israel was faint and weary, and he feared not God. He did not meet the mighty men in the front; he went to the back to slay the women, the children, and the old ones. That same spirit works against the nation's young and old today. The Lord hath sworn that the Lord will have war with Amalek from generation to generation. By the time Moses rehearsed it in Deuteronomy, forty years had passed and the children of Amalek had done nothing themselves; hundreds of years after that the Lord sent Saul by Samuel to smite Amalek for what was done coming out of Egypt. God be true and every man a liar: the nations do not get away with what they did to His people, and the judgment carries to the seed. Saul did not finish Agag's line, and in Esther's day Haman the Agagite of that same seed rose against Israel; the war truly runs from generation to generation. Today that seed says they are Jews and are not, but are the synagogue of Satan, robbing Israel of identity and prospering off the oppression. The Lord says He will make them come and worship before thy feet, and to know that I have loved thee. The whole world is set up between Jacob and Esau, and Esau is the end of this world, the so-called white man, with Amalek leading; it is not speaking of the Arab man, for if Ishmael had a rulership still to come, Israel would have another captivity to enter, and Christ has already redeemed us from the curse of the law. The enmity was set from the garden between the serpent's seed and the woman's seed. They bruised Christ's heel, but at the end of the world Jacob bruises the head: the God of peace shall bruise Satan under your feet shortly.

name: Daniel
charge: Purposing in his heart not to defile himself with the king's meat; praying three times a day with his windows open toward Jerusalem, decree or no decree
summary: A captive boy in Babylon refused the king's meat and wine and asked for pulse and water; ten days later he looked better than the rest. Sixty years later, an old man under Darius, he kept his windows open and prayed as before, knowing the den was signed. He was in the den one night and the God he served shut the lions' mouths.
offense: Daniel purposed in his heart not to defile himself with the king's portion. He requested an alternative and proposed a ten-day trial, answering the officer's fear without abandoning his purpose (Daniel 1:8-16). Service in a foreign court did not require surrender of his obligations to God. Under Darius, his enemies could find no fault in his administration and sought occasion against him through the law of his God. After learning that the decree against petitioning any other than the king was signed, Daniel continued kneeling, praying, and giving thanks three times daily toward Jerusalem, as before (Daniel 6:4-10). The threat did not create his devotion, and it did not stop it.
judgment: God had brought Daniel into favour and tender love with the prince of the eunuchs. At the end of ten days their countenances appeared fairer and fatter in flesh than all the children which did eat the portion of the king's meat. God gave them knowledge and skill in all learning and wisdom: and Daniel had understanding in all visions and dreams. My God hath sent his angel, and hath shut the lions' mouths, that they have not hurt me: forasmuch as before him innocency was found in me. So Daniel prospered in the reign of Darius, and in the reign of Cyrus the Persian. Ezekiel names him with Noah and Job; Gabriel calls him greatly beloved.
offenseFull: Daniel purposed in his heart not to defile himself with the king's portion. He requested an alternative and proposed a ten-day trial, answering the officer's fear without abandoning his purpose (Daniel 1:8-16). Service in a foreign court did not require surrender of his obligations to God.

Under Darius, his enemies could find no fault in his administration and sought occasion against him through the law of his God. After learning that the decree against petitioning any other than the king was signed, Daniel continued kneeling, praying, and giving thanks three times daily toward Jerusalem, as before (Daniel 6:4-10). The threat did not create his devotion, and it did not stop it.

entries.commentary: In the third year of Jehoiakim king of Judah, Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon came to Jerusalem and besieged it, and the Most High gave Jehoiakim into his hand with part of the vessels of the house of God. Nebuchadnezzar carried those vessels into the land of Shinar to the house of his god and put them in his treasure house. This came to pass exactly as the prophets had warned. -

The king commanded to bring certain of the children of Israel, of the king's seed and of the princes: young men without blemish, well favoured, skilful in all wisdom, cunning in knowledge, understanding science, and able to stand in the king's palace. They took the best and the most educated among us, taught them the learning and the tongue of the Chaldeans, and set them to build up their kingdom. It is the same thing today, where our people serve in the governments and the congresses and are used to build up a system that is not our own. Often those who are chosen are not loyal to their own people; they are assimilated to believe they are a part of the system and accepted by that society, and they are well rewarded for it. When our people were carried over in the dark ages they were a civilized, educated people, engineers and men of every profession, and they were used to serve and build up Babylon. Israel is the greatest nation the earth has known, and Babylon benefited off our wisdom and our knowledge. The king also appointed them a daily provision of the king's meat and of the wine which he drank.

Among those taken were of the children of Judah: Daniel, Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah. The prince of the eunuchs gave them new names, Belteshazzar, Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego, part of assimilating them into the king's service.

It pleased Darius to set a hundred and twenty princes over the kingdom, with three presidents over them, of whom Daniel was first, so the king should have no damage. Daniel was preferred above the presidents and princes because an excellent spirit was in him, and the king thought to set him over the whole realm. He was set in a very high position in government.

The presidents and princes sought occasion against Daniel concerning the kingdom but could find none, because he was faithful and no error or fault was found in him. He was blameless. This is how our forefathers rolled, and the same kind of spirit we should be rolling in. They concluded they could only find something against him concerning the law of his God. -

The presidents and princes assembled and persuaded Darius to sign a firm decree that whoever asked a petition of any god or man for thirty days, save the king, would be cast into the den of lions, by the unchanging law of the Medes and Persians.

When Daniel knew the writing was signed he went home, and with his windows open toward Jerusalem kneeled and prayed three times a day, giving thanks as he did before. The men assembled, found him praying, and reported to the king that Daniel, of the children of the captivity of Judah, regarded neither the king nor the decree but made his petition three times a day. They really hated Daniel and knew the only way to find fault was concerning the law of his God.

The king was displeased with himself and laboured till sundown to deliver Daniel, but the men pressed that the law could not be changed, so he commanded Daniel cast into the den, saying, thy God whom thou servest continually, he will deliver thee. The king already understood why he was under the realm of Babylon and had seen what was going on. A stone was laid on the den and sealed with the king's signet.

The king went to his palace and passed the night fasting, with no instruments of music brought before him and his sleep gone from him. Why would the king be fasting. He rose very early and went in haste to the den, crying with a lamentable voice, O Daniel, servant of the living God, is thy God able to deliver thee from the lions.

Daniel answered that his God had sent his angel to shut the lions' mouths because innocency was found in him and he had done no hurt. The king was glad and commanded Daniel taken up, and no manner of hurt was found on him because he believed in his God; then the accusers, their children, and wives were cast in and the lions brake their bones before they reached the bottom. -

Darius wrote to all people, nations, and languages that in every dominion men tremble and fear before the God of Daniel, for he is the living God, stedfast for ever, whose kingdom shall not be destroyed and who delivereth and rescueth and worketh signs and wonders. So Daniel prospered in the reign of Darius and of Cyrus the Persian. He had a wise and humble spirit, was beloved by the king, could answer visions and interpret dreams, and was of the king's seed as shown in chapter one. --- Topics: [Idolatry](/encyclopedia/idolatry) · [Sacrifice and Atonement](/encyclopedia/sacrifice-and-atonement) · [The Priesthood](/encyclopedia/the-priesthood)

In the first year of Darius the son of Ahasuerus, of the seed of the Medes, made king over the realm of the Chaldeans, Daniel understood by the books the seventy years of the desolations of Jerusalem spoken to Jeremiah. This is the same Darius dealt with when the Persians and Medes were shown in chapters 7 and 8.

Daniel set his face unto the Most High to seek him by prayer and supplications, with fasting, sackcloth, and ashes, confessing that the people had sinned, committed iniquity, done wickedly, and rebelled, departing from his precepts and judgments. They had not hearkened unto the prophets who spake in his name to their kings, princes, fathers, and all the people of the land.

Righteousness belongs to the Most High, but confusion of faces to the people of Judah, the inhabitants of Jerusalem, and all Israel, near and far off, driven through all the countries because of their trespasses. Our people were scattered everywhere because of our transgressions, exactly as the law warned. -

All Israel transgressed the law by departing, so the curse was poured upon them and the oath written in the law of Moses, because they had sinned against him. The oath that was written is [Deuteronomy 28](/bible/deuteronomy/28), verses 1 through 68. -

Daniel appealed to the Most High who brought his people out of Egypt with a mighty hand, confessing they had sinned and done wickedly, and asking that his anger and fury be turned away from his city Jerusalem, his holy mountain. He pleaded for the Most High to hear, forgive, hearken, and do, not for their righteousness but for his great mercies, since the city and the people are called by his name.

While Daniel was speaking, praying, and confessing his sin and the sin of his people Israel, the man Gabriel, whom he had seen in the vision, was caused to fly swiftly and touched him about the time of the evening oblation. Gabriel came to give him skill and understanding, for at the beginning of his supplications the commandment came forth, and Daniel was greatly beloved.

Seventy weeks are determined upon the people and the holy city to finish the transgression, make an end of sins, make reconciliation for iniquity, bring in everlasting righteousness, seal up the vision, and anoint the most Holy. From the going forth of the commandment to restore and build Jerusalem unto Messiah the Prince shall be seven weeks and threescore and two weeks, the street built again even in troublous times. After threescore and two weeks Messiah is cut off, but not for himself, and the people of the prince that shall come destroy the city and the sanctuary. He confirms the covenant with many for one week, and in the midst of the week causes the sacrifice and oblation to cease. Daniel was given the four beasts first, then this further vision of the seventy weeks by Gabriel in the midst of his prayer and supplications. The bishop's class on the seventy weeks opens this up in full.

Certain of the elders of Israel came and sat before Ezekiel, and the word of the Lord said these men have set up their idols in their hearts, setting up something above God, and put the stumbling block of their iniquity before their face. The Most High asks whether He should be inquired of at all by them. Every man of the house of Israel that sets up his idols in his heart and comes to the prophet, the Lord will answer according to the multitude of his idols, that He may take the house of Israel in their own heart, because they are all estranged from Him through their idols and spiritual idolatry.

The Most High tells the house of Israel to repent, come back to His laws, and turn themselves from their idols and away from all their abominations. Every one of the house of Israel, or the stranger that sojourns in Israel, who separates himself from Him and sets up idols in his heart and comes to a prophet to inquire, the Lord will answer by Himself and set His face against that man. He will make him a sign and a proverb, meaning a curse, and cut him off from the midst of His people as an example, that they may know He is the Lord.

If a prophet is deceived when he has spoken a thing, the Lord Himself has deceived that prophet; do not try to deceive yourself in this truth, and when we get counsel we should take it and keep it moving. He will stretch out His hand upon that prophet and destroy him from the midst of His people Israel, and both shall bear the punishment of their iniquity. This is so the house of Israel may go no more astray from Him nor be polluted any more with their transgressions, but be His people and He their God. -

The word of the Lord came saying that when a land sins by trespassing grievously, He will stretch out His hand upon it, break the staff of its bread, and send famine to cut off man and beast. Though these three men, Noah, Daniel, and Job, were in it, they should deliver but their own souls by their righteousness. No one can save anyone else; it does not matter who you are or what your status is in Israel, you have to save yourself by your own righteousness.

If He causes noisome beasts to pass through the land and spoil it so that it is desolate and no man may pass through, this is one of His judgments. Though these three men were in it, as the Lord lives they shall deliver neither sons nor daughters; they only shall be delivered by their righteousness, but the land shall be desolate.

If He brings a sword upon that land to cut off man and beast, though these three men were in it, they shall deliver neither sons nor daughters. They only shall deliver themselves by their righteousness.

If He sends a pestilence into the land and pours out His fury upon it in blood to cut off man and beast, though Noah, Daniel, and Job were in it, they shall deliver neither son nor daughter. They shall but deliver their own souls by their righteousness; everyone has to work out their own righteousness in fear and trembling, delivering their own soul by keeping the Most High's commandments. -

[Leviticus 11](/bible/leviticus/11) tells you what you can and cannot eat. Among all the beasts of the earth, ye shall eat whatsoever parteth the hoof, and is clovenfooted, and cheweth the cud. A cloven hoof is a hoof split into two toes; mammals with this hoof include cattle, deer, antelopes, gazelles, goats, and sheep. Chewing the cud means the animal has more than one stomach: it chews its food, brings it back up into its mouth to be chewed again, and then digests it through another stomach.

Both marks must be present. There are animals that chew the cud and animals that divide the hoof but do not have both; those are unclean. The camel cheweth the cud but divideth not the hoof: you cannot eat camel. The coney is the pika, a small mountain dwelling mammal that resembles its close relative the rabbit, found at heights among the highest of any mammal. The scriptures already had it right: the rocks are a refuge for the conies, and the conies, a feeble folk, make their houses in the rocks. You cannot eat coney, and the hare likewise is unclean. The swine has only the one mark: he divideth the hoof and is clovenfooted, yet he cheweth not the cud; he is unclean unto you. You cannot eat pork; leave it alone. Their carcase shall ye not touch sits inside the dietary law: it goes into sacrificing the unclean thing and eating it, touching it with the mouth. It does not mean a dead animal in your path cannot be moved out of the way with the hands; the tabernacle itself had to be built by hand with badgers' skins.

Of all that are in the waters, ye shall eat whatsoever hath fins and scales; whatever has not fins and scales is an abomination. No shrimp, no crab, no lobster, no bottom dwellers. The Most High gave an excellent dietary law: high blood pressure and the like come from eating shellfish. He made these animals and knows what they do; if you eat what he allowed you will be fine. It is simple: if it does not have both fins and scales, leave it alone. A fish must have both scales and fins. Tilapia has scales and fins, so it may be eaten if you want it; sardines do not show both, so it looks like sardines are a no.

These are the fowls in abomination that shall not be eaten: the eagle, the ossifrage, the osprey, the vulture and the kite after his kind, every raven after his kind, the owl, the nighthawk, the cuckow, the hawk, the little owl, the cormorant, the great owl, the swan, the pelican, the gier eagle, the stork, the heron after her kind, the lapwing, and the bat. Look these up. The ossifrage, the bone breaker, is an older name for the bearded vulture, a scavenger famous for dropping bones on rocks to crack them open. The osprey is the seahawk or fishhawk, a fish eating bird of prey. The kite is a bird of prey in the family of the eagle. What is interesting is that all of these are scavengers and hunters; even in the waters the Most High did not want you to have the scavengers, and no shark, a hunter. He gave you this diet because he made these animals and knows what they do. After his kind: when the Most High made one, he made many of them, so the rule covers the whole family. On duck: the swan's closest relatives include the geese and ducks. The swan is unclean, and duck falls in the family of the swan, so you cannot eat duck; they are related, and it is the same thing.

All fowls that creep, going upon all four, are an abomination, yet those which have legs above their feet to leap withal upon the earth may be eaten: the locust, the bald locust, the beetle, and the grasshopper after his kind. You can eat locusts; John the Baptist ate locusts.

The carcases of every beast which divideth the hoof and is not clovenfooted nor cheweth the cud are unclean; whoever touches them is unclean until the even, and whoever bears the carcase washes his clothes. Whatsoever goeth upon his paws, among all manner of beasts that go on all four, is unclean: you cannot eat mountain lion, tiger, cougar, gorilla, dog, or cat; they have paws and walk on all fours.

These creeping things are unclean: the weasel, the mouse, the tortoise after his kind, the ferret, the chameleon, the lizard, the snail, and the mole. You cannot eat tortoise. If you find a dead mouse in your house, do not touch it: sweep it into a bag and throw it out. Whatever vessel one of them falls into when dead is unclean until the even and must be put into water; if it falls into one of your pots, clean that pot out and cook nothing in it until the even. An earthen vessel it falls into is broken and thrown out, and ovens and ranges for pots are broken down. If any part of their carcase falls on sowing seed which is to be sown, the seed is clean; but if water be put upon the seed and the carcase fall thereon, it is unclean and no good.

Even of a beast which ye may eat, if it die of itself, he that toucheth, eateth of, or beareth the carcase is unclean until the even and washes his clothes. Every creeping thing that creepeth upon the earth is an abomination: whatsoever goeth upon the belly, whatsoever goeth upon all four, and whatsoever hath more feet. You cannot eat centipedes and millipedes.

Sanctify yourselves, and ye shall be holy, for I am holy: for I am the Lord that bringeth you up out of the land of Egypt to be your God. This is the law of the beast and of the fowl and of every living creature that moveth in the waters and of every creature that creepeth upon the earth; the Most High explained everything and then summed it all up, to make a difference between the unclean and the clean, and between the beast that may be eaten and the beast that may not be eaten. Do not confuse yourself with [1 Timothy 4:4](/bible/1-timothy/4#v4), that you can eat whatever you want. Every creature is good and nothing to be refused if it be received with thanksgiving, for it is sanctified by the word of God; so find what the word of God sanctified, and that is the law of the beast in [Leviticus 11](/bible/leviticus/11). What is sanctified is what he already made clean. The law perisheth not, but remaineth in his force; that law did not change at all. Do not let anybody confuse you, especially if you are new in the truth: eat what the Most High instructed you to eat.

name: Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego
charge: Refusing to fall down and worship the golden image; not careful to answer the king in this matter
summary: Every people, nation and language fell down at the sound of the music. Three officers of the province of Babylon stood. Told they would go into the furnace and asked who was the God that should deliver them out of the king's hands, they answered that their God was able, and that if he did not, they would still not serve Nebuchadnezzar's gods. The furnace killed the men who threw them in and did not singe their hair.
offense: Nebuchadnezzar required the assembled peoples to worship his image at the sound of music, threatening the furnace for refusal. Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego would not comply. Brought before him, they declared that their God was able to deliver them, but that even if not, they would not serve his gods or worship the image (Daniel 3:16-18). Their obedience was not conditional upon receiving an escape from suffering. The commandment against idolatry settled whom they would worship before the king decided what he would do to them. His question about a God able to deliver from his hands could not enlarge the authority of those hands over their worship.
judgment: Lo, I see four men loose, walking in the midst of the fire, and they have no hurt; and the form of the fourth is like the Son of God. Upon whose bodies the fire had no power, nor was an hair of their head singed, neither were their coats changed, nor the smell of fire had passed on them. Nebuchadnezzar spake: Blessed be the God of Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego, who hath sent his angel, and delivered his servants that trusted in him, and have changed the king's word, and yielded their bodies, that they might not serve nor worship any god, except their own God. Then the king promoted them in the province of Babylon. The men that took them up were slain by the flame of the fire.
offenseFull: Nebuchadnezzar required the assembled peoples to worship his image at the sound of music, threatening the furnace for refusal. Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego would not comply. His question about a God able to deliver from his hands could not enlarge the authority of those hands over their worship.
judgmentFull: The king heated the furnace exceedingly, and its flame killed the men who carried them up. Yet he saw four walking loose within it, unhurt. The three came out with no hair singed, no change in their coats, and no smell of fire upon them (Daniel 3:19-27).

Nebuchadnezzar blessed their God, acknowledging that they had trusted Him and yielded their bodies rather than worship another. He issued a decree against speaking amiss of their God and promoted them in Babylon. The king who demanded their bowing publicly acknowledged the deliverance his threat had declared impossible.

name: The Chaldeans who accused the Jews
charge: Informing against the Jews to have them cast into the furnace for keeping the second commandment
summary: Certain Chaldeans came near and accused the Jews, reciting the king's own decree back to him and naming the three men who would not bow. They did not come for an offense against themselves; they came because Shadrach, Meshach and Abed-nego kept the commandment, and the decree made that a capital matter.
offense: At that time certain Chaldeans came near, and accused the Jews. They rehearsed the decree to Nebuchadnezzar — every man that shall hear the sound of the cornet shall fall down and worship the golden image, and whoso falleth not down shall be cast into the midst of a burning fiery furnace — and then laid the charge: There are certain Jews whom thou hast set over the affairs of the province of Babylon, Shadrach, Meshach, and Abed-nego; these men, O king, have not regarded thee: they serve not thy gods, nor worship the golden image which thou hast set up. Envy of men set over the province, dressed as loyalty to the king.
judgment: The account records no personal punishment upon these accusers. The men killed by the furnace were those who carried the three bound servants into it; they are not identified as the Chaldeans who brought the accusation (Daniel 3:22). The accused emerged unharmed. Nebuchadnezzar blessed their God, declared that no other god could deliver in this manner, and promoted them (Daniel 3:28-30). The accusation succeeded in bringing them before the furnace but failed to accomplish their destruction. The king's public acknowledgment reversed the disgrace the charge had sought to fasten upon their refusal.
offenseFull: Certain Chaldeans approached the king with an accusation against Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego. They repeated the command to worship the image and its penalty, then named the Jewish officers as men who disregarded the king and did not serve his gods (Daniel 3:8-12).

The charge made refusal of idolatry appear as disloyalty in office. The men had indeed refused the worship, but the king's decree could not make that worship righteous. The accusers invoked public authority to bring faithful servants under a sentence of death.

It pleased Darius to set a hundred and twenty princes over the kingdom, with three presidents over them, of whom Daniel was first, so the king should have no damage. Daniel was preferred above the presidents and princes because an excellent spirit was in him, and the king thought to set him over the whole realm. He was set in a very high position in government.

The presidents and princes sought occasion against Daniel concerning the kingdom but could find none, because he was faithful and no error or fault was found in him. He was blameless. This is how our forefathers rolled, and the same kind of spirit we should be rolling in. They concluded they could only find something against him concerning the law of his God. -

The presidents and princes assembled and persuaded Darius to sign a firm decree that whoever asked a petition of any god or man for thirty days, save the king, would be cast into the den of lions, by the unchanging law of the Medes and Persians.

When Daniel knew the writing was signed he went home, and with his windows open toward Jerusalem kneeled and prayed three times a day, giving thanks as he did before. The men assembled, found him praying, and reported to the king that Daniel, of the children of the captivity of Judah, regarded neither the king nor the decree but made his petition three times a day. They really hated Daniel and knew the only way to find fault was concerning the law of his God.

The king was displeased with himself and laboured till sundown to deliver Daniel, but the men pressed that the law could not be changed, so he commanded Daniel cast into the den, saying, thy God whom thou servest continually, he will deliver thee. The king already understood why he was under the realm of Babylon and had seen what was going on. A stone was laid on the den and sealed with the king's signet.

The king went to his palace and passed the night fasting, with no instruments of music brought before him and his sleep gone from him. Why would the king be fasting. He rose very early and went in haste to the den, crying with a lamentable voice, O Daniel, servant of the living God, is thy God able to deliver thee from the lions.

Daniel answered that his God had sent his angel to shut the lions' mouths because innocency was found in him and he had done no hurt. The king was glad and commanded Daniel taken up, and no manner of hurt was found on him because he believed in his God; then the accusers, their children, and wives were cast in and the lions brake their bones before they reached the bottom. -

Darius wrote to all people, nations, and languages that in every dominion men tremble and fear before the God of Daniel, for he is the living God, stedfast for ever, whose kingdom shall not be destroyed and who delivereth and rescueth and worketh signs and wonders. So Daniel prospered in the reign of Darius and of Cyrus the Persian. name: Nebuchadnezzar
charge: Pride: is not this great Babylon, that I have built?
summary: Warned by Daniel's interpretation of the tree dream to break off his sins by righteousness and his iniquities by showing mercy to the poor, the king walked on his palace roof twelve months later and took the credit for the empire. While the word was in his mouth a voice fell from heaven.
offense: Nebuchadnezzar received a dream warning that his greatness would be cut down until he knew that the Most High rules in the kingdom of men. Daniel interpreted it and counseled him to break off his sins by righteousness and his iniquities by showing mercy to the poor (Daniel 4:19-27). The warning offered instruction before the sentence fell. Twelve months later the king walked in his palace and boasted of Babylon as the work of his own might for the honor of his majesty. He treated entrusted dominion as an achievement belonging wholly to himself. The words were still in his mouth when the heavenly answer declared that his kingdom had departed (Daniel 4:28-32).
judgment: He was driven from men, ate grass as oxen, and was wet with the dew of heaven until the appointed times passed. His dependence was exposed beneath the grandeur in which he had gloried. At the end he lifted his eyes to heaven, his understanding returned, and he blessed the Most High. His counselors sought him again, his kingdom was restored, and he confessed that the King of heaven can abase those who walk in pride (Daniel 4:33-37). The restored king's testimony gave God the honor his former boast had claimed for himself.

verses.text: 27Wherefore, O king, let my counsel be acceptable unto thee, and break off thy sins by righteousness, and thine iniquities by shewing mercy to the poor; if it may be a lengthening of thy tranquillity. 28All this came upon the king Nebuchadnezzar. 29At the end of twelve months he walked in the palace of the kingdom of Babylon. 30The king spake, and said, Is not this great Babylon, that I have built for the house of the kingdom by the might of my power, and for the honour of my majesty? 31While the word was in the king’s mouth, there fell a voice from heaven, saying, O king Nebuchadnezzar, to thee it is spoken; The kingdom is departed from thee. 32And they shall drive thee from men, and thy dwelling shall be with the beasts of the field: they shall make thee to eat grass as oxen, and seven times shall pass over thee, until thou know that the most High ruleth in the kingdom of men, and giveth it to whomsoever he will. 33The same hour was the thing fulfilled upon Nebuchadnezzar: and he was driven from men, and did eat grass as oxen,

34And at the end of the days I Nebuchadnezzar lifted up mine eyes unto heaven, and mine understanding returned unto me, and I blessed the most High, and I praised and honoured him that liveth for ever, whose dominion is an everlasting dominion, and his kingdom is from generation to generation: 35And all the inhabitants of the earth are reputed as nothing: and he doeth according to his will in the army of heaven, and among the inhabitants of the earth: and none can stay his hand, or say unto him, What doest thou? 36At the same time my reason returned unto me; and for the glory of my kingdom, mine honour and brightness returned unto me; and my counsellors and my lords sought unto me; and I was established in my kingdom, and excellent majesty was added unto me. 37Now I Nebuchadnezzar praise and extol and honour the King of heaven, all whose works are truth, and his ways judgment: and those that walk in pride he is able to abase.

entries.commentary: Nebuchadnezzar proclaimed to all people, nations, and languages the signs and wonders the high God worked toward him, whose kingdom is everlasting, then told how a dream made him afraid and he decreed to bring in all the wise men of Babylon to interpret it. Remember from the day before that he had already brought in all his wise men once and they could not recall or interpret his dream; when the captain went out to slay the wise men he came upon Daniel, who was granted favour, consulted the Most High, and was given the vision.

The magicians, astrologers, Chaldeans, and soothsayers could not make known the interpretation, but at last Daniel came in, named Belteshazzar after the king's god, in whom is the spirit of the holy gods. Daniel was named after one of the king's gods. It is the same thing as Hadassah, whose name was changed to Esther; this is not new for us.

Nebuchadnezzar saw a great tree reaching to heaven, feeding and sheltering all flesh, then a watcher and a holy one came down and commanded it hewn down, its stump left bound with iron and brass, its heart changed to a beast's, till seven times pass over him. The matter is by the decree of the watchers, to the intent that the living may know that the Most High ruleth in the kingdom of men and giveth it to whomsoever he will and setteth over it the basest of men. That is what we see today, the basest of men ruling the earth. -

Daniel, astonished for an hour, told the king the dream was for his enemies: the tree is the king himself, grown strong to the ends of the earth. The decree of the Most High is that he shall be driven from men to dwell with the beasts and eat grass as oxen, wet with the dew of heaven, till seven times pass and he knows the Most High ruleth; the stump left means his kingdom is kept for him once he knows the heavens do rule. Daniel counselled him to break off his sins by righteousness and his iniquities by shewing mercy to the poor, that his tranquillity might be lengthened. You need to walk in righteousness and show mercy to the poor.

Twelve months later, walking in his palace, the king boasted, is not this great Babylon that I have built by my might for the honour of my majesty. He was very proud and boastful. While the word was in his mouth a voice from heaven pronounced the kingdom departed, and the same hour he was driven from men, ate grass as oxen, his hairs grown like eagles' feathers and his nails like birds' claws.

At the end of the days Nebuchadnezzar lifted his eyes to heaven, his understanding returned, and he blessed and honoured the Most High, whose dominion is everlasting and before whom all the inhabitants of the earth are reputed as nothing. None can stay his hand or say unto him, what doest thou. When the Most High declares a thing shall come to pass, it comes to pass. -

His reason and the glory of his kingdom returned, and he praised and extolled the King of heaven, whose works are truth and ways judgment, and who is able to abase those that walk in pride. We already understood that the Most High can bring one up and set another down, but the heathen had to learn it by being jacked up, literally turned to crawl like a bird with the heart of a beast; as soon as his understanding returned he praised the one true living God. -

Belshazzar the king made a great feast to a thousand of his lords and, while tasting the wine, commanded the golden and silver vessels his father Nebuchadnezzar had taken from the temple in Jerusalem be brought so he, his princes, wives, and concubines might drink in them. This is Belshazzar the king, not Belteshazzar, who is Daniel. They drank and praised the gods of gold, silver, brass, iron, wood, and stone. -

In the same hour fingers of a man's hand wrote on the plaster of the wall, and the king's countenance changed, his knees smote together, so terrified that the joints of his loins were loosed. Picture him sitting back drinking with his lords, wives, and concubines, having a good time, and then a hand starts writing on the wall; he was terrified out of everything. He cried aloud for the astrologers, Chaldeans, and soothsayers, offering scarlet, a gold chain, and to be third ruler in the kingdom to whoever could read it, but none of his wise men could read the writing or interpret it, and he was greatly troubled.

The queen came into the banquet house and told the king of the man Daniel, in whom is the spirit of the holy gods, whom Nebuchadnezzar his father had made master of the magicians because an excellent spirit, knowledge, and understanding were found in him. Daniel was brought in, and the king offered him scarlet, a gold chain, and the third rulership if he could read the writing and make known the interpretation.

Daniel told the king to keep his gifts and rewards, then recounted how the Most High gave Nebuchadnezzar his kingdom and greatness, and how, when his heart was lifted up in pride, he was deposed and driven to dwell with the wild asses until he knew the Most High ruleth in the kingdom of men. Belshazzar had not humbled his heart though he knew all this, but lifted himself against the Lord of heaven, drank from the temple vessels, and praised gods of silver, gold, brass, iron, wood, and stone that see not nor hear, while the God in whose hand his breath is he did not glorify. -

Daniel read the writing: MENE, MENE, TEKEL, UPHARSIN. MENE, God has numbered the kingdom and finished it; TEKEL, the king is weighed in the balances and found wanting; PERES, the kingdom is divided and given to the Medes and Persians.

Belshazzar clothed Daniel with scarlet, put a chain about his neck, and proclaimed him third ruler, but that same night Belshazzar the king of the Chaldeans was slain and Darius the Median took the kingdom, being about threescore and two years old. Immediately after the interpretation the kingdom was translated from Belshazzar to the Medes and Persians.

Nebuchadnezzar made an image of gold, threescore cubits high and six cubits broad, and set it up in the plain of Dura, then gathered the princes, governors, captains, judges, treasurers, counsellors, sheriffs, and rulers to its dedication. We have seen things like this before. When they build a monument or a new federal building they hold a dedication and a ribbon-cutting ceremony. This is very similar.

A herald cried that when the people heard the cornet, flute, harp, sackbut, psaltery, dulcimer, and all kinds of music they were to fall down and worship the golden image. We see the same thing today when they play the national anthem at ball games and ceremonies. You are supposed to take your hat off and put your hand over your heart. That is a form of worshipping the image of the eagle today.

Whoever did not fall down and worship would the same hour be cast into the midst of the burning fiery furnace, so when the music sounded all the people, nations, and languages fell down and worshipped the golden image.

Certain Chaldeans came near and accused the Jews, telling the king that Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego, whom he had set over the affairs of the province, did not regard him, serve his gods, nor worship the golden image. The reason we did not bow was according to the law. -

In his rage Nebuchadnezzar brought the three men and demanded whether they would fall down and worship, threatening the furnace and asking, who is that God that shall deliver you out of my hands. He is talking tough, talking big, challenging our God when he asks who is going to deliver you out of his hands.

The three answered that they were not careful to answer him in this matter: their God whom they serve is able to deliver them from the burning fiery furnace and out of the king's hand. But if not, be it known unto thee, O king, that they would not serve his gods nor worship the golden image. This is exactly what was read in [Exodus 20](/bible/exodus/20).

Full of fury, Nebuchadnezzar commanded the furnace heated seven times more than usual and had his mighty men bind the three in their coats and garments and cast them in. The furnace was so hot that the flame slew the men who carried Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego up to it. For more of this history the Song of the Three Holy Children can be read; for the sake of time it was only referenced here.

The three men fell down bound into the furnace, but Nebuchadnezzar rose up astonished and said he saw four men loose, walking in the midst of the fire, unhurt, and the form of the fourth was like the Son of God.

Nebuchadnezzar called them servants of the Most High God to come forth, and the fire had no power on their bodies: not a hair singed, their coats unchanged, nor the smell of fire on them. It was as if they had never fallen into the fire; not even the smell of smoke was on these brothers.

Nebuchadnezzar blessed the God of Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego, who sent his angel to deliver the servants that trusted in him and would not serve nor worship any god except their own God. He understood at that time that we had our own God. Why do people not understand that today. He decreed that any people, nation, or language that spake amiss against their God would be cut in pieces, because there is no other God that can deliver after this sort, and he promoted the three in the province of Babylon. When the nations get jacked up they come to know who has the real, true, living God; other heathen rulers came to the same acknowledgement, such as Antiochus and Naaman the Syrian. -

The Most High tells Jeremiah to make bonds and yokes, put them on his neck, and send them to the kings of Edom, Moab, Ammon, Tyrus, and Zidon by their messengers to Zedekiah. The Most High made the earth, man, and beast by His power and outstretched arm and gives it to whom it seems meet to Him; He has now given all these lands and the beasts of the field into the hand of Nebuchadnezzar His servant. All the nations shall serve him, his son, and his son's son until the time of his land comes, when many nations and great kings shall serve themselves of him; the Most High uses people, He used Nebuchadnezzar, Cyrus, and Pharaoh alike.

The nation and kingdom that will not serve Nebuchadnezzar and will not put its neck under the yoke of Babylon the Most High will punish with the sword, the famine, and the pestilence until they are consumed. Therefore they must not hearken to their prophets, diviners, dreamers, enchanters, and sorcerers who say they shall not serve the king of Babylon, for they prophesy a lie. The nations that bring their neck under the yoke and serve him He will let remain in their own land to till it and dwell there; this is the Most High saying that whatever we are commanded to do, even the other nations are told to serve Babylon or answer to Him.

Jeremiah speaks the same words to Zedekiah, telling him to bring his neck under the yoke of the king of Babylon and serve him and live, rather than die by the sword, the famine, and the pestilence. He is not to hearken to the prophets who say he shall not serve Babylon, for they prophesy a lie in the Most High's name that will drive the people out to perish along with the prophets themselves.

Jeremiah warns the priests and all the people not to listen to the prophets who claim the vessels of the Lord's house will shortly be brought back from Babylon, for they prophesy a lie; they should serve the king of Babylon and live. If they were true prophets they would make intercession that the remaining vessels not go to Babylon, but instead the pillars, the sea, the bases, and the residue of the vessels shall be carried to Babylon and remain there until the day the Most High visits them and restores them to this place. The whole warning is that Babylon is one the Most High will use to take over everything, and the people had better listen and serve him, because all these prophecies were meant to happen and they did happen. --- Topics: [Clean and Unclean Meats](/encyclopedia/clean-and-unclean-meats) · [Esau and Edom](/encyclopedia/esau-and-edom) · [Idolatry](/encyclopedia/idolatry) · [The Priesthood](/encyclopedia/the-priesthood)

name: Belshazzar
charge: Drinking from the temple vessels and praising the gods of gold and silver
summary: At a feast for a thousand lords, Belshazzar called for the gold and silver vessels Nebuchadnezzar had taken from the house of God in Jerusalem, drank wine from them with his wives and concubines, and praised the gods of gold, silver, brass, iron, wood, and stone. Fingers of a man's hand wrote on the plaster.
offense: Belshazzar commanded that the vessels taken from Jerusalem's temple be brought to his feast. He and his company drank from them while praising gods of gold, silver, brass, iron, wood, and stone (Daniel 5:1-4). Holy vessels became instruments in a public display of contempt for the God whose house they had served. Daniel reminded him of Nebuchadnezzar's humbling and charged that he had not humbled his own heart though he knew it. The gods praised at the feast could neither see nor hear, while the God holding his breath and all his ways received no glory (Daniel 5:18-23). Knowledge of the earlier judgment increased his accountability.
judgment: The writing on the wall announced that God had numbered and finished his kingdom, weighed him and found him wanting, and given the kingdom to the Medes and Persians. Gifts and advancement offered to the interpreter could not purchase a different interpretation. Belshazzar clothed Daniel in scarlet and proclaimed his rank, but that night the king was slain and Darius the Median received the kingdom (Daniel 5:25-31). The sentence reached the ruler while the honors he could distribute still appeared to be in his hand. His feast could not preserve the breath he had failed to acknowledge as God's gift.

verses.text: 1Belshazzar the king made a great feast to a thousand of his lords, and drank wine before the thousand. 2Belshazzar, whiles he tasted the wine, commanded to bring the golden and silver vessels which his father Nebuchadnezzar had taken out of the temple which was in Jerusalem; that the king, and his princes, his wives, and his concubines, might drink therein. 3Then they brought the golden vessels that were taken out of the temple of the house of God which was at Jerusalem; and the king, and his princes, his wives, and his concubines, drank in them. 4They drank wine, and praised the gods of gold, and of silver, of brass, of iron, of wood, and of stone.

22And thou his son, O Belshazzar, hast not humbled thine heart, though thou knewest all this; 23But hast lifted up thyself against the Lord of heaven; and they have brought the vessels of his house before thee, and thou, and thy lords, thy wives, and thy concubines, have drunk wine in them; and thou hast praised the gods of silver, and gold, of brass, iron, wood, and stone, which see not, nor hear, nor know: and the God in whose hand thy breath is, and whose are all thy ways, hast thou not glorified: 24Then was the part of the hand sent from him; and this writing was written.

25And this is the writing that was written, MENE, MENE, TEKEL, UPHARSIN. 26This is the interpretation of the thing: MENE; God hath numbered thy kingdom, and finished it. 27TEKEL; Thou art weighed in the balances, and art found wanting. 28PERES; Thy kingdom is divided, and given to the Medes and Persians. 29Then commanded Belshazzar, and they clothed Daniel with scarlet, and put a chain of gold about his neck, and made a proclamation concerning him, that he should be the third ruler in the kingdom. 30In that night was Belshazzar the king of the Chaldeans slain. 31And Darius the Median took the kingdom, being about threescore and two years old.

In the first year of Cyrus the word of the Most High spoken by Jeremiah is fulfilled. The Lord stirs up the spirit of Cyrus to make a proclamation throughout his kingdom. Cyrus was one of the first kings of Persia, and the Most High used him to give the order to rebuild Jerusalem. His coming was prophesied long before by name. -

Cyrus calls for any of the Most High's people to go up to Jerusalem and build the house of the Lord God of Israel. Those who remained behind were to help the returning ones with silver, gold, goods, and beasts, beside the freewill offering for the house of God.

The chief of the fathers of Judah and Benjamin, with the priests and the Levites, rose up, all whose spirit the Most High had raised to go build the house of the Lord. Those around them strengthened their hands with vessels of silver and gold, with goods and beasts and precious things, beside the freewill offerings.

Cyrus brings out the vessels of the house of the Lord that Nebuchadnezzar had carried from Jerusalem and stored among his own goods. He sends them back by the hand of Mithredath the treasurer and numbers them to Sheshbazzar the prince of Judah.

The vessels are counted out, gold and silver charges, basins, knives, and other vessels totaling 5,400. All these Sheshbazzar brings up with the captives that returned from Babylon to Jerusalem. The same account is recorded in 1 Esdras.

The Most High raises against Babylon a destroying wind and sends fanners to fan her and empty her land. Spare not her young men; destroy utterly all her host. The slain fall in the land of the Chaldeans, thrust through in her streets, for Israel has not been forsaken, nor Judah of his God, though their land was filled with sin against the Holy One of Israel.

Israel and Judah have not been forsaken of the Most High. Flee out of the midst of Babylon and deliver every man his soul; do not be cut off in her iniquity, for this is the time of the Lord's vengeance. -

Babylon has been a golden cup in the Lord's hand that made all the earth drunken; the nations drank of her wine and are mad. All the nations partook, and even the children of Israel were made to drink of the cup of our own destruction. Babylon is suddenly fallen and destroyed. We would have healed Babylon, but she is not healed; forsake her, and let everyone go into his own country.
Her judgment reaches unto heaven and is lifted up even to the skies. The Most High has brought forth our righteousness; come, and let us declare in Zion the work of the Lord our God.

Make bright the arrows and gather the shields; the Lord has raised up the spirit of the kings of the Medes, for his device against Babylon is to destroy it, the vengeance of his temple. Set up the standard upon the walls of Babylon, make the watch strong, set the watchmen, and prepare the ambushes. The standard is the Bible, and the men are made ready, for the Most High has both devised and done what he spoke.

Babylon dwells upon many waters, abundant in treasures, but thine end is come. She dwells upon many waters because her embassies reach into every land, from South Africa to Europe to the Philippines; her treasure was built on the backs of the slaves and the stolen Western Hemisphere. The Lord of hosts has sworn to fill her with men as with caterpillars who lift up a shout against her. She is destroyed from within, because being a melting pot, the other nations infiltrate and destroy America from the inside out, the way a caterpillar becomes an infestation that devours a whole land.

He made the earth by his power, established the world by his wisdom, and stretched out the heavens by his understanding; he brings the wind out of his treasures. Every man is brutish in his knowledge, and every founder is confounded by the graven image, for his molten image is falsehood and there is no breath in them. But the portion of Jacob is not like them, for he is the former of all things, and Israel is the rod of his inheritance.

Thou art my battle-ax and weapons of war; with thee the Most High breaks in pieces the nations and destroys kingdoms, the horse and his rider, the chariot and his rider. With thee he breaks in pieces man and woman, old and young, the young man and the maid, the shepherd and his flock, the husbandman and his oxen, and the captains and rulers. The sisters who love feminism had better humble down, because the woman is named right alongside the man. -

The Most High will render unto Babylon and to all the inhabitants of Chaldea all the evil they have done in Zion. Behold, he is against thee, O destroying mountain that destroys all the earth. He will stretch out his hand, roll her down from the rocks, and make her a burnt mountain; they shall take of her no stone for a corner nor foundation, but she shall be desolate forever.

Set up a standard in the land, blow the trumpet among the nations, and prepare the nations against her; call the kingdoms of Ararat, Minni, and Ashkenaz, and appoint a captain against her. Prepare the nations with the king of the Medes, the captains, the rulers, and all the land of his dominion against Babylon.

The land trembles and sorrows, for every purpose of the Lord is performed against Babylon to make it a desolation without inhabitant. The mighty men of Babylon forbear to fight and remain in their holds; their might fails and they become as women. One post runs to meet another to tell the king of Babylon that his city is taken at one end and the passages are stopped. The daughter of Babylon is like a threshing floor; it is time to thresh her, and the time of her harvest shall come.

Nebuchadnezzar has devoured Israel, crushed her, made her an empty vessel, and swallowed her like a dragon. Let the violence done to Zion be upon Babylon, and her blood upon the inhabitants of Chaldea. The Most High will plead Zion's cause, take vengeance for her, and dry up Babylon's sea and springs. Babylon shall become heaps, a dwelling place for dragons, an astonishment and a hissing without inhabitant.

They roar together like lions and yell as lions' whelps. In their heat the Most High makes their feasts and makes them drunken, that they may sleep a perpetual sleep and not wake. He brings them down like lambs to the slaughter, like rams with the he-goats.

How is Sheshach taken, the praise of the whole earth surprised, and Babylon become an astonishment among the nations? The sea is come up upon Babylon, covered with the multitude of its waves. Her cities are a desolation, a dry land and a wilderness, where no man dwells and no son of man passes by.

The Most High will punish Bel in Babylon and bring out of his mouth what he has swallowed, and the wall of Babylon shall fall. My people, go out of the midst of her and deliver every man his soul from the fierce anger of the Lord. A rumor shall come one year and another rumor the next, with violence in the land and ruler against ruler. Do not let your heart faint at the rumor that is heard.

The days come when the Most High does judgment upon the graven images of Babylon, and her whole land is confounded and her slain fall in her midst. Then heaven and earth and all in them sing for Babylon, for the spoiler comes from the north. As Babylon caused the slain of Israel to fall, so at Babylon shall fall the slain of all the earth.

Ye that have escaped the sword, go away, stand not still, remember the Lord afar off, and let Jerusalem come into your mind. We are confounded because strangers have come into the sanctuaries of the Lord's house. Though Babylon should mount up to heaven and fortify the height of her strength, yet from the Most High shall spoilers come unto her.

A cry and great destruction come from Babylon, for the Lord has spoiled her. Her mighty men are taken and their bows broken, and the Lord of recompense shall surely requite. He makes drunk her princes, wise men, captains, rulers, and mighty men, that they sleep a perpetual sleep and not wake. The broad walls of Babylon shall be utterly broken and her high gates burned with fire, and the people shall labor in vain.

Jeremiah commanded Seraiah, when he went with Zedekiah to Babylon, to read all the evil written against Babylon and then declare that the Most High has spoken to cut off this place forever. After reading the book, Seraiah was to bind a stone to it and cast it into the midst of the Euphrates, saying, thus shall Babylon sink and not rise from the evil the Most High brings upon her. Thus far are the words of Jeremiah.
